So, do you know what’s going to happen with the baby? I mean, it’s been a week since she was born and I’m still not sure how we’re going to manage everything. Honestly, I don’t know either. Morning everyone, thanks for waking up. I’ve made some eggs and toast, and there’s coffee brewing. Morning, love. I’m more of a coffee person, so I’ll take a cup. How’s the weather looking today? Well, I've been meaning to ask you both, what's with the rat puppet? I saw it in the corner of the living room, and it's got more personality than most of the people I know these days. So, do you know what you're going to do today, Mum? I was just thinking about going to the museum or maybe grabbing some gelato. I was actually planning to do a bit of shopping first. So, do you guys ever get tired of eating Chinese food? Like, I mean, it’s good, but I feel like I could eat something else every week. Honestly, I think we’re all just used to it. Well, I think we've got a decent amount of stuff in here. I was just thinking, maybe we should start clearing out the old stuff from the attic. It’s been ages since we've done anything with it. Well, I've been meaning to ask you all, what do you think about the new software they've been pushing at the local library? I tried to download it, but it just kept crashing. I've been thinking, you know, about the schools in my day. I was in a small village school like Costessey, and it was just a one-room school. We had to sweep the floors and tidy up the desks. You know, I still remember the sound of the bell ringing at my old school in Birmingham. That was the signal for everything to start. I used to love that. It made you feel like the day was just beginning. Yeah, I think the bell was a big deal back then. Now, you have mobile phones, and the kids don’t even notice when the bell rings. It’s like they’re always in their own little world. I think it’s great, but I’m not sure if it’s the best way to teach. You know, sometimes the kids just need to have a bit of down time, and they don’t get that anymore. I agree. No buses, no cars. It was a bit of a trek, but it was good exercise. Now, the kids are driven everywhere. I don’t know if they have the same sense of independence. Oh, I hear you. My grandson goes to a school nearby, and he’s always rushing to get out of the car. I think he’s more excited to get to the playground than to actually learn anything. I mean, sure, it’s important for kids to have friends, but if they’re not learning, what’s the point?

You’ve got that kind of drive.      Honestly, I’ve thought about it a little. I’ve always been in sales and marketing, so I guess I’ve been working in a corporate environment for most of my career. But I also know how much work it takes to run a business. I mean, when I got my first job as a civil servant, I was terrified, but now I really enjoy it. It’s stable, and I know exactly what’s expected of me.      That’s true, but I still think there’s something to be said for the freedom of a small business. I mean, I’ve got two kids, and I can’t imagine giving up the stability of my current job. But I do miss the idea of having more time to do the things I want to do—like knitting, which I used to do all the time.      Oh, I know what you mean. I used to knit too, before the kids came along. My mum still knits, though. She’s always making me a new scarf every Christmas. It’s kind of a tradition.      That’s sweet. I don’t knit, but I do love the idea of having a hobby that you can do at your own pace.

So, do you know what’s happening with the new flat in town? I heard it's going to be like a proper student hub, with all the amenities and everything. So, do you think we should go to the market tomorrow? I mean, I’d love to try some local food, but I’m not sure if I’m up for it after a long day of walking around the town. I think it’s a good idea. But I’m not sure if we should go there. I mean, it’s a bit of a drive, and I don’t want to waste time if it’s not worth it. You know, I think it’s worth the drive. I went there last week, and the food was amazing—especially the seafood. They even have a few local specialties that aren’t available back home. Plus, it’s a nice way to spend an evening. Yeah, I guess that’s true. I just don’t want to end up with something I can’t eat. I’ve had some weird food experiences in the past. I can relate. I once tried a dish at a local restaurant and ended up with a stomachache for a whole day. But I definitely wouldn’t say no to trying something new again. I think I’ll go with you, just because I’m curious. I mean, I’ve heard so many good things about it. Also, I’ve been wanting to try some of the local snacks. That sounds amazing. But I also want to take some time to explore the town. I mean, the architecture is so different from back home. I’d like to see the old buildings and maybe even get some photos. That’s a good plan.

I've just got back from Cornwall, lass. You'd have thought I'd been to Mars with the way I got the sun on me. Oh, you were out there? I heard you were volunteering at YHA. Did you enjoy it? Yeah, I heard you were out there. I remember you talking about it last week. How did it go? It was alright, I suppose. Got to meet all sorts of people, some of them were quite interesting. You’re always talking about all these places. I think you’d make a great travel writer if you weren’t retired. Oh, I wouldn’t say that.

So, do you know what’s for dinner tonight? I’ve been meaning to ask. I think it’s pasta with some sort of sauce, and I’m pretty sure there’s garlic bread. I can’t believe it’s already Monday. I feel like I just got back from Barcelona yesterday. I know, right? It’s hard to believe how fast the weekend went. Did you have a good time? Oh, it was amazing! The sun was out every day, and we managed to fit in a few things. We visited Park Guell, had tapas every night, and even took a boat tour of the city. That sounds incredible. I was stuck in the office all weekend. It was so rainy, and I didn’t get to do anything fun. You should come with me next time. I mean, we can plan a trip together. We could go to Paris too. I’ve always wanted to see the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre. Paris? That sounds like a great idea. I’d love to go. But I’m not sure if I’ll have time. I’ve got this big project coming up at work. I understand. Let’s just plan something for the next holiday. Maybe we can take a weekend trip to the countryside. I’ve heard there are some beautiful places in the south of England. That sounds nice. I could really use a break. I’ve been working way too much lately. I think I need to get away for a few days, even if it’s just a short trip. I agree. Maybe we can start planning something soon. I’m thinking of a few spots. Have you ever thought about doing something like that? Not really. I’ve been too focused on work. But I would love to take a break and just relax. Maybe we can go to the coast or somewhere with good food. That’s a good idea. I could take you to one of the seaside towns I’ve visited. I think there’s a nice little place in the south called Brighton. It’s got great cafes, and the sea views are beautiful. I’m really looking forward to it. I can’t wait to get out of the office and have some time for myself.

So, do you live in the UK still? I mean, I know it's not exactly the same as living here in North Cyprus, but I’m curious how your life has been lately. I actually moved back to London a few years ago. It’s a bit of a culture shock after spending so much time abroad. But I guess it’s the same old London—just more expensive and harder to get a table at a decent restaurant. Oh, I can imagine. I’ve only been here a couple of times, but the food is amazing. That sounds incredible. I’ve always wanted to travel more, but I just never had the time or money. I guess I’m a bit of a workaholic. Though I’ve started to realize that work isn’t everything. I think you’re right. I remember when I first started teaching, I thought I’d never go anywhere. Now I’m thinking about taking a sabbatical next year.

So, do you think we should get a dog? I mean, we’ve been housemates for like, what, three months now, and I’m starting to feel like I need a bit more structure in my day. A dog? That’s a big decision. You can’t just get a dog and then realise you can’t handle it. What about the other housemates? They’ve got their own routines. Yeah, I know. Exactly. And maybe we can start small. Like, just get a pet for a few weeks and see how it goes. If it doesn’t work, we can always back out. Yeah, maybe. I’m just tired of feeling like we’re just living in the same house but not actually living together. It’s like we’re all separate, you know? We’re not even really talking about our future plans. I know what you mean.

Well, I've just got back from the shops, love. I thought I'd pop in and get a few bits and bobs, but it turned into quite the adventure. Oh, did you get everything you needed? You used to make the most amazing lasagne. I still miss that. I know, it’s been ages since I’ve had the time or the energy to do it. I think I’ll try again soon. Maybe next week, when I’ve got a bit more of a plan. That sounds good. You should. I’ll help you. I’ve got a few ideas for the sauce. You would, wouldn’t you? Oh, I bet you’ve got some fancy recipes now. I bet you’re making soufflés and all that. Well, I’ve got the basics down. Maybe some of the more complicated ones are a bit too much, though. I can imagine. You know, I’ve been thinking about going to the market again.

Well, it’s getting late, and I do have to get up early for my exam tomorrow. I was just thinking, I should probably get the heating on a bit more, don’t you think?      Yeah, it’s pretty cold in here. I’ve been keeping my feet under the blanket, but I’m still shivering. I reckon we should all get into our pyjamas and make ourselves comfortable. It’s been a long day, and we’ve had a lot to talk about.      Oh, I’ve been meaning to talk about that. I heard from the postman today that Grandpa’s coming over next week. Oh, that sounds like the kind of story that could fill a few books. I remember when I was young, I used to ride a bicycle up and down the streets of Hull. It wasn’t a horse, but it still got me where I needed to go.      Yeah, those were the days. I remember my dad used to tell me about his own childhood—how he used to walk miles through the fields to get to school in North Ferriby. He said it was freezing, but he never complained. Just a tough little kid, that one.      Sounds like you all had similar experiences. I mean, I’ve only been to York a few times, but even there, the winters are pretty harsh. I once had to walk a mile to the library to borrow that graphic novel I mentioned earlier. The snow was so deep, I had to kick it out of the way as I went.      Oh, you mentioned that one before. I still think you’re a little too young for graphic novels, but I suppose that’s what growing up is all about.      Yeah, I remember when I was a student, I used to read the same kind of things. They were a bit more like comic books, but I think they helped me through the long nights studying. Although, honestly, I’d rather read a good book than spend all that time in the dark.      That’s the life of a student. But I think you’re doing the right thing, laddie.

So, do you think we should be buying all these health products? I mean, I’ve been reading so much about probiotics and supplements lately. I don’t know, man. I feel like it’s just another gimmick. I mean, what’s the point of taking a pill if it’s not going to actually do anything? Yeah, I’m with him. I mean, I take a multivitamin every day, and I feel like it’s just a way for companies to make money. But hey, if it works for you, who am I to say? I think it depends on what you're doing. Like, if you’re training for something or you have a specific issue, then maybe it helps. But I’m not sure. I’m still trying to figure out what works for me. Honestly, I’ve started taking something called ashwagandha. It’s supposed to help with stress. I’ve been feeling pretty overwhelmed lately with uni, you know? Oh, I’ve heard of that. I think it’s an Indian herb or something. I’ve never really tried it, but I’ve seen people talking about it on social media. Yeah, it’s all over Instagram. Like, everyone’s into health stuff these days, and it’s just a marketing thing. But I guess some of it is real. I mean, I’m not against it, but I just feel like people are being sold a load of stuff. Like, how many different kinds of protein powders are there? It’s wild. I used to think that protein powder was just for gym bros, but now I see people using it for everything. Even kids are taking it. I don’t know. I mean, if it helps you feel better, why not? But I also think people are overcompensating. Like, eating healthy, exercising, and then taking supplements just to be extra safe. I think it’s about balance. Like, if you’re doing all the right things with your diet and exercise, then maybe supplements aren’t necessary. But if you’re not getting enough nutrients from food, maybe it’s worth it. Yeah, I guess so. But I still think it’s easier to just eat real food. I mean, I’ve been trying to cut out all the processed stuff, and it’s been a bit of a struggle, but I feel better.

Okay, so I just thought of something. We need to make a shopping list for tomorrow, right? I was thinking we should pick up some fresh fruit and veggies, maybe some bread and milk. Yeah, that sounds good. Did you think about what you want to cook? I was thinking about making some pasta with pesto. But if we don’t have pesto, maybe we can just buy some tomatoes and mozzarella. That could work. I could also grab some eggs and cheese. I heard from my friend that the local store is having a sale on dairy products. Oh, I heard that too. I think they’re also selling some nice seasonal fruit. Maybe we could pick up some apples or pears. I’m not sure about the apples. The ones in the store are usually a bit bland. But maybe we can get some fresh ones from the market. Yeah, the market’s got better quality produce, for sure. I’ll make a note to include that on the list. Wait, I just remembered—there’s this bug in the kitchen. I tried to kill it, but I think it got away. Oh no, what kind of bug was it? It was like a big, long one. I tried to crush it with a magazine, but it just squirmed away. Ugh, those are the worst. I’ve had one of those in my room before. I tried to kill it with a piece of paper, and it just ran up the wall. Yeah, those are the ones that are really hard to get rid of. Have you tried using something like insect spray? I did, but it barely worked. I think the best way is to just trap them in a jar and then throw them out. That’s what I do. I put them in a jar with some oil and then release them outside. It’s a bit gruesome, but it works. I don’t want to kill them, though. I think they’re just trying to survive. I get that, but they’re still pests. If you get bitten, it can be really painful. Yeah, I had a big one bite me the other day. It felt like a bee sting, but it was way worse. I had that too. I ended up with a huge red mark and it itched for days. What did you do?

So, do you know what’s up with Mrs. Thompson in Science? I swear, she’s been so strict this term. I think she’s trying to make us all fail. Yeah, I know, right? She’s like a robot. I tried to ask her about the homework last week, and she just stared at me like I was an alien. I think she’s got a grudge against us.
