I tried once, and I thought I was funny, but it just sounded like I was talking to a wall. Yeah, but I think she’s actually pretty good at it. I mean, she’s got like a million followers, so she must be doing something right. I wish I could be like her. I know, but you’re still really smart, Lucy. You just need to stop overthinking everything. I mean, I think you’re just being too hard on yourself. Thanks, I guess. I just feel like everyone else is doing better than me, and I’m not even sure why.

I’m not sure I can handle this cold anymore. I’ve been sneezing for three days now, and I feel like I’m going to collapse. You need to take it seriously, then. I’ve got a cold too, and I’ve been researching on the internet about how to recover faster. I read that staying hydrated is key, and maybe some herbal tea. Yeah, I’ve been drinking a lot of water, but I still feel awful. And I’m so tired, I can barely keep my eyes open. I wish I could just lie in bed all day. I know the feeling. I’ve been so run down, I’ve been thinking about how much I miss my old life before university. You know, when I could just go out and do things without worrying about getting sick. That’s the thing. I’m in a research role now, and it doesn’t feel like I’m getting any time to myself. I’ve been working long hours and not taking care of myself at all. I think I need to take a break, even if it’s just for a couple of days. You should definitely take some time for yourself. And maybe try to get some rest. I’ve been watching some TV shows about health and wellness, and they keep saying that rest is just as important as exercise. I’ve seen that. I don’t know if I can trust all of it, though. I mean, there’s so much conflicting information out there. I saw a video about Lloyd Grossman the other day—did you watch that? No, I didn’t. Who’s he? He’s this guy who made a video about health and eating. He’s the one who said that you can get food poisoning from eating boiled eggs. I don’t know if I should even trust him. That’s a bit extreme, isn’t it? I mean, food poisoning can happen, but it’s not something you get from just eating eggs. I think he’s just trying to make a point about how important it is to be cautious with what you eat. Maybe. But I’ve been thinking about vaccinations too. I remember my mum saying that she had a lot of bad reactions to vaccines when she was a kid. I’m not sure if I’m ready to get vaccinated for anything right now.

I just landed a new word, "quarantine." It's not the best, but it's better than nothing. Oh, I’m more of a "stalemate" kind of player. I keep ending up with those scrabble letters that don’t fit anywhere. But it’s fun, isn’t it? It’s always good to have a game to focus on. Though I must say, I’m still trying to get my head around the rules of this new edition. I think someone mentioned a few changes to the scoring system? Yes, they’ve made some adjustments, but it’s still essentially the same game. I remember when we used to play back in the eighties. It was just a board and some tiles. No fancy apps or anything. I know, it’s a bit sad how modern technology has made even simple games like Scrabble more complicated. But I suppose it keeps us on our toes. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about the recipe for that lasagna I tried last week. It was decent, but I’d like to get it just right. Oh, I tried that recipe too. It was good, but the sauce was too runny. I think I used too much water. Maybe I should check out that food blog my cousin mentioned. He said it has some really good vegetarian recipes. That sounds like a good idea. I’ve been meaning to start posting more on Facebook. I’ve got a few photos of the garden and some recipes I’ve tried. It might be nice to share them with the family. Yes, and I’ve been thinking about starting a Facebook group for people who love cooking. I’ve noticed that there are a lot of people on Facebook who are into food, and they’re always sharing tips and tricks. It might be a good way to connect with others who share your interests. That’s a great idea. I’ve been meaning to start a blog too. I’ve got some thoughts on music magazines and how they’re changing. You know, with all the digital content now, it’s hard to find real, high-quality magazines. I’ve noticed that too. I think it’s a shame because music magazines used to be such an important part of the music scene. I still miss the days when you could find a really in-depth review of a new album in a magazine.

Well, do you know, I’ve been thinking about the old days. I was in Germany for a while, you know, back in the late '70s and early '80s. It was a mad time, full of exhibitions and all that sort of thing. Oh, really? I’ve heard a lot about the exhibitions in Germany, but I never got the chance to go myself. I always thought it would be fascinating to see how they do things there. It was, honestly. I was part of a team that set up these printing systems, you know, the ones that helped the printing industry move from manual to more automated. I used to work with a fellow called Pete, and we had the best time. You know, we were like inventors, constantly trying to tweak the machines to make them work better and faster. That sounds like a great career. I always wanted to do something creative, but I never got the chance to be part of anything like that. I was more of a desk job kind of guy. Well, I suppose it’s different for everyone. But I can tell you, it was a real thrill. We were working on the edge of technology, pushing the boundaries of what was possible. And it wasn’t just about the machines—it was about the people. You had to be able to explain things to engineers, to clients, to everyone involved. That’s a good point. You had to be a bit of a communicator, someone who could bridge the gap between ideas and execution. Exactly. And that’s why I ended up going into the arts as well. The skills were transferable. You learn how to make your ideas clear, how to adapt to different audiences. It’s the same whether you’re trying to sell a new printing system or a painting. I admire that. I think that’s something a lot of people don’t realize. You can take skills from one field and apply them to another. It just takes a bit of flexibility. Oh, I think it’s about passion too. If you care enough about what you’re doing, it shows. And that’s what made the difference in our work. People remember that. That’s true. I wonder what it would be like if I had pursued something like that instead of the path I took.

Dad, do you remember when we were in school and we had to learn all those weird spellings? Like  quinoa ? Oh, I remember that! I used to think it was a type of spider. Not sure why, but I got it wrong on the spelling test. Yeah, I still can't say it properly. It’s like  kwin-oh-ah  or something. I think it’s from Spanish, isn’t it? Yeah, I think it is. You know, the word  quinoa  comes from the Quechua language, which is spoken in the Andes. People there have been eating it for thousands of years. That’s interesting. I never thought about where words come from. I mean, I know English has a lot of Latin and French roots, but this is from South America? Exactly! And I think it's becoming more popular in the UK now. I’ve seen it in supermarkets and health shops. You can even get it at the farmer’s market in Bolton. Yeah, I saw it once. It looks like little seeds, right? But I’ve never tried it. Is it good? It’s pretty healthy. I think it’s got more protein than rice. But it’s also a bit of a pain because you have to cook it for a while. It’s not like rice or pasta. I guess that’s why it’s kind of trendy. Like, people think it’s healthy. But I don’t know if I’d want to eat it every day. I prefer my chips. That’s fair! We all have our preferences. I think you’d like it if you tried it. Maybe we can get some on our trip to Cornwall. There are some local markets there that sell organic stuff. That sounds cool. But I’m not sure about the spelling. Should I practice it before we go? Like,  quinoa ? I don’t want to spell it wrong in front of people. No worries. Just say it how you like. People won’t care. It’s better to have a funny pronunciation than to be too perfect. Okay, fair point. But I still think it’s weird that a word from South America is now in our everyday language. It’s like English is constantly changing, isn’t it? Absolutely. That’s one of the cool things about the language. It evolves with the times and the people who use it.

Alright, I’ve just thrown the pasta in. It’s gonna be ready in ten minutes, so we just need to get the veg sorted and maybe baste it a bit. Aye, and I’ve got the peas and carrots sorted. You know, I remember my nan used to make this exact same kind of pasta. She’d always say, “It’s not just about the food, it’s about the family.” Yeah, but I’m not sure I’ve ever had a proper family meal. My mum was always too busy working two jobs to cook, and my dad… well, he just sort of drifted away. That’s harsh, man. You know, I think the best thing about being in a place like Cambridge is that you’ve got this mix of people—everyone from all walks of life. Like me, I’m an events co-ordinator, but I grew up in Doncaster, and I still remember my mum making Sunday roasts. It’s the kind of thing that brings people together. Yeah, and that’s why I like cooking, really. It’s a way to connect with people, even if it’s just friends like us. Although, I might have to ask—what’s the point of making such a big meal if we’re just gonna eat it in five minutes? Oh, I dunno. Sometimes it’s just about the process. You know, the smell of the spices, the way the food smells as it’s cooking. It’s like a memory. I used to work in a café when I was younger, and I used to love the way the kitchen filled up with the smell of garlic and olive oil. That’s a nice way to put it. I mean, I’m not cooking for the love of it, but I like the way it makes me feel connected to my roots. My grandma always said, “If you don’t cook, you don’t know what you’re eating.” That’s a bit intense, but I can see where she’s coming from. I mean, I’m a labourer—my job’s physical, not culinary—but I still think food is the best way to bring people together. I get that. I mean, I’ve never had a job that required me to cook, but even in my day job, I’d go out and buy chips and a burger just to feel like I was part of something.

So, how’s the new job going? You mentioned you were going to start teaching English full-time a few months back. Oh, it’s going okay, I suppose. It’s a bit of a change from what I was doing before, but I think I’m settling in. The students are pretty good, and the pay isn’t bad either. That’s great to hear. I guess you’ve been working on your teaching qualifications for a while, then? Yeah, I did a postgraduate course last year, which took a few years to finish because of my other commitments. But it was worth it. I mean, I always loved languages, and now I get to do it for a living. That’s cool. I’ve always found languages fascinating, but I never had the guts to take it seriously. I mean, I can barely speak Spanish, let alone teach it. I still have that fear of being exposed. Oh, I get that. I remember when I first started teaching, I was so nervous. I would second-guess everything I said, worried I’d make a mistake. But I think it’s just a matter of practice. And honestly, once you get into it, you start to feel more confident. You’re probably right. I guess I just need to start pushing myself. I’ve been thinking about going back to school for a while now. Maybe something in marketing or something similar to what I’m doing now. That sounds like a solid move. You know, I’ve noticed that people who do things they’re passionate about tend to be more successful in the long run. If you’re not happy in your job, it shows. It’s hard to give your best when you’re not excited about what you’re doing. Yeah, that makes sense. I mean, I’m not unhappy in my job, but I do feel like I’m not reaching my full potential. I’m just waiting for the right opportunity to take the leap. That’s exactly what I was doing. I was working in customer service for years, doing what I thought I was supposed to do, but I wasn’t really enjoying it. Then I took the plunge and went back to school. It’s been one of the best decisions I’ve ever made. I’m glad to hear that.

Right, right, I've got to get going, I'm late for break time. Oh, don’t you worry about it, you’ve got ten minutes. You’re not late, you’re just early. No, no, I’ve got a meeting with the community centre, it’s important. You know, they don’t care if you’re late. I’ve heard that before. It’s just a coffee meeting. Yeah, but I’ve got to be there. You know how these things go. Right, I get it. You’re still thinking about the banners and the donation box, aren’t you? Yeah, well, the bell ringing is going on, and I’ve got to help out. And the plants – aren’t they doing well? I saw a new one in the window. Yeah, they’re starting to look good. I’ve been watering them every day. Good for you, I’ve been meaning to start a small garden myself. You should. I’ve got some seeds from Gambia, you know. Oh, really? I thought you were going to plant them in the community garden. I was, but I thought maybe we could make a little patch in the back. That sounds nice. What about the coffee? You haven’t mentioned it. Oh, the coffee? It’s been delicious. I got some beans from a local roaster, they’re great. I’ve had some from the same place, I think. It’s a bit of a local thing. Yeah, I remember when I was a child, my dad used to take me to the coffee shop near the station. Oh, you used to live near the station? Yeah, I lived in Middlesex, not far from Harrow. That’s not far from where I’m from, actually. Right, and you’ve got a lot of experience with children, being a childminder. Yeah, I’ve got a lot of experience with kids, but I’ve never met anyone with Munchausen Syndrome. Oh, I think that’s a real condition, isn’t it? Yeah, I read about it once. It’s when someone fakes illness in a child to get attention. That’s pretty serious. I can imagine how that would feel. It’s like you’re trying to get sympathy, but it’s not real. Yep, it’s a bit of a tragedy. Well, I think it’s just something to be aware of.

So, do you guys ever just get bored of scrolling through your phone all the time? I feel like I’m addicted to Instagram and TikTok. It’s like I can’t even go five minutes without checking my phone. I know, right? I’ve tried to cut back, but it’s so hard. I mean, I used to think it was just me, but then I saw this app called Forest that helps you stay off your phone. It’s like you plant a tree and if you don’t leave the app, it dies. It’s kind of cool. Oh, I’ve heard of that. I tried it once, but I just kept getting distracted by other apps. Honestly, I think the problem is that we’re all living in a world where everything is on our phones, and it’s hard to disconnect, even if you want to. I totally agree. But sometimes I think we need to use these apps to our advantage. Like, I use a food delivery app to order takeout, and it’s way better than cooking. Plus, I can save money by using coupons. Yeah, but I worry that we’re losing the ability to be present in the real world. Like, when we’re out with friends, we’re all on our phones instead of talking to each other. I mean, I know it’s kind of normal, but I feel like we’re missing out on real moments. I get that. I’ve been trying to be more mindful. Last week, my friends and I went to a movie, and we didn’t bring our phones. It was weird at first, but honestly, it was refreshing. We actually had a proper conversation instead of all being on our phones. That sounds like a good idea. I should try that. Maybe next weekend, we could all try a movie night without phones. No one brings their phone, just like old times. It’d be like a tradition. I could be down for that. But I think I might have to leave my phone at home just in case. I’m such a phone addict. I’ve even started to fantasize about living without one. I’ve thought about that too. But honestly, I’m not ready. I mean, I still use my phone for work and social media. Maybe one day, I’ll be able to break the habit.

So, do you think we’ll get a lift from the postman or something? I’ve been waiting for like... twenty minutes now, and I’m starting to think he’s not going to show up. You don’t think he’s going to show up? You can’t just assume that. I mean, he  has  to come, doesn’t he? It’s not like we’re on a mountain or anything. Oh, I don’t know. I’ve seen some of the roads around here lately. If the car’s not working, it’s not like he’s going to fetch it. You know how these things go. Yeah, but he’s got that old Renault. It’s been sitting in the garage for months. I mean, he’s not even driving it, is he? No, he’s got a flat tire on the back. I saw it myself. I was passing by yesterday and noticed the wheel was sort of... hanging off. I told him to get it fixed, but he said he’d do it when he had time. And he doesn’t have time, does he? He’s got a full-time job as a postman, and he’s got a wife and two kids. How does he manage it? He does manage, I suppose. But I’ve seen his car on the road before. It’s like a tank. It’s got a broken headlight, and the exhaust’s leaking. I don’t know how he gets from one end of the village to the other. I think he just drives and hopes for the best. You know, like, "If it’s not broken, don’t fix it." That’s the attitude of a man who’s been doing this for decades. I suppose that’s true. But I still think it’s a bit reckless. I mean, what if he gets into an accident? He’s not a young man anymore. Yeah, but he’s not the only one. We all have our cars. I mean, I had a bit of a problem with mine the other day. My battery died, and I had to wait for a friend to come and pick me up. That’s not fair. If your battery dies, you’re just in the same boat as everyone else. You can’t just sit there and wait forever. You’ve got to get somewhere, don’t you?

So, do you think we should go ahead with moving house, Sarah? I know it's been a while since we last talked about it, but I've been feeling like I need a change. I hear you, Ma. I’ve been thinking about it too. The house is getting a bit old, and I can't help but notice the cracks in the walls and the dusty corners. It's not a bad place, but I think it's time for something newer. Yeah, I agree. I mean, we've been living here for over twenty years. It's time to move on. I just hope we can afford it. With the economy the way it is, it's not easy to sell a house without a good price. I know, I know. I've been looking around, and it's not as easy as I thought. I mean, the market is really competitive. But I still feel like if I don't do something, I'll be stuck here forever. I can understand that. But maybe we should consider buying something smaller, like a flat or a condo. That way, we can save some money on maintenance and property taxes. That's an interesting idea. I've been reading about it. I remember when I was in the oil industry – we had a lot of people moving into smaller homes for the same reason. It's all about lifestyle and budget now. I suppose you're right. I just don't want to feel like I'm making a mistake. I mean, I've always been a bit of a planner, and this is a big decision. What do you think, Paul? Honestly, I think it's about what makes you happy. If you're not happy here, then it's probably time to move. But maybe you should take your time and look at a few options before making any final decisions. Yeah, and maybe even visit some places. I mean, I remember when I first moved out of my parent's house, I was so nervous about everything. But once I got there, it was like a whole new chapter in my life. That's true. I remember feeling the same way when I moved out of my parent's house the first time. It's a big step, but sometimes it's necessary for growth. Exactly.

Mummy, I’m so upset. I can’t believe my bike got stolen. I left it outside the house, and when I came back from school, it was gone. I had to walk all the way home. I know, sweetie, I’m really sorry. But don’t worry, I’ve just got some good news. The police found your bike this morning. Really? Where? How? They were doing a routine check in the area, and some kids turned it in. It was in the woods near the old bridge. They said the owner was a girl who had to leave it there when she got on the bus. That’s amazing! But why didn’t you tell me earlier? I wanted to wait until I had the full story. It’s not just about the bike, though. I want to talk about what happened. You were a bit upset when you came home, and I didn’t want to make it worse. Okay, but I still feel so sad. I had that bike for so long. It was my first real one, and I even got it painted with your help. I know, and I’m so glad they found it. You know, I was thinking about how it’s not just about the bike—it’s about how you feel. Sometimes, when something like this happens, it’s not just about what was lost, but what it represents. Like what? Like freedom. You used to ride to school every day, and it made you feel so independent. Also, it’s a reminder that even though things can go wrong, there are people who care and try to help. I guess. But I still feel like I can’t trust anyone. What if it happens again? I know it’s scary, but that’s part of growing up. You have to learn how to deal with loss and how to move on. You’re not alone in this, love. I know. I just hope I don’t have to go through this again. It’s so frustrating. I understand. But I also know you’re stronger than you think. And I’m here for you, always. Let’s get your bike back, and then maybe we can go for a ride together. Just you and me. How does that sound? Yeah, that sounds nice. I’d like that. Great. And maybe after that, we can go to the café and get some cake.

So, I just wanted to say, I think the way we’ve been playing  Ticket to Ride  has been fantastic. It’s been a great way to bond and keep our minds sharp, especially with the long holiday here in Hereford.      Yeah, agreed. It’s a bit of a challenge, but I love how it combines strategy with a bit of luck. I’ve been trying to figure out the best routes, but I think I might be missing something.      You’re not alone. I’ve been doing the same. Didn’t you just get stuck with those trains in the north? I think it’s because you’re trying to connect too many cities at once.      Exactly. I remember when I first played, I thought I was doing really well, but then I ended up with no trains left and couldn’t complete my route. It’s a bit frustrating, but I still enjoy it.      I’ve been trying to help you out, but honestly, I’m not much better. I still get confused with all the different colored trains and the scoring.      I think that’s part of the fun, though. It’s not just about winning—it’s about enjoying the process. Plus, it’s a good way to talk about the places we’ve visited or want to visit.      True. I was telling the kids about how the train system in Wales is different from what they might expect, and it led to a nice little discussion about how the railways have changed over the years.      Speaking of trains, have you heard about the new high-speed rail line they’re planning to build? I think it might connect Hereford to London in under two hours.      Oh, I’ve heard about that. It’s going to be a huge boost for the economy, but I have to say, I’m not sure if it’s going to make a big difference for small towns like ours.      I’ve always thought that trains are a bit more reliable than cars, especially when it comes to being on time. Even with the delays, I think they’re still better than trying to drive in this weather.      Absolutely. That’s one of the reasons I love living in Hereford—there’s always a train schedule to follow, and that gives us something to look forward to.      So, have you ever been to any places that you’d like to visit by train?

I can't believe we've got this far in the game. I think we've just landed on the last space before the finish line. Yeah, and I think I've got the last move. Let me see… Do we have to roll again or can I just take the final turn? No, I think we can just take the final turn if it's your turn. You're on the last space, right? Yeah, and I've got a few more moves to make. If I can just move forward two spaces, I win. You're doing really well. I’ve been trying to catch up all game, but the luck hasn't been with me. Yeah, I know. The dice have been a bit cruel to you. I mean, what are the chances of landing on the same square twice in a row? Honestly, I think it's almost like the board’s trying to mess with me. Maybe I should’ve taken a different route. Or maybe it's just fate. I mean, I do like to think that board games are more than just luck—they're about strategy as well. You’ve got to plan ahead, right? I suppose. I did try to plan ahead earlier. I remember trying to get to the bonus square, but it just kept pushing me back. I think the game is trying to teach me patience. Ha! Patience, right. I've heard that said in every game I've ever played. It's like the ultimate lesson. I wonder what the designers are thinking. Maybe they’re just trying to make us feel like we’re in control, even when we’re not. Although, I'll admit, I did enjoy the part where I got to drink the rum. That was a highlight. Oh, I remember. That was the first time I ever had that kind of drink. It was a bit strong, but the game called for it, so I had to go along with it. Yeah, and it was kind of funny to see you reacting to it. I think you were the first person in our circle to actually go full-on exotic with the drink. That was a go. I think I’ve had more of those kinds of drinks in the past week than in the last year. I can’t be the only one, can I?

So, how’s the new place coming along, Kerrie? I heard you had to move out of that flat in London last month. It’s actually going pretty well, thanks. We’ve got a nice little house in the countryside now, not too far from the motorway. It’s a bit of a mess, though — we’re still sorting out the kitchen and the bathroom. I remember when I moved out of my old house in Swansea, it was a nightmare. I had to dump all that old furniture and start from scratch. You’d think by now, we’d all know how to handle a move properly. I know, right? It’s like every time you think you’ve got the process down, something goes wrong. I left my old flat in Germany, and I accidentally left the bin outside the door for three days. The landlord was absolutely furious. Oh, I can imagine. My sister had a similar problem when she moved into her first flat. She forgot to put the bins in the correct area and got fined. It was ridiculous. I remember when I moved into my first house, I thought I’d be clever and organise everything myself. Then, when the council came to check on the bins, they asked me about the white goods. I had no idea what they meant. I spent the whole afternoon panicking trying to figure out what I was supposed to do. Oh, I’ve heard that one before. I think the term “white goods” refers to the big appliances: the fridge, the washing machine, the fridge. Some people still don’t know what it means. That’s true. It’s so confusing when you’re about to move. You think you’re being efficient, but you’re just setting yourself up for a disaster. I mean, I got the new fridge delivered the other day, and it was so heavy, I had to call someone to help me carry it in. I used to work in a shop that sold white goods, so I thought I knew what I was doing. But when I actually had to move, I learned that even the biggest appliances can be the most problematic. Yeah, and you think you’ve got it all planned out, but then something go wrong with the fittings or the cables or the layout. I think I spent more time trying to figure out how to arrange the furniture than actually moving the stuff.

So, do you think we’ll get stuck in traffic again today? I swear, every time we go to North London, it’s like we’re stuck in a time warp. Oh, you know me, I always say we should’ve taken the Tube. It’s safer, and it’s not like we’re dealing with the usual traffic gridlock. Yeah, but I like driving. I mean, I love the feel of the car under my hands, especially on a day like this. Plus, it’s nice to have some time to chat without being in a rush. That’s the spirit. But I also think you need to be careful. I remember when I first started driving, I had this friend who got into a bit of a scrape with a driver who was really aggressive. I still remember the look on his face when he turned around and gave him the finger. Wait, really? That’s not something I’d expect from London. I mean, I know road rage is everywhere, but I always thought the city was more about politeness. It can be. But some people just get too stressed. You know, work, family, and all that. It can really bring out the worst in people. Speaking of work—I’ve been thinking about applying for that job at the TLS. I mean, it’s not like I’m getting paid well, but it’s something I’d really enjoy. And the work-life balance seems better than what I’ve seen at my current university gig. That’s great. I’d say go for it. You’ve got a good head on your shoulders, and you’re not afraid to take a chance. But I do have one piece of advice—don’t let the digital age take over completely. I still think print has its place, especially when you’re reading something like literature or poetry. Yeah, I agree. There’s something about holding a physical book. It just feels more… personal. Although I do love my e-reader for when I’m on the go. That’s the thing. It’s all about balance. And with your plan to move to North London, I suppose you’ll be spending more time in the city. Are you thinking about buying a house or renting? I’m not sure yet. I mean, I’d love to have my own place, but I’m still figuring out what I’m going to do with my career.

So, do you remember that time we tried to go camping in the Lake District and ended up getting lost for like three hours? Oh yeah, that was  bad . I remember we thought we were following the trail, but we ended up in some kind of forest that wasn’t on any map. We had to use the GPS, and even then, it kept saying we were going the wrong way. I swear, halfway through the night, I thought we were in a zombie movie. Like, the trees were just…  too  quiet. No birds, no nothing. Just… us. I think it was  too  quiet because we were all so drunk. I was trying to sing that one song by The Proclaimers, and everyone just stared at me like I was from the future. I think the real issue was that you brought the wrong tent. Remember how it kept falling apart? You said it was “reinforced,” but it was basically a Mega Bloks structure. Yeah, and then when we finally got to the campsite, we realized it was  three  hours away from the car park. We were like, “Oh, we  could  have just walked back!” And then when we got there, the guy who ran the campsite said, “You’re lucky you didn’t get lost. That area’s been known to swallow people whole.” He was  literally  joking. Honestly, I think that was one of the best holidays of my life. It was so stressful, but in a good way. Like, we were all just… being  us . Yeah, and then we had this weird group conversation about the meaning of life. I said something like, “Life is like a budget—once you’ve spent it, you can’t get it back.” And you all just stared at me like I’d just told a dirty joke. I remember you said it was a metaphor for the money we had in the tent. You were trying to calculate how long we could survive on that single pack of crisps. I think that was the  real  lesson. Spending money on a tent that doesn’t work is like spending money on a go-kart that doesn’t move. It’s just a waste. I’m still not over the fact that we had to use the GPS to find the way  back  to the car. Like, we were out there for three days, and we had to walk three miles back just to get home.

So, do you really think wild winter camping is a good idea? I mean, I’ve heard stories about people getting lost or freezing to death out there. It seems pretty risky. It can be, but it’s also about preparation and mindset. I’ve done a few trips myself, and if you’re properly equipped and know what you’re doing, it’s actually really rewarding. The silence, the fresh air—it’s like nothing else. I agree. I think it’s a great way to disconnect from the noise of daily life. I once went camping in the Cairngorms with a group of friends, and it changed how I see the world. There’s something about being out in nature that clears your head and gives you perspective. Yeah, but I still worry about the cold. You know, I’ve heard about people getting frostbite or hypothermia, especially if they’re not used to it. I mean, I’m not saying it’s not worth it, but you have to be careful. Absolutely. That’s why I always stress the importance of proper gear—thermal clothing, a sturdy tent, and knowing how to build a fire. It’s not just about the adventure; it’s about survival. Exactly. And then there’s the mental aspect too. When you’re out there, you’re forced to slow down and really be present. No emails, no phones, just you and the environment. It’s like a reset button for the mind. That does sound nice. I guess I just never had the chance to try it. My job’s pretty demanding, and I always end up being too busy to take time off. But I’ve heard your stories about how it helps with stress. Maybe I should give it a shot? You should. It’s not for everyone, but if you’re someone who feels overwhelmed by modern life, it could be exactly what you need. I can even help you plan your first trip if you’re interested. I’d be happy to as well. You don’t have to do it alone. It can be a great way to bond with friends or family too. I remember one time I took my nephew out, and it was amazing to see how he connected with the landscape. He was really inspired. Well, I’ll think about it. I’ll admit, it’s a bit intimidating, but I suppose it’s better to try than to regret not doing it.

So, do you know what’s on at the cinema this week? I saw this film called  The Silent Sea  or something like that—some sort of sci-fi thriller. I think it’s got a bit of a cult following. Not sure if it’s worth the time, though. Yeah, I saw the trailer. It looked a bit intense, but I reckon it’s not as bad as the last one. I actually liked the last one more— The Echoes of Silence  was a bit too slow for me. You know, I prefer something with a bit more action or at least some emotional meat. I get that. I like a good story, but I don’t mind some action either. My brother said it’s like  Inception  meets  The Thing . I’m not sure if I can handle that kind of mix. Though I did hear it has some great visuals. Maybe I’ll check it out. Yeah, the visuals are supposed to be top-notch. I remember reading somewhere that the director’s got a real eye for cinematography. It’s one of those films that’s more about atmosphere than plot, I think. That might be a bit off-putting for me. I like a bit of substance. Maybe I’ll just stick to the classics for now. Although, I’ve been meaning to watch  The Good Nurse  again. That was quite a rollercoaster. Do you know what I mean? Oh, I’ve heard of that. I think it’s based on a real story, right? I remember reading an article about it—there was a documentary too. It’s got that gritty realism that I really like. Maybe I should give it a try. I’ve been meaning to catch up on some good films lately. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to watch more films that have depth, like  The Queen’s Gambit  or  The Power of the Dog . Though I don’t know if I’d call  The Power of the Dog  a classic. It’s more of a modern drama. I’d say it’s a modern classic. It’s got that psychological depth and some really powerful performances. I think it’s one of those films that leaves you thinking long after it’s over. It’s not just entertainment—it’s commentary on power, masculinity, and human nature.

Alright, do you remember the story about the time I tried to teach Excel to your dad? It was a disaster. Oh yes! He kept trying to make it do something like a magic trick, and it just… crashed. Yeah, and then he said it was a "digital eenie meenie miney mo" and ran out of the room. That’s the one. I had to explain that Excel is more like a calculator than a magician. It doesn’t do tricks, it just does numbers. But isn’t it supposed to be fun? I mean, I’ve been trying to learn how to use it for school projects, and it feels like trying to put together a Lego set blindfolded. Oh, I know, I know. You have to be precise. I think the hardest part is knowing where to find the right button. It’s like looking for a specific Lego piece in a giant box. I tried to use PlayStation once, and it showed me a tutorial that was like a 10-minute story about a robot who lived in a tree. It was so dramatic. That’s the thing with games, though. They’ve got stories now. I mean, I remember when all we had was a typewriter and we had to write our own stories. It was so much harder, but it felt more like… creativity. I think I still like the old way. I mean, I just got a storybook for my birthday, and it was like a giant book with pictures. It was so much better than a tablet. You can’t swipe through a storybook like that. Yeah, I like the feel of a real book. But I still think PlayStation is better. I can play for hours and not even notice the time. I remember when I was your age, I used to dream about playing games like that. I used to imagine I was in a world where you could just pick up a controller and go anywhere. I never thought I’d be the one teaching Excel to your dad. He’s not that bad, really. He just needs patience. I think he’s getting better, even if he still calls Excel “the magic number goon.” I think he’s trying to impress you, though. He’s always trying to be the smart one. Yeah, but he doesn’t have to be.

Morning, John. How's your day shaping up? Morning, Sue. It's been a bit of a whirlwind. I was just finishing up a meeting when I got a call about roadworks near my house. You know those ones that never seem to finish? They’re everywhere now. Oh, I know. I was just saying to my wife about how the roadworks in Bradford have turned the whole area into a construction site. I’ve had to take a different route to work every week. That’s not the only thing that’s changed. I’ve been getting more junk mail lately. I mean, I still get the usual bills, but now there’s this stuff about selling old houses. I don’t even own a house anymore, and yet I keep getting letters about it. It’s bizarre. I can’t believe it. My mum’s still living in her old place, and I keep getting catalogs for people who want to buy it. She’s not even thinking of selling, but the mail just keeps coming. I suppose it’s all part of this digital age. I mean, we’re all connected to the world through phones and emails, but we’re also bombarded with advertisements. I’ve been trying to cut down on the junk mail by unsubscribing from some services, but it’s not easy. It’s not just junk mail, though. I’ve been thinking about growing herbs in my kitchen garden. I’ve got a small patch of soil, and I’ve been experimenting with basil and thyme. It’s a bit of a hobby, but I love being able to use fresh herbs in my cooking. That sounds great. I’ve always wanted to try that. I’ve had a few plants in pots, but I’m not sure if I’m doing it right. I think I need to do some research. You should. I’ve found that growing herbs is actually a lot easier than I thought. I mean, I’ve got a few little ones that survived the winter, and they’re already starting to bloom. That’s encouraging. I’ve also been thinking about going back to the old ways of cooking with jam. I remember my mum making homemade jam every year. It was a big event in the house, and I always loved the smell of it. Oh, I can still remember that.

I just got a new moisturiser, and I think it’s going to be the best one yet. The skin’s been feeling so soft lately. Oh, really? I've been using the same old thing for years. I don’t think I've ever bothered to try anything new. I mean, I'm not exactly a skincare expert, but I know when something works. Yeah, I’ve been using a serum lately. Got it from a friend who said it was amazing. It’s got this little bit of vitamin C in it. I’ve never had such clear skin. That’s cool. I think I’m going to try a serum too. I’ve always been a bit of a dry skin type, so I guess I need to up my game. What do you think, Dad? Hmm, not sure. I mean, if it’s not breaking the bank, why not? But I’ve always said that skincare is a bit of a luxury. I’m more of a “get out the door” type of person. You know, minimal fuss. I get that, but I think it’s worth it. Especially if you’re going to a place like Spain for the summer. You don’t want to look like a desert when you get there. Exactly! I’m thinking of going to Spain for a few weeks. Maybe even take some time off work. I’ve been thinking about it for a while now. That sounds like a good idea. But you need to book the flights soon. I’ve been meaning to go out there myself, but I haven’t had the time. Still, I’d love to see the beaches again. Yeah, I’d love to go to Spain too. I’ve never been. I’ve always wanted to see the Alhambra in Granada. It’s one of those places that’s on my bucket list. That’s a beautiful place. I remember reading a book about it once. It was supposed to be like a dream. You know, those white buildings with the orange trees around them. Sounds like a dream. I’ve tried to imagine it, but I can’t really picture it. I think it’s better in person. I think it would be perfect for a weekend trip. You could just spend a few days there and then go back home. You don’t have to do too much.

So, how’s the part-time job going? I know you said you were trying to get more hours, but I haven’t heard much about it lately. Honestly, it’s been a bit of a struggle. I’m only doing a few hours a week at the moment, and it’s not even enough to cover my rent. I’m thinking about switching to something else, maybe something more flexible. I can see why. I mean, I’m in a similar boat, but at least I have a proper job now. I’ve been working as a copywriter for a few months now, and it’s actually going pretty well. I’m doing some nice campaigns for local businesses, and I’ve even managed to get a few freelance gigs on the side. That sounds great, honestly. I’m just so frustrated with how little I’m earning right now. It feels like I’ve got to work so much just to survive, and I’m not even making enough to cover my bills. I was thinking about moving back in with my parents for a while, but I don’t want to be a burden. I can understand that. I know how hard it can be to be independent when you’re just starting out. But I think it’s important to keep pushing, even if it’s slow. You’re still learning, and I know you’re smart enough to figure it out. Thanks, I appreciate that. It’s just so hard sometimes, you know? Like, I want to work full-time and save up for my postgrad, but I just can’t afford it right now. I’d rather have a bit more money and be stressed than be in debt for years. I get that. I was in the same situation last year, and it was really tough. But I think the key is to be proactive. Have you thought about applying for any part-time jobs that might offer better pay or benefits? I’ve actually started looking. There are a few roles in tech and marketing that I’m interested in, but I’m waiting to see if any of them come up. I’m also doing some freelance work on the side to keep myself busy and earn a bit more. That’s smart. You’re already thinking ahead, which is good. I think you’ll be fine.

So, do you think we should go for a run tomorrow? I’ve been feeling really sluggish lately and need to get some exercise in. I’d love to, but I’ve been thinking about house prices again. You know, with everything going on, I’m not sure if it’s a good time to buy. Yeah, I know what you mean. My agent said the market’s a bit unstable, but I think it's still a good idea to keep an eye on it. I’ve been looking at a few properties in the area and it’s surprising how much they’ve gone up. That’s true, isn’t it? I mean, the prices are still way too high for what you get. I keep telling my brother, it’s not worth it. But he just shrugs and says he’ll take the risk. I suppose it’s about the long-term investment. I mean, even if you don’t buy now, you could always rent and save up. But then again, you never know when the market might crash. I think I’m just going to wait a bit longer. I’ve been working on a new book, and I don’t want to get distracted by all this financial stuff. I’d rather focus on my writing. That makes sense. I mean, you can’t let money dictate your life. I’m trying to keep things balanced—work, exercise, and hobbies. But honestly, I’m not sure how I’m going to manage with everything I have on my plate. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to be more organized. I’ve started using a planner to make sure I don’t miss anything important. It’s helped a bit, but I still feel like I’m juggling so many things. You know, I’ve been thinking about cooking too. Maybe I should start trying some new recipes. I’ve been eating out so much lately, and I want to get back into the kitchen. Plus, it’s a great way to unwind. That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to try out some new meals. I’ve been looking at some cooking blogs and found a few recipes I’m excited to try. Maybe we can do a cooking night soon? I’d like that. Just don’t expect me to be the one doing all the work.

So, do you know what’s going on with the Budget? I’ve been trying to keep up with the news, but it’s all so confusing. I mean, I know it’s about the government spending, but it feels like they’re always making changes that don’t really make sense. Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. I think it’s all about trying to balance the economy without hurting growth. But honestly, I’m not sure how they’re managing it. I mean, I’m a civil engineer, so I do a lot of calculations, but this stuff is way more complicated than any bridge or building I’ve ever designed. I can imagine. It’s like trying to predict the weather, but with more consequences. I’ve been thinking about how it might affect my job. I’m a corpus administrator, so I work with data and language, but I’m worried about how budget cuts might impact the funding for research and development in my field. That’s a good point. I’ve heard some of my colleagues in the engineering sector talking about the uncertainty. They’re worried about project delays and reduced resources. It’s a bit of a drag, especially with all the postgraduate work I’ve done. You’d think having a higher education would make you more secure, but it seems like the opposite is happening. I feel you. I’ve been trying to stay positive, but it’s hard not to feel like the whole system is on shaky ground. Although, I guess we can’t all just sit back and do nothing. I’ve been thinking about how maybe I can upskill or take on more responsibilities at work. It might be the only way to stay ahead. That’s a solid approach. I’ve been thinking about the same thing. I’ve got a few ideas for new projects I could lead, and I’m trying to get my manager on board. It’s not easy, but I think it’s worth the effort. Plus, I’ve been really into musicals lately. Maybe it’ll help me keep my head above water. You know, I’ve been to a few shows recently. The one I saw last week was  Hamilton . It was incredible—so much energy, so much history. It’s a reminder that even in tough times, there’s always something to look forward to.

So, do you reckon the council will actually do anything about that council house they've got in the old factory site? I mean, it's been empty for years, and I can't see how they're going to get it up to standard without some serious investment. Honestly, I don’t think they’re going to do much more than leave it as a eyesore. You know how they are with these things—always talking about regeneration but never actually doing anything. I’ve heard the planners are even considering turning it into a community centre, but I doubt it’ll happen. That’s a shame. I mean, it’s not like it’s in the middle of nowhere. It’s right on the edge of town, and if they could just get someone to take it on, you know, maybe turn it into a workshop or something. I’ve been thinking about starting up a small art studio, and if there was space, it’d be perfect. Haha, you and your art. I still remember that time you tried to paint the side of the old bus shelter and ended up painting over the bus schedule. You were so proud of it, too. Oh, come on, that was an accident. I was trying to add some texture to it, and the next thing I knew, the buses were all late because people couldn’t read the times. Still, I think it turned out quite nicely, don’t you? Well, maybe. Though I’d say the people who actually use the shelters probably weren’t too happy. Anyway, enough about that. I was just thinking about something else. I saw a couple of old paintings down at the market the other day, and they looked like they could be worth something. You know, the kind of stuff that people collect for nostalgia. That’s interesting. I’ve been thinking about buying some old books for my collection. My sister’s got this secondhand shop that’s been passed down through the family, and she’s been getting some really rare books in. If you’re up for it, maybe we could check it out sometime. That sounds good. I’ve been meaning to expand my collection anyway. I’ve got a few old films I’m trying to source, and if I can get some classic ones, I’d be happy.

So, do you think we've seen everything on this road yet? I mean, it's been a few hours and we still haven't really stopped to take it all in properly. Honestly, I think we've only just started. I mean, we’ve passed some really nice villages, a few old castles, and there were these beautiful fields that stretched out like a green sea. It’s like a postcard come to life. Yeah, I felt that. And the sky was just so clear today. You can see the mountains so well. Didn’t you want to pull over and take some photos? I did, but I kept thinking we might run into someone else who wanted to stop and take a look around. I mean, it’s not like we’re the only ones on the road, is it? True, but I think we’ve been pretty lucky so far. I mean, we’ve only seen a couple of people on the road, and both were friendly enough. I even saw a couple of hitchhikers earlier. One of them was holding up a sign that said “Free hugs.” That was… unusual. I know! It’s funny how people can still be so open and friendly, even in a place like this. I mean, I remember when I was teaching in Bury, and sometimes we had students who came from the city and were quite cynical about everything. But out here? It’s like the world slows down a bit. Exactly. It’s also made me think about clearing the clutter in my life. I mean, I’ve been unemployed for a while now, and being on the road like this has given me a chance to just… breathe. I don’t know if I’m ready to go back to work yet. I get that. Sometimes, you just need a break. And besides, you’re not the only one who’s been feeling that way. I’ve been thinking about taking a more permanent break from teaching, you know? Maybe I can find something more… flexible? That’s interesting. I mean, I’ve always thought about doing something with travel, or maybe writing. I’ve got this blog going, but it’s not getting the attention it deserves. You should really get back to that. It’s a good start, and I think it’s important to have a creative outlet, especially when you’re feeling your way through life.

So, do you think we’ll get there in time for the Hay Festival? I mean, it’s not like we got lost on the way here. I think we’re fine. It’s not that far from St Anne’s. But the roads are usually a bit busy this time of year. We might want to plan our route properly. Yeah, I remember when I was a kid, we used to go to the Hay Festival every year. My dad would always say it was the best time of the year. He’d take me to the book stalls and buy me a new storybook every time. That sounds amazing. I’ve never been. I mean, I’ve heard about it, but I don’t think I’ve ever actually gone. I guess I just never had the chance. You should go. It’s such a cultural event. There are so many authors and talks. I remember when I was in college, I went once and it changed my whole perspective on literature. It’s a shame I can’t go this year. I’ve been stuck with the kids and the house. But maybe next year? I’d love to go again. I’ve got a few books I’ve been meaning to read, and I think it’d be the perfect time to do it. I hope you get to go. It’s something I’m actually really looking forward to. I’ve been saving up for a book from the festival. I heard they have some really good deals there. That’s a great idea. You should start looking into what you want to buy. It might help you get a head start. I mean, it’s not like you can just walk into a bookstore and find all of them. I know. I’ve been trying to make a list of the books I want to read. I think I mentioned that to my sister. She said she’s got a few she wants to read too. Maybe we could go together? That would be awesome. I mean, if you’re going, I could come too. It’ll be fun. And we can all take turns buying books. That sounds like a plan. I think I’ll start looking into some of the events too. There are always some interesting panels about writing and publishing. I just hope the roads are okay.

Well, it’s a bit like coming back to my own kitchen, isn’t it? I mean, it's got the same smell, same kind of…  chaos . Yeah, it’s like you’ve been away for years, but it feels like just yesterday. I’m glad you came, Mum. Yeah, it’s good to see you. You’ve been gone for ages. Didn’t even know you were coming until yesterday. Oh, I thought I’d keep it a surprise. You know, like a grand entrance. But honestly, I didn’t expect you to be so busy. I mean, I didn’t know you had a special day today. Well, it’s my birthday. I didn’t even tell you, Mum. I thought I’d keep it a secret. But I guess you found out through the school. They’re always telling me things. Yeah, they mentioned it. I mean, you’re a teacher, so you’re always on top of everything. But I didn’t know you were coming. I was just about to go out with my mates. Well, I’ve had a lot on my mind lately. You know, clearing out the old stuff from the house. It’s been a bit of a struggle, but I think I’ve made some progress. It’s amazing how much stuff you can accumulate over the years. I know. I’ve been doing the same. I’ve been sorting through my grandmother’s things. There were so many old letters, and some stuff I didn’t even know she had. Wait, did you say your grandmother? I thought you were from Darlington. How come you’ve got stuff from your grandmother? Oh, my grandparents are from Darlington, but I was raised in York. I lived with my grandmother for a few years when I was little. She had a massive attic full of… well,  things . Some of it was useful, some of it was just really weird. I could tell you stories. I had a cousin who used to collect old films and boxes of letters. One time, she found a letter from the 1920s that was written by someone she didn’t even know was her ancestor. Wow. That’s like something out of a comedy show. Like  Blackadder  or something. Yeah, I think that’s exactly what she thought. She tried to send it to a historian, but it turned out it was just a love letter between two people who had no idea they were related.

So, do you reckon this new laptop’s gonna be any good? I’ve had it for a week now and it’s still a bit slow, even after I did the whole disk cleanup and all that. Yeah, I can see what you mean. It’s not like the old one. That one ran like a dream, even with all the games and stuff. I still use it for basic stuff, though. I got a laptop a few years back that was just as bad. Took me ages to get it to run properly. I had to take it into the shop and they had to replace the hard drive. That’s not the worst, though. My old one had a broken screen, so I had to get it fixed. It cost me more than the new one. I think it’s just the age of the thing. My old one was like five years old and it was still going strong. Maybe I should’ve upgraded sooner. You know, I heard that the best way to make a laptop run faster is to do a full factory reset. I’ve heard people say it’s like giving it a fresh start. Yeah, but I’m scared to mess with it. What if I delete something important? My photos are all on the cloud, but I still don’t want to take a chance. It’s not that bad. I did one on my old laptop and it worked fine. You just back up everything first, then you can wipe it and start fresh. I did that once, and it worked. It was like having a new computer. Though I had to set it up again from scratch, which took a few hours. Man, I wish I had your patience. I’m not sure I’d be able to do that. I just want something that works without me having to fix it every week. I know what you mean. I was thinking about getting a used one from eBay. They’ve got some pretty good deals, and you can always test it out before buying. That’s what I did with my old one. Got it from a friend who had it for years. It was a bit of a gamble, but it ended up working great. I’ll think about it. I just need to get this one to run properly first.

So, do you like the bistro? It's a bit of a different vibe from the ones back home, isn’t it? I’m still getting used to it, to be honest. The food is decent, but the decor feels… I don’t know, a bit forced. Like they tried too hard to be  hip  or something. Yeah, I noticed that too. I mean, the lighting is nice, but the walls are all covered in these abstract paintings. It’s like someone’s art gallery mixed with a café. Not sure if it’s intentional or just a gimmick. Maybe both. Anyway, I think it’s a good place to hang out. It’s got that nice, calm atmosphere. I’m just glad it’s open—what with the weather being so weird lately. I’d rather be in here than outside. Definitely. But you know, I still can’t get over how much I miss the pubs in England. The way people used to chat, the ale, the warmth. It feels like a different world here. I know, right? I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately. It’s like, I’ve got a job, I’ve got a flat, I’m working with international students from all over the world—but sometimes I feel like I’m not  me  anymore. You know? Yeah, I get that. I mean, I’m not working full-time anymore, and I’ve kind of lost that sense of identity. I used to think my purpose was to teach, but now I’m just… floating. It’s strange being in a place like this, where people are so busy and driven, yet I feel like I’m not living up to anything. I keep thinking about my dreams, you know? Like, what do I want to do with my life? Maybe I should start something, like a fitness class or something. You know, help people with their health? It’s a bit cliché, but I’m trying to find my way. That’s not cliché, actually. You’ve always had that kind of drive. You were the one who used to go running every morning, even when it was raining. You were like a human metronome. Maybe it’s time to bring that back. You’re right. I’ve been so distracted with work, I haven’t even thought about training. Maybe I could start small—like going to the gym twice a week.

So, do you think we should go to the Dorset Steam Fair this weekend? I heard it’s a really big event and there are so many things to do. I've heard about it, but I don’t think I’ve ever gone. I’ve always been more into the countryside than big events. But if you want to go, I'm sure it’ll be fun. Just don't forget to book your ticket early though, they can get sold out. Oh, I was just thinking about that. We need to make sure the ticket is accessible for the disabled too. I know some of the facilities there aren’t as good as others. I heard there's a special section for people with mobility issues. Yeah, I remember reading something like that. I think there are some ramps and maybe even a special entrance. I’ll check the website later to make sure we’re covered. Also, we’re planning to bring our cat, Miso, along for the day. I was worried about the noise, but maybe the fair’s not too loud? Miso’s a clever cat, isn’t she? She used to follow me around the house like a shadow. I think she'd be fine as long as we keep her in the car or maybe in a quiet spot. I’m more worried about the weather, though. If it rains, the whole day could be ruined. I know what you mean. I've been looking at property prices in the area and it's just gone up again. I think I might need to move soon. The house I’m in now is getting a bit too much for me and I want to be closer to the town center. That’s about the same as me. I’ve been thinking about moving too, but I’m not sure what to do with all the furniture. I barely use half of it. It’s such a pain to haul everything over. Maybe we can get some help from the local council? You could always ask for advice from the care assistant’s union. I know some people there have experience with moving and they might be able to help out. Plus, with the cost of living going up, it’s better to be prepared. I’ve heard that some of the local councils go out of their way to help people like us.

I just got a message from the estate agent saying we might have to move again. It's such a pity. I thought I'd finally settled in Thirsk after all these years. I know, it's really hard to hear, but I think it's for the best. You’ve been on your own for so long, and with the new housing policies, it's not easy to find a place that’s affordable and safe. But Grandma, you said you loved this house. You said it reminded you of the old days when you used to go to the church every Sunday and the parishioners all knew your name. I know, love, but things change. The church is closing, and the vicar has said they’re going to be moving their services online. You know how I feel about that. It’s not the same without the community. I hear you, but I think it’s still worth trying to stay. Maybe we can look for a place nearby, in the village. There are some nice artisan businesses and a new café that’s really popular with the locals. Yeah, and it’s not like we don’t have options. I know a few people who are moving into the area and they all say it's a lovely place to live. Plus, it’s still close to the school, which is important for the kids. But what about the weather? I don’t think we’d be able to enjoy the gardens in the summer if we move. I mean, it’s already been so wet this year, and the lawns are muddy and the roses are looking pretty sad. Oh, I know, love. I’ve been trying to keep the garden up as best as I can. I’ve even started using social media to share photos of the roses. You should see them. They’re just blooming like crazy. That’s a great idea. You could even start a blog or something. With all the attention on social media these days, people love stories about gardening and local life. Exactly. And with your experience, you could even write about it. I mean, you’ve been a teacher for years, and you have a real gift for storytelling. You could share your journey of moving house and adapting to new places. Well, I suppose I could try.

I just got a call from the dentist. They said they’re going to be doing free hearing tests for children and teenagers in the village. Maybe we should check that out? Really? That sounds good. I don’t think we’ve ever had a hearing test. I mean, I know I haven’t. Do you think Ashaad would be interested? Ashaad? Is that the friend from school? The one who always has that weird nickname? Yeah, that’s the one. He’s a bit of a tech geek and always talking about how his ears are sensitive. I think he’s been complaining about some noise issues. That’s true. He always says he can hear things that other people can’t, like the hum of the fridge or the buzz of the lights. Maybe he’s just picky, but it’s funny. Or maybe he’s just been listening to too much music. I mean, he’s always in his room with headphones on. I remember once he came to our house and was like, “This is so loud, I can feel it in my bones!” I think that might be a sign to get a hearing test. Or maybe just a little bit of noise sensitivity. But it’s good that the dentist is offering these tests – especially for kids and teens who might not think about it. Yeah, and don’t forget, next week is the birthdays for both of us. We’ve been meaning to plan something special. Maybe we could get a birthday cake and a surprise? It’s been a while since we had a proper celebration. I’d like that. But I don’t think we can afford a big cake. Maybe we could do a small one? Or even just a birthday card from our parents. That’s a good idea. I mean, it’s not like we’re the only ones with birthdays this week. Monet’s also turning 10. And I remember she said she wants a special birthday, like the one with the chocolate eggs and the stickers. Yeah, and I think she’s been saving up her allowance for a while. She told me she wants to buy a book and a set of stickers. Maybe we could do something simple but still go the extra mile. I think it’s important to make sure we don’t forget our birthdays.

So, how’s the new flat? I heard you moved in last week. Oh, it’s alright, I guess. It’s a bit of a mess, though. You mean the usual chaos of moving in? Yeah, exactly. I’m still unpacking. I’ve got boxes everywhere, and I haven’t even started sorting through them yet. I can’t imagine doing that. I’m still in my old place, just waiting for the new one to be ready. It’s so weird, isn’t it? I thought I’d be more excited, but honestly, it’s just a load of stuff. I know, I know. But once you get settled, it’ll be fine. I mean, I’m still waiting for the lights to be installed in my new place, and I’m already thinking about the garden. Yeah, I’m thinking about the garden too. I plan to plant some herbs. I’ve always wanted to grow my own. That sounds great! I’d love to have some herbs in the kitchen. I’ve been buying them from the market every week, but it’s so much cheaper to grow them. Exactly. My nan used to have a beautiful herb garden. She always said it was the best part of the house. That’s so nostalgic. I don’t even have a garden, just a small balcony. But I’ve got a few pots of basil and mint already. That’s cool. You’re ahead of the game. I still haven’t even got the balcony sorted out. I’ve been meaning to get some plants, but the weather’s been so unpredictable. Yeah, it’s been pretty grim. I mean, it’s supposed to be spring, but it’s like winter again. I know. I just wish we could get some proper sunshine. I’ve been trying to get my sun loungers out, but honestly, it’s too cold. I feel you. I’ve been sitting on the couch with a blanket and a book, just trying to get through this week. I know what you mean. I’ve been working overtime so much lately, I just need a break. I’m thinking of taking a weekend trip soon. Maybe to Brighton? That sounds nice. I’ve been wanting to go to Brighton too. I heard the beaches are amazing this time of year. Yeah, I heard that too.

So, I was just thinking about that long cycle ride I did when I was a kid. You know, when we used to ride all the way from Almondsbury to Bristol just for the fun of it. It was a real adventure, wasn’t it?      Oh, I remember that! My dad used to take me on one of those rides too. He said it was good exercise for the legs and the soul. Although, I have to say, riding through the countryside with nothing but a bottle of water and a sandwich was quite the experience.      That’s nothing compared to what I did as a kid! I used to ride all the way to Manchester, just to see the city. It was a real test of endurance, but it made me who I am today.      Speaking of endurance, I still remember my early days as a dentist. Back in the 70s, we didn’t have all the fancy equipment we have now. You’d have patients coming in with terrible teeth, and you had to do the best you could with what you had.      I can imagine. I mean, we all had different experiences, but I think the NHS gave us some perks back then—like the sailing trips. Do you remember the one where we had lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon?      Oh, that was something! We did have a few lectures on the boat. It was a bit strange, but it gave us a break from the usual routine. And the view from the sea was just amazing.      That sounds like a great way to unwind. Anyway, I was thinking about a trip to Prague. I heard about some amazing bargains there. You can get a week’s accommodation for less than a week in London.      I’ve heard about that too. Maybe we should do that. I’ve always wanted to go back. Though I must say, I’m more into theatres and exhibitions. But sometimes, it’s impossible to get in even when you’ve got a ticket.      That’s a real shame. I’ve had a couple of times when I got to the venue just in time and missed the show. It’s such a disappointment.      Yeah, and I think we should talk about the jive event we’re planning. The barn is looking good, but we need to make sure it’s all set for the night.

So, do you think we could base our business around social networking and how it's impacting education? I mean, with all the changes in how students learn now, maybe we could create a platform or a service that helps teachers integrate social media more effectively into their teaching methods. That’s an interesting idea. I mean, there’s definitely a lot of research on how social media affects learning. But have you thought about the potential challenges? I mean, not all teachers are comfortable using social platforms in the classroom. Some might be concerned about privacy or distractions. Yeah, that’s a good point. But maybe we could focus on creating short, case studies that show how learning materials and development of moving images can be used effectively in educational settings. You know, like how to use videos or interactive content to engage students. Exactly, and I think there’s a growing trend towards blended learning. Maybe we could develop training modules or workshops for teachers that show them how to incorporate digital tools into their curriculum. It’s not just about the technology—it’s about the pedagogy behind it. I agree. We could even partner with some educational institutions or online learning platforms to pilot our ideas. It might be a way to get real-world feedback and build credibility. That sounds like a solid plan. But have you considered how we would market this? I mean, if we’re targeting teachers, we need to make sure our message resonates with them. Maybe we could use social media itself to promote our services. It’s a bit of a catch-22, but it’s a start. Yeah, it’s a bit of a loop, but maybe we could start with a blog or a YouTube channel where we post our case studies and educational content. That way, we can showcase our work and attract the right kind of attention. I like that. We could also create some downloadable resources for teachers—like lesson plans or guides that make it easy for them to implement new strategies. It’s all about making the tools accessible and relatable. Exactly. We could even include interactive elements, like quizzes or discussion prompts, to make the learning process more engaging. It’s not just about delivering content—it’s about delivering experiences. I think that’s the key. If we can help teachers see social networking and digital tools as resources rather than distractions, we might be able to create something truly impactful.

I just thought of something, you remember that weekend we went to Brighton with the Browns? That was the one where we got lost and ended up on the beach at Hove instead. Oh yeah, and we were so proud of ourselves for getting there without a map. Remember how we told them we were “adventuring”? Exactly. And then we sat on that bench for ages, just watching the waves. It was so peaceful. I don’t think we’ve had a conversation like that since. You’re right. It was one of those moments where you just feel like you’re part of the sea, you know? Like, everything else fades away, and all you can hear is the sound of the water. Yeah, it’s like the sea has this way of making you feel small and yet completely at ease. I wonder if that’s why we keep going back. It’s not just about the place, it’s about the feeling. I think you’re right. It’s kind of like how we feel when we’re walking by the river near the university. That place always makes me feel calm. You know, the way the water flows and the breeze on your face. It’s interesting, isn’t it? We’re both lecturers – we’re used to thinking, analysing, making sense of things. But the sea doesn’t need explaining. It just is. And that’s what I love about it. Sometimes, you don’t need to overthink things. You just need to be there, and let the moment wash over you. I feel like we’ve been talking about the sea a lot lately. Maybe it’s because we’re both feeling a bit restless, or maybe it’s just the way the summer is going. The weather is so variable, and the sea changes every day. I think it’s the contrast between the chaos of life and the calm of the sea. Like, the more busy we get, the more we need that moment of stillness. Exactly. And I think that’s why we’re always saying we want to go back to the coast. It’s not just about the view or the water, it’s about the way the sea makes us feel connected to something bigger. Yeah, and it makes me think about the people we’ve met along the way too.

So, do you think the way we dress now is actually more fashionable or just more practical? I mean, like, I don’t know, I’ve seen so many people wearing all black or just basic t-shirts and jeans, but I don’t know if that’s really fashion or just comfort. I think it’s a bit of both. Like, some people just want to be comfortable, especially with the weather being so unpredictable these days. But I also think there’s a lot of influence from social media, like Instagram and TikTok. People are inspired by what they see online, even if it's just a random outfit someone posted. Yeah, I agree with that. I mean, I’ve noticed that a lot of influencers are promoting minimalistic styles—you know, the "clean girl" or "effortless" look. But then again, there are still so many people who are into vintage and retro fashion. I mean, I actually bought this cute blouse from a thrift store last week, and it’s so much better than what I could buy in a store for the same price. That’s true. I think there’s more variety now than ever before. Like, people are mixing and matching different styles. I mean, I’ve seen people wearing cargo pants with a little dress or something. It’s like fashion is becoming more about personal expression rather than following strict rules. Exactly. It’s not just about looking good anymore. It’s about identity. Like, if you dress in a certain way, people can tell a lot about you. Or at least, that’s what I think. I mean, I have a friend who always wears these oversized sweaters and jeans, and people just assume she’s laid-back and artistic. That’s kind of what I was thinking. I think fashion is evolving so fast now that it’s almost hard to keep up. Like, one trend comes and goes in a matter of weeks. I mean, I saw a friend of mine wearing this neon pink jacket last week, and the next day, it was already out of fashion. I don’t know how people even keep track of what’s in or out. It’s almost overwhelming. I mean, there’s so much to choose from, but it’s also hard to know what to wear when you’re out.

Mummy, I just got back from the weekend trip with my friends. I had so much fun! That’s great, love. Did you take any pictures? Yeah, a lot! I even took some of the cliffs and the beach at Hastings. I think I’ve got some good shots. That’s brilliant. You know, I used to take photos all the time when I was younger. I even got into photography a bit, but then life got in the way. Really? What kind of photography did you do? Mostly landscapes and portraits. I loved capturing people’s expressions. I used to take pictures of my friends and family. It was like capturing memories. Although, I still don’t like the ones in the garden. They’re so big! You’re so brave for even being outside with them. I still get terrified just thinking about them. I’ve been meaning to read more too. I’ve been really busy with work lately. I’ve had a few clients come in, and it’s been a bit overwhelming. I know, I heard you were working late last week. I’m thinking of doing photography. I’d love to learn more about it. That’s amazing, love. You’ve always had a good eye for pictures. You’ll do great. I’m really proud of you. Thanks, Mummy. I can’t wait to show you all my pictures when I finish the course. I can’t wait to see them.

I just popped round, didn't want to intrude, but I thought I’d check in and see how you're all doing. Oh, don’t worry, we were just having a cup of tea and catching up. You know how it is—get a bit of a backlog of things to say when you're together. Yeah, and it's not like we've got a lot of visitors these days. Not since the kids all moved out. I know what you mean. It's strange, isn’t it? The silence, the stillness. You start to miss the noise of the house. I’ve been thinking about that.
