He’s got the right skills, and he’s got a good work ethic. I mean, he’s had to be, considering he’s been out of work for so long. Yeah, I know. But I’m not sure if I’m ready for that kind of pressure. I mean, I’ve done a lot of things, but it’s not like I’ve been waiting for a job all these years. That’s not true. You’ve been waiting, but you’ve also been trying to keep yourself busy. You’ve got that garden, you’ve got the car, you’ve even started that 3D printing project. Yeah, and I think it's time he took a bit more of a step forward. It’s not like the world has moved on, and he’s been left behind.

I just wanted to talk to you about something important, love. I’ve been thinking a lot lately, and I feel like I need to share this with someone I trust. Of course, dear. You know you can always talk to me. What’s on your mind? Well, I’ve been thinking about bringing my daughter from abroad to live here. She’s been in Australia for a few years now, working, but I think it’s time she came back. She’s been feeling quite isolated, and I just… I miss her. I miss having her around, you know? That’s understandable, really. It’s never easy to be far away from family, especially when you’re in a new country. But have you thought about how this would affect you both? I mean, you’re not exactly young anymore, and moving her back might be a big adjustment for both of you. I know, I know. It’s a big decision, and I’m not making it lightly. She’s been through a lot down there. Her job is stable, but it’s not fulfilling, and she’s been feeling quite down. I think she needs a change of scenery, and I think coming back here might help her find her way again. That sounds like a genuine concern. But have you talked to her about it? I mean, she’s an adult, and she might not be ready for that kind of change. I have. She’s been in touch with me a lot lately, and she’s actually been asking about coming back. She said she’s tired of the loneliness and wants to be closer to her family. I think she’s ready, and I think it’s about time. I can see why you’d feel that way. But I just want to make sure you’re not doing this because you feel lonely yourself. It’s easy to think, ‘she’s my child, she should come home,’ but you have to be honest with yourself. Are you ready for that kind of responsibility again? I don’t know. It’s been a while since I’ve had to take care of someone like that. I’m not the same person I was back when she was a child. But I do miss the days when she was here, when we were all together. I understand.

So, how’s the job interview going, Dave? I heard you had one last week. Oh, it was alright, I suppose. It wasn’t too bad, but I think I might have been a bit too eager to impress. I mean, I was really enthusiastic about the role, but maybe I came across as a bit over the top. You know, enthusiasm is good, but you’ve got to balance it with professionalism. I mean, it’s not like you’re applying for a job as a motivational speaker or something. It’s just a teaching position, right? Yeah, but I wanted to make sure they saw how much I care about education and the students. I mean, I think I did pretty well, but I’m not sure if I got the job. Well, you can’t know until they get back to you. But speaking of jobs, have you heard about the Scottish referendum? I mean, it’s been in the news a lot lately, hasn’t it? Yeah, I have. It’s quite a divisive issue, isn’t it? I mean, I understand the arguments on both sides, but I think the vote is going to have a big impact on the whole country. I just hope it doesn’t cause more division than it needs to. I agree. It’s really interesting to see how the political climate is shifting. I mean, I think people are becoming more aware of the issues that affect them directly. Like, someone like me, who’s in higher education, I’m seeing how different policies can impact the students and the overall academic environment. Exactly. And it’s not just about politics, it’s also about how people are dealing with the present situation. I mean, my daughter is starting college next year, and I can’t help but think about how the decisions being made now will affect her future. That’s true. It’s a bit worrying, isn’t it? I mean, we’re all trying to navigate this uncertain time, and it’s hard to know what’s going to happen next. Yeah, it’s a tough time for everyone. But I guess we just have to keep going and try to make the best of it. I suppose that’s the thing about being a teacher or a lecturer, isn’t it? You’re always looking ahead, preparing for the future, even when the present is a bit uncertain.

So, do you think we've got everything we need for the mousetrap game? I mean, it's not like we're building a real trap, just a game, right? Yeah, I think we do. We’ve got the wooden box, the string, the small metal rod, and the sticky pad. But I don’t think we’ve got the lever part. Where’s that? Oh, I think I saw it in the shed. Let me go and check. By the way, do you remember when we tried to set up the mousetrap in the garden last summer? It didn’t even work. The mouse just ignored it. Yeah, that was a disaster. It was like the mouse was on some kind of mission. I think it was trying to get to the bread we left out. I mean, the mouse had more sense than we did. I still can’t believe that thing worked at all. I mean, we were all sitting around trying to figure out how to wind it up and get the lever to spring. It was like trying to assemble IKEA furniture without the instructions. Oh, I remember that. You tried to use a rubber band to wind it up, and it just snapped. I was so proud of myself for thinking of that. But then the whole thing came apart in my hands. And then we had to call the pest control guy. He laughed when we told him about the mousetrap. He said it was one of the strangest things he’d ever seen. You know, I’d rather have a real mouse problem than being stuck in a room with a bunch of people trying to build a mousetrap. It’s like you’re all talking about America, but you’re actually just trying to figure out how to catch a mouse. Hey, I think I found the lever! Okay, so we need to put this here, and then attach the string. Wait, is this the right size? I mean, I’ve seen these kinds of traps in museums. They were way more complicated. Don’t you think it’s a little strange that we’re all trying to build a mousetrap in the middle of our living room? I mean, I’ve been on a trip to America, and I saw these things in the country. They’re just regular traps. You don’t need to make them your own.

I’m home! How was your day? It was okay, just a bit busy. I had to attend a couple of meetings. But I’m glad I’m back. I brought something home with me, actually. Oh, really? What did you get? I used to go to the same shop every week when I was in university. It was a bit of a comfort. I can imagine. I’ve been trying to find a local shop that I can go to regularly. I think it would help me stay more connected to the community. That sounds like a great idea. It’s nice to support local businesses, especially when you can build a relationship with the staff. Exactly. Plus, it’s reassuring to know that the people behind the counter care about what they’re selling.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about babies a lot lately. I mean, it’s not like I’m going to have one any time soon, but it’s funny how much you start thinking about it when you’re around people who do. Yeah, I can imagine. I mean, I’ve got a cousin who just had a baby, and it’s like every time I see her, she’s talking about how exhausted she is but also how amazing it is. She’s right. I mean, it’s so different from when you’re just a kid. You think you’re ready, but when it actually happens, it’s like, “Oh, I didn’t sign up for this.” I know. I think I’d be terrified. I mean, I’m not even sure I’d be able to remember how to change a nappy, let alone feed a baby. Oh, you’ll get the hang of it. You know, it’s funny because when you’re young, you think you know everything, but then you’re like, “Wait, what is this even?” Exactly! Anyway, I was just thinking about babies, but I was also thinking about moving house. I mean, my parents are finally getting around to it, and it’s so weird because they’ve been in that house for, like, forever. Oh, I can relate. My parents are planning to move too, but they’re having such a hard time deciding where. It’s like, “Where do we go? We don’t want to be too far from family, but we also don’t want to be in the city anymore.” Yeah, that’s the problem. You know, it’s not just about the house—it’s about the whole lifestyle. Do you want to be near the university, or do you want to be in the countryside? I think I’d prefer a bit of both. Maybe somewhere that’s not too crowded, but still has access to the city. You know, like a small town with a good train link. That sounds perfect. I mean, I could totally see myself living in a place like that.

So, I just wanted to bring up something I’ve been thinking about – your accent. I’ve noticed you’ve got this really smooth way of speaking, like you’re from somewhere posher than Bedford. Are you from somewhere else? Or is it just… I don’t know, a natural thing?      Nah, I’m from Bedford too, but I’ve got this thing where I tend to drop my ‘r’s and stuff. I think it’s just because I studied English Literature and started hanging out with people who do that. It’s like a bit of a hobby. But don’t get me wrong, I like to keep it real, too—especially when I’m teaching.      Yeah, like that one time when you were teaching that class and you said, “Let’s go to the  r estaurant” and I nearly fell off my chair laughing. It was so funny. But honestly, I think your accent is just…  charming . I mean, don’t get me wrong, I’ve got my own way of speaking too—like, I’m from Luton, and I don’t know what it is, but I swear people from elsewhere think I’ve got this  weird  way of saying things. It’s like…  worse  than a posh accent. It’s just…  different .      You’re not wrong. I’ve heard people say that before. Like, when I was in London, people would say, “Oh, you’ve got that Luton lilt.” Like it was a crime. But I don’t think it’s a bad thing. It’s just…  unique . I mean, I’ve got my own way of speaking too, with that Bedford accent. I used to think it was too posh for my liking, but now I kind of like it.      You know, I think that’s the thing. Everyone’s got their own way. I mean, I’ve got this friend from Cornwall who speaks like a surfboard, and he’s like, “Wot’s up, mate?” and you just think, “Where’s the  actual  English coming from here?” It’s just funny how accents change depending on who you’re around.      Speaking of accents, have you ever thought about learning another language? I mean, I’ve been thinking about picking up Greek or something, because I’ve got this Greek cousin and I can’t even understand what she says half the time. It’s like, we’re both British, but we’re like two different languages.

I can't believe I've been driving this car for almost three years now. It's starting to feel like it's got a mind of its own. I know, I've been telling you for ages it's time for a new one. Your old car's been giving you more trouble than it's worth. I know, I know. But I’ve been saving up, and I just haven’t felt ready to part with the money. But I’m trying to save up for something else too. You know, like a holiday or maybe even a bit of a down payment on a house. I don’t want to spend all my savings on a car. I get it, but maybe you can start looking into some options. There are quite a few affordable cars out there. You don’t have to go for something too fancy, just something reliable. Yeah, maybe. But if you’re thinking about saving up, maybe you can start a budget and track your expenses. That way you’ll know exactly how much you can allocate towards a new car without sacrificing other things. That might be a good idea. I’ve been trying to keep track of my spending, but I think I need a more structured approach. I mean, I’m not sure if I can afford to pay for a car outright, so maybe I should look into financing options too. Yeah, I think that's a solid plan. You could even start by checking out some car finance companies. There are a few that offer flexible repayment plans. Just make sure you read the terms carefully and don’t end up with a loan that you can’t handle. I’ll definitely look into that. I just need to make sure I’m not rushing into anything.

Oh, I’ve been meaning to ask—did you two get the milk? We’re running low again. Yeah, I grabbed a pint yesterday, but it’s gone. I think it’s been in the fridge for a few days now. Should we go to the shop? You know, when I was your age, we’d have just walked down to the local shop. No phones, no deliveries, just a quick journey and you’d be back with a loaf of bread and a pint of milk. You two are too lazy. Yeah, and we’d have brought back more than just milk. We’d have had a chat with the shopkeeper, maybe even bought a few eggs and some fruit. Nowadays, you just buy the essentials and walk away. I know, but with the cost of living and everything, you can’t afford to waste time or money. Plus, I’ve got exams to mark, and I need to be in a good mood for that. I get it, but you can’t keep putting it off forever. We’ve got a few things to do today—like sorting out the garden, and maybe planning the next family dinner. You know, something to do that doesn’t involve sitting in front of the TV. Oh, someone’s got an opinion today. I say we just order the groceries online. It’s faster, and you don’t have to deal with the hassle of going out. Although, I do miss the good old days when we could actually talk to people face to face. Yeah, and not just because of the shopkeeper. I remember when the postman used to stop by every morning. You’d have a chat, hear about the weather, maybe even get a few bits of gossip. Now, all he does is drop the letters and leave. I suppose it’s a bit of a sad state of affairs. But I do miss the old days. Even though I was too busy with work to go out much, I still enjoyed the little things—the chat, the local news, the sense of community. Maybe we can start small. Maybe we can walk to the shop once a week, just to see what it’s like. It’s not like we have anywhere else to be. Or we could take the kids with us. The grandkids love going out, and it’s a chance for them to learn about the old ways.

Alright, do you two want some toast? I’ve got some fresh bread in the fridge. Yes, please. I’m starving. I’ve been playing with my pirate ship all morning. Me too! I made a pirate flag out of a piece of paper and a sock. It’s not very good, but I think it looks like a real pirate flag. Oh, that’s great! I bet your pirate ship is full of treasure, then? Yeah, it’s got gold coins and a treasure map. I found a chest of gold in the kitchen cupboard earlier. It was really heavy, but I managed to carry it to the ship. You’re a real pirate, then. I remember you were telling me last week about your pirate doll. I thought you were just playing with sticks in the garden. Well, I’ve been planning this whole pirate adventure for weeks. I even got a sword from the toy shop. It’s not real, but it’s sharp enough to pretend with. I have a sword too, but mine is made of plastic. It doesn’t cut anything, though. That’s probably better for you. I wouldn’t want you to cut your fingers on a real sword. Although, if you’re into pirates, maybe you should read some pirate stories. There’s a book called  Treasure Island  by Robert Louis Stevenson. It’s about a real pirate adventure. Oh, that sounds cool. But I already read a book about Shakespeare. I thought it was about pirates too. No, that was  The Tempest . It’s a play about a magician and a shipwreck. But Shakespeare week is coming up, right? You know, the one where we’re going to Stratford to see the plays. Can we see  Macbeth ? I like the witches. I think we’ll be doing  A Midsummer Night’s Dream  this year. It’s about fairies and a magical forest. You might like that. It’s got a lot of magic and dancing. That sounds fun! I like magic too. I’ve been trying to make my own magic tricks with the toys we got for Easter. I even made a stop-motion animation of a witch flying on a broomstick. Can I help you with that? I can make the witch move. You’d be great at that. And maybe after the Shakespeare week, we can go to the circus workshop.

So, do you remember that time we tried to sail from Jeddah to Cyprus? I still can't believe we got arrested for it. Oh, I remember that! You were so enthusiastic about that boat, weren’t you? I think you even named it after a Greek god or something. Yeah, I remember the look on your face when the customs officer said we couldn’t go. You were like a kid caught with a candy bar. And don’t forget, we were in Saudi Arabia teaching at the time. You were teaching English, right? I still remember how you used to talk about the local culture and everything. Oh, I still do. It was amazing. My students were so curious, especially about the food. One day, I brought in some chocolate and told them it was a treat. A whole class of boys chased me around the classroom trying to get it. I nearly got caught. Haha, you should have seen the look on their faces when you finally gave it to one of them. I think it was the only time they looked at me like a hero. You know, I heard that alcohol is banned in many places in the Middle East. I wonder how you managed to keep a drink on board during that trip. Oh, I didn’t. I just had water. But the funny thing was, we did have a bottle of something in the boat, and we almost got in trouble because of it. We had to hide it under the floorboards. That’s not the worst story, though. There was that time I got into a bit of a scrape with the dental magazines. I was trying to get some for a friend, but I had to go through a lot of trouble to get them. Oh, that’s right! You were trying to smuggle them in. I think you got caught with a whole stack in your bag. I remember you were so embarrassed when you got caught. You were trying to explain it like it was a legitimate business. It was hilarious. And don’t forget the time we tried to sail from Jeddah to Cyprus. You said you could get there in three days, but you ended up taking five because of the weather and the bureaucracy. Well, I do love a challenge, don’t I? That trip taught me a lot about patience and perseverance.

So, do you think we should get a new bathroom? I mean, the one in the house is getting a bit old, and with the kids coming and going, it's not really up to scratch anymore. Yeah, honestly, I've been meaning to talk about that. We've had the same one for years now, and it's starting to feel like a bit of a dump. Especially with the teenage boy in the house, he’s always doing something to it, like cracking the tiles or leaving wet towels everywhere. Hey, I didn’t do that! I told you, I just left my towel there because it was drying. I didn’t crack anything! Oh, come on, you know you did. You’ve been in there like five times this week. I’m not saying you broke them, but it’s not exactly the cleanest place anymore. Exactly! And I don’t know if we’re ready for a full renovation, but maybe a bit of a refresh would do. Just updating the tiles, maybe a new toilet, and some fresh paint. It’s not the end of the world, but it would make the place feel a bit more welcoming. Honestly, I don’t mind the bathroom. I mean, it works. It just needs a bit of a clean-up, maybe some new soap, and that’s it. I don’t want to be the one to pay for a new one, though. You two are the ones who have the money. Well, I don’t know about the money, but I do know that with the holidays coming up, maybe we can start looking at some options. I mean, we’ve got the kids off school, and it’s a perfect time to do some home improvements. Yeah, I agree. It would be nice to have a proper bathroom again. And besides, I think the kids would appreciate it too. Especially if they’re going to be staying over more often now with their friends. It’s not just about us anymore. Speaking of which, did you hear about the party plans for the weekend? My mates are trying to get a group together for the weekend. I think they’re going to be staying in the house. That’s great news. But I hope you’re not planning on using the bathroom for the whole weekend.

So, do you think truffles are worth the hype? I mean, I've seen them on TV, and it's like, €500 for a bit of fungus? That's insane. I don’t know, love. I mean, truffles are a luxury item, but if you’re in the right place, like Istria, and you know where to look, they can be pretty amazing. I remember my mum once told me that a truffle can be worth more than a whole chicken. Yeah, but I heard once that truffles are just like, you know, mushrooms with a fancy name. Like, people pay so much for them because they think they’re special, but really, they’re just a bit of dirt with a strong smell. I mean, I guess if you're a chef, truffles are like the holy grail, but for regular people, it's just a bit of an overhype. I’d rather just have a good steak and some proper British pie, even if it's not fancy. I think you're both missing the point. Truffles are not just about the food — they’re about the experience. I mean, think about the way they’re presented, the way they’re used in dishes. It's part of the culture. And besides, I’ve had truffles in London, and it was worth every penny. Yeah, but I was in a restaurant in Milan once and the chef put a truffle on a plate and said, “This is from the Alba region.” I was like, what does that even mean? It's just a mushroom. I get it, but there's something about how people treat them. Like, you can't just walk into a store and buy one — you need a guide, you need to know where they’re coming from. It's almost like a treasure hunt. And then there's the part about the smell. I remember once my dad tried a truffle, and he said it smelled like a wet dog. I was like, really? That’s not a good thing. Oh, I think it's more about the context. If you're in a restaurant where they serve it with a nice wine and some good company, it's a different experience. If you're just trying it at home in a bag, it's just a strong mushroom. Yeah, but I still think it’s a bit of a gimmick.

So, do you know what’s going on with the new project they’re launching? I heard it’s something related to AI and language processing. Yeah, I think it's about integrating machine learning into their publishing systems. They want to automate some of the editing and formatting processes. But honestly, I’m not sure how much of a difference it will make in the long run. I heard they’re also considering using chatbots for customer support. I mean, it’s a bit of a trend, isn’t it? Everyone’s jumping on the AI bandwagon these days. It’s a bit of a double-edged sword, isn’t it? On the one hand, it can make things more efficient, but on the other hand, there’s a risk of losing the human touch. I mean, what’s the point of a book if the process of creating it is too mechanized? I guess that’s the debate, isn’t it? But then again, the publishing industry is constantly evolving, right? If they don’t adapt, they might fall behind. I mean, look at the way reading habits have changed—people are consuming content differently now. Yeah, and with everything being digital, it’s hard not to embrace some of these technologies. But I still think there’s something special about the traditional aspects of publishing, like the physical book. You can’t replace the feeling of holding a real book in your hands. Absolutely. There’s a kind of nostalgia that comes with it. But I also think that there are ways to blend the old and the new. Maybe the key is finding a balance between technology and tradition. That’s a good point. I think the challenge is to use the technology to enhance the experience, not replace it. Maybe chatbots can help with customer queries, but the actual creative and editorial work should still be handled by humans. I agree. There’s a lot of potential here, but it has to be done thoughtfully. I mean, the last thing we want is for the publishing house to become just another tech company. Exactly. It’s about maintaining the core values of what publishing is—storytelling, education, and connection. Technology can support that, but it can’t go against it. I think that’s the main thing. If they can do that, then the new project might actually be a success.

So, do you think we’ll make it in time for the party? I was just checking the map again. It says the drive from here to Tarnow should take about an hour and a half, but I’m not sure if that’s with or without traffic. Yeah, it’s probably about an hour and a half, but we’re driving on good roads, so I’m confident we’ll get there before the sun sets. I just hope the campervan doesn’t break down again. It’s been acting up a bit lately. Oh, don’t get me started. I swear it’s like the campervan has a mind of its own. One minute it’s running smoothly, the next it’s sputtering and making these weird noises. I’m starting to think it’s just trying to give us a hard time. I know, it’s been a bit of a nightmare. I mean, we’ve been on the road for a week now, and it’s been non-stop maintenance. But, hey, it’s a classic, and I guess we’ve got to give it a bit of love and care. Though I’m not sure we’re doing it right. That’s the thing, isn’t it? I tried to do a little bit of research before we left – about campervans and what to expect – but honestly, I think I just ended up confusing myself more. I mean, I thought I knew what I was doing, but now I’m second-guessing everything. I can relate. When I first started teaching, I thought I had it all figured out. But then I realized that teaching is a lot like driving a campervan – it’s about adapting as you go. And honestly, the more you learn, the more you realize how much you don’t know. Exactly. I think that’s the key to everything, really. Whether it’s teaching or traveling or even just surviving in this weather. I mean, the weather here is something else. I thought Poland would be colder, but it’s been raining all day, and now it’s just this constant drizzle. Yeah, it’s been a bit of a letdown, honestly. I thought it would be like a fairytale – go to a new country, meet new people, have an adventure. But I guess it’s not that simple. Still, I’m looking forward to seeing your cousin.

So, do you think the new Manchester City strip is going to be a hit or not? I mean, they’ve got that white with some red accents, but honestly, I can’t tell if it’s going to look good on the pitch or not. Honestly, I think it’s gonna be a bit of a gamble. I mean, they’ve gone for something that’s definitely not your traditional blue and white. It’s a bit bold, but I guess that’s the trend now. You know, football kits are getting more and more experimental these days. It’s like fashion meets sport. Yeah, I guess. But I also think the sponsors are playing a big role in that. You’ve got these big companies putting their logos all over the kits. I mean, the Nike sponsorship with Manchester City is massive, isn’t it? It’s not just the club anymore—it’s like a giant marketing campaign. Absolutely. You look at the kit, and you can almost see the brand. I mean, that’s part of the deal. Football clubs are businesses now, and they need to make money. If a company is willing to pay top dollar for a sponsorship, the club is going to do whatever it takes to keep them happy. It’s not just about the game anymore—it’s about branding. I get that, but sometimes I think it takes away from the spirit of the game. It’s not just about the players anymore. It’s about who’s paying for the stadium lights, the buses, the kits. It’s like everything’s a business decision now. I can see both sides of it. On one hand, it’s obvious that the clubs need money, and they’re not going to make it without sponsors. But on the other hand, when you look at the kits, you can’t even see the players anymore. It’s like they’re just part of the logo. Exactly. I mean, even the kits are starting to look more like ads than actual football gear. But I guess it’s part of the sport now. You can’t really complain about it, can you? You just have to accept it. Yeah, I guess so. Although, I still think it’s a shame that the kits are becoming so commercialized. There was a time when football was more about the game itself.

I just got a message from my cousin, and she’s mad at me because I didn’t answer her texts. I got so caught up in my own problems I completely forgot about her. You’re not the only one. I’ve been trying to get in touch with my brother for weeks. He’s been on and off the phone, but he’s just saying he’s busy. I don’t know if he’s just being evasive or if he’s really got a lot going on. I get that. It’s like everyone’s got their own life, but it’s annoying when you feel like you’re being ignored. I mean, I know he’s got a kid now, and he’s probably got more on his plate than ever. Yeah, but I’m not the only one with family drama. I had a fight with my mum last week. She’s been saying I should get a job and stop relying on Job Seekers Allowance. She’s always been like that. I can see where she’s coming from, but it’s not like it’s easy to find work. I mean, I’ve been looking for a while, and it’s just not happening. I tried applying for a few jobs, but they all turned out to be scams. Yeah, I’ve seen that too. There’s this one website that’s supposedly for job listings, but it’s just a front for fake employers. I almost fell for it. Oh no, that’s not good. I tried to order something from eBay the other day, and the delivery got delayed. I was so stressed, I almost called the police. I know how that feels. I got a package from someone who said they were selling a used cooking appliance, and when it arrived, it was barely working. I had to write a complaint to the site, but it didn’t do much. It’s just frustrating, isn’t it? I was thinking about cooking something tonight, but I don’t have the right equipment. I’ve got a George Foreman Grill, but I don’t know how to use it properly. Yeah, I tried once, and it burned everything. I think it’s because I didn’t read the instructions properly. I guess it’s one of those things you have to figure out by trial and error.

So, do you think we should go to the new convenience store down the road or just stick with the larger retailers? I mean, it's been a while since we've picked up anything for the house. I think the convenience store is better, honestly. You know, the prices are a bit cheaper, and it’s more convenient. Plus, the selection is decent now. They’ve started stocking more fresh stuff. I don’t know, love. I prefer the bigger ones, just because I like to check out the fresh fruit and vegetables. The convenience store always feels a bit too small and like they’re trying to make you buy more than you need. Yeah, I get that. But honestly, I’ve been meaning to try the new one. They’ve got a range of things that aren’t usually found in the big stores. Like, I saw some nice cheeses and a few breakfast items that look actually good. Oh, and the coffee there is amazing! I mean, it’s not the same as the café, but it’s way better than the shop’s instant stuff. I’ve been buying my coffee there for weeks now. Hmmm... I might go with you on that, love. I do like a good cup of coffee. Although, I must say, I still think the traffic around here is a nightmare. I was nearly in an accident the other day because of the sat nav. Oh no, really? That’s not good. I always get confused with the sat nav, especially when I’m not used to the area. I think I might have to get a better one. Yeah, I nearly did that once. I was trying to get to the supermarket and the sat nav said to take a left, but there was no way to go left. I had to turn around and go the other way. Oh, I’ve had worse. A few years ago, I was driving on the motorway and the sat nav told me I was going the right way, but I had to go the opposite. I nearly ended up in the wrong city. That sounds terrifying. I hope you didn’t get into any trouble. No, I didn’t. I just had to get out of the car and walk for a while. It was a bit of a nightmare, honestly. I’ve heard stories about people getting into plane crashes because of the sat nav, though.

So, do you know what’s happening with the new trainee teachers? I heard they’re all really strict. I mean, I don’t know if I’m ready for that. Yeah, I heard that too. I think some of the older students are really nervous. They’re saying that the new teachers are like,  “No more doodling on your worksheets!”  Oh no, that’s not fair. I mean, I do doodle sometimes, but it’s not like I’m distracting the whole class. It’s just me and my pencil. I know, but I heard one of the trainee teachers made a whole speech about how doodling is unproductive. It’s like they think we’re all just wasting time. I think it’s funny, honestly. Yeah, maybe, but I think it’s just because they’re new and they don’t know how to handle us. I mean, I’m not the only one who does that. I’ve seen Emily and Jake doing it too. Yeah, I guess. But I still think it’s annoying when they start taking points off for doodles. I mean, we’re still trying to learn, right? Like, aren’t we allowed to have a little fun? Exactly! I remember last week when we had that English lesson, and the teacher was going on about Shakespeare. Someone in the back started drawing a cat on the board. And the teacher didn’t even notice. I thought it was hilarious. Oh my god, I wish I had been there. I would’ve had a laugh. But I think I was in the library at the time. You would have been the one doing the laughing. I can just picture you trying to keep it quiet and not getting caught. That would’ve been epic. Yeah, but I think that’s just how we are. We’re always trying to make things interesting, even if it’s not supposed to be. I mean, who cares if we’re being a little bit chaotic? I think that’s what makes school fun. Like, even with all the tests and stuff, we still have our little moments. You know, like the time when we had that science project and accidentally set off a fire alarm. Oh man, that was a disaster. I remember that. We were in the lab, and we were trying to do this experiment with something that was supposed to be safe, and we ended up blowing up the whole thing.

Alright, let’s talk about something serious. You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about religion lately. Especially with the nuns coming to visit next week. It’s been on my mind ever since I heard about their charity work. Yeah, I heard about that too. But honestly, I’m not sure if I believe in any of it. I mean, what if all this stuff about heaven and hell is just a myth? Like, what if it’s all fake? Mummy! Nuns are like… like… superheroes? They can do magic! Oh, you’re still so young, love. You think nuns can do magic? They just wear cute little dresses and say prayers. Though I’ll admit, they do have a way of making things seem special. I don’t know, Mum. I’ve heard about all these different religions—Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, even Scientology. They all say different things. How do you know which one is right? That’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s hard to know. But I think it’s more about the way people live their lives. For instance, I know some of the nuns here in Cork—they’re very kind, very selfless. They help people who don’t have much. And that makes me think there’s something real about their faith. But what if Scientology is just a scam? I mean, they’ve been in the news a lot. I saw a documentary about them a while back. It was weird. Some people seem to think it’s a real religion, and others think it’s all make-believe. I don’t know. I think people believe what they need to believe. It’s like a comfort, you know? For some people, religion is the only thing that keeps them going. But then again, what about the Matrix? I mean, that movie shows how everything could be a simulation. What if all this religion stuff is just another layer of programming? Nuns are real! They do lunches and stuff! Yes, they do. And you know what? Some of them are just regular people who chose to live a certain way. I think that’s what matters more than the actual beliefs. Living with kindness and purpose. I guess. But what if you don’t believe in any of it? What if you just go through life without any religion? I think you can still be a good person without religion.

So, do you think I should actually go to those dancing lessons? I mean, I know it's been on my list for ages, but I’m not sure if I’m ready. Honestly, I think you should. You’ve been talking about it for months, and it’s not like it’s going to hurt. Plus, it’s a chance to get out of the house and meet people. I know, but I’m just nervous. What if I’m terrible? I mean, I’ve never even danced in front of anyone before. You don’t have to dance in front of anyone, you know. It’s more about the fun and getting into the rhythm. Besides, I think it’s a great way to get some exercise and maybe even meet some new friends. Yeah, but I’ve heard that some of the classes are pretty competitive. I don’t want to feel like I’m just messing up everyone else’s fun. I get that, but honestly, everyone’s there to learn. You don’t have to be perfect. Just show up, have a good time, and maybe even find a partner to dance with. You’re right, I guess. I just don’t want to feel out of my depth. You’re not. I mean, you’ve got the confidence to be here talking to me about it, so I think you’ve got what it takes. Thanks, I appreciate that. But seriously, what do you think about the idea of a holiday? I was thinking of going to the Lake District next summer. That sounds amazing! I’ve always wanted to go there. It’s so peaceful, and the scenery is just stunning. Yeah, it’s got that sort of vibe. And I think it would be a great way to unwind after the semester. Definitely. Though I have to say, I’d rather go somewhere with a bit more action. Maybe somewhere like Barcelona or Rome. Oh, I can see that. You always want something exciting. Well, I do. Though I’m not sure I’d be able to handle the heat in Barcelona. I get hot easily. Yeah, I guess you’d need to be careful with the weather wherever you go. Exactly. I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately, especially with the hours I’ve been working. It’s making me realize how important it is to take time off and do things I love.

So, do you think we should stop at the next market? I’ve heard they have some amazing fresh produce. I think it’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to try some local olive oil and wine. Not to mention the chance to pick up some fresh vegetables for our caravan trip. Yeah, I’d love to try some local food. I heard Istria has some of the best olive oil in Croatia. Do you think we can find it at the market? Definitely. And maybe we can also find some good wine to pair with our evening meal. I’ve heard the vineyards here are amazing. That’s exactly the kind of thing I was thinking about. But let’s not forget, we still have to plan our route. We need to make sure we’re not missing any of the key spots. Right, and we’ve got to think about where we’ll camp. I’ve been thinking about a place in the center park near the coast. There’s supposed to be some great views and a great spot for watching the sunset. Sounds perfect. But I’m not sure about the roads. I’ve heard some of the roads here can be a bit tricky, especially if we’re going to be driving a caravan. Yeah, I know what you mean. I still remember that time we tried to drive through the mountains in Italy and got stuck in a tunnel for an hour. Let’s make sure we check the GPS before we set off. And maybe we can stop at one of the local restaurants on the way. I’d love to try some traditional Croatian dishes. I’ve heard the food here is incredible, especially the seafood. That would be cool. But I still haven’t seen the first episode of  Sons of Anarchy  yet. I think I’ll need a break from all that food and wine. Maybe I can catch up on that tonight. That’s a good idea. But I was thinking, maybe we could also check out some art galleries or museums while we’re here. I’ve heard there’s a good one in Pula. Yeah, that’s not a bad idea. And don’t forget, we’ve got a couple of days here. We can map out a few routes and see where we want to go.

So, do you remember that time we were at the pub in Doncaster and that guy started playing that weird game with the rubber chicken? Oh yeah, I remember that. I thought it was hilarious at first, but then he started doing it in front of the whole group. It was kinda awkward. Honestly, I was just trying to avoid eye contact the whole time. I didn’t want to laugh, but I couldn’t help it. It was so cringey. I mean, I’ve seen people do that in games, but not in a public place like that. It was like he was trying to be a comedian, but he was just making everyone uncomfortable. Yeah, I agree. I think it was one of those games where you’re supposed to be funny, but it just went too far. I mean, it’s one thing to do it in a private setting, but not in front of a bunch of strangers. Exactly. I remember thinking, “Oh god, what if someone sees this on social media?” But then, of course, no one did. I mean, we were all just there for a few drinks and a laugh. Wait, so have you ever seen someone do that kind of thing – like, talking about anal stuff in a game? Yeah, actually. It was at a party in Cambridge. One of the guys was playing a game where he had to describe things someone had done in the past. And he kept bringing up weird stuff, like, I don’t know, “Have you ever done something with your… er… anal?” Oh my god, did he actually say that? No, he just hinted at it. But it was so awkward. I mean, I didn’t even know what he was talking about. I just kept saying, “I don’t know,” and he was like, “Come on, you know what I mean!” That sounds like a nightmare. I don’t know how anyone could handle that. I mean, if you’re not into that stuff, it’s just so uncomfortable. Yeah, I think it’s like a game of chance. You never really know what someone is going to bring up. But I guess that’s part of the fun, right? I guess. But honestly, I’d rather play something that doesn’t involve talking about private parts. Totally. I mean, we’re all friends, but even so, there are lines that shouldn’t be crossed.

Alright, lads, how’s the coffee? Alright, just a bit too bitter for my taste, but it’s better than nothing. Yeah, I’d say it’s fair enough. Not bad for a university library, I guess. Yeah, I mean, it’s not like we’re in a proper café, but at least it’s not the same old instant coffee from the vending machine. No, that’s right. I’ve had worse. Once I had to drink that coffee from the machine in the staff room, and it was like liquid regret. I remember that. You said it tasted like wet cardboard and regret. Oh, I did! Oh, you’re not the only one. I once skinny-dipped in a pool in Australia and I think I turned blue. I looked like a giant jellyfish. That’s not even real. You’re just trying to make me feel better about my own experience. No, it’s true. I was there. I saw it. And I still have the bruises. You know, I’ve been thinking about Australia since I got back. I mean, I love the UK, but sometimes I wonder what it would be like to live there. I’ve heard the food is really good, but the weather is just… odd. Oh, it’s not odd at all. It’s just hot, dry, and always sunny. But you can’t just walk outside without getting sunburned. I’d rather live in the UK, honestly. I mean, even though it’s raining all the time, at least I don’t have to worry about the sunburn. True. But you know what I would  love  to try? A zombie apocalypse. I mean, I’m not saying I’d be the hero or anything, but I’d at least be the one who could survive on my own. You’d be the one who would run away as soon as they showed up. No, I’d survive! I’ve read a lot of survival guides. I even know how to build a shelter and find water. Oh yeah? Well, I’ve read some survival guides too, and I can tell you one thing: the biggest threat in a zombie apocalypse isn’t the zombies—it’s the snoring. What? Yeah, I had this friend who went camping once, and he was so loud that the zombies  got  him.

So, do you remember that time we were at the theme park and we got caught in the middle of a security check? I mean, it was a normal day, and we were just walking through the gates, and suddenly, they were scanning everyone like they were at an airport. Oh, yeah! I still remember that. I was so confused because I thought we were just going on a ride. And I remember that guy in the uniform saying, “Do you have any prohibited items?” and I was like, “What? We’re just here for the rollercoaster!” Exactly! I mean, the only thing we had was a bag of peanuts. I think the security guard thought we were smuggling something. It was so ridiculous. I mean, who even brings peanuts to a theme park anymore? I don’t know, but I think they’re becoming more strict now about border security. I remember reading somewhere that they’re expanding checks at all major tourist sites in the UK. It’s like they’re trying to make sure no one is bringing in anything illegal, even if it’s just a bag of snacks. Yeah, I mean, we’re not even from the same country. I’m British, but I was born in Sunderland, so I’m not sure how much of a national security risk I am. But I guess with all the recent issues, they’re just being extra cautious. Honestly, I think it’s all about the paranoia. I mean, they’re also cracking down on people using fake IDs or trying to get into places they aren’t supposed to. I was at a film convention a few weeks ago, and they had a whole team checking everyone’s credentials. It was crazy. That makes sense. I mean, the more people are allowed to travel freely, the more difficult it is to track down those who might have malicious intent. But I still think it’s a bit over the top. I mean, I had a friend who got stopped for having a Nintendo Switch on him. He was trying to play a game on the train, and the security guy said it was a “potential weapon.” It was so absurd. Oh man, that’s ridiculous. I mean, you can’t even bring a phone these days without getting questioned. I remember when I was a kid, we’d just go to the park, ride the rides, and eat peanuts.

So, how’s the rowing going? You mentioned you were going to start lessons last week, right? Oh, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster, honestly. I got the first lesson in, and honestly, I felt like a total beginner. I mean, it’s not like I’ve never been on water before—rowing’s just different. I’ve always enjoyed kayaking, but rowing feels like a whole new level of coordination. Oh, I can imagine. I tried to do a bit of kayaking when I was younger, but I always got seasick. Though I suppose rowing is more controlled. I mean, you’re not battling the wind and waves like in a kayak. Exactly! I think that’s why I’m leaning more towards rowing now. I can feel more in control. Although, I did get a bit of a scare during my first session when I accidentally leaned too far back and almost capsized. The instructor just laughed and said, “That’s how you learn.” That’s true. I remember when I was learning to drive—my first time behind the wheel, I almost clipped the car in front of me. It took me ages to get used to the controls. But it’s all part of the learning process. Speaking of learning, I was thinking about that story you told me about your cousin coming to visit from Manchester. You said you hadn’t seen her in years, right? Yeah, that was a big deal. We hadn’t seen each other since she moved out to do her masters in psychology. It was a surprise when she turned up at my door, all dressed up in a nice coat and looking about ten years younger. I couldn’t believe it. That must have been nice. I’ve been meaning to reach out to my sister, but she’s been in and out of hospital with that illness. It’s been really hard. I feel like I should be doing more, but I just don’t know where to start. I know how you feel. It’s tough when someone you care about is going through something like that. I think it’s important to just be there, even if you don’t know what to say. Sometimes the presence is enough. Yeah, you’re right. I mean, I’ve been trying to help out by doing some of the errands, and I’ve also been helping her with her French lessons.

Dad, do you remember how to send a message in Morse code? I was trying to teach my little brother and I got stuck on the word “apple.” Hmm, I remember a bit, but it’s been ages. Let me think… A is dot-dot, P is dot–dash–dot, P is again, L is dash–dot–dot–dash, E is dot, and then L again. A lot of dots and dashes! Why do you want to learn it? Well, my teacher said it’s part of the history of communication, and I thought it would be cool to use it instead of texting sometimes. Plus, I heard that some people use it to send messages without phones. That’s true, but it’s not as fast as texting or using emojis. You know, I used to use text messages all the time when I was in school. Now I just use WhatsApp, and I’m always getting notifications. It’s like a never-ending stream of messages! Yeah, I get that. But I still think texting is kind of outdated. I mean, why not use emojis to show your feelings instead of words? Like, if you’re sad, you can just put a crying face 😢. It’s so much quicker! True, but sometimes it can be confusing. Like, if you just send a 😅, does that mean you’re laughing, or are you trying to be mysterious? I’ve had that happen before. I once got a message with just a 🤔 and didn’t know if it was a joke or an accusation. Haha, that’s funny. I guess texting has its own kind of language now. But I still miss seeing people in person. Especially on results day. I’m so nervous about my GCSE results. I know I did well in some subjects, but I’m not sure if I’ll get into the university I want. You’ll do fine, love. I remember when I was your age, I was so nervous about my A-levels too. But you know what? It all worked out in the end. Just try not to stress too much. Thanks, Dad. You always know how to calm me down. Oh, and by the way, I need to get a new water bottle. The one I had broke last week, and I had to drink from a plastic cup all day.

So, man, it's been a while, right? How have you been? Yeah, shit, it's been ages. I’m good, I’ve been keeping busy with uni stuff, but it’s been a wild ride. How about you? Honestly, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster too. I’ve been studying non-stop for exams, and honestly, I’ve been surviving on coffee and takeaways. Oh man, I get that. I’ve been trying to stay on top of my workload, but sometimes I just feel like I’m drowning in deadlines. I know, it’s the same for me. But hey, at least we’re still in the same boat. Speaking of which, have you ever thought about going to Japan? Yeah, actually, I’ve been thinking about it a lot. I’ve always wanted to visit Tokyo. I mean, the culture, the food, the tech—it’s just everything I love in one place. That’s awesome. I’ve been planning to go there for a while too. I’ve been saving up for a trip to Tokyo next summer. I’ve heard the food there is out of this world. For sure. I’ve heard about the ramen and sushi, and I’ve seen some videos of the streets and the neon lights—it’s just next-level. Yeah, I’ve been researching a lot. I think I’m gonna take the train from London to Tokyo, maybe catch a flight to somewhere in the middle and then do some road trips. It’s gonna be intense, but I’m excited. I’m jealous. I’ve been thinking about the same thing, but I haven’t really got the money together yet. Maybe I can try and find some part-time work to save up. You should. I mean, if you’re going to be in university, you might as well make the most of it. Speaking of which, how’s your uni life going? It’s going well, but it’s been a bit stressful. I’m doing a degree in computer science, and it’s a lot more intense than I thought. Yeah, I can imagine. I’m doing a similar degree, but I’m in a different field. I’m studying environmental science, which is a bit of a different vibe. Oh, that’s cool. I’ve always been into tech, but I’ve been curious about the environment stuff too.

So, do you remember that photo we took at Buckfast Abbey last summer? It was the one where I was holding that big white cross and you were trying to get the whole family in the shot. It’s still on my phone, but I can’t find it anymore. Oh, I still have it! I saved it to my Facebook album. It’s one of those moments where you think, “This is going to be a meme one day,” and then you’re like, “Wait, was I even in that photo?” You were in it, love. You were squinting like you were trying to read the sign. I remember you said something like, “What does ‘spend a day in the footsteps of the saints’ even mean?” I still don’t know what it means. I just wanted to take a photo with the religious stuff, like you do. You’re always posting those pictures of churches and cathedrals on your timeline. It’s like your personal pilgrimage. Well, I like to think of it as keeping up with the times, seeing the world, and not just sitting in the same old house all day. Although I did have a bit of a car trouble on the way back. The GPS said we were going east, but we were actually going west. I thought, “David Cameron would have known where we were going.” You know, I still remember when I was a young man, we’d go on these long trips in the car. No GPS, no mobile phones, just a map and a compass. Some of the best adventures came from getting lost. It was part of the journey. Yeah, but I don’t think I’m ready for that anymore. I still haven’t mastered the art of cooking without burning the toast. Let alone driving without getting pulled over. Although, speaking of pulling over, I found out that the insurance company is sending someone out to check the car. I’m dreading it. Oh, you don’t have to dread it. I did a Google search for “how to survive an insurance inspection” and it said something like, “Stay calm, do not argue, and maybe offer a coffee.” I think that’s the key. You know, I’ve had more insurance inspections than you’ve had cups of tea in your lifetime. You just have to remember, they’re not there to find faults.

So, I just had to tell you about the time I tried to use the sat nav in Belgium. I thought it was going to be easy, you know, like everywhere else. But no, it was like trying to read the mind of a frightened cat.      Sounds like the same thing that happened to me when I tried to drive in France with a sat nav. It told me to take a route that went through a village that didn’t exist, and I ended up in a field with a cow staring at me.      Oh, I had even worse. I was trying to get to the market in Brussels, and the sat nav said to take a turn that didn’t exist. I turned anyway, and I ended up driving through a residential area, past a few houses, and then came to a dead end. I had to reverse back and ask someone for directions.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? The sat navs in Europe are not like the ones we have back home. They don’t know the roads properly, or maybe they do, but they just don’t tell you the real way. I ended up in a tiny village called... something like... Beaulieu? I think that’s what it was. And I couldn’t find my way back, so I had to ask a local.      You don’t say. I remember the time I tried to cycle in Belgium too. I thought it’d be easy, but the cycle lanes are all over the place, and they don’t have the same rules as we do. I got pulled over by a police officer about five times, and he kept telling me to ride on the right side of the road.      I think I got pulled over too. I was riding on the left side like I was used to, and the cop just said, “You’re going the wrong way.” I was so confused. I thought that was how it was done there!      Oh, and the food? I thought I was going to love the chocolate, but it was way too sweet for me. And the waffles? They were so good, but I couldn’t eat more than one because they made me feel sick.      I had the most amazing chocolate croissants. I had to stop and buy a whole box just to take back home with me.

I just thought I'd try making this new recipe I found online. It's a herby chicken dish with some roasted vegetables and a drizzle of balsamic glaze. I think it’ll be nice with a little bit of garlic and rosemary. Sounds good. I love a good roast. I’ve been thinking about trying to make some pesto lately. Maybe we could try that with the chicken? Or maybe just have it on toast? It’s a bit of a comfort food for me. Pesto’s a great idea. I’ve been craving it, too. But I’ve been getting into more complex recipes lately, just to switch things up. Though I have to say, sometimes simplicity is better. My mum always said that cooking should be about joy, not stress. I couldn’t agree more. It’s funny, though – I sometimes feel like I’m not really cooking if I’m not using a bit of flair. But then again, I’ve been thinking about how different accents can influence how you even think about food. I mean, I grew up in Edinburgh, and there’s something about the way people talk about their local cuisine that really shapes your palate. Oh, that’s true. I’ve noticed how people in different parts of England have such distinct ways of talking – even about food. I remember growing up in Kent, and there was this local thing about “proper” tea, like you couldn’t just have it any old way. It made me curious about how food is tied to identity. Exactly. And it’s not just food. I think it’s the way people live, the way they speak, even the way they carry themselves. You know, I’ve been trying to work on my accent a bit, trying to sound more “south-eastern” or whatever. It’s funny because I know I have an Edinburgh accent, but sometimes I feel like I’m not really part of the “mainstream” anymore. I can see that. It’s something I’ve thought about too, especially when I work with people from different regions. There’s a kind of pride in how you speak, but also a bit of self-consciousness. I mean, I’ve been known to say “bath” instead of “bat” by mistake, and it always makes me blush. Oh, I’ve done that, too! I think we’re both just trying to fit in, even though we’re both from the same country.

So, do you know much about Australia? I've been thinking about visiting down under for a while now. Oh, I’ve been there a few times! I used to work in business, and we had some clients in Brisbane. It's a very different country, though. The way people dress, for instance—business men over there wear very smart suits, even in the summer. It's a bit of a shock if you're used to more casual styles back home. I know what you mean. My brother was living in Brisbane for a few years, and he told me how strict the dress code is. Still, I’ve always been curious about Australia. I’ve only been to Queensland once, and it’s a beautiful place. The beaches are amazing. Yes, I’ve heard so much about the beaches in Queensland. I’ve even thought about moving there, just for a while. But then again, I’ve got family here in Bristol, and it’s not easy to leave. I can see that. I was born and raised in Manchester, and even though I’ve travelled quite a bit, I can never quite get used to the idea of moving away from home. Though, I must say, I’ve always appreciated the Sheffield dialect. It has a certain character to it. Oh, I hear you! I’ve lived in Sheffield for most of my life, and I still get a kick out of hearing the local dialect. There’s something about the way people speak there—so distinct. It’s a bit of a language in itself, really. That’s true. I’ve noticed that when I visit, people are always so friendly and talk so fast. It’s like they’re trying to fit all their thoughts into one sentence! Exactly! I think it's part of the charm, though. The way they say ‘’’brolly’’’ instead of ‘umbrella’ or ‘’’chips’’’ instead of ‘crisps’—it all adds to the atmosphere. You know, I once taught English as a foreign language in South Korea, and I remember the way the students would try to mimic the Sheffield accent. It was hilarious! That sounds like a lot of fun. I’ve always had an interest in teaching, but I never thought I’d be teaching English overseas. Well, I suppose if you’re lucky enough to get a job with a good employer, it’s a chance to see the world and learn something new.

So, do you ever find it hard to stay off social media? I mean, I know it's everywhere, but sometimes I feel like I’m just scrolling for hours and I don’t even remember what I did. Honestly, I’ve tried to cut back a bit. I used to be on it all the time—Instagram, TikTok, you name it. But now I’m more into podcasts and watching some TV shows from the UK or the US. I find it much easier to focus on one thing instead of getting distracted by endless notifications. That’s a good point. I think I need to try that more. I’ve been trying to read more, but the thing is, when I get home from work, I just fall into my phone. It’s like a habit now. Yeah, I feel you. I think it’s just about setting boundaries. Like, if I’m going to watch a show, I tell myself I’ll only do it for an hour and then I’ll stop. But honestly, I end up watching three hours. And then I feel guilty about it. Oh, I know that feeling. I try to be disciplined, but once I start, I can’t stop. It’s like watching a binge. But I also think it’s funny how much of our lives we spend on screens. I mean, we’re supposed to be connecting with people, but often we’re just scrolling through their lives instead. That’s exactly it. I think people get so caught up in what others are doing that they forget to actually live their own lives. But then again, I have a podcast I listen to every morning. It’s called  The History of Everything  and it’s amazing. I’ve learned so much about the Renaissance just from that one episode. Oh, I’ve heard of that! I should check it out. Maybe I’ll start with that. I’ve been trying to get back into history, actually. I used to love it in school, but now I just don’t have the time. That’s a great idea. I think if you start with something you’re interested in, it’s easier to keep going. I also love some of the YouTube channels that explain things in a way that’s easy to understand. It’s like learning without even realizing you’re studying.

Alright, Pippy, you ready for your Blue Peter badge? I think we need to get that photograph done soon. I’m ready! I’ve been practicing my smile for ages. I mean, it’s not like I can do anything else, right? You could make a better face if you tried, Pippy. It’s not that hard. You just have to smile like you’re excited about something. Yeah, I know, but you’re only five. It’s not like you can do a full-blown smile like the grown-ups. Though I do think you have a nice smile. I do! I think I’m going to be the youngest Blue Peter badge holder ever. Just you wait and see. Well, you’ll have to wait until you’re six, and I think the badge is for six-year-olds, aren’t they? Maybe they do it at seven. I’m not sure. But the point is, we need to get you to the photographer. And I think we should do it before the Travelling Circus comes, otherwise we’ll be too busy. Right, that’s a good point. ANON said the circus is coming to Comberton next week. I’d love to take the kids to see it. But first, we need to get that photo done. Can we take the dog? I think the dog would like to see the circus too. Well, that depends. If we take the dog, we might have to take him to the circus too. And I’d rather not have a dog running around with the kids. Although, I suppose it’s worth a try. Or we could just take the dog for a swim instead. I hear the water’s really good this time of year. That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to take the dog for a swim for ages. And with the weather getting warmer, it’s the perfect time. I like swimming. I can float on my back. It’s like being in a big bath. Yeah, I think I can float too. I just have to close my eyes and think about the sea. That’s the way to do it, Pippy. Think about the sea and you’ll be floating in no time. Although, maybe we can start with the pool and work our way up to the sea. I think I’m ready to go to the sea.

I just want to talk about something, you know, personal. Like, I've been reading a bit about erectile dysfunction, and I’m just… a bit confused. Not sure if I’m going through it or not. Hmm, okay… I mean, I’ve heard about it, but I guess I never really thought about it before. Is it something that just… happens with age? I don’t know, I guess age plays a part, but I’m only 22. I mean, I haven’t had any issues before, but I’ve heard people say it’s more common than you think. I just don’t want to be worrying about it too much, you know? Yeah, I guess it’s something that a lot of people deal with. But I’m not sure how to even start talking about it. Like, should I mention it to someone? Or is it better to just… not think about it? I don’t know. I feel like it’s one of those things that’s a bit taboo. Like, you don’t want to bring it up, but if you’re struggling, you might need to. Like, maybe it’s not just about age, maybe there’s something else going on. Stress, lifestyle, diet, all that. Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I mean, I’ve been studying a lot, and I haven’t been sleeping well. Maybe that’s contributing? I don’t know. It’s just… hard to talk about. I know, it’s not something people really discuss. But I think it’s important to know the facts. Like, if you’re experiencing problems, it’s not a sign of weakness. It’s just a health issue, like anything else. I guess. But I feel like it’s easier to just… ignore it. Like, maybe I’ll just figure it out on my own. Or maybe I’ll just keep thinking about it and it’ll go away. I don’t know. I get that. But I think if you’re really concerned, it might be worth talking to a doctor or someone who knows. Like, maybe your GP? I mean, I know it’s a bit awkward, but it’s better to be safe than sorry. Yeah, I guess so. I mean, I’d rather not think about it too much, but I don’t want to be in denial either.

So, do you know what’s the deal with these free food boxes from Slimming World? I’ve been getting one every week and it’s honestly a bit too much. I can’t even eat all of it before it goes bad. I know, I swear, I tried to make a meal out of the cauliflower cheese last week, but it just didn’t taste right. I think I overcooked it. Yeah, that’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s all so healthy, but it’s like, how do you even make it taste good? I mean, I’ve had the roast chicken with the quorn, and it was okay, but I still feel like I’m missing out on the real thing. Yeah, and then there’s this 0-calorie syrup they recommend. I’ve been trying to use it in my tea, but honestly, it just tastes like nothing. I almost feel like I’m being tricked. I know! I told my sister about it and she was like, “You’re paying for nothing!” But she’s a gym teacher, so she doesn’t get it. Anyway, I was thinking about Saturday. We need to have our treat day. I’m planning on getting some pizza from the takeaway. Should I get the veggie one or the regular? Definitely the regular. You know what they say—once you go veggie, you can’t go back. Plus, someone has to enjoy the cheese. Fair point. I’ll definitely get the regular. Also, I was thinking about buying a bottle of frylight. I’ve heard it’s good for frying without oil. I tried it once, and it was fine. But I still can’t get over how much it costs. I mean, it’s not even real oil. I know, it’s like paying for a brand name. But maybe it’s worth it for the health benefits. Although, I still can’t believe that Quorn is considered a meat substitute. Yeah, it’s just weird. I mean, I’ve been eating it for a while, but sometimes I still feel like it’s not the same as actual meat. But I guess it’s better than meat that’s full of preservatives. Exactly. Speaking of food, I’ve been getting these veg boxes. It’s supposed to save money, but honestly, it’s just a bit expensive.

I've been thinking a lot about our holiday plans. I really want to go somewhere that's not too touristy, you know? Just somewhere we can relax and not have to worry about crowds or overpriced souvenirs. I agree. I’ve been wanting to go somewhere with good hiking trails and maybe some local culture. I heard somewhere in the Lake District is really nice this time of year. Quiet, peaceful, not too busy. That does sound nice. I’ve always wanted to visit the Lake District. It’s so picturesque. But I also think about the kids. Do you think they’d enjoy it? Or would they rather be somewhere with more activities? Honestly, I think they’d like it. The kids love being outside and exploring. Plus, there are plenty of places to walk with them, and I think it would be a good chance for us to just be together without the distractions of daily life. Yeah, I like that idea. It would be a nice break, you know? I’ve been working so much lately, and I feel like I haven’t had a real holiday in ages. I think I need some time to just reflect and recharge. I completely get that. I’ve been feeling the same way. But I also want to make sure we don’t go somewhere too remote. I mean, we have to be able to access basic amenities, and I don’t want to end up stranded somewhere with no signal. True. I think we should plan a place that’s a few hours from the city but still has some kind of connection to the outside world. Maybe somewhere with a small town nearby so we can grab groceries or something if needed. That makes sense. I was also thinking about something else—what if we go somewhere and then decide we don’t like it? I mean, we could end up wasting money and time. How do you feel about that? I’m not sure. I think it’s a risk, but I think we can mitigate it by doing some research beforehand. We could look into reviews and maybe even check out a short trip first to see if we like the area. Yeah, that sounds like a good idea. I like the idea of a short exploratory trip before committing to a full holiday. It gives us a chance to see if the place is right for us.

Well, I've just got a postcard from Scotland, you know. From the Highlands, actually. The weather’s been pretty wild there, but the views are still breathtaking. I can't wait to see the pictures when I get home. That sounds lovely. I remember you talking about wanting to visit there for the holidays. I suppose the independence issue must be on everyone’s mind these days, especially with the recent elections. Oh, it’s a tricky one, isn't it? I think the people there have a lot to consider. But I don’t think it’s the right time for a vote just yet. The economy’s still a bit shaky, and the transition would be complicated. I agree. I mean, I’m not sure what’s going to happen in the next few years. But I do hope they find a way to keep things stable. It’s a big decision for a whole country, you know. Definitely. I suppose it’s not just about politics—it's about identity, too. People want to feel connected to their roots, but I think the UK has done a lot for Scotland over the years. I don’t want to see that broken down. I think there's a lot of love for Scotland, both in the UK and abroad. But the referendum was a big moment, and I think it really brought a lot of people’s opinions to the surface. Yes, and it's interesting to see how the conversation is still going on. I think it's a topic that won’t go away anytime soon. But maybe we should focus on something more positive for now. What about the birthday weekend next week? Oh, right! I was just thinking about that. I've got the decorations all set up, and I’ve booked the caterer. We should be fine. I've also talked to the kids about bringing their friends. It’s going to be a big guest list. That’s great. I’ve already sent out the invitations, and I’ve got a few surprises planned. I think your brother is coming from Manchester. I’ll make sure he gets here on time. Perfect. I’m also thinking about the music for the evening. I’ve got a few old favorites that people go crazy for. It’ll be a real celebration. Sounds like a solid plan.

Alright, do you two want to go and draw a chair for the Syrian refugees? I think it’s a really good idea to show some support. A chair? Like, you know, a physical chair? Yeah, like the kind you sit on? Exactly! I saw this campaign online where people are drawing chairs to symbolize the need for more shelter and support for refugees. It’s a really simple way to show solidarity. Oh, I get it. Like, each chair represents a person who needs a safe place to sit, or a place to live? That’s the idea. It’s not about the chair itself, but what it stands for. It’s a visual reminder that these people are just like us—human, with needs, and who deserve dignity. That’s really touching. I mean, it’s not like we’re doing anything too big, right? Just drawing a chair. Exactly, and it’s something we can all do. I think the school is doing a similar project, so maybe we could do it together. It’d be good for the kids to get involved. Do you think the school would like that? I mean, the kids have tests coming up. I don’t want them to be stressed. I think it would be a good way to teach them about empathy and global issues. I just got a message from Lucy. She’s been trying to get in touch with me for days. She says she’s in a bit of a panic about her baby’s first vaccinations. Oh no, is everything okay? You know, I just thought of something. When we were at university, we had this lecturer who always said that if you ever saw a policeman with a dog, you should run. Or when you see a group of people trying to act like they’re not looking at you, but they’re definitely checking you out.

So, do you two remember that time we tried to play that 80s rock band album on the car audio system and it completely blew the speakers? It was chaos. Oh, I remember that! So, I just wanted to say, I think the way we drive here is completely different from when I was a kid. I mean, no one ever used to park properly, and now it’s just chaos! So, do you think we should go vegetarian? I mean, I’ve been thinking about it more since I started reading about the environmental impact of meat production. Honestly, I've been there. That’s a big one. I’ve also been thinking about synthetic meat. I mean, it’s not perfect, but if it’s lab-grown, maybe it’s a step in the right direction, right? I’ve heard about it, but I’m not sure if it’s actually better than just eating plant-based foods. I mean, there’s still a lot of ethical concerns about the process and the companies involved. Maybe something like shmeat, like the ones they’re making in the US? Yeah, I remember reading about that. It’s kind of like a lab-grown version of real meat. But I don’t know, it still feels a bit like a gimmick. Like, are we just trying to justify eating animals in a new way? That’s a good point. I guess that’s part of the transition. Yeah, I’ve been reading about that too. It’s not as simple as just switching from meat to veggies. You have to be careful with your intake, especially with things like B12. That’s something I didn’t think about. I mean, I’m not a huge fan of pills, but I guess it’s part of the package.

Well, it’s a lovely day today, isn't it? Not too cold, just right for a bit of a walk or a chat. Yes, I agree. I've been thinking about the old days, you know, when we used to go trick or treating around the village. Do you remember how it used to be, Bob? Oh, I remember well! Everyone used to dress up and go from house to house, and the kids would have so much fun. It was a time of year when the whole village was full of excitement. Didn’t you get into some sort of trouble once? Oh, I remember that. I used to dress up as a pirate and get chased by my cousin’s dog. I was so scared, I nearly dropped my bottle of rum. Oh, that was the year you turned nine. You were always the most daring one of us. I still remember how your mother had to chase you down for hours after that. You were always the adventure seeker, weren’t you? I think I still have a costume I made when I was seven, though it was more like a hat with a paper crown.
