But I did enjoy the chocolate. I still remember the taste of that sticky, sweet candy. It was always my favorite part. Oh, I can still smell the smell of the lanterns and the bonfires. It was like the whole village was celebrating together. You know, it made me think about how different things are now. With all the gadgets and everything, it’s not the same. I know. I think it’s a shame that Halloween has become more about the commercial side of it rather than the tradition. I miss the way it used to be. I think it’s a bit of both, though. The kids still enjoy the candy, and the decorations are nice. It’s just different. Speaking of different, have you ever thought about going horse-riding? I’ve heard it’s quite a popular thing in the countryside. It’s something I’ve always wanted to try. Oh, I’ve tried it once, actually. It was at a local riding school.

I can't believe we've been stuck in traffic for over an hour. I thought it would be easier to get here from the M25 with the weekend rush over. I mean, it's the Steam Fair, everyone is excited, but honestly, this is ridiculous. I know, I know. I’ve been here before, and it’s always the same. The council seems to think that just because it’s a ‘heritage event’ or whatever, they don’t have to actually plan for the traffic. Honestly, it’s like they’re doing it on purpose to chase people out of the area. You'd think they’d at least provide some proper parking spaces. I heard they’re trying to add more disabled parking this year, but I’m not sure if it’s going to be enough. I know a few people who use mobility scooters or have mobility issues—like my mum, actually. She’s been asking about accessible routes and parking for ages. They need to be more proactive about that, not just slap a few spaces on the side of the road and call it a day. Yeah, and it’s not just about disabled people. There are quite a few elderly folks who come to the fair too. I’ve seen a couple of my grandparents trying to get around without much help. It’s just frustrating when you’re planning to go and then you’re stuck in traffic for hours, and then you have to fight for a parking spot. It all adds up. I remember when I was younger, there were more houses with gardens and real space. Now, it’s all about high-rises and cramped flats. I think the government’s got a lot to answer for when it comes to housing. I mean, even if you’re not disabled, the lack of space makes it hard to live a normal life. You can’t even park your car in front of your own house anymore in some places. I know, it’s been tough for people like me. I live in a semi-detached house, but it’s not really semi-detached anymore. The council did a ‘regeneration’ project that meant knocking down a few houses and building flats. I lost my garden, and I’m not even sure if I’m going to get it back. I mean, I can go out and get some fresh air, but not really like I used to.

So, do you think we should go for the one near the river or the one on the edge of the woods? I was looking at the map again this morning, and both seem pretty good. Hmm, well, I think the one near the river would be easier to access, especially if we want to water the plants regularly. Plus, the soil there seems to be better for growing vegetables. But I do love the idea of having some trees around for shade. Yeah, I can see the benefits of the river one. But I also like the idea of the woodland area—it might be more peaceful, and the natural cover could make it feel more like a hidden garden. Although, I suppose we would have to worry more about animals getting in. That’s true. Maybe we could put up some fencing or build a simple wooden fence. I’ve seen some people use bamboo stakes and wire to keep out rabbits and other small pests. It’s not too expensive, and it’s relatively easy to do. That’s a good idea. I’ve actually been thinking about getting some raised beds too, just to make it easier on my knees. I don’t want to end up with back pain after a few months of digging in the soil. Oh, I completely understand. I’ve heard about raised beds being a great solution for people with mobility issues or those who just want to make gardening more comfortable. Maybe we could use some old wood from the barn at the weekend, and build a couple of them in the corner of the plot. That sounds like a solid plan. I was also thinking about planting some native flowers and herbs around the edges to attract pollinators. It would be good for the environment and also add some color to the area. I love that idea. Bees and butterflies are so important, and they help with pollination. We could even set up a small bird feeder nearby if we wanted to encourage some birds to nest in the area. Yeah, that would be nice. I think we should also consider getting some compost bins to recycle our kitchen scraps. It’s a sustainable way to keep the soil healthy and reduce waste. Absolutely. I think once we get the plot sorted, we’ll be able to go out there every weekend and enjoy the process.

So, do you know what’s up with Lucy? I haven’t seen her in ages, and it’s like she’s just disappeared off the face of the Earth. Yeah, I know, she’s been really quiet lately. I think we should try to catch up with her and see how she’s doing. That sounds like a good idea. I’ll message her and see if she’s available. I think it would be nice to have her back in the loop, even if it’s just for a bit. Yeah, and maybe we could take her out for a drink or something.

So, do you play any games? I’ve been trying to get into the new FIFA, but it’s like a whole other language to me. I’ve got FIFA on my phone, but I just play it when I’m waiting for the bus. It’s not like the console version. I’ve got the PS5 version. It’s amazing. I’ve been trying to get a good squad together, but I keep getting stuck on the transfer market. Yeah, that’s always the worst part. I once tried to chase a player and ended up paying more than I had in my whole account. Oh no! That’s not fun. I’ve had that happen before, but I didn’t know it was a thing. I think the game is just designed to make you spend money. It’s like a giant money trap. I know, but it’s so addictive. I’ll just play for an hour and then I’m like, “Oh, I should check my inbox.” Then I’m in for another hour. Exactly. I think I’ve lost more time to games than I’ve ever spent on actual work. I can relate. I’ve got a backlog of assignments, but I’m always thinking, “Just one more level.” I’m telling you, if you’re not careful, you’ll end up playing games instead of studying. I’ve seen someone at the uni who’s basically a walking FPS simulator. I think it’s just the way our brains are wired. It’s like a reward system. You get a bit of dopamine every time you win a match or get a gold. I think I’m starting to see that. I’ve been trying to fix my time management, but every time I step away from my computer, I just feel like I’m missing out on something. You know, I was thinking about the last time I tried to play a game with someone. We ended up arguing about who got the better character. That’s the worst. I’ve had that happen with my mates too. We were playing this RPG, and we couldn’t even agree on which map to go to. I had a friend once who got so into a game that he started talking about it in class. He was like, “I’m going to build this empire, it’s going to be the best in the game.”

I just watched this new film on Netflix called  The Last Tree —you know, the one with that old actor from  The Forsyte Saga ? It was absolutely  shocking . Oh, I’ve heard about that one. I didn’t get round to watching it yet. Why was it shocking? Well, it starts off with this beautiful forest, all green and vibrant. You think it’s going to be this peaceful, eco-friendly kind of story. But then— poof —the whole thing turns into a horror film. Trees are getting hacked down, people are screaming, and the soundtrack is just  trumpets . I couldn’t believe it. Wow, that’s a strange twist. I guess they were trying to make a point about deforestation? Exactly! And I think the director is trying to make a statement about how we’re destroying nature. But honestly, it felt more like a  thriller  than a documentary. And the ending—it was just so…  sad . There was one scene where a child was holding a tree stump, and it made me cry. That sounds quite intense. Did you watch it with someone, or were you alone? I watched it on my own. I had a bottle of wine, and I just sat there in my pyjamas, feeling all emotional. But you know what? It got me thinking about my old friend, Mary. She used to live in the countryside, and she always used to say that trees were like people. She believed every tree had a soul. That’s a lovely way to look at it. I’ve always thought that nature has a way of making you feel smaller. It’s humbling, in a way. Yeah, that’s true. I remember when we were kids, we used to climb trees in my old garden. I used to think I’d be the first one to reach the top. But my brother, he was just…  there . He used to laugh at me, waiting till I was halfway up before he climbed after me. He always said, “You’ll never be a tree climber, you’ll always be a tree  hugger .” Oh, that’s such a funny line. I bet you still think about it every time you’re in the woods. Oh, I do. And I can’t help but wonder what he’d say if he saw how much the woods have changed. I mean, even the trees are different now.

So, do you remember that board game we tried to play last week? The one with the weird rules and the minigames? I swear it was like playing a computer game in real life. Oh, don’t even get me started. I was so confused by the turn order. I think I accidentally knocked over the whole board and then got blamed for it. It was basically a conspiracy. Haha, I think that’s the point though. The whole idea is to make it chaotic and unpredictable. Like, you never know if you’re going to win or end up in a prison cell. Exactly. I mean, I still don’t know the rules, and I’ve played it like three times. I should have asked for a cheat sheet or something. But no, I figured I’d just wing it. You’re not the only one. I’ve been trying to remember if I’ve ever actually won a game. I think I only won once, and that was by accident. I think the dice landed on my favor, not my strategy. You know, maybe it’s better to just play something simple. Like, a classic like Monopoly or Scrabble. No fancy rules, just good old-fashioned fun. Yeah, but I think the point of board games now is to be complicated. It’s like trying to outsmart the game itself. I mean, what’s the point of a game if you don’t have to think? I think it’s also about social interaction. Like, the more confusing the game, the more you have to talk to your friends and try to figure things out together. It’s like a team-building exercise. I guess that does make sense. I just wish the rules weren’t so convoluted. I mean, I was trying to remember if it was a ‘team’ game or an ‘individual’ game. I ended up playing against myself. That sounds like a whole new level of chaos. I mean, I tried that once, and I ended up in a loop of trying to win against myself. It was like trying to catch your own shadow. I think I need to set some boundaries. Maybe I should just play the games that are straightforward. I need to find something that doesn’t make me feel like I’m in a language barrier, even with my own friends.

I can't believe the washing machine still hasn't finished. It's been ages since I put the clothes in. Yeah, I was just thinking the same thing. I've been waiting for it to finish so I can get my jeans out. I swear it’s been running for over an hour now. I’m starting to think it’s broken. Maybe it’s just taking longer because of the load? I saw this film last night about a chef who started a food truck. It was really inspiring. Oh, what was the name of it? I think it was  Street Chef  or something like that. Anyway, it was about people who have a passion for food and how they started from nothing. That sounds interesting. I might have to watch it.

I just can’t believe how much the house prices have gone up since I retired. I mean, I thought I’d be able to sell my old place in Dublin and find something reasonable in the North, but it's like trying to hit a moving target. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about moving too. I’ve been working from home for a while now as a transcriber and editor, so I don’t need to be anywhere specific. But even so, the prices in the South are just crazy. I was looking at some houses in Bristol the other day, and they were asking for like three times what I make in a month. That’s not even fair. I mean, what’s the point of living in the South if you can’t afford a house? I still remember when I was in the oil industry, we had this guy who used to say, “If you can afford a house in London, you can afford anything.” But now I’m not even sure that’s true anymore. Exactly! And it’s not just the South—prices in places like Manchester and Liverpool have gone up too. I mean, we’re not even in the North anymore. We’re in Hunsonby, which is kind of a nowhere place, and yet the prices are still higher than what I could get in Dublin, and I had a decent salary there. It’s so frustrating. I think it’s partly because of the VW scandal. I mean, the whole country’s been in a bit of a slump. People are more cautious with their money, but the banks are still pushing houses like they’re selling ice cream. It’s like they don’t care about the people anymore. I hear you. I remember the scandal really well. I had a friend who used to work at a dealership, and he told me how it all started. It was like the whole company was just cutting corners. And now, after all that, people are just more suspicious of the whole system. But you know what? Even with that, house prices haven’t gone down. It’s just gotten more expensive to live in a place where you can actually breathe. That’s the thing. I think people are just getting more desperate. They want to get out of the cities, get back to the countryside or something.

I don’t know, I just feel like I’ve been dragged down by the whole pension system, you know. It’s like they don’t care about us old folk anymore. I mean, I’ve got a decent pension, but it’s not enough to live on, and I’m not even sure how much of it I’ll actually get. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been on a pension for ten years now, and I still feel like I’m barely scraping by. It’s not like we’re asking for gold, just a few quid more to cover the basics. I hear you both. I’ve been running a childminding business for years, and when I retired, I thought I’d be fine. But with the cost of living going up and the government not giving a toss, I’m barely making ends meet. I had to take in a couple of more kids just to cover the bills. That’s not fair. I mean, we all worked hard our lives, and now we’re just being left in the lurch. I was a civil engineer for over thirty years, and I still feel like I’m not getting the respect or the support I deserve. It’s like the government’s forgotten about us. And then there’s the housing issue. I know we’re supposed to be in our own homes, but with the cost of housing and the lack of support, it’s just not possible for us to stay in our own homes. We’re being pushed out by developers and the government doesn’t seem to care. I know exactly what you mean. I’ve been in the same house for over thirty years, and I still feel like I’m not in control of my own life. I used to run a childminding business, and I had a good income, but now that I’m retired, I’m just stuck in this cycle of not having enough money to do anything. I know what you mean. I used to work in engineering, and I always thought I’d be in a better position when I retired. But the truth is, I’m just as stuck as you are. I’ve been living on a pension for years, and I still feel like I’m not getting the support I need.

So, do you guys remember that video of the guy who tried to talk to a spider like it was a human? It went viral, right? Oh yeah! That was so weird. I watched it like 10 times. He was like, "Hey, Spider, how’s your day going?" And the spider just stared at him. It was like a comedy sketch. I mean, it was kind of funny, but also kind of creepy. Like, what if the spider actually understood him? Would it be like, "Oh no, you're not cool" and then bite him? That would make sense. I mean, spiders are the real MVPs. They’re like the ultimate survivors. You can’t even see them, and they’re everywhere. They’ve been around for millions of years, and humans are just… here. Yeah, but wait, what if we’re just the same? Like, if we had six legs, and lived in the dirt, and we were the ones looking down at the insects? What if we were the creepy ones? That’s dark. But maybe that’s why we’re not as evolved as spiders. I mean, look at them—no need for phones, no need for social media. They just do their thing and live. Maybe that’s the key to survival. I don’t know. It’s not like we’re not trying. Like, we’re doing biology now, right? We’re learning about evolution, and how species adapt. Like, if a spider had a language, or a culture, would we even know? Exactly! And what if spiders  do  have culture? Like, maybe they have their own social hierarchies, or the way they spin webs is like a language. We just don’t understand it. Wait, but what about that video with the spider that made the web in a certain pattern? I think it was supposed to be a message. Or a warning. Like, "Don’t mess with me." That’s probably just a myth. Though, honestly, if that’s true, we need to start respecting spiders more. They’re like the unsung heroes of the ecosystem. Yeah, and go back to the topic of evolution. I mean, if we’re evolved, why are we still so into stuff like social media and fashion? Like, why are we trying to be something we’re not? That’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s like we’re obsessed with looking cool, but in the end, we’re just… mammals.

So, how’s the new car coming along? I heard you were thinking about getting an MOT and new tyres. Oh, it’s been a bit of a struggle, honestly. Oh, you were a skier? That’s amazing. I’ve never been able to get the hang of it. I always end up falling over. It’s not for everyone, I guess. I tried once, and I completely lost it on the slopes. I ended up with a black eye and a bruised knee. I think I’d rather just sit in a chair and read a book.

Alright, so I was just thinking about what we were talking about earlier—slavery and war. It's like... it's so hard to wrap your head around how people could do that to each other. I mean, it's not just history anymore, is it? It's still happening in some places, isn’t it? Yeah, I know. I remember reading something about a place in Africa a while back where people were still being forced into this kind of thing. It’s just so sad. I don’t even know how to explain it to my friends. They just don’t get it. I don’t get it either. I mean, why would people do that? If you’re like, working, or even if you’re not, why would you be treated like that? It doesn’t make sense. I think it’s about power, you know? Like, when one group has more power than another, they can just take advantage of them. It’s not just about money, it’s about control. And then, once it becomes normal, people stop seeing it as wrong. Yeah, I guess that’s part of it. Like, when people are used to seeing injustice, they don’t even notice it anymore. It becomes just… the way things are. But isn’t that just wrong? I mean, even if you don’t know it’s wrong, it’s still wrong, right? Exactly. And that’s why it’s so important to talk about it. To teach kids, to make sure they understand what happened and what’s still happening. Because if we don’t, it could happen again. I guess that’s why we’re talking about it now. We’re trying to understand it. Maybe that’s part of learning, you know? To see the bigger picture. I don’t know. Sometimes it feels like history is just something that happened to other people. Not to us. But maybe it’s not that far away. That’s true. War and slavery are linked, too. You know, people get pushed into slavery because of war. Some soldiers, some people who are forced to take sides, or just the poor who can’t afford to survive. It’s like a cycle. Yeah, and it’s not just in the past either. There’s still conflicts all over the world where people are being treated like that.

I’ve been too busy with work, and honestly, I’ve been thinking about my holiday. I need to take a break, you know. I’ve been working non-stop since January. Alright, do you two want to help me unload the dishwasher? I’ve been trying to get it done for like an hour and I’m not making much progress. Can I? Yeah, I can help too! Great, then. So, do you know what’s up with Words With Friends? I’ve been trying to get back into it, but every time I log in, it’s like the game’s been updated or something. It’s not even the same board anymore. Ugh, I can't believe we’re still paying full rent for this flat. It's been months and we're still not sorted. So, do you remember how we used to spend Christmas when we were kids? It was always such a big deal, wasn’t it? Oh, absolutely. I remember we’d all gather at my parents’ place, and we’d have the biggest Christmas dinner you could imagine. My mum was the queen of the feast—she’d make everything from scratch, and the house would be full of the smell of roasted turkey and freshly baked mince pies. Yeah, and you used to get so excited about it. You’d start planning weeks in advance. Didn’t you once get the whole family together to decide the menu? Oh, I still remember that! We had a massive debate about whether to do the turkey or the chicken. I was so convinced it had to be the turkey, and my dad was all for the chicken. In the end, we compromised and did both. It was one of those days when everyone was so happy, even if we ended up with two huge roasting trays in the oven. I can still picture the table. You’d have all your aunts and uncles, cousins, and even the occasional distant relative who showed up unannounced. It was chaos, but in the best way. Exactly! And then there was the tradition of the Christmas tree. I remember we’d have that one tree in the living room, and my brother would always try to climb it and knock it over. My mum would chase after him with a broom, and we’d all laugh like it was the most natural thing in the world. Oh, and the presents! You used to have this rule where no one could open any presents until after midnight. We’d all sit around the tree, counting down the hours, and my dad would have this ridiculous habit of pretending he was about to fall asleep. He did! And he’d do it every year. I think it was his way of making sure we all stayed up until the last possible minute. I miss those days. I do too. It’s funny how the traditions we had growing up are the things we still hold onto, even now. I’ve tried to do something similar with my own kids—though they’re not too interested in the tree or the turkey. They’d rather watch Christmas movies and eat chocolate.

Dad, it’s been two years since I’ve seen you. How’s everything going? Oh, it’s been a bit of a whirlwind. I’ve had to deal with a lot of changes in the area. I’ve had to think twice about how I drive now. And then there’s the license – I had to renew it, and it was a bit of a hassle. But I suppose it’s just part of growing older. I’ve been trying to get back into board games too. I’ve been playing a lot of  Risk  with some friends, and it’s gotten me thinking about old times. That’s a good way to pass the time. I remember when we used to play  Monopoly  all the time. It’s amazing how life changes. Yeah, I know. I’m trying to keep up with everything, but sometimes I feel like I’m losing track.

I can't believe we've walked all the way from the university to here without seeing a single tree. It's like the whole city's been built around this smog. Yeah, I know. It's ridiculous. I mean, we're in China, of course it's polluted, but even so, it feels like every street we walk down, there's just this constant haze. I remember when we first came here, the air was so clear, and the sky was so blue. Now it's like breathing in a cloud of exhaust and dust. I know. I feel like I'm constantly coughing, and I can't even open my windows because it's so bad. It’s like the city is trying to suffocate us. I tried to explain to my students the other day that air pollution in cities like this is a major health concern, but they just roll their eyes and say, “We know, it's everywhere.” It's not even that they don’t know — they just don’t care. That’s the thing, isn’t it? People get used to it. They don’t notice it anymore. You know, I used to think that as long as we had clean water and food, we'd be fine, but now I'm starting to see that it's not just about that. It’s not just about that. It's about how everything is connected. If the air is bad, the soil is bad, the food is bad — eventually, everything starts to affect you. I've been feeling more tired lately, and I think it's not just because of the workload. I’ve noticed that too. I've been waking up with headaches and feeling like I can't breathe properly, even when I'm indoors. I’ve started taking my mask with me everywhere. It's not even that I'm scared — it's just that I don't want to feel like I'm wasting my time living here. I get that. I think it's hard to adjust when you're used to a different kind of environment. I mean, we've both lived in cities before, but this is on another level. Yeah, and it's not just the pollution. It's the noise, the constant rush of people, the way everything's so crowded. I miss the quiet of the countryside, even if it wasn’t the most polluted place.

I can’t believe we’re actually doing this tonight. I thought we’d end up just eating takeout again like last week. I know, I was going to say the same thing. So, do you know about the new bus route they're planning to open next month? I heard it's supposed to connect the university with the city centre faster. Yeah, I think I read about it in the local paper. They’re trying to reduce congestion around the campus. But honestly, I’m not sure if it’ll make much of a difference. Have you ever read anything from there? Yeah, actually. I picked up a copy of  The Origins of the British Constitution  last year—it was a bit dry, but it was useful for my history module. I think I got it for half price though, which is lucky. That’s the thing. I was thinking the other day, maybe I should take a course or something. I mean, I’m not sure if I’m ready for a postgrad, but it’s about time I stopped just managing the corpus and started learning more myself. That’s a good idea. You’ve got the right attitude for it. I mean, I started as a consultant engineer, and I still feel like I’m learning something every day. It’s not always easy, but it keeps you on your toes. I guess I need to stop being so afraid of failure. I mean, what’s the point of working in a job that just involves spreadsheets if I’m not growing? Exactly. And if you do end up goin’ back to school, you’ll be in good company. I mean, I’ve got a few friends who are doing postgrads, and they all say it’s worth it in the long run.

So, do you think we should bring some of those truffle cakes from the café in Manchester? I know they’re a bit pricey, but they’re really worth it. I think they are, honestly. But I’m also thinking about the kids. You know how they can be with food. They might not even finish their portions if we bring something too fancy. Yeah, they’re a bit picky these days. But it’s nice to see the kids enjoying themselves, and I think it’ll be a good transition for them to get used to having someone else around. That’s true. I agree. And we can always talk about the food later. I mean, we’re not in a rush. Besides, it’s not every day we get to have a proper meal out. It’s a bit of a luxury. Definitely. But let’s not forget about the boyfriends. I think they’re going to be here this Saturday. We should make sure the place is ready. I mean, I know they’re not the most sophisticated, but we can’t let them feel out of place. Right. I’ll make sure to set the table nicely. And maybe I can bring some of my own dishes to mix things up a bit. You know, just to keep things interesting. That sounds like a good idea. I do love a bit of variety. But I’m not sure if I’ll be able to go out of my way to cook anything. I think I’ll just stick to the basics, you know, like a roast dinner or something.

I can't believe we've walked all this way from Woolwich. I thought it’d be a nice walk, but honestly, my legs are shot. I know, I've been telling you all week that we should’ve taken the bus. I mean, it's not like we're in a rush or anything. Well, you didn’t want to take the bus. You said it was too expensive, and we could just walk. Honestly, I’m not sure if I’ve ever walked this far in my life. I know, I know. But the view is worth it, right? Look at all these landmarks—those buildings, the bridges, the way the river flows. It’s like a postcard. Yeah, it is. But I’m still not sure about the O2 Arena. I mean, the way it stands there in the middle of the Thames, it doesn’t really fit. It’s like some giant alien spaceship in the middle of the city. You know, I think it was meant to be a symbol of something bigger—like progress, maybe? But I still don’t get it. Why not build it on the banks of the river, where it would actually make sense? I don’t know. Maybe it's just one of those things that people think is cool, but really, it doesn’t make much sense. It’s not like we can just go back and change it. True. But then again, sometimes people do things that don’t make sense just because they think they should. I remember talking about this with my sister a few weeks ago. She said that when you’re in your 40s, you start to question everything—philosophical questions, like, what’s the point of it all? Oh, I know. I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately. Like, what’s the point of working so hard just to pay rent and buy groceries? Where’s the meaning in it? I mean, I used to think there was, but now I’m not so sure. I get that. It’s like, we keep pushing forward, but do we even know where we’re going? I mean, I’m an administrator, and I can go through all these reports and manage people, but does it mean anything? I don’t know. I guess that’s the problem with modern life. It’s all so complicated.

So, I just got this really cute  Build a Bear  for the kids for their birthday. It’s a unicorn, and it’s so soft. I think it’s going to be the hit of the day.      Oh, I love those things. They’re so comforting. My mum always had one when she was a kid. I remember her saying that it was the only thing that made her feel safe when she was little.      Yeah, but I’m not sure about the kids. We’ve got the twins, and they’re already into  everything  – including the potty training. I swear, they’re like little superheroes with their little potty pants on.      Oh, I’m so sorry. I know how hard that can be, especially with twins. I mean, I used to think I was doing so well with my little brother, and then he started asking, “Why do I have to go potty?” in the middle of the grocery store.      Oh, I remember that. I had a friend who was trying to potty train her son, and he would always ask, “Is it time to go potty?” in the middle of a dinner party. Her husband just started saying, “No, we’re not going potty.” And then the kid laughed, and everyone started laughing too. It was the best thing ever.      That sounds like a classic family moment. I mean, I’m just trying to get the twins to remember to put their clothes on properly. One of them left a  Build a Bear  at the park the other day and came back in a tutu.      Oh, I’ve been trying to get my little brother interested in sports. He’s into swimming, though. We went to the local pool last week, and it was a  mess . The water was so cold, and he just kept screaming.      I remember when I was a kid, I was terrified of the pool. My dad used to say, “You’re not going to die in the water.” But I still thought I would.      That’s funny. I think that’s what my sister used to say to me when I was little. “You’re not going to die in the water.” But I still thought I would, even when I was 12.      I swear, I have a  Build a Bear  in every room now. Even in the kitchen. I was just making a cup of tea, and I almost knocked one over.

So, do you think we should start thinking about where we're going to live next? I mean, with everything that's going on with the business and the kids, it's time to plan properly. I was thinking about that too. I mean, we've been living in the same place for over ten years, and I think we're both ready for something new. But I’m not sure yet where. Do you have any ideas? And as we plan for the future, I think it’s important to keep the family aspect in mind too. We should talk about how we want the kids to grow up and the kind of environment we want them to be raised in. Agreed.

So, I just wanted to say, I think I’ve figured out why people in the North always sound like they’re from Manchester, even if they’re from Wigan or Warrington.      Oh yeah? What’s your theory?      It’s not just the accent, it’s the way we say things. Like, “I’ve just been to the shops,” or “I’m gonna have a pint.” It’s like we’ve got this built-in dialect that’s not just about where you’re from, but how you grew up.      I don’t know, I think it’s just because we’re all so close-knit, and we’ve got that Northern charm.      Yeah, but I’ve heard people from Leeds sound like they’re from Manchester too, and I’m from Leeds!      Maybe it’s the combination of the weather and the fact that we all have a bit of a “grit” about us.      Grit? That’s a bit harsh, but I get it. I mean, we’re not all the same, though. Like, I’ve got friends from Wigan, and they sound different from me. But then again, maybe it’s just the way we all grew up around the same kind of vibe—work, pubs, football, and a fair bit of flatulence.      Oh, I can’t argue with that. I mean, I’ve heard you talking and I thought, “Wait, she’s from Warrington, but she’s got a Liverpool accent!”      No, no, no! That’s not me. I have a proper Warrington accent.      She’s just trying to be posh.      I think the real issue is that people in the North just say things differently. Like, instead of “I’m gonna go to the shops,” we say, “I’m gonna go to the shop.” It’s subtle, but it makes a difference.      And also, we’re always trying to sound like we’re from somewhere else. I’ve heard people from Leeds trying to sound like they’re from Manchester, and it’s so obvious.      It’s like a regional identity thing. You can’t really escape it. Even if you move away, you still sound like you’re from the North. I’ve lived in London for three years, and I still get asked where I’m from.      Exactly! I’ve had people think I’m from Liverpool because I say “chips” instead of “crisps.”

Well, I've just had the most extraordinary weekend. You know that old saying, “If you don’t like the weather, wait five minutes.” Well, I think it was more like an hour. It started off fine, then it rained like a waterfall, and then it stopped, and the sun came out again. I swear, I felt like I was in a British weather documentary. Oh, I’ve been through that too. I think that’s just the way it is in Norfolk. One moment you’re sitting in the garden, and the next, you’re trying to get the kids inside before the sky opens up. I’ve even had to cancel a few birthdays because of the weather, and that’s not something you want to do. I remember when I was growing up in Norwich, the weather was always a topic of conversation. My mum would say, “Don’t you ever get tired of the same old British weather?” But I think it’s part of the charm, don’t you think? It gives you something to talk about every day. Absolutely. It’s like the weather here is a character in its own right. I mean, yesterday, it was so hot, I had to turn the thermostat down just to get to sleep. And then this morning, it was so cold, I had to wear a sweater just to walk to the post office. Yeah, and don’t get me started on the football. I watched the match last night, and it was the most ridiculous thing I’ve ever seen. One team had a man in red, and the other had a man in blue, and they just stood there for ten minutes, not even trying to play. I thought, “Is this about the weather too?” I mean, it was so cold, maybe they were trying to keep warm. I was watching the same match. The commentators were so confused. One of them said, “It’s like they’re trying to make a point.” I thought, “What point? That they’re all just trying to stay warm?” I mean, I’ve never seen a game like that. I think it’s just the way people act during the winter. It’s like, no one wants to get out of the house. I mean, I’ve been trying to get my kids to go to the park for ages, and they just say, “It’s too cold.”

So, do you think I should drop out of uni? I mean, I know it's not the best idea, but I feel like I’m just not getting anything out of it. I’m studying English, and honestly, I don’t feel like I’m learning anything useful. I mean, I’m not even sure I want to be a teacher or a writer. You know, I get that. I’ve been thinking about it too. I mean, I’m not even sure what I’m going to do after this. I’ve been stuck in the same lectures for months, and I just feel like I’m not growing. But, I also know that dropping out is a big decision. You don’t just walk away from it without thinking through all the consequences. Yeah, I know, but I feel like I’m not even enjoying the courses anymore. I mean, I used to love reading and writing, but now it just feels like I’m just doing it for the sake of it. I’m not getting any satisfaction, you know? I can totally relate. It’s like I’m just going through the motions. But, I guess I’m also nervous about what it would mean for my future. I mean, what if I drop out and then I don’t have a degree? What if I can’t find a job? I know it’s scary, but I also feel like I’m not making the most of my time here. I don’t know. I mean, I’ve always been the type to follow through with things. I never really thought about dropping out before. But lately, I’ve just been so frustrated. It’s like I’m stuck in this giant loop, and I can’t break free. I feel like I’m not even learning the skills I need to be successful. Yeah, that’s exactly how I feel. And I think part of it is just the pressure to succeed. I mean, everyone around me is so focused on their future, and I feel like I’m falling behind. But maybe I need to take a step back and figure out what I really want. I guess that’s the thing, right? It’s not just about the degree. It’s about what you want to do with your life. I mean, I’ve always loved being creative, but I’m not sure if that means I have to go to uni to do it.

I can't believe it's been almost two years since we last saw each other. Time flies, doesn't it? Yeah, it feels like forever. I’ve been so busy with work and trying to figure out what I want to do next, I’ve barely had time to catch up with anyone. I know what you mean. It’s been crazy with work too—switching roles, managing projects, all that. But I have to say, I’m enjoying it more now. It’s like I’ve finally found my groove. That’s great to hear. I’ve been feeling like I’m just going through the motions. I love my job at Pearson, but sometimes I wonder if I’m on the right path. I mean, I got my graduate degree, but I’m not sure if I want to stay in marketing forever. It’s totally normal to feel that way. I think everyone goes through that phase where you question whether you’re on the right track. But I’d say, if you love what you do, it’s worth sticking with. If not, it’s okay to pivot. I guess that’s what I’m trying to figure out. I’ve been thinking about taking some time off or maybe doing something different. But I don’t want to throw everything away. Plus, I’ve got a mortgage and all that. I know, it’s not easy. But you know what? I’m actually planning to take a break for a few months after this project finishes. I’ve been working non-stop, and I just need a change of scenery. Maybe travel? Or do something creative? That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to travel, but I never seem to have the time. Do you have any plans yet? Not yet, but I’m thinking of heading to Spain. I’ve heard amazing things about the food and culture. Maybe I’ll do some volunteer work too. It would be a nice way to reset. That sounds like a great idea. I should really think about taking a break too. Maybe I’ll propose to my boss that I take some time off to travel or learn something new. That’s a good move. You know, I’ve been meaning to reach out more. It’s been way too long since we last talked. What about we do something together soon?

Right, do you want to take a look at these deals I found on eBay? I think there’s a few bits of kit we could pick up without breaking the bank. Yeah, cool, I was just checking Amazon for some new headphones, but I’ve heard people say eBay can be a bit of a minefield. You never know if something’s going to be what it says on the tin. Aye, but if you know what you’re looking for, it can be a real bargain. I’ve got this old vacuum cleaner I found on eBay for about a third of what it would cost new. It’s still working fine, and it’s got a few years left on the warranty. That’s a good point. I guess it depends on what you’re buying, though. I mean, if it’s something like electronics or gadgets, you can get ripped off pretty easily if you’re not careful. Exactly. I always check the seller’s feedback and the product descriptions carefully. Sometimes, you can even get a bit of a discount if you’re willing to negotiate. But then again, some people just want to get rid of stuff quickly and don’t care about the price. I’ve tried that with some books, though. I was looking for a few old maths textbooks for revision, and I found one seller who had all the books I needed, but he was asking way too much. I ended up buying them all from Amazon for a bit more, but at least I knew exactly what I was getting. That’s true. I think it’s all about knowing your limits. If you’re not sure about something, it’s better to go with a more reliable seller, even if it’s a bit more expensive. You don’t want to end up with a broken item that you can’t return. Yeah, especially if it’s something like a phone or a laptop. I’ve heard stories about people getting faulty products on eBay and not being able to get a refund. It’s a bit of a headache, isn’t it? It can be. But then again, there are always some great finds. I recently picked up a vintage camera from an eBay seller, and it’s in amazing condition. I think the guy was selling it because he didn’t use it anymore.

So, do you know, I was just thinking about how things have changed since I was your age. You know, back in the day, we used to do more of everything, even if it wasn’t always the best. I suppose, but I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s worse now. It’s just different. I mean, I didn’t grow up with all the technology we have now. I’ve only just started using that new app for project management, and honestly, it’s a bit overwhelming. Oh, I remember when I was working in the factory. It was hard work, but there was a sense of community. Everyone knew each other, and we had to rely on each other. Now, you know, people are more isolated, even if they’re living in the same city. I guess that’s true. I mean, I do work with a lot of people, but it’s mostly through emails and meetings. There’s not much face-to-face interaction. I miss the days when you could just walk into the office and chat with someone. Yeah, I remember that. I used to take my lunch breaks with the lads from the factory and we’d have proper conversations. Now, even when I go out, it’s all about the phone. I can’t even remember the last time I had a real conversation with someone without looking at my phone. It’s sad, really. I think part of the problem is that we’ve all got this obsession with being always connected. But maybe it’s just the way things are now. I mean, you can’t really blame people for wanting to stay in touch with their friends and family. Not really, but I do think there’s something to be said for slower living. You know, taking time to actually talk to people instead of just sending a message. It’s not like we’re not busy, but maybe we just need to make time for the things that really matter. I agree. I’ve been trying to slow down a bit myself. I’ve started doing some gardening, and it’s actually quite calming. It’s a bit of a break from the constant noise of the city, even if it’s just in my own backyard. That’s a good idea. I think I should try that.

So, do you think we’re actually going to be able to get everything sorted for Christmas? I’ve been thinking about it all week, and honestly, I’m feeling a bit overwhelmed. Yeah, that’s one of my favorite parts of Christmas. I mean, I love the food, but I also love the traditions.

So, do you think we’re gonna get a bad reception in Cambridge? I mean, it’s a bit of a long drive from Birmingham, and I don’t want to miss the meeting because of a dropped signal or something. So, did you watch the new Marvel movie last night? Yeah, I did! It was  so  epic. I mean, like, the action sequences were just insane. Honestly, I didn’t get the chance to see it. I was stuck doing physics homework all night. Physics? That’s your thing, right? I still can’t wrap my head around how gravity works. It’s not that hard, honestly. Like, you just have to remember that gravity pulls everything toward the center of the Earth. Yeah, but how does that make sense when you’re on a rollercoaster? I mean, you’re going upside down, and you don’t fall off! Oh, that’s because the rollercoaster is moving so fast that the inertia keeps you in place. It’s all about acceleration and forces, man. Okay, I’m starting to get it. But what about that new album by the band  The Shadows ? I heard it’s like their best one yet. Oh man, I’m obsessed with it. The song  “Echoes of the Past”  is just so emotional. Like, it’s got this haunting melody that makes you feel like you’re in a movie. I’ve been listening to it too. But I think the lyrics are a bit too cryptic for me. I mean, they’re talking about someone who’s lost, but I can’t tell if it’s literal or metaphorical. Wait, isn’t that the one with the music video that’s basically a ballet? Yeah! I mean, the way they choreographed the movements with the music—it’s like watching a whole story unfold. I tried watching it, but I got distracted by the  Atom  movie playing on my phone. I mean, it was just so cool. You know, like, the superheroes fighting the villains, and there’s a theme about saving the world. That’s the one! I saw the trailer, and I was like, "That’s the best movie of the year!" I told you! It’s so much better than the last one. And the fight scenes—they’re just so dynamic. It’s like they’ve finally mastered the action sequences. I still don’t get why people pay so much for tickets to see those movies. I mean, you can just stream it for cheaper, right? Yeah, but I think the experience of watching it in a theater is different. Like, you’re surrounded by people who are excited, and the lights are dimmed, and the sound is way better.

Alright, do you remember how we talked about balanceability last week? I think it was when we were discussing how to help the kids with their schoolwork. Oh yes, I remember. I think you said it's all about finding the right balance between work and play, right? Exactly! I was thinking about how important balance is, especially when it comes to school. It's not just about doing homework all the time or having no time for social activities. It's about succeeding at something without burning out. Yeah, and I heard from one of my friends at school that they're having a hard time with their assessments. They were really excited about the project, but now they’re stressed about the deadline. I can imagine. I remember when I was in school, I used to get really anxious about exams. It's such a big deal for kids, especially when they’re trying to do well and also keep up with their friends. And I think part of the problem is that they’re being homeschooled now. I heard from one of the other parents that the way they're learning is completely different from when we were kids. Oh, that's true. I’ve been thinking about how homeschooling can be both a blessing and a curse. On one hand, you can tailor the curriculum to your child's strengths, but on the other hand, it can be really isolating for them if they don’t interact with other kids much. I think my friend is also dealing with that. Her new house is being renovated, and she’s not getting much time to hang out with her friends. They’re all trying to make the most of their time together. That makes sense. I mean, the school friend’s new house being renovated is a big change. I wonder how that affects their school life. Do they still have time to do activities like swimming or the manmade waterfall we talked about? I remember talking about the waterfall a few weeks ago. It was so cool, wasn’t it? I told the kids about how you have to be careful when diving into water, especially if there are rocks or currents. Yeah, that’s such an important lesson. I was thinking the other day about how dangerous it can be to dive into water without knowing the conditions.

So, do you ever find it hard to balance work and exercise? I mean, I know it’s a common problem, but I’m always juggling between planning events and trying to fit in a decent workout. Oh, absolutely. I’ve got this job where I’m always on my feet, and then I’m expected to be on call for the factory. It’s exhausting. I’ve actually been thinking about starting a gym membership, but I keep putting it off because I’m so busy. That sounds tough. I mean, I get it. I run a conference business, so I’m always juggling meetings, clients, and deadlines. But I try to make time for at least a bit of exercise every day. It helps me stay focused. Yeah, I can see how important that is. I feel like when I don’t exercise, I get so stressed and my mood goes downhill. I remember when I was in uni, I used to go to the gym all the time. It was my escape. That’s a great way to look at it. I used to tell myself that if I didn’t work out, I’d feel like a total wreck by the end of the week. But then I got into yoga, and it really changed my mindset. It’s not just about physical health—it’s mental too. That’s exactly what I’ve been trying to tell myself. I feel like I’ve been neglecting my mental health lately. I’m just stuck in this cycle of work and stress. I don’t even know where to start. Maybe you should start small. Like, just try to do 10 minutes of stretching every morning, or even a short walk. Once you get into the habit, it’s easier to build up from there. I know it sounds cliché, but it works. You’re right. I do need to start somewhere. Maybe I’ll look for a local gym that has affordable memberships. I’ve heard it’s a bit easier to stick to a routine if you have a place to go regularly. Yeah, that’s a good idea. And if you ever need help planning your schedule or anything, just let me know. I know how hard it can be to fit everything in. Thanks, I appreciate that. I feel like I’m slipping a bit, but I don’t want to let it get out of control.

Alright, lads, I’ve got a load of pizza in the oven – just need to wait a few more minutes. You two are welcome to help yourselves to a drink if you like, or we can wait for the pizza to finish. Thanks, Grandpa, that sounds great. I’m starving after the Domino Drive. Aye, me too. That drive was a right beast. A lot of people got stuck in the snow, didn’t they? Aye, and some of the roads were so icy that the council had to close them. I heard a few people had to take taxis just to get home. That’s not fair. I mean, you can’t just close the roads like that. It’s dangerous, sure, but I think the council should’ve given people more notice. Well, I agree with you, lad, but sometimes it’s just happened. You can’t plan for everything. I remember the time when we had that log slide out of the fireplace. That was a real mess. Oh, don’t remind me! I had to clean up the whole living room for days. You were so proud of yourself, weren’t you? Aye, I was! I thought it was brilliant. I even took a photo of it on my phone. You know what? I’ve been thinking about getting a haircut. I’ve got this really long fringe that’s been getting in my eyes all week. You should definitely get it done. You look like a right mess with that fringe. What’s the deal with your hair, anyway? I don’t know, it just keeps growing. I’ve had it like this for ages. Maybe I should get it cut short. Maybe you should. My nephew had that same look once. He looked like a mohawk, but it was just a mess. Aye, and he ended up waiting till the last minute to get it done. I swear, he nearly missed his birthday because of it. That’s not fair. You’re trying to make me feel bad. I’m just telling the truth, lad. You’re not the only one who’s had a bad hair day. Speaking of hair days, what’s the deal with that big brother of yours? He’s been out every night with his mates, and he’s got more hair than I’ve ever seen. Yeah, I know.

So, do you know what’s the worst thing about Cambridge? It’s the pubs. Every time I go out, I end up with some weird local who’s more interested in talking about their veggie smoothie than actually having a conversation. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve had that experience too. I mean, the pubs here are good, but honestly, it’s like they’ve all turned into health cafes by accident. I swear, I went to a pub last week and the barman asked me if I wanted a kale salad instead of a pint. Oh no, that’s not even fair. I mean, I like a good kale salad, but I also like a pint of bitter. It’s like the whole vibe of the place has shifted. I think it’s because of the students. Everyone’s so into health trends now. Yeah, and it’s not just the students. I mean, even some of the older academics are into this whole “clean eating” thing. I remember seeing one of the professors at the university with a smoothie instead of a coffee, and I was like, “Is that your morning ritual?” I think it’s part of the whole Cambridge culture. You know, we’re all so into our research and our studies, but we’re also hyper-aware of our health. It’s like we’ve got a PhD in everything, including how to eat. Exactly. I mean, I’ve even started eating more vegetables. Not because I’m trying to be healthy, but because I want to fit in with the rest of the crowd. I mean, I still like my chips and my burgers, but I’ve started incorporating more greens into my meals. Oh, you’re not telling me you’ve become a vegan? Because I would not be surprised. I mean, I’ve seen you in the café, and you’ve been staring at the kale bowl like it’s the holy grail. No, no, no. I’m not a vegan. I just like to pretend I am. It’s a safety blanket. But seriously, do you think I’ve gone too far with this? I mean, I’m trying to live a balanced lifestyle. I think you’re doing it right. It’s about balance. But I still think the pubs are losing their soul. I mean, the other day, I went to a pub and the only thing on the menu was quinoa burgers and beetroot fries.

I can’t believe we've got to this point. I think I’ve got one. Let me think...  pauses and squints at the board  It's... "Deck of cards"! No, wait, that's not it. Wait, the word is "Deck of cards" — but I think that's not the one. I think the one I was thinking of was something like...  snaps fingers  "Operation"? No, that’s not it. I’m getting confused. Alright, let’s see… I’ve got a King of Hearts. That’s a good start, isn’t it? Yeah, but I’ve got a Queen of Spades. That’s a bit of a boss move, wouldn’t you say? Oh, come on, you’re just trying to flex. I’ve got the Ace of Diamonds. You’re all jealous of me. Yeah, yeah, you’ve got the best card. But don’t get too cocky, old man. I’ve got the Jack of Clubs. That’s the one that can really mess you up. Right, right, we all know that. Still, I think I’m going to win this round. I’ve got the high card. Oh yeah, and you’ve got the highest card. But I’m gonna make you regret that. Let’s just play this properly. We can’t be arguing over cards all the time. Come on, it’s just a game. We’re all here to have fun, not to be serious. Well, it’s not like we’re in a real game. This is just… Yeah, yeah, just a little bit of fun. I mean, I’ve got a bit of a strategy here. I’ve been watching you all play, and I know what you’re going to do. Oh, you’ve been watching? That’s a bit much. You’re a teacher, not a mind-reader. I think he’s got a point. I mean, I’ve been in this game for a while, and I’ve seen a lot of people play. Yeah, and I’ve been playing since I was a kid. I know the ins and outs of this game. Maybe you should tell us your secrets, then. What’s your secret to winning? I don’t know, maybe you just have to be lucky. Yeah, but I think luck has a lot to do with it. I mean, I’ve been here all week, and I’ve seen people lose their temper over a card. Yeah, that’s true. But I think I’m going to go for the Queen of Hearts next. I think that’s the one that’s going to win me the game. Oh, you think so? I’ll take that from you. Alright, alright, let’s just play the next round. I think we’re all getting a bit worked up about this.

So, do you think I should go to university or do an apprenticeship? I’m really confused. I think it depends on what you want to do. If you like studying, then uni is probably better. But if you want to get into the workforce straight away, an apprenticeship could be a good option. Yeah, but I think uni is more stable in the long run. I mean, I’m doing a trainee accountant course, but I still have to work while studying. It’s a bit tough, but I like it. Honestly, I think it’s better to go to university if you can afford it. I’m studying for my degree in Navel Combat Systems engineering, and it’s going to open up a lot of doors for me. But I’m not sure. I’m doing a retail job and a student job, but I don’t really know what I want to do. Maybe I should just take a gap year and figure it out? Yeah, I’ve heard about gap years. I mean, it’s not like we have to decide right now, right? I think it’s okay to take some time. My mum did that before she started her care support work. It really helped her figure out what she wanted. That’s true. I mean, I’m not sure if I want to be an accountant for the rest of my life. What if I change my mind? I’ve been thinking about it too. I want to do something with technology, but I’m not sure if I want to go straight into a university program or get an apprenticeship in a tech company. I know! Maybe we could all meet up and talk about our options. Like, maybe we can make a study group or something. That sounds like a good idea. We could share our experiences and help each other out. Yeah, I’d love that. I mean, we all have different paths, but it’s good to know we’re not alone in this. I’m in. I’m really enjoying learning about accounting, but I want to make sure I’m on the right track. I’m in too. I think it’s important to have people around you who understand what you’re going through. Cool! So maybe we can all meet up next week after Christmas?

Well, do you think we should go for a walk tomorrow? The weather looks nice, and it’s been a bit too hot in here all day. I’d love to, but I have to work tomorrow. I’m on shift at the store. But maybe later this week? I’d like to, but I’m not sure I can manage. I’ve been feeling a bit off lately. Maybe I should just stay in and rest. Oh, don’t be silly, you know you can always take it easy. But what about the cycling? I heard there’s a new route near the university that’s pretty peaceful. That sounds nice, but I’ve been trying to get back into cycling. I’ve been a bit out of shape since I moved here. I’d need to start slow, and I’m not sure if I can handle it yet. You know, I used to cycle all the time when I was younger. It was the best way to get around, especially when I worked. I could go to the market, pick up some fresh veggies, and get back home in no time. That’s true. I remember when I lived in London, I used to ride my bike everywhere. But these days, I just take the bus or the train. Although, I do miss the freedom of being able to go where I want without worrying about parking. Yeah, I understand. I’ve heard that Cambridge is one of those places where you can still get around without a car. But I’m not sure I’m ready for that yet. Also, I think the roads can get pretty crowded at certain times. I know what you mean. I used to drive all the time, but now that I’m retired, I just don’t feel the need. I’m not as mobile as I used to be, and I don’t like the stress of driving anymore. I can see that. I used to drive all the time too, but I’ve been thinking about getting a car recently. I don’t know, it just feels safer for me to have one, especially with the amount of walking I do these days. That’s a good point. I’m not sure I’d ever get a car, though. I think I’d rather walk or bike, even if it takes longer.

So, do you know much about the Basque language? I’ve been reading up on it for a project and it’s fascinating how it’s completely unrelated to any other language in Europe. Oh, I’ve heard a bit about it. I think it’s a language isolate, right? Like it doesn’t connect to any other language family. I remember reading that it’s still spoken in parts of the Basque Country, but it’s not as widely used as it used to be. That’s true. It’s one of the oldest languages in Europe, actually. I’ve studied it a little in my time, even though I’m more into linguistic theory. It’s quite unique, especially with its system of vowel length and tone. That’s interesting. I was also wondering about the differences between Spanish and Catalan. Do you think they’re considered separate languages or just dialects? I think they’re definitely separate languages, but in some contexts, people might refer to them as dialects depending on where you are. In Spain, Catalan is more like a regional language, often spoken in Catalonia and Valencia, while Spanish is the official language. And then there’s the situation in China, where Mandarin is the official language, but there are so many dialects – like Cantonese, Shanghainese, and Hokkien. It’s quite complex. Yes, I’ve always found that fascinating. It made me think about how language can be both a barrier and a bridge. I was in London recently, and I noticed how many different accents and dialects there are even within the city. Definitely. I remember when I was doing fieldwork in Wales, the contrast between the English spoken there and the Welsh was really striking. It’s not just about the words you use, but the way you structure your sentences and the intonation. Exactly. And then there’s rugby – I always think language and sport go hand in hand. I mean, it’s a very physical game, but the language used to describe it, the chants, the strategies... it’s all part of the culture. I love rugby, too. But I find it interesting how some parts of the world go out of their way to use English in sports, like in football or cricket. It’s like a global language. And what about Spain? I’ve never been, but I’ve heard how passionate people are about football there.

So, how’s the kid doing? I heard you’ve been going through the adoption process again. Yeah, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. We’re waiting on another assessment, and it’s been over a year now. I mean, it’s been two years since we last met, and we’re still not officially on the list. That's really frustrating. I can't imagine how hard that must be, especially with all the emotional ups and downs. It's not easy waiting for something like that. Yeah, it's not easy. But I have to say, the way you both handled the last one was amazing. You stayed strong, and you kept each other going. My mum keeps saying I should be an example for people, but honestly, I’m just trying to keep up with the rest of the family. You know, we've been talking about when we finally get the call, we’re going to take a trip. Maybe somewhere warm, like Spain or Greece, to celebrate. You ever think about doing that? I’d love to, but I’d rather not take any chances with the visa or the travel arrangements. I’ve got too much on my plate with the kids and the job. Still, it’s good to have a plan – even if it’s just a dream. Totally understandable. I mean, I don’t know how you do it. I work in recruitment, and I’m always filling in forms for people. I think I’d lose my mind trying to track a child through the system. Yeah, I know. It’s not the same as having a regular job, but it’s worth it. I mean, I’m not saying it’s easy, but the fact that we’re trying and not giving up—that’s what matters. Exactly. And besides, we’re not the only ones going through this. There are so many people out there, and it’s just not fair. I think we should start a support group or something. Maybe even on Facebook? That’s a good idea. I’ve seen so many people use Facebook to keep in touch with family and friends, but I haven’t seen many posts about adoption. Maybe we can start a group or go viral or something. If we go viral, I might just be the one that gets all the attention.

I just can’t believe how much this coffee machine costs, you know. I thought it would be cheaper than that. I know, I’m still trying to figure out how they can charge so much for something that just makes coffee. It’s like they’re making a profit off of our morning routine. Yeah, and then there’s the cost of the beans. I’ve been trying to find a good brand that doesn’t break the bank, but I’m not sure if I’m even looking in the right place. I tried buying some organic coffee beans the other day, and it was like three times more expensive than the regular ones. I don’t know if it’s worth it. I think it’s all about marketing. They make you feel like you need to buy the fancy stuff. But honestly, I just want a cup of coffee that doesn’t taste like it’s been sitting in a warehouse for a year. I agree. I mean, I used to have a machine that didn’t cost anywhere near that. And it worked fine. I think I’m just going to try to find a used one or something. That might be a good idea. I’ve been thinking about getting a second-hand one too. Maybe we can all pool our money and buy one together? That’s a great idea! It’s not like we’re not used to sharing things. I mean, we all live in the same house, right? Yeah, and we also have to think about the storage. If we get a new machine, where’s it going to go? I mean, it’s not like we have extra space in the kitchen. I’m thinking about the cupboard above the sink. It’s not the most glamorous spot, but it’s dry and it keeps the machine out of the way. Plus, we’re not using that spot for anything else anyway. That sounds reasonable. I’m just worried about the cost of removal and storage. If we have to pay for someone to move the old one out, that could add up quickly. I know. I’ve heard stories about people getting charged ridiculous amounts for just moving things. I think we need to be careful about that. I think we should do our research. Maybe look up some local companies that do removals and see what the rates are like.

So, do you think we should go back to my mum’s for Christmas this year? I know it’s a bit far, but I really miss the whole family vibe. Oh, I was just thinking the same thing. It’s been a while since we all got together. I mean, it’s not like we can go anywhere else with the weather being as bad as it is. Yeah, and with the kids getting older, they’re starting to want to be part of the traditions. I mean, we had the best Christmas ever when the whole family was there. The tree, the carols, even the mince pies—everything was just right. You know, I still remember the time when the kids used to run around the house like they were in a race, trying to get the last piece of cake. They were so full of energy, and the whole place was alive. It’s funny, isn’t it? Now they’re more interested in their own stuff, like their phones and their games. I wonder if they’ll even remember what Christmas is about when they’re older. Well, maybe we can still make it special for them. I was thinking of setting up a little Christmas craft corner in the living room. You know, the kind where they can make their own decorations, and maybe even a small gift exchange. That sounds like a great idea. I could help with the crafts, and maybe even bring some of the old family recipes. I’ve been trying to perfect my Christmas cake, and I think it’s getting closer to the original. Oh, I’d love to see that! You know, I still remember your mum’s Christmas cake—it was the best. She used to make it every year, and even though it was a bit messy, it was always a hit. Yeah, and I think I’m going to make it again this year. I’ve been doing some research on the recipes, and I’ve even tried a few variations. I think I’ve got it down to a science now. That’s great. I can’t wait to taste it. And maybe we can set up a little Christmas tree in the living room, like we used to. It’ll be nice to have everyone together again, even if just for a few days.

So, do you remember that time we were all at the Poacher last week and someone started snoring so loudly it was like a foghorn? Oh, yeah, that was  the  night we were all over here with the Waterfields and the Bakers. I swear, for a second I thought the snoring was the actual sound of the bar closing. Yeah, I remember that. It was actually one of the Bakers, wasn’t it? The one who always orders the Richmond sausages and the Yorkshire pudding. Definitely. He was right in the corner, head on his chest, and that snore was like the sound of a train. I almost had to cover my ears. Yeah, and then when he finally stopped, the silence was so loud, it felt like the whole pub was holding its breath for a second. I remember thinking, “Is he still alive?” in the middle of it. And then the next thing you know, he just sat up, like nothing happened, and said, “Sorry about that, lads. I’ve been a bit tired.” He looked like he’d been asleep for days. But then he went and ordered another round. How does he even function? I think it’s the Richmond sausages. It’s got to be something in them. I’ve never had one, but I’ve heard the stories. Honestly, I think it’s the handkerchiefs. I remember seeing one of the guys with a handkerchief around his neck, like a necktie, and it was like he was about to fall asleep while he was still standing. Yeah, and I swear, he was holding it so tight, I thought he was trying to keep himself awake. I mean, if you’re going to snore in a pub, maybe you should at least do it in a  private  booth. I don’t know, maybe that’s the point of the handkerchief – to catch the snore? Like a giant, loud, public handkerchief. That’s the spirit. Next time, I’m bringing a pillow. I’d bring a sleeping bag. I’d be out like a light. Exactly. We could have a  snore convention  in the Poacher. You know what I’ve been thinking? Maybe we should start a group called “The Snoring Society.” You know, like a club for people who snore in public. That’s genius. We could start with a meeting at the Poacher. Yeah, and we could make it official.

So, did you have a good weekend, Dad? I know you mentioned something about going to the countryside. Oh, it was great, really. I went up to the Peak District with a few mates. It was a proper weekend away, no phones, no emails—just the two of us and a couple of lads from the farm. That sounds lovely. Did you do anything special? Well, we got up early, had a proper breakfast, then we went hiking. The views were stunning. The sun was shining, the sky was brilliant blue. Wow, that sounds like a real change of pace. I've been stuck in meetings all weekend. I've had a hell of a week with the new project, and I just needed a break. I know, love. I think it's important to take a step back now and then. You can't work all the time. You're right. I was just so busy trying to get everything sorted with the new clients. I barely had time to breathe. I remember when I started out, I used to work 16-hour days. But you get to a certain age, you realize life isn't just about work. You've got family, you've got friends, and you've got to enjoy the little things. I'm trying, Dad. I really am. It's just hard when you're in the middle of something big. I know it is. But you're doing well. I noticed you've been a lot more relaxed lately. Yeah, I guess I have. I’ve been trying to take it slow. I even managed to fit in a bit of reading the other day. I finally finished that book I’ve been meaning to read for months. That’s a good sign. You know, I read that same book when I was your age. It was a bit of a classic. You should try reading something a bit more modern, though. I might. I’ve been thinking about it. Maybe something from the 80s? I’ve heard it's been getting quite a bit of attention lately. Oh, you mean the one about the goth band and the lake? That's a bit of a cult classic, really. I remember that was a big deal back in the day. Yeah, I think that’s the one. I’ve been meaning to check it out, but I’m not sure if I’ll ever get around to it.

So how’s life treating you these days? You mentioned you were going to be on maternity leave soon, right? Yeah, it’s all set. I’m going to be taking a year off to look after my baby. It’s a bit of a big step, but I think it’s the right one. I’ve been thinking about it for a while now. That’s great, I mean, I can’t imagine how tiring it must be, but I also think it’s such an important part of life. You’re going to be an amazing mum. Thanks, I hope so. I guess it’s also a bit of a relief, to be honest. I’ve been working like a dog for the last few years, and I think I needed this break. I’m not saying I’m burnt out, but I just want to be present for my little one. I get that. I’ve been teaching languages for a few years now, and while I love it, I do miss having time for myself. I mean, I’m not going on maternity leave, but I have a lot of responsibilities too—my own kids, my job, everything. Yeah, it’s a balancing act. I always thought I’d be the kind of person who’d work until I’m 65, but now I’m realizing that’s not the way for me. I want to be there for my family more than I thought. That’s totally valid. I mean, I still think about learning a new language sometimes, though. I’ve been thinking about taking a break from teaching for a year and maybe learning Spanish or something. I’ve always wanted to be fluent, but I’ve never had the chance. That sounds amazing. I mean, I can’t imagine being fluent in another language, but I think it’s something worth pursuing. You’re so good at languages, though—how do you even manage it? It’s a mix of passion and discipline. I love the way languages work, how they connect people, how they open doors. Plus, I have to say, I always found it easier to keep up with the language when I was teaching. I’d be teaching Spanish one day and then practicing it the next. I think I’d struggle with that. I mean, I’ve tried picking up Italian a few times, but it just never stuck.

Well, I've just been out in the garden sorting the bird feeders. You know, I've been putting up some new ones, and I’ve got a few nests I’ve had to clear out. Some of them are in the trees, and they’re getting a bit messy. Yeah, I saw that. I was out earlier, feeding the birds. I reckon it’s about time we got a bit of a tidy up. I don’t like the look of those nests hanging off the branches. They’re like little tents, and they’re getting full of leaves and stuff. I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about getting some new bird feeders myself. I’ve got a few old ones that don’t work anymore. I remember when I used to take the kids to the park and we’d feed the birds. It was fun, wasn’t it? Oh, it was. I still remember when we used to have all those little balls in the park. I think the birds were quite fussy back then. They’d only eat the ones with the seeds in them. Yeah, and we used to have these little plastic bowls. I’ve still got one of them, actually. I’ve been thinking of putting it in the garden. Maybe put some sunflower seeds in – that’s what they like, isn’t it? I’ve got some sunflower seeds in the kitchen. Maybe we could make some bird food out of that. It’s not like we’re going to use it all. And it’s better than just letting them go to waste. That’s a good idea. I’ve got some old boxes from when I was a child, so we could make little feeders out of those. I remember the kids loved making them. It was like an art project. I’d love to see that. Maybe we could do something like that for the garden. It’d be nice to have a bit of activity, even if it’s just for the birds. I mean, it’s not like we’ve got anything else to do these days. That’s true. It’s sad, really, not having much to do. I’ve been thinking of trying to bake a cake or something. Maybe a simple one, like a Victoria sponge. I’ve got the ingredients for that.

I can't believe we've made it to Cyprus for the summer. It's been ages since we've been away from the UK, hasn't it? I know, it's been over ten years since I've been here. I feel like I've missed out on a lot. But it's good to be back, especially with the weather like this. Yeah, it's absolutely stunning. I’ve only ever been to Cyprus once before, and I remember how much I loved the food. I think I'll try the moussaka today. It’s one of my favorites. I'll go with that too. And maybe a glass of ouzo to start. I've heard it's a local favorite. Although, I must say, I still find it a bit strong, but I like the way it makes me feel. That’s the point, isn’t it? It’s supposed to be a bit of a kick. I’ve been trying to learn a few Turkish words just in case, you know, for the locals. I’ve been counting up to ten, and it’s not as hard as I thought. That’s a great start. I remember when I was younger, I used to love watching people interact in different languages. It always fascinated me. Though I can’t say I’ve ever been great at languages myself. Yeah, I’m not too bad with languages. I studied French and Spanish at university, but I always thought Turkish would be easier. Though, I’m also trying to remember my old German. It’s been so long since I’ve had to use it. That’s surprising. I thought you were more of a visual learner. Maybe I am. I can remember the shapes of the words more than the sounds. Although, I know that’s not the best way to learn a language. I just have to keep at it. Maybe I’ll start learning some phrases for when I’m out and about. If you ever need help with that, I’m always here. I could teach you a few words. I know a few Turkish expressions, especially with food. That would be great. I’d love to try speaking a few words in Turkish with the locals. It would be a nice way to break the ice. You’re on. I’m sure it’ll be fun.

Mum, Dad, I just got back from the station and I’m starving. Did you make any lunch? Oh, we had a bit of a salad and some sandwiches, but we’re about to make some proper lunch. Why don’t you take a seat and help yourself to a drink? I was just about to say the same thing. I reckon we should make something a bit more substantial today. A Sunday roast would be nice, don’t you think? That sounds lovely. I’ve been working non-stop all week and I could do with something hearty. You’re not the only one. I’ve been feeling a bit sluggish myself. I’ve been working with the exams and it’s been a bit of a marathon. Yes, I know what you mean. It’s been one of those weeks. I’ve had to deal with a few logistical issues with the farm, and then there’s this renovation project we’ve been planning. Oh, I heard about the renovation. Are you going to start soon?
