So, do you think we could actually make this work, Reg? I mean, with the rackets breaking like that, and the strings snapping all the time. It’s getting ridiculous, isn’t it? I know, I know. That’s why I’m thinking about this whole idea of using cable ties. You know, the kind that you use to bundle up wires. It's strong, it's cheap, and it's pretty much everywhere. What do you think? Cable ties? I mean, they’re not exactly the most elegant solution, but if it works, it’s better than nothing. I’ve seen a few people use them on rackets before. But I wonder—what do you think about the size? Do you think they’d hold up under the tension of the strings? I think they’d hold up. I mean, we’re not talking about breaking the laws of physics here. As long as we use the right thickness, maybe even double them up. I’ve also been thinking about the positioning—maybe we can put them around the grip, or near the head, where the tension is the highest. That way, they can help prevent the strings from breaking in the first place. That sounds like a plan. But we should also consider the cost. If we’re going to sell these, we can’t be charging too much. People are already reluctant to spend on rackets, let alone on repairs. Yeah, I know. That’s why I was thinking about using cheaper materials—like maybe some kind of fabric or mesh that we can wrap around the string ends. It might be a bit more practical and look better than cable ties. That could work. But I’m still not sure about the word ‘fleet’—I mean, when I was teaching, I always thought that was a word that only came up in the context of ships. Why are we using it here? Because it’s a word that’s been used a lot in marketing. ‘Fleet’ sounds strong, reliable, and professional. I think it could really resonate with people who are into sports and want to feel like they’re using the best equipment. Hmm, I suppose. But I wonder if it would work the same way in primary schools as it does in secondary schools. I mean, in primary, the kids are just starting out, and they don’t know what a ‘fleet’ of rackets even is.

Well, I've been meaning to talk to you about that painting you've been trying to get your head around. It's the one with all those bright reds and yellows, isn't it? It's got this real energy to it, don’t you think? Oh, it’s been on my mind too. I’ve been looking at it all week. It’s like it’s trying to tell a story, but I just can’t figure out what. I mean, the colours are so vivid, but the shapes are all over the place. It makes me feel a bit uneasy, honestly. That’s because it’s modern art, isn’t it? It doesn’t always make sense. I think it’s more about emotion than traditional representation. The artist is trying to convey something more abstract. Exactly. I used to think modern art was just a gimmick, but the more I study it, the more I see that it’s about interpretation. It’s like a puzzle, you know? You have to look at it from different angles and let your own feelings guide you. I get that, but it’s still hard for me. I’ve always preferred something more… grounded. You know, like a portrait or a landscape that tells you exactly what it is. This one, though – it’s like looking into a mirror and not seeing yourself. I think that’s the point, though. Maybe it’s meant to make you question what you see. There’s something about that red and yellow contrast that really catches the eye. It’s almost like it’s shouting at you. It does, doesn’t it? I think that’s the power of it. It doesn’t just sit there quietly. It demands your attention. And the fact that it’s so bold and unapologetic is what makes it stand out. Yeah, and that’s what I like about it. It challenges you. It doesn’t just let you sit back and admire the work – you have to engage with it. You have to feel something. I suppose that’s what I’m trying to get to. Maybe with time, I’ll start to see the beauty in it. I mean, I do like a good colour, and the way the light plays off those hues is pretty impressive. I think you’re on the right track.

I swear, I don’t know how people do it. Every time I go out, it’s like the first girl I see is some kind of bimbo, and I can’t even talk to her without her making me feel like I’m wasting my time. Oh come on, you’re just not trying. You’ve got the look, the vibe, the confidence. You just need to stop overthinking. Yeah, right. I’m not even sure I  want  to be trying. I mean, I like my independence. I don’t want to be chasing someone around like a lost puppy. I get that, but you can’t just sit at home and expect everyone to come to you. You’ve got to put yourself out there. And if you’re still single, maybe it’s because you’re not actually doing anything. Ugh, I know, I know. I just feel like no one is  real . We’re all looking for someone who’s going to match us, not just some random girl who thinks she’s the best thing since sliced bread. Exactly. I went out with this guy, and he was just like, “Oh, you’re into tech?” And I was like, “Yeah, obviously.” That’s not even a conversation. That’s just wasting your time. You know what I mean? Yeah, I do. I just feel like everyone I meet is either too into themselves or too into someone else. I can’t even begin to think about dating when I’m still figuring out what I want to do with my life.

I just don’t get how people can still smoke. I mean, I know it’s a vice, but it’s got to be so harmful. You know, I don’t even know how someone can justify lighting up these days. I know, I know. But some people just can’t stop. I mean, my mum still does it. She says it’s her way of coping with stress. Though I reckon she just likes the ritual of it. Oh, I get that, but it’s not just coping. It’s also about habit. And when you get into it, it’s hard to break. But I just can’t imagine going through that. I mean, I can’t even stand the smell of cigarettes. It makes me feel like I’m going to be sick. You’re not the only one. I think the key is to understand why someone is doing it. If it’s just a habit, then maybe they can quit. But if it’s a coping mechanism, it’s a whole different story. I mean, I know people who use alcohol in the same way. Yeah, and I think sometimes it’s a combination of both. Like, people start off with cigarettes as a way to deal with stress, and then it turns into a habit. And then when they’re stressed again, they reach for the same thing. It’s like a cycle. Exactly. And it’s not just about the physical addiction. It’s the psychological one too. You know, people get used to the way it makes them feel. It’s like a crutch. I guess. But I still don’t see the point. I mean, are there any benefits to smoking? I mean, besides the obvious ones, like the smell or the taste. Not really. I mean, you get a quick hit of nicotine, but it’s not worth the long-term damage. Plus, it’s not like it gives you any real clarity or focus. In fact, it does the opposite. I think that’s the problem with vices in general. People use them to feel in control, but they end up feeling more out of control. And then it’s like a snowball rolling down a hill. Exactly. And I think that’s where the whole common sense vs. intelligence thing comes in. Because people are intelligent enough to know the risks, but they still do it.

Yeah, I was just thinking the same thing. I've been meaning to get back in touch with some old friends, and it would be nice to catch up properly. But I need to check if everyone's available. It's the one time of year when you can just relax and spend time with the people you care about. I know, it's the same for me. I’ve been working on some research, and even though I've been doing some pretty interesting stuff, it's not the same as being with friends. Have you seen any good movies lately? Oh, I agree. There’s something special about classic films. They just have a timeless quality. But I think it’s also nice to watch new stuff too. I think I'll make a list of the films I want to see before the holiday.

Alright, so I just saw this tweet about a new café in Margate that's supposed to be  the  place to be. But honestly, the review said the coffee was like "worse than my ex's cooking." What even is that? Oh yeah, I saw that too. It’s one of those places that’s all about the aesthetic, right? Like, they’ve got these minimalist designs and Instagrammable corners, but the food? It’s just a gimmick. I mean, I know someone who tried it and said the cappuccino was colder than the outside. Yeah, but I think it's just the whole "design over substance" thing that's become so popular these days. My café, it's not about the Instagram filter. It's about the coffee, the service, the vibe. I mean, every time someone comes in and immediately starts taking photos, I just want to say, "Do you want to taste it or just take a picture?" That’s so true, and honestly, it’s gotten to the point where I can’t even trust a five-star review anymore. I mean, I’ve seen people give out five stars to places that are basically just a glorified takeaway. It’s like, how do you even rate a café on a scale from one to five if you haven’t even tasted the coffee? Exactly. I mean, I used to check reviews all the time before I opened my own place. But now, I just skip them. I think people are so suspicious of them now. Like, if you give a five-star review, you're either a complete fanboi or you’re getting paid to write it. I know, and honestly, even some bad reviews can be good for business. I had one guy write that my latte was “so bad it made me cry,” and the next day, I had a line of people waiting outside. It was like the worst thing that ever happened to me, but the most effective marketing. Haha, that’s so unfair. I mean, I’ve had some  terrible  customers too. Like, the guy who came in during the middle of the day and ordered a takeaway coffee, then sat around for an hour and started arguing with the barista about the temperature of the milk. Oh, I had one of those too. He said the milk wasn’t "properly frothed," and then proceeded to take a sip and say, "This is like drinking a puddle."

Alright, let’s get this dinner started. I’ve got the veggie sticks and hummus ready. Who’s up for some chocolate ice cream? I’m ready! I’ve been waiting for this. I’m starving. I’m ready too. Mom, can I have some raspberries? I brought some from the garden. Of course you can, sweetie. I’ve got a little bowl ready. Did you pick them yourself? Yeah, I did. They were so fresh and sweet. I tried to pick some for Oisin too, but he just ate the leaves. Oh, don’t worry. He’s a little explorer. He loves to taste everything. Just keep an eye on him though. He’s a good kid, but he’s got a curious appetite. I remember when he was little, he tried to eat a bird egg once. He didn’t like it. I had to give him a banana instead. Oh, that’s cute. I remember when I was little, I tried to eat a gerbil once. I thought it was a candy. Mom had to stop me. Haha, that sounds like a classic childhood moment. You know, I was thinking about how we all used to cycle around the neighborhood. I remember biking with my brother and trying to catch the fastest one. It was so much fun. I never had a bike. My dad used to take me on walks in the park. We used to collect bird eggs and try to identify them. I think I had a little notebook for it. That sounds amazing. I want to do that when I grow up. I’m thinking about getting a pet gerbil. I’ve seen them on YouTube and they’re so cute. That’s a great idea. Gerbils are low maintenance, and they’re fun to watch. Just make sure you research their needs first. They need the right habitat and food. I’ve heard about them. I think they like carrots and seeds. Do they eat vegetables? Yeah, they do. They enjoy vegetables like carrots, kale, and even some fruits like raspberries. Just make sure the raspberries are washed and not too sweet. Oh, I have some leftover raspberries from today. I can give some to the gerbil. That sounds nice. I used to grow vegetables in my garden too. I had a tomato plant that grew so tall. I had to tie it up with string so it wouldn’t fall over.

So, do you think we should go to the supermarket tomorrow or do you need me to do it for you? I’ve got a couple of hours after work today, and I can take the car. Oh, that would be great, thank you. I’m just not sure if I can manage on my own. I’ve been feeling a bit dizzy lately, and it’s not easy getting around with a wheelchair. I can help you, love. I’d be happy to go with you. It’s not like I’m doing anything else. That’s very kind of you, but I think I can manage. I’ll take the list, and I can do it in about an hour. Just let me know what you need. I’m not sure what I need, to be honest. I’ve been relying on my daughter for everything lately. She’s been coming over every couple of days to help me with the shopping and cooking. I know, dear. It’s a shame that the NHS isn’t helping more with things like that. I remember when I was still working, I used to pick up groceries for my friends and family when they were in trouble. Yeah, I remember that too. It’s so much harder now with everything being so busy. I still try to help out when I can, but I’m not sure if I’m doing enough. You’re doing more than enough. I just feel guilty when I ask for help. I know it’s not fair to burden you. Don’t be silly, love. We’re all family. If I can help, I will. I’ve got the time. That’s what I like to hear. I’ll take the list tomorrow. I was thinking of stopping by the chemist as well to get some painkillers for the back. Oh, you should. I’ve been trying to manage with just paracetamol, but it’s not helping much anymore. I had that same issue. I ended up seeing a physiotherapist, and it cost quite a bit, but it was worth it. I can’t stand the pain anymore. That’s a good idea. I’ll mention it to the pharmacist. And while you’re there, could you get some of that eyebrow waxing stuff I mentioned? I think it’s called  DepiLex  or something like that.

So, do you think we've weaned the baby yet? I mean, it's been a week since we started, and I’m still not sure if she's ready. I think she's getting there, but it's not easy, is it? I mean, she’s been so upset in the mornings. I swear, she cries like she’s been abandoned. Yeah, I know. I feel awful, but I think it's just a phase. And honestly, I was dreading this. I wasn’t ready to give up breastfeeding. But I think it's the right thing for her now. I can see why. I remember when I weaned my first child, it was like the hardest thing I’d ever done. But now that she’s older, I think she’s more willing to try new things. Yeah, you're right. And I’m starting to get the hang of it too. It’s just a bit of a learning curve, you know? Exactly. I think the key is to be consistent. It helps if you both stay calm and try to make it as stress-free as possible. Like, we’ve made a schedule and stick to it as much as we can. That’s a good idea. I’m trying to be patient, but I’m not sure how much longer I can keep this up. I’m so tired. I know what you mean. It’s not just the baby—it's the whole routine. But hey, we’ve got a few days off coming up, so maybe we can use that to focus on this. What are the plans for the week? Well, my parents are coming over on Thursday. They’re excited to meet the baby, and I think they’ll be helpful. But I also have that sign language class I’ve been meaning to attend. I’ve got the leaflet for it, and I was thinking maybe we could go together? Sign language? That sounds great. I’ve been meaning to start too. You know, since I’m working with kids, it might be useful. But wait, do you think the baby will be okay with us going out? I think so. We’ll have the baby sitter over, and I’ll leave her with some toys and a book. You know, the usual. I think she'll be fine. Okay, that’s settled.

I just love this place, don’t you? It’s so peaceful here, away from the city buzz. Yeah, it’s a real breath of fresh air. I can’t believe we got this flat in Norfolk. I know, it’s like a different world. The hills here are so different from London. I mean, you can see the countryside for miles. Aye, and the villages are so charming. They’ve got that old-world feel, you know? Like they’ve been around forever. It’s true. I love how the little villages seem to have their own character. Every one of them is different, yet somehow connected. Yeah, I’ve noticed that. Like, some have that traditional market square, others are more modern, but they all have that sort of local vibe. Exactly. And when you walk through them, you can tell people are proud of where they live. You can see it in the way they talk about their area, the way they take care of the place. I think it’s the rural way of life. You’re more connected to the land, to the community. It’s not like cities where everything’s so fast-paced. Definitely. I mean, I’ve spent so much time in cities, and I miss this. The quiet, the open spaces, the fresh air. And the sense of community. You know, in the village, people know each other. They help each other out. It’s not just about looking out for yourself. Right. I remember when we first moved here, we were invited to a village fête. It was such a warm welcome. We were treated like locals from day one. That’s the thing about the countryside, isn’t it? You feel like you belong. You’re not just passing through—you’re part of something bigger. Yeah, and it’s not just about the people. The landscape here is so beautiful. The hills, the rolling fields, the way the light catches the trees in the morning… it’s magical. I know. I’ve been taking photos of the views every day. It’s like a living canvas. You’re not the only one. I’ve seen other couples walking around with cameras, just like us. It’s like everyone’s here to take in the beauty. Maybe we should go explore more of the area. I feel like we’ve only scratched the surface.

So, do you remember that film we watched last year? The one with the guy who gets stuck in a time loop? I thought it was brilliant, but I couldn’t help but notice how much the protagonist hated cyclists. Like, every time he saw one, he just lost it. Oh yeah, I remember that. I mean, the movie was pretty good, but honestly, I found it a bit ridiculous. Why would someone hate cyclists so much? I mean, they’re just people riding bikes. It’s not like they’re attacking him or anything. It’s just… a bit of a stretch. I know, right? But I think it was supposed to be a metaphor for how people can be so frustrated with things they can’t control. Like, the protagonist is stuck in this loop, and the cyclists are like the little annoyances in his life that he can’t avoid. It’s kind of symbolic, if you think about it. Hmmm, maybe. But I still think it’s a bit over the top. I mean, I’ve had my fair share of close calls with cyclists, but I don’t go around hating them. I just stay calm and let them pass. It’s not like they’re going to hit me or anything. I mean, unless I’m being really reckless – which I’m not. Yeah, I guess that’s the thing. It’s not about hating the whole group, it’s about being aware of your surroundings. I mean, I work in a place where there are a lot of cyclists, and I’ve learned to be more careful. But it’s not like I can just avoid them all the time. Exactly. And besides, I think the film was more about the protagonist’s personal issues than the cyclists themselves. I mean, he was dealing with a lot of stress and pressure, and the cyclists were just the catalyst. It’s like he was looking for someone to blame. That’s a good way to look at it. I think it’s easy to take out our frustrations on people who aren’t even responsible for our problems. Like, if you’re stressed at work, why take it out on a stranger on a bike? Exactly. I’ve definitely been there. Sometimes I just go out of my way to be rude or short with people I don’t even know.

You know, I just thought of something – do you remember that time we tried to grow marigolds in the garden last year? I swear they were the only flowers that survived the frost. Oh, I remember. You were so excited about them, and you even wrote a whole blog post about it. "The Resilience of Marigolds in the Face of Adversity." It was adorable. I know, I know! I got a few likes, but honestly, it’s just a hobby. I mean, I’m a lecturer, not a botanist. But I do love the idea of growing things, you know? It’s so different from sitting in front of a screen all day. I get you. I think that’s what makes us so compatible – we both love the idea of doing things with our hands, whether it's in the lab or in the garden. I mean, even when I was doing my research on cash crops, I was always thinking about how they could be grown sustainably. That’s true. It’s interesting how the economics of farming tie into everything. I remember one of my students talking about how some farmers in Norfolk are moving away from traditional crops like wheat and barley and going for things like rapeseed or even strawberries. It’s all about diversification, isn’t it? Exactly. And it’s not just about money, it’s about climate change too. You know, with the weather getting more unpredictable, you have to be adaptable. I think that’s why some of the smaller farms are doing better – they’re not as rigid. It’s also surprising how much the language of farming has changed. I mean, I remember my granddad talking about “the good old days” when you just planted a seed and hoped for the best. Now you’ve got to track soil pH, crop rotation, and even think about carbon footprints. Yeah, it's fascinating. I think that’s one of the reasons I love research – there’s always something new to learn. I was reading about how some farmers are using AI to predict yields and manage their land more efficiently. It’s a bit mind-blowing, but also really cool. I can see how that would go hand in hand with your work. It’s not just about the data, it’s about making sense of it in a real-world context.

So, do you know if we’ve got anything sorted for the weekend? I was just thinking about the football match we were supposed to go to. Not yet, honestly. I’ve been trying to get my head around the parking situation. I know the match is on Saturday, but I’ve heard it’s going to be a bit of a nightmare with all the fans coming in. Yeah, I’ve heard that too. I think they’ve got some new parking arrangements this year. I remember someone mentioning something about a dedicated car park near the stadium. But I’m not sure. I’ve been thinking about it, honestly. I was just talking to my cousin, and he said he managed to get a spot by arriving early. He said it’s not impossible, just a bit of a hustle. That’s what I was thinking. Maybe we should plan to get there early. Wait, do you remember that time we tried to park at the last match and ended up driving around for an hour? It was a disaster. Oh, don’t even mention it. I remember we had to park on the side of the road, and it was like a parking lot of chaos. I still have nightmares about that. I remember when we got there and the car was practically wedged between two other cars. I had to get out and walk the entire way to the stadium. It was ridiculous. And we were both wearing the same team colours, so someone almost thought we were part of the crowd. I thought I was going to get mobbed. I know, and then we got to the match and it was like we had missed the whole game. It was so stressful. I still haven’t forgiven myself for that. But maybe this time we’ll be better prepared. I was thinking of asking around for some tips. My sister’s got a friend who’s a regular at the games. That’s a good idea. But I was also wondering about the Angel of the North. I think we should make a trip up there. You know, just for a bit of a break. It’s one of those places that really sticks in your mind. Yeah, I’ve been meaning to go there. I remember seeing it from the motorway once. It was amazing.

So, do you know what’s been going on with the geese around the lake? I swear they’re like a whole flock of celebrities out there. Oh, I know! They’ve been doing this weird thing where they start migrating earlier than usual. It’s like they’re trying to get ahead of the season or something. Migrating? I thought they were just going back to where they came from. I mean, I’ve seen them fly over the field by my house every morning. They’re so loud, I can hear them from the kitchen. Yeah, but they’re not just flying over—those geese are like the real deal. I saw one of them on the news the other day, and it turned out to be one of the celebrities from the trials. D’you know, the one who turned up at the festival in Peterborough last summer? No way? I mean, I saw some of the trials on social media, but I didn’t think they were real. I mean, why would anyone want to do that? Well, it’s not just about the trials anymore. It’s like they’ve become a whole thing. People are going out watching them, taking videos, and then posting them online. It’s wild. I still think it’s all a bit much. I mean, I love birds, but I don’t know what the big deal is with these geese. They’re just birds. Yeah, but they are wild birds, and they do things that make you go, “Oh, wow.” I mean, I’ve seen them honking in the middle of the night, and I swear they sound like they’re having a conversation. I know, and some of them are so brave. I mean, they’ll fly right up to the edge of the road and just stand there, like they own the place. You know, I used to think all wild birds were the same, but now I see how different they are. Like, I’ve seen a sparrow once trying to catch a piece of bread from my plate, and it almost looked like it was laughing at me. Oh, go on—you’re making it up. No, I’m not. It was the most ridiculous thing. I swear, it looked like it was trying to be clever. I didn’t even know sparrows could do that. It’s funny how we talk about wild birds like they’re people.

So, do you know what’s happening with the baby? I mean, I know it’s not  my  baby, but I’ve heard you’ve been talking about it a lot lately. Oh, it’s all very exciting! We’re due in about six weeks. I can’t believe it’s actually happening. I feel like I’m still in the first trimester, but I’ve already started nesting. I’ve been cleaning the flat like mad, and I even bought a new baby blanket. It’s all so overwhelming, isn’t it? I can only imagine. I had a baby once, but it was a long time ago—like,  way  back when I was still working in the school system. I still remember the first time I held my daughter. It was surreal, to be honest. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s one thing to plan for it, and another to actually be in the middle of it. I’m just trying to figure out what to do with my time now. I mean, I still have to go to work, but I feel like I need to start preparing. Do you have any advice? Honestly, I think the best thing is to just take it one day at a time. I was so worried about everything—diapers, feeding schedules, sleep deprivation, and then there was the whole thing with the grandparents. Oh, and did you know that my mother-in-law actually tried to take over the baby’s routine? It was a disaster. No way! That sounds chaotic. I can’t imagine that. I mean, I have my parents helping out, but they’re still in the UK, so it’s not like I can just call them every day. I’m worried about the job interviews I have coming up too. Have you heard about the new teaching roles? Yeah, I have. I think there’s been a lot of movement in the education sector lately. They’ve been trying to modernize the curriculum a bit, which is both exciting and a bit terrifying. I’ve got an interview next week for a language teaching position in Manchester. I hope it goes well. That’s great! I wish I had the courage to apply for something new. I’ve been thinking about moving back to the Midlands, but I don’t know if I’m ready for a big change.

So, do you ever think about what’s going to happen in the next five or ten years? Like, what’s the future going to look like? I think about it all the time, honestly. I mean, with everything that’s going on in the world — climate change, politics, technology — it’s hard not to. But do you ever get worried about what it’s going to be like for us? Yeah, I do. I mean, I’m not sure what the world’s going to be like when we’re older. I keep thinking about how things are changing so fast. Like, the way we work, the way we communicate, even the way we live our lives. It’s wild, isn’t it? I remember when I was in school, everyone was talking about the future — like, how we’d all be living in smart homes, flying cars, and robots doing all our work. But now I wonder if some of that is actually going to happen, or if it’s just fantasy. I mean, some of it  is  happening. Like, the way we use technology is changing every day. But I worry about the downsides. Like, what happens when everything is automated? Will there be jobs left for people like us? Yeah, that’s a real concern. I mean, I work in admin, and I’m not sure how long that’s going to be a viable career. I guess it’s not just about automation — it’s also about the way companies are moving towards remote work, and how that’s affecting people’s livelihoods. Exactly. I think the future is going to be a mix of exciting and terrifying. On one hand, we have all these new technologies that can improve our lives — like AI, renewable energy, and medical breakthroughs. But on the other hand, it’s all so uncertain. I don’t even know if I’m going to be in the same job in five years. I guess that’s the beauty of it, though — it’s unpredictable. You can’t plan too far ahead, but that’s also what makes it so interesting. I mean, I’ve always been someone who likes to plan, but now I’m learning to be more adaptable. I know what you mean. I used to think about my career in such a specific way, but now I’m like, ‘Maybe I don’t need to have it all figured out.’

So, do you know what’s up with Lucy? She’s been acting so weird lately. I think she’s got a boyfriend now, but she keeps saying she doesn’t. It’s so confusing. Yeah, I noticed too. She’s been spending a lot of time with this guy named Tom. I saw them at the café last week, and he was just… there. Like, always. It’s like he’s got a secret or something. Wait, isn’t Tom the one who used to ask her out all the time? He always said he was going to ask her to the prom, but then he never did. And now he’s just… popping up out of nowhere? Exactly! And then there’s this new girl, Emily. She’s from Cambridge, right? I think she’s the one who’s been sitting with Lucy at the library all the time. I don’t even know if they’re friends or if it’s something else. I heard they were in the same group project last semester. But I thought Emily was more into her studies than relationships. She’s got that graduate degree, for goodness’ sake. Yeah, but I think she’s just as into boys as the rest of us. She’s been making all these “casual” comments about being single, but I think she’s just trying to get attention. Anyway, what do you think? Do you think Lucy’s actually in love or is she just faking it? Honestly, I think she’s just trying to keep everyone guessing. She’s so into the whole “mystery” thing. I mean, she’s got this way of making everyone think she’s got it all figured out, but really, she’s just as clueless as the rest of us. I think part of it is jealousy. I mean, she’s always been the one who gets all the attention. Maybe she’s just insecure now that she’s not the center of the group anymore. Or maybe it’s just that she’s trying to keep up with the rest of us who are already in relationships. Or maybe it’s just that she’s not ready to settle down yet. I mean, she’s still in college, right? She’s got time. But I still think it’s weird that she’s so vague about everything. You’d think she’d want to talk about it.

Alright, let’s see, what’s for dinner? I thought we’d have spaghetti again, but if you don’t mind, I could make something else. No, that’s fine. Spaghetti is good. I’m quite hungry. Did you bring the pasta from the shop? I did. I picked it up on the way home from work. And I also got some fresh herbs from the market. I thought we could make it a bit more interesting than usual. Cool, that sounds nice. I was just thinking about what we could do this weekend. I’ve got a few mates coming over, and I was wondering if we could go to the hockey match on Saturday. That’s a good idea. I’m not sure if I’ll be able to go, though. I’ve got a meeting with a client that might run late. But if I can manage it, I’ll try to be there. Yeah, I’ll be there for sure. I’ve been looking forward to it. It’s a local team, right? Yeah, the Fradley Wolves. They’ve been doing pretty well this season. They might even qualify for the next round. I’ve been following them a bit. That’s awesome. I remember when we used to go to their games when I was younger. It used to be a big deal in the village. We’d all gather around and cheer them on. Definitely. Our parents used to take us to the games when we were kids. It was one of those traditions. Even though I haven’t gone in a while, I still feel a bit nostalgic about it. I know what you mean. I think the team’s the same, but the atmosphere is different now. It’s more like a proper match now with better facilities and stuff. Yeah, and there’s more interest in the sport now. I think it’s growing. I’ve been talking to some of the younger kids about it. They seem really passionate about it. That’s good to hear. I’ve been trying to get back into hockey myself. I’ve been playing with a few mates from school. It’s a bit rusty, but I’m getting back into it. That’s great. If you’re serious about it, you could even think about joining a team or something. There are a few local clubs that you could try out for.

So, do you remember that time last summer when we all went to that family gathering in Brighton and my cousin tried to explain the whole ‘transgender’ thing like it was a football match? It was so awkward. Oh, I remember that! You know, I was sitting next to my aunt and she just started nodding like she understood everything, but I could see she was completely confused. And my cousin kept saying, “It’s just like changing your name, really!” like it was a simple thing. Yeah, and then my uncle just said, “So, does that mean you’re not a man anymore?” and everyone just froze. I mean, we were all sitting there, trying to figure out if it was a joke or if he was being serious. It was ridiculous. You know, I think my brother-in-law actually got it. He just said, “So, if you’re a woman, then you’re a woman, right?” and then everyone laughed, even though it was kind of a weird way to say it. But he was trying to be supportive. Yeah, he’s always been the one who’s not afraid to say what he thinks. It’s funny how some people get so defensive about it, but others just don’t even know where to start. I guess it’s all about how you approach the conversation. Exactly. I think it’s part of the problem that we’re not really talking about it enough. Like, if you’re not someone who’s been through it, you don’t know how to react. I mean, I’m not saying it’s easy, but I think the more people talk about it, the better we’ll understand it. I agree. I think it’s also the fact that we’re so used to certain gender roles. Like, suddenly telling someone they’re not the gender they were born into is a huge shift. It’s hard to wrap your head around at first. And I think it’s also something that’s happening more and more in our families. You know, my cousin’s partner is a trans woman, and they’re just so open about it. I think it’s good that they’re not hiding it, but sometimes it’s still hard for some people to accept. I think it’s getting better though. Maybe one day, people will just accept it without all the drama.

Alright, do you want some chicken kievs? I made a few extra just in case. Yeah, I’ll take one. I’m starving after that football game today. Oh, you were at the rugby match? I heard it was a thrilling game. Yeah, it was. I mean, it was a good game, but I’m still not sure who won. I think it was Wales, but I might be wrong. No, it was Ireland. They beat Wales in the end. You should’ve come along, mate. I know, I know. I just didn’t feel like going. It’s been a bit of a stressful week. You’ve been working too much. You need to relax, take a break. So, do you think we should go to the local market tomorrow? I saw they’ve got a real vintage section. Definitely. I was thinking about it too. So, do you think the bank is going to be okay with that deposit we made last week, Dad? I mean, it’s not like we’re doing anything illegal or anything, right? Oh, I don’t think we’re in the same boat as those people who’re getting caught for money laundering. We’re just, you know, helping the family out a bit. Yeah, but you’ve got to be careful, you know. If you’re not being transparent, then you’re setting yourself up for trouble. And with the way the banks are now, they’re always watching. If something looks suspicious, they’ll flag it. Even if it’s just a few transfers here and there. Yeah, and with the way the government’s cracking down on tax evasion and everything, you don’t want to be the one who gets caught in the middle of it. Especially with the fines they’re handing out now. I had a client who got fined for not keeping proper records. It was a small business, but the fine was over £10,000. Wow. That’s a lot. I can’t even imagine how that would affect someone’s life. I mean, if you’re not careful, it could affect your ability to get your own business started.

So, do you think we’ll get any rain today? It’s been so dry lately, and I’m starting to worry about the garden. So, do you know where the best sandwich place is around here? I’ve been trying to find a decent lunch spot, and I’m not exactly a fan of the café food. So, do you think we've got everything sorted for the Mongolia rally yet? I was just checking through the list again, and I’m not sure if we’ve got all the visa applications done. So, did you hear? Anon’s arm is still in a sling. Seriously? I thought it was just a minor injury. Yeah, I heard he went to the hospital last night. So, did you enjoy the anniversary party yesterday? Yeah, it was good. A bit chaotic, but fun. I know, it was a bit of a mess, but it was nice to see everyone. Especially the kids. I mean, even though it was a mess, I think people felt happy. That’s the main thing. We all just wanted to celebrate and spend time together. I guess that’s what makes it special, isn’t it?

Dad, do you remember when we were moving house last year? I think we had to get a new washing machine and everything was so chaotic. I just got a new client, and it’s been a bit of a nightmare trying to get the audio files sorted. I mean, some of them are so poor quality, I can barely understand a word. It's like they recorded it in a washing machine or something. Yeah, I’ve been in the same boat. I had to transcribe a meeting where the person was basically speaking through a phone on a train. I had to ask them to repeat it three times, and even then, it was still a mess. You’d think with the tech we have now, people would know how to record properly. I’ve heard that before. I used to work in the education sector, and we had to deal with all sorts of audio recordings from students. Some of them were so muffled, I had to play the audio back and forth just to get the words right. It was like trying to read a book written in Braille. I can imagine. I’ve had to listen to some of my own work, and even I can’t make out what I said half the time. I suppose it’s a bit of a curse being self-employed. You don’t get as much time to focus on the details as someone in a more structured job. I mean, I’m a carpenter, so most of my work is hands-on. I don’t get to sit around listening to audio all day. It’s not just about the quality. There’s also the issue of the format. Sometimes people send you files in formats you can’t even open. I had one file that was a .wav file, but it was actually a .mp3 with a .wav extension. I had to spend an hour trying to figure out what was going on. I almost gave up on that one. That sounds frustrating. I know that sometimes you get audio files that are unlabelled or just have generic names like “Recording 1” or “Audio_001.” It’s like trying to find a needle in a haystack. You have no idea what you’re looking at, and you just have to figure it out on your own. I think a lot of people don’t realize how much work it takes to transcribe something properly. It’s not just about typing words down; it’s about understanding context, picking up on tone, and even recognizing accents.

Alright, do you two remember what we were going to do for Mother’s Day? I think we had a plan... or was it just a vague idea? I think we were going to take a trip to the Forest School. I remember you said something about it being a great way to get out of the house and spend some quality time with the kids. Yeah, and also, I think you wanted to make a special lunch for Mummy. I remember you saying something about making a cake or something sweet. What was it again? Oh, right! I had this idea of making a special Mother’s Day cake. I was going to do something with fruit and maybe some candles on it. But honestly, I’m not sure I’m up for it. I’ve been feeling a bit off lately. I think it’s okay if you don’t make the cake. We can still do something special. Maybe we can just go to the Forest School and have a picnic. That way, we can enjoy the sunshine and be outside. Yeah, and maybe we could tell some stories or play some games. I remember you used to tell us those silly jokes about idioms. You said something like “it’s raining cats and dogs” and then explained it. Can you do that again? Oh, I remember that one! It’s a common idiom, but people often don’t know what it really means. It’s a way of saying it’s raining very heavily. I think it started in the 17th century, and people thought that the cats and dogs were actually falling from the sky during heavy rain. That’s so cool! I never thought about where idioms came from. I wonder if there are more like that. Like, what about “the ball is in your court”? What does that mean? Oh, that one means it’s your turn to take action. It started in sports, where the ball would be passed to the other team, and it was their turn to play. So when someone says “the ball is in your court,” they mean it’s your move. That’s really interesting! I think I’ll try to remember some of these idioms and use them when I’m talking to my friends. They’ll be impressed. You’d be surprised how much people enjoy hearing idioms.

I just got a call from my sister. She's been really down lately. She's been dealing with some serious health issues again. Oh no, what's going on? Is she okay? She's been diagnosed with cancer again. It's the same type she had a few years ago, and it's come back. It's really hard on her. That's awful. I'm so sorry to hear that. How is she coping? She's trying her best, but it's tough. She's always been strong, but this time it's different. She’s not as energetic as she used to be. She’s been spending a lot of time with her kids, trying to make the most of what she has. They’re all trying to be strong, but they’re not immune to the stress. My niece is only 16, and she’s taking it really hard. She’s been asking questions about what happens next, and it’s breaking her heart. It’s so hard to explain things to children in a way that’s honest but not too harsh. Yeah, that’s really tough. That’s why I’m just trying to be there for her as much as I can. She wants to talk, she wants to feel supported. We’ve been going for walks in the park, just to take her mind off things. She’s starting to get more hopeful again, thanks to the treatment. That’s good to hear. Maybe that’s the key, isn’t it? Keeping things as normal as possible, even when things are difficult. It helps them feel like life is still going on. Yeah, I think that’s the best we can do. We can’t take the cancer away, but we can take the pain away with our love and support. Exactly. And it’s not just about the illness. It’s about being there for each other, even when it feels like the world is falling apart. That’s the thing, isn’t it?

So, did you get the lecture notes from the linguistics class today? I was supposed to go through them before our study group meeting, but I got distracted by the new episode of  Game of Thrones . Yeah, I got them, but honestly, I’m still trying to wrap my head around the topic on language acquisition and how it differs across cultures. I think it’s fascinating, but honestly, I feel like I’m just reading the same old stuff over and over again. I know what you mean. It’s like the same content every week, just with different examples. But I think it’s actually helping me get a better grasp on how language learning is affected by social and environmental factors. You know, the whole thing about how people in South Korea are so obsessed with English, especially the younger generation. Yeah, I remember reading an article about that in one of the assigned readings. It said that in South Korea, English is seen as a gateway to success, so people are really pushing for it, even if it’s not the most natural way to learn. It’s interesting how it’s not just about grammar or vocabulary—it’s about identity and social status. Exactly. And I’ve heard that in China too, English is considered a second language, but the way it's taught is very different from how it's done in the UK. It’s more about rote memorization and tests, right? I think so. And I’ve been thinking about how that affects someone’s ability to actually use the language in real-life situations. Like, I mean, if you’re just memorizing vocabulary and grammar rules, but you’re never actually using the language to communicate, how do you become fluent? That’s a good point. I mean, I’m an English language instructor, so I know that teaching grammar and vocabulary is important, but without the context of real-life communication, it’s just like learning a song without knowing the meaning. It’s all about practice and exposure. I guess that’s why I’m so into studying linguistics. It’s such a broad field, and it really connects to so many different aspects of life—culture, history, even technology. I mean, think about how social media and online communication have changed the way we use language now. Definitely.

It’s all just a big, confusing mess.

So, do you remember that time last summer when we got stuck on the motorway for three hours? Oh, I remember that! It was one of those days where the traffic was absolutely gridlocked, and we were just sitting there, like, "What even is happening?" I think it was the guy in the car behind us too. We were all just so stressed out, and it felt like everyone was trying to blame each other for the delay. It was like a total scene. I was just trying to read a book, and then I looked up and saw this guy with a dog in the back seat. Like, the dog was actually more relaxed than me. That’s gold. I remember that. He didn’t even look stressed. Maybe he was just glad he wasn’t stuck in the same traffic as us. Anyway, what were we doing that day again? I think we were heading to that weekend market in Milton Keynes. Yeah, that’s right. We were supposed to meet up with some friends, but we ended up getting stuck on the way. It was like the whole journey was a joke. I mean, it was funny in a way. I think I ended up laughing so hard that I almost cried. You know, like, the kind of laugh where you’re still laughing even when you’re exhausted. I know exactly what you mean. I used to do that all the time when I was in university. There was this one time when I got lost in the city center and ended up walking for two hours, but I was just laughing so hard I didn’t even care. You know, I think that’s what makes those moments so memorable. Even when things go wrong, they become stories you can laugh about later. Absolutely. I think that’s why we still talk about it. Even though it was a disaster, it’s kind of a funny memory. I guess it’s like how people say "the best laid plans of mice and men often go awry." You never really know what’s going to happen, but sometimes the unexpected stuff ends up being the best part.

Well, I've been feeling rather under the weather these past few days. I've got this terrible cough that won't seem to go away, and I've been feeling pretty run-down. I think we’re due for a bit of a break from this rain, though. It's been going on for weeks now. Yeah, I know. I've been trying to get some outdoor time, but it's just too wet. It's a bit over the top, but it's nice to have. You're joking, aren't you? A smart kettle? That's not something I'd ever consider. I still have a regular kettle, and it works just fine. I mean, I can’t be bothered with all that fancy tech. I know, I know. But I think it's the future, you know? It's just a matter of time before everyone is using smart devices. I mean, even my kettle knows when to boil. It’s like the kettle has a brain. Well, I have to admit, it's a bit of a novelty. I don't use it much, but I did try it out the other day. It’s surprising how quickly it boils the water. I think it's probably more efficient than the old ones. Exactly. Plus, it's got an app. You can even set it to boil at a certain time. I set mine to boil in the morning so I can make a cup of tea when I wake up.

So, do you know if Lucy is going to be coming over for dinner this week? I was just thinking we should all catch up properly, you know, like we used to before everyone got so busy with work and stuff. I don’t think she’s confirmed yet, but she mentioned something about it on Facebook the other day. I think she’s got a bit of a backlog of stuff to do before she can make it. But if we all get together, I’m sure she’d come. Yeah, and we should probably do it soon before the whole wedding thing starts getting too big. I mean, we’ve already got Mary and Paul coming over, and we need to make sure everything’s set for the actual day. It’s going to be a bit overwhelming if we don’t get some time to just chill and catch up properly. Definitely. I remember when we all got together last month, we ended up talking for hours about the weather, which was so weird. But I think it was nice to just have a normal conversation without the pressure of planning or anything. Exactly, you know? It’s funny how quickly things can change. Like, one minute you’re just hanging out, and the next thing you know, you’re getting married and planning a whole new life. I can’t believe it’s actually happening. I know, right? It’s all so surreal. I mean, I never thought I’d be getting married at 26, let alone in a few months. But then again, maybe that’s just the way it is now. People are getting married younger than ever. Hey, don’t start that. I’m not even fully committed yet, and I’m 27. I’m just saying, it’s not like we’re not doing anything. I mean, I’m still figuring out if I want kids or not, and I’m not even sure if I want to get married at all. Come on, you know you’re not going to survive without a partner. It’s just the way things are. And besides, you’re already planning to move out of Peterborough with your new job. So you might as well do the whole thing. I’m not saying I’m against marriage or anything, but I think it’s more about timing.

Well, I've been trying to get my computer to work properly for days now, Peggy. I think it's gone off again. I tried to email the doctor about my back, but it just keeps freezing. Oh, don’t you worry, Arthur. You’ll get it sorted out. I remember when I was your age, we used to sit and write letters by hand. No emails, no computers. Just pen and paper. That’s true, Peggy. I used to write to my sister every week. She lives in Yorkshire. But now, I just get so frustrated with these gadgets. I don’t understand half of it. I can’t even get the TV to work properly these days. You know, I’ve got a new tablet. It’s got a lot of apps for teaching, but I still find it tricky. I think I’m going to start by just learning how to use the basic functions. Maybe I’ll take some online courses. Online courses? That’s a good idea, Colin. I was thinking the same thing. I’ve got a friend who’s got a book on how to use computers. I’m going to ask him to teach me. That sounds like a good plan. I tried learning on my own once, but it just made me more confused. I think I’d rather have someone to show me step by step. Yeah, I agree. You know what I found strange, though? My granddaughter’s got a tablet. She uses it for games and watching videos. I tried to teach her how to do some basic things, but she just laughs at me. That’s funny, Arthur. My son’s got a tablet too. He uses it for work, but he still plays games on it. I think it’s a good way to keep the mind active. It’s not all bad, you know. True, Colin. I used to play cards with the neighbours. But now, the only people I see are my grandchildren. They come over every weekend, and they always bring their games with them. That’s nice, Peggy. I do miss the days when we all used to gather round the table for a game of bridge. Now, it’s all about screens and gadgets. It’s a bit of a change, but I suppose it’s the way things are going. I think we’ll all have to adapt.

So, how’s the weather been down in Essex? I heard it’s been quite damp this week. Oh, it’s been the usual, love. Not too bad, but the damp has been doing its usual thing. I’ve had to take the dog out more than usual to make sure he doesn’t get too mucky. That’s always the thing with the weather, isn’t it? One minute it’s sunny, the next it’s drizzle. Aye, and you know what I say? It’s all part of the charm. You can’t have everything, can you? That’s true. I suppose it’s better than the south of England, where it’s always too hot or too cold. Oh, you’ve been to the south? A few times, actually. I taught in Brighton for a while. The sun was brilliant, but the traffic in the summer was a nightmare. Oh, I can imagine. I once had to drive from Hereford to London just to get a cup of tea, and I got stuck in gridlock for over an hour. That’s not something I’d ever want to experience. No, it’s not. But I suppose, like everything, it’s all part of the journey. Speaking of journeys, I’ve been thinking about going on a weekend trip somewhere. Maybe a bit of a change of scenery. That sounds like a good idea. Where’re you thinking of going? I was thinking of going up to the Lake District. I’ve never been there, and I’ve heard it’s beautiful this time of year. Oh, that’s a lovely place. I used to go there with my family when I was a kid. We’d go fishing and sit by the lakes. It was peaceful. That sounds idyllic. I’d love to do that. I’ve been reading about the local pubs and the countryside. Oh, you should try the one in Ambleside. It’s got a great view of the mountains and the people there are very friendly. I’ll have to remember that. I’m also thinking of trying out some local food. I’ve heard the fish and chips there are second to none. You won’t be disappointed. I’d say it’s worth the trip. But don’t go alone, love. You’ll need someone to keep an eye on you. Don’t worry, I’ll have a friend or two with me.

So, did you go out on Friday? I haven’t seen you all week. No, I didn’t go out. I stayed in and watched some movies. You know, I think I watched three or four. Not sure which ones, honestly. Oh, that’s not fair. You were supposed to go out with someone. It’s Valentine’s Day, for goodness’ sake! I know, I know! I just got so stressed about it. I was trying to figure out what to do, and then I just decided to do what I always do—nothing. That’s not really  nothing , though. You’re watching movies, right? You can’t just say you didn’t go out because you watched a few films on your own. Okay, fair point. I guess it’s just that I felt so anxious about it. Like, what if I ended up with someone I didn’t like? Or worse—what if I ended up alone? Have you even tried to do anything? I mean, you could’ve gone out with someone from the café or the library. I mean, we all know that people still go out on Valentine’s Day, even if they’re not in love. Yeah, I know. I just felt like I didn’t have the energy. Plus, I was really busy studying. I’m trying to get my assignments done before the weekend. I get that, but you should’ve gone out anyway. It’s not like you’re alone. It’s Friday night, and there’s a whole world out there. Or at least, a cinema. You’re right. I think I did miss out on something. Although, I watched  The Shape of Water  and  La La Land —they were both pretty good. I mean, not as good as  Crazy, Stupid, Love  though. Oh, you’ve got to watch  Crazy, Stupid, Love . It’s the ultimate Valentine’s Day movie. I watched it last year, and it made me feel all emotional. Even though I was alone, I still felt like someone was there with me. I’ve heard it’s good, but I’ve never actually seen it. Maybe I’ll check it out next time. You should. It’s like the perfect combination of romance and comedy. And it’s got all the right accents too—British and American, it’s like a fusion of our dialects! Oh, that sounds amazing.

So, do you think the housing crisis is just a symptom of capitalism or is it something deeper? I mean, it feels like it's not just about supply and demand anymore. I think it's a mix of both. Capitalism, in its current form, definitely plays a role. With property being treated like an asset, people are more incentivized to buy rather than rent. But I also think there's a structural issue in how housing policy has been handled over the years. It's not just about money; it's about power and control. Yeah, I agree. And then there's the racism angle. I’ve heard a lot about how certain areas are gentrified, and that often leads to displacement of long-term residents, especially people of color. It’s like the same system is being used to push marginalized communities out. Exactly. I remember reading an article about how Black and South Asian communities in London are more likely to be affected by rent hikes and evictions. It’s not just about having a home—it’s about belonging and security. And that’s something that’s being deliberately undermined. I think that’s one of the most frustrating parts. It feels like the system is rigged for the people who already have power. I mean, I’m in a higher professional occupation, so I can afford a decent place, but I know people who are in similar situations but can’t even afford to live in the same area. Yeah, it’s been a real eye-opener. I work in journalism, so I often read about these issues, but it’s one thing to read about it and another to see it happening in your own neighborhood. I mean, I live in Kensal Rise, and I’ve seen the changes over the years. It’s like watching a slow-motion disaster. I know what you mean. I live in Watford, and even there, there are signs that the city is starting to change. I mean, it’s not as bad as some of the other areas, but it’s still worrying. I think people are starting to realize that the housing crisis isn’t just about being poor—it’s about systemic inequality. That’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s not something that can be fixed with just a few policy changes. It’s deep-rooted and requires a complete overhaul of how we approach housing and wealth distribution.

So, do you know when you're going to start nursery for the baby? I just wanted to check if you’ve got any plans yet. Yeah, I think I’m going to start next month. I’ve got a few places to look at, and I’m waiting for the nursery to confirm the availability. I was thinking of going with one that’s closer to the house, so it’s not too far from work. That makes sense. I remember when I had my kids, it was so hard to find a place that fit my schedule. Didn’t you want to start earlier? I know, I wanted to, but I kept putting it off because I was worried about how it would affect the baby’s routine. I’m still a bit nervous, honestly. I mean, I know it’s good for the baby to be out of the house sometimes, but it’s still hard to leave them. I get that. It’s a big step. But I think it’s better to start early than to wait too long. You’ll get used to it, and the baby will, too. I remember when I first dropped my daughter off, I cried for the whole morning. But after a while, it got easier. I hope so. I’ve also been thinking about when I’m going back to work. I know I’ll have to do some part-time hours at first, but I’m not sure if I’ll be back full-time. That’s totally understandable. It’s a big decision. You don’t want to feel like you’re not giving enough to the baby, but you also need to be able to support yourself. Maybe you can take some time off and then gradually come back? Yeah, that’s something I’ve been considering. I’ve been looking into some part-time roles that are more flexible. I think I can manage it, but I’m still not sure. It’s so much to think about. You’re not alone in this, love. We’ll figure it out together. And I’m sure the baby will grow up to be a happy, well-adjusted kid with all the support you can give. Thanks, Mum. I really appreciate you being here for me. I can go back to work, but I need to be sure it doesn’t take away from the quality time I can give the baby.

So, did you get the chance to talk to the police about that incident at the store last week? I did, actually. They took a statement, and it's all pretty straightforward. I mean, it was a misunderstanding, wasn’t it? Yeah, I heard. I think the customer was just being difficult. I mean, I can’t believe someone would accuse a store manager of something like that. I know, right? It’s just a bad day. But you know, I was thinking—maybe we should all take a step back and try not to get too worked up about it. It’s not like we’re in the police force or anything. I agree. But I still feel like the system is biased. I mean, if you’re not from the right background, you get treated like a criminal just for being in the wrong place at the wrong time. That’s a bit harsh, isn’t it? I mean, we’re all just doing our jobs. I know it’s frustrating, but I think we should just focus on moving forward. Yeah, but it’s not just about moving forward. It’s about making sure we’re not being taken advantage of. I mean, I’ve seen it happen before. People get accused of things, and then it just goes on and on. I know what you mean. I’ve dealt with some pretty unfair situations in my role as a director. It’s one of the downsides of the job, honestly. But I think we should all try to stay calm and not let it get to us. That’s the thing, though. I don’t want to be the one standing up for myself all the time. I just want to be able to do my job without having to fight every day. I get that. But we can’t let it define us. I mean, we all have our challenges. I had a few issues with the EE phone bill last month too. You know, the one where they kept charging me for something I didn’t use. Oh yeah, I remember that. Was it fixed? Not yet. I’ve been trying to go through the process, but it’s been a bit of a nightmare. I just want to get that sorted out. I’ve had some issues with that too. I mean, I’ve had to call them multiple times, and it never feels like they’re listening.

So, how’s the new life treating you, ANON? I heard you got married, and you’re living in Bedford now. It’s good, yeah. I mean, it’s a bit of a change from the old flat, but it’s nice to have my own place. Plus, I’ve got my own garden to look after, so I feel like I’m actually doing something useful now. That’s great! I’ve got a friend who’s a gardener, and he said it’s not all just digging in the dirt. He said it’s like therapy. You know, like, you get out there, you plant something, and then you watch it grow. It’s kind of like… Like a meditation? Yeah, I suppose. I mean, I do get a bit of a zen vibe when I’m out there with the plants. Although, sometimes it’s more like a war zone when the weeds are coming in. I can imagine! You know, I’m kind of envious. I’m stuck teaching English to a bunch of people who don’t even speak it properly. I mean, I get a bit of a high when they actually start to grasp the language, but it’s not exactly the same as seeing a plant grow. I know what you mean. I mean, I’ve got a few herbs growing in the back, like rosemary and thyme. I’ve been using them in the kitchen lately. It’s funny, but I think the taste is a bit different than the ones you buy in the shop. Oh, I’ve been trying to make my own bread recently. I’ve got a mortar and pestle from my granddad, and I’ve been grinding my own flour. It’s a bit of a process, but I love the way it smells when it’s all done. That must be cool. I’ve been thinking about starting to bake too. I mean, I’ve got some nuts and chickpeas in the cupboard, so maybe I can make some hummus. I’ve never done it before, but I’ve seen it on a few TV shows. They show it like it’s the easiest thing in the world. Yeah, I tried it once. It was like a science experiment. I think I ended up with more of a paste than a hummus. But it’s worth it, right?

So, did you get your English test results back yet? Not yet, but I think I got a decent mark. I was pretty sure I knew most of the answers. Yeah, me too. I was so nervous about it, but I think I did okay. I mean, the test was really hard. There were so many questions about grammar and vocabulary. I know! I had to write an essay about a book we read in class. I wasn’t even sure what the question was asking. Oh no, that’s not fair! I couldn’t even finish the essay. I just kept getting distracted by the other kids talking. I remember you were like that in English lessons too. You’d be so focused on what the rest of the class was doing that you’d miss the teacher’s instructions. Yeah, I know! I’m always like that. But I’m getting better, I think. Well, maybe you should try joining the school orchestra. I heard they’re having a rehearsal tomorrow. The wind-band? I don’t know… I’ve never been into music much. Oh, come on! It’s not that bad. Plus, it’s a chance to meet some new people. I guess. But what if I can’t play anything? You don’t have to play anything. You can just sit in the back and listen. Besides, I heard the teacher’s really nice. Hmm… I’m not sure. I’m more into art than music. Yeah, I know. But the art lessons are so boring. I wish we had more French lessons instead. Yeah, I agree. I like French. It’s fun to learn new words and phrases. I wish we had more time for French. I think it’s one of the easiest subjects. I know! I can already say "bonjour" and "merci" pretty well. Yeah, but I still can’t say "au revoir" without messing up. You’re getting there though. Maybe you should practice more. I will. But I’m more worried about the English test. I don’t want to get a bad mark. Me neither. I’m hoping the teacher gives us some extra credit for the essay. Yeah, maybe. I think we should all study more for the next test. Agreed. I’m going to start reviewing my notes tonight. Me too. Yeah, let’s make sure we do well this time.

So, how’s the new job going, Sue? You said you were starting at the college next week? Oh, it’s not really a job, it’s more like a temporary thing. Got it because my old job at the school closed down, and they’re not taking me back. Got a bit of a rough time with the funding, I guess. Yeah, I heard that. A lot of schools are having trouble these days. Still, you’re lucky you got something, right? Yeah, and it’s not like it’s the worst place in the world. It’s a small college, but it’s got a good reputation. I’d rather do something like that than be stuck at home. I know, and I’m not really looking for anything else, I guess. Just trying to keep my head above water for now. I can’t say I blame you. I’ve been in education for a while, and it’s not easy, even if you’re not working. I mean, I still help out with the local community center sometimes, just to stay in the loop. That’s a good idea, actually. You’ve got a network, and it keeps you connected. I got a bit isolated after my last job. Still, I’m glad you’re getting something, Sue. Thanks, Claire. I don’t know what I’d do if I didn’t have this. I mean, I’ve got my pension, but it’s not enough. I’ve been thinking about taking up some part-time work at the hospital, you know, something in the community. That’s a good idea. I know a few people who work there, and they say the vibes are pretty good. Not the best pay, but you get the satisfaction of helping out. Yeah, that could work. And it’s not like you have to be up at the crack of dawn or anything. Just a few hours a week. I was thinking about that too. Maybe I’ll try it out. It’s better than sitting around the house all day. You know, I’ve got this idea for a weekend trip to the coast. I’ve been meaning to go to Filey or Scarborough for a while. Thought maybe we could go together. That sounds nice. It’s been a while since I’ve had a proper holiday. I’d love to get away for a bit.

So, do you think the government is doing anything about the obesity crisis? I mean, it’s everywhere now. I saw a news story about a local school having to ban crisps from their canteen. Yeah, I heard about that. It’s a bit extreme, but I get it. I mean, I used to eat a lot of snacks when I was younger. I used to think it was just part of life, but now I see the stats, it’s pretty scary. My mate Dave’s got type 2 diabetes, and he’s only 52. Oh no, that’s terrible. I mean, I’ve never been much of a snacker, but I do have a sweet tooth. I used to have a lot of chocolate. I guess I just never thought about the consequences. It’s not just about snacks. It’s about the whole lifestyle. I think we’re all guilty of it to some extent. I’ve been trying to cut back, but it’s hard when you’re surrounded by takeaways and fast food. I mean, even my lectures – do you know how many times I’ve had to explain to students that they’re not allowed to eat in the seminar room? It’s a mess. Yeah, I can imagine. You’re always trying to be professional, but the reality is, people act like it’s a free buffet. It’s funny, though. I remember when I was a kid, we didn’t have all this. We had to walk a mile to school, and the food was real. Now, people are just sitting in front of screens, eating junk and being lazy. That’s true. I think we’ve become so dependent on convenience. I mean, I still cook, but I’m not cooking for myself. My husband does that. I’m more of a consumer now. That’s a real problem. I think education is key. If people understand the health risks, they might make better choices. But I’m not sure it’s enough. I mean, I’ve seen the same habits in my own family. My sister’s always been a bit of a couch potato, and now she’s overweight. I think it’s a combination of genes and environment. I agree. I think it’s got a lot to do with genetics too. My mum’s got a family history of heart disease, and I’ve already had some issues.

I just can’t get my head around Moodle. I mean, I know it's an LMS, but every time I try to set up a module, it feels like I'm fighting the system. I know what you mean. It’s like it’s designed to be user-friendly, but somehow it’s the opposite. I’ve been trying to set up a new course this week, and it’s been a nightmare. I had to delete and redo the same thing three times. Yeah, I’ve been there. I remember the first time I tried to upload a file, it just wouldn’t work. I thought I had a virus or something. I ended up having to ask my IT support for help, and they said it was a permissions issue. So I had to change the file format, and then it worked. I think the worst part is that you feel like you’ve done everything right, but it just doesn’t go through. It’s frustrating because you’re supposed to be using it to make your life easier, not harder. Exactly. I mean, I get it’s supposed to streamline the process, but maybe I’m just not used to it. I’ve been using other platforms for years, like Blackboard or Canvas, and they’re a little more intuitive. I know what you mean. I tried using Canvas for a while, but the university switched to Moodle, and now I’m stuck with it. I’ve heard some people say it’s better than Canvas, but I haven’t seen it yet. It might be that it's just a matter of getting used to it. I think the more you use it, the more you start to understand how it works. I’ve been trying to use it more consistently now, and it’s starting to make a bit more sense. That’s the thing, isn’t it? You just have to keep going. I mean, if you’re teaching, you have to be able to use these tools. It’s part of the job. I suppose so. I just hope the system doesn’t break down completely. I had a student email me recently saying they couldn’t access their assignments because the link was broken. That’s not something I want to deal with. Yeah, I had a similar issue last week.

I can’t believe how much jetlag I’m still feeling. I swear, I think I’ve got a mini-time zone shift going on in my brain. I know, right? It’s like my body’s still in London and my mind is in Barcelona. But at least the baby’s sleeping through the night now, so that’s a win. Yeah, I’ve been trying to get used to the idea of her not waking up every two hours. It’s weird, but I think I’m starting to get the hang of it. Still, I’m exhausted, though. I totally get it. I feel like I’ve been running on autopilot all week. But hey, it’s worth it if it means we can actually get some sleep. And honestly, I’m ready for the weekend, even if it’s just lying in bed and pretending to be a human being. I’m with you on that. I’ve been thinking about our plans for the drama performance next week. We talked about going to that one at the local theatre. I mean, it’s not like we have a lot of options, but it’s something to look forward to. Yeah, and it’s not just about the show. It’s about getting out, getting some fresh air, and – most importantly – not having to worry about the baby for a few hours. I’m starting to think we should just go as a family. It’ll be nice to have the kids along, even if they’re just there to sit and watch. That actually sounds good. I think they’d like it. They’re both really into stories and characters. Plus, it’s a chance for us to all have a little adventure without any of the usual chaos. Exactly. I just hope we can get the timing right. I know it’s not the easiest thing to plan with a baby, but I’m willing to try. And if we can’t make it, I’m sure there will be another show soon enough. For sure. I’m just glad we’re both on the same page. It’s been a bit of a rollercoaster with the jetlag and the baby, but I think we’re getting through it. Just need to make sure we don’t go overboard on the coffee. Agreed. I think we’ve both had enough of that.

So, do you know if you’ve got any friends in Germany? I mean, I know you’ve been living here for a while, but I’ve heard you’ve got some family back in Kurdistan. Yeah, I’ve got a few friends in Germany, actually. They’re from the same area as me, so we’ve got a good connection. But I reckon most of my close friends are still in Iraq. A lot of them have been in the UK for years, working as translators or interpreters. That’s interesting. I always thought people from your background would be more spread out. I mean, with the political situation and everything. Yeah, it’s complicated. Some of them have been here for years, others are still back in Kurdistan. And I think the ones who are still there, they’re not exactly safe. The oil politics in the region are really unstable. You know, the Wahabi influence has been messing with a lot of things. I heard about that. It’s a bit of a hot topic, isn’t it? I mean, the way the oil is controlled, the way it’s used to fund different groups. It’s like a deadly game. Exactly. And then there’s Libya. I mean, the whole thing with Gaddafi, the way the oil was used to finance his regime. People like him are still around, but things have changed. It’s funny, isn’t it? You think about the Middle East and the way oil has shaped everything. But then you start thinking about what’s happening with young people these days. I mean, they’re more connected than ever, but are they really any better off? I don’t know. It depends on where you are. In some places, young people are heading to Europe or the US for better opportunities. But in others, they’re stuck in the same cycle. And then there are those who are just trying to survive. Do you think moving house is something you’ve considered? I mean, I know you mentioned you’re looking to get a visa, so maybe it’s a way to settle down. It’s on my mind. I’ve been thinking about it a lot. But it’s not just about the visa. It’s about the whole process. I’ve got a lot of friends who’ve tried to move, and it’s not always smooth.

I just love this roast lamb. It’s practically falling apart, isn’t it? Oh, it’s absolutely divine. I’ve been waiting for this all week. I think we’ve had a little too much of the same old stuff lately. Well, it’s not every day you get to eat something this good, especially with a bit of Scottish tablet on the side. Though I must say, I’m not sure if that’s a traditional pairing. Oh, it’s a bit of a family tradition. My mother used to make it every Sunday. She said it helped the whole house feel like a proper home. That’s sweet. You know, I’ve been thinking about going on that cruise we talked about. It’s been a while since I’ve had a real holiday, and I think it’s time. A cruise sounds lovely, but I’ve been meaning to take up some sort of workout routine. I don’t want to get too old before I even start. That’s admirable, but you should know, I’ve been thinking about starting one too. I’m not quite sure where to begin, though. Maybe you could try a local gym? I know there’s one near the office that’s quite good. Though I’ve heard they’re a bit pricey. Oh, I did consider that. But I was thinking more of doing some gardening or maybe even walking the dogs. It’s not about being in the best shape, it’s about staying active. That’s a good point. I think I’ve been a bit too sedentary lately, especially with all the transcribing I’ve been doing. Well, I can see how that would take its toll. I’ve been trying to keep myself busy with work, but I still feel like I’m not getting enough exercise. And with that, I think I’ve also been a bit too lenient with my rental situation. I’ve been living in this place for years, and I’m starting to feel like it’s time to find something a little more suited to my needs. I hear you. I’ve been thinking the same thing. I’ve been renting for so long, and I think it’s time to look into buying, or at least moving somewhere a bit more comfortable. It’s all so complicated, isn’t it?

So, do you think we should get a fridge? I mean, we’ve been eating out so much lately. It’s getting a bit expensive. Yeah, I mean, we can’t keep doing this. It’s not like we’re going to be here forever. We need to start thinking about proper living arrangements. I totally agree. I feel like we’re just surviving, not really living. I mean, I’ve got a part-time job, and I’m studying, but it’s not like I can just afford to buy groceries every week. I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about it too. I’ve been saving up for a fridge, actually. Maybe we could pool our money and get one together? That’s not a bad idea. I mean, if we all chip in, it’s not like we’re making a huge investment. Just something we can use, you know? Yeah, and it’ll make things easier. I mean, we’re all in the same boat here. We’re not exactly in the best financial shape. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about moving out. I mean, I’ve got a flatmate, but it’s not really working. We’re both in the same situation, so it’s just… messy. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to find a place to rent, but it’s not easy. The market’s not great, and the prices are through the roof. That’s not a good sign. I mean, if we’re all struggling to find a place, then the housing market is definitely not in our favor. I’ve been talking to my cousin about it. He’s got a flat in Manchester.
