He said it’s not the cheapest, but it’s doable. He’s even offering to help us with the deposit. That sounds like a good move. I mean, if we can get a place of our own, it’ll give us more control over our lives. We could actually cook, save money, and not have to rely on others. Yeah, and we could start thinking about university applications too. I mean, I’ve got a few options, and I go to a local college. I think it’s a good start. I’m still figuring out what I want to do. I’ve been thinking about applying for a degree, but I’m not sure if I can afford it.

Alright, so I’ve got this baking lesson tomorrow, and I need to bring something for the class. Do you think I should make some cupcakes or maybe a cake? Cupcakes would be nice, but I don’t think we’ve got the right ingredients. We’ve got flour, sugar, and some butter, but no baking powder. Maybe we could find some at Morrisons? Yeah, I saw some baking powder in the aisle last time. But wait, are we even sure what the lesson is about? I thought it was about how to make a basic cake, but the email said “baking for a lesson” – does that mean something else? I think it’s just about baking in general, but I’m not too sure. The teacher mentioned something about a half birthday celebration, so maybe we need to make something special. Oh, and she said she wants us to bring something from Tomodachi Life – is that a book? Oh, right, Tomodachi Life is that game where you take care of a virtual pet? Or was that something else? I think the teacher wants us to read a book about it, or maybe a book that inspired the game. I’m not exactly sure. I think it’s a book called  Tomodachi Life – The Real Story  or something like that. I remember seeing it in the library. But maybe we can find it at Morrisons too? I think they have a book section now, even though it feels a bit out of place. That sounds good. I’ll check the store on the way home. But just to be safe, maybe I should bring a few extra ingredients in case there’s a last-minute change. I don’t want to be the one who’s underprepared. Yeah, that’s smart. I’ll make sure the kids help me find the baking powder. My sister’s got a baked goods obsession, so she might even want to help. She’s been talking about making a cake for her own half birthday. You mean the one with the candles and everything? I remember her doing that last year. She made a chocolate cake and tried to light the candles with a match, but it caught fire. She had to call the fire brigade! Oh no, that sounds like a real disaster! I hope the teacher doesn’t ask for anything like that.

So, do you ever actually use Facebook anymore? I mean, I know it's still around, but I feel like I’ve been off it for ages now. Honestly, I think I’ve been off it for ages too. I mean, I still have the account, but I just don’t log on. I find it more of a time sink than anything useful these days. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that. I used to be all over it, but now I just feel like it’s taking up so much of my time and I’m not even getting anything out of it. It’s like, every time I open it, I feel like I’m being spammed with ads or people trying to sell me something. Exactly! And it’s not just the ads. It’s the whole idea of keeping up with everyone’s lives. You know, everyone’s always posting about their latest trip, their kids, their new job, and you feel like you’re falling behind if you don’t keep up. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s like you’re always in a race to be the most up-to-date person, even if it’s not really necessary. Plus, I’ve been trying to get back into the car scene again, and I feel like Facebook is one of those places where people just post tons of pictures of their cars and never really talk about them in depth. That’s true. I mean, I do like the car community on Facebook. There are some really good groups for classic car enthusiasts, and they’ve been really helpful. But honestly, I’d rather just go to a real car show or meet up with friends and talk about cars in person. There’s something about seeing a car in real life that you can’t get from a photo. That’s exactly it. I think I’m going to start up a local car club with some friends. We can meet up once a month and just swap stories and show off our rides. No need for any of that online stuff. That sounds like a great idea. It’s nice to get back to doing things face to face. I think I might join you. I’ve been feeling like I need a bit more of a real-life connection lately.

I just got off work, and I’m starving. Have you seen what they served for lunch today? It was like a sad sandwich with a tiny bit of salad. Not even enough to cover the bread. Yeah, I saw that too. I mean, it's supposed to be a sandwich, but it looked like they just stacked two slices of bread and called it a day. I actually had to bring my own snack from home. Honestly, I’m so used to working in places where they actually care about food. You know, the kind of place where the sandwiches come with proper condiments and maybe even a decent portion of something. I can’t believe they’re still doing this. I know, right? It’s like they’re trying to make us feel grateful for the crumbs. But hey, at least the TV is on. I just started watching  Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs  again. I love that movie. Oh yeah, that’s the one with the food floating out of the sky. I mean, why would anyone make that up? Unless they’re trying to say something about how food is always disappearing in real life. Exactly! It’s like a metaphor for how much we take for granted. And the characters are so funny. I mean, the food is basically the hero, and the town is just trying to survive the mess. It’s kind of a weird film, but in a good way. I remember when I was a kid, I thought the floating meatballs were real. I asked my parents if I could eat one, and they just laughed. I think they thought I was crazy. Oh, I remember that too. I used to think the same thing. I still kind of do. I mean, what if they’re right? What if food  can  float out of the sky? Maybe the world is just waiting for someone to wake up and realize that. I think that’s the point. The film is about how we don’t pay attention to the things that could change the world. Like, maybe we should start taking food more seriously. Or maybe we should start taking the remote seriously. I’m still trying to figure out how to fast forward through the credits. I think the buttons are labeled in a different language. I’ll help you. It’s the same remote as the one at work.

So, do you watch much football, mate? I mean, I know you're from Liverpool, so it's not like you're not into it. Oh, I've been into it all my life, yeah. Even when I was driving, I'd be listening to the radio, or watching on my phone when I had a bit of downtime. But I reckon it's not as big in Finland as it is back home. I suppose not. You know, I was in Finland for a few months teaching, and I got to see some interesting things. The people there love their sports, but football is more of a niche thing. Still, I think the passion is there. Yeah, I mean, I’ve watched some of the matches on TV. I didn’t know you were into it, though. I’m not really a big fan of the Premier League, to be honest. I mean, I love the game, but the politics around it is a bit much, to be fair. Especially with the way things have gone in recent years. Yeah, listen, I’ve been keeping an eye on the news. It’s all about who’s in power, isn’t it? I mean, it’s not just football. It’s everything – politics, economy, the government, and, let’s be honest, the media. Exactly. You know, I think the divide between New Labour and the current government has been a big part of it. I mean, Tony Blair was a big figure back in the day. Some people still think he was a good leader, and others don’t. Oh, I think he did his job. He pulled the country out of the mess of the 90s, made things more stable. But I also think he pushed the country too far in the direction of the market, and that’s what caused the problems later on. I can see your point. I think he was a bit of a controversial figure. Some people still call him a ‘socialist’ and others say he was a ‘capitalist with a heart’. It’s a bit of a mess, really. Yeah, it’s funny, isn’t it? You think you know what you want from a leader, and then you find out it’s not that simple. I mean, I’m not sure what the answer is, but I know it’s not easy. Definitely not.

So, do you know what’s been going on with the BNC recordings? I was trying to upload some new ones last night, but the system keeps glitching. It’s so frustrating. Ugh, I know, I’ve been trying to upload some too. I think the problem might be that the server is overloaded with all the recent submissions. It’s been really busy since the new funding came through. I’ve been trying to use LinkedIn to see if there are any updates, but honestly, it’s like trying to find a needle in a haystack. You can’t even tell if the updates are real or not. Yeah, I’ve been feeling the same. I mean, I can understand the need for more data, but it’s getting too chaotic. I’m starting to think maybe I should just switch to using some other platform for my recordings. I’ve been thinking about moving some of the old ones to a private cloud storage system. Do you think that would help? I hear you. I’ve been thinking about that too. I mean, why not? I’ve been using one for my own stuff for a while now. It’s way more controlled. You can edit and back up everything without worrying about the internet dropping. Although, I still can’t get past the fact that I’m scared of flying. I’m supposed to be going to the Maldives for a few weeks, and I’m literally having nightmares about it. Oh no, you’re not the only one. I’ve been terrified of flying for years. I mean, I tried to go to Spain last summer, and I had to cancel at the last minute because I couldn’t even get on the plane. My friend said it was just about time I faced my fears. I’m still not sure. I think you should try. I know it’s scary, but I’ve been doing some research on that. My sister went through a therapy program for it, and it actually helped. She’s been flying to the Maldives a few times now. I’ve been telling her how cool it is there. She said the beaches are amazing. You should’ve seen the whales! I’ve been watching some videos of them jumping out of the water—it’s like something out of a dream.

So, do you still have that tattoo on your arm? I remember you got one when we were in Bristol. No, I had it removed a few months ago. I was getting too old for it, honestly. Not that I regret the trip or anything—Londons were great, but it’s just that now I’m more into minimalism, you know? Yeah, I can see that. I still have mine, though. It’s a small one—just a lion, which is kind of cheesy, but it’s got meaning. Didn’t even think about removing it. You know, like, it’s part of who I am. I get that. You know, I always thought tattoos were a bit of a rebellion, like a way to mark your own story. But now, with the kids and the work, I just don’t want to be reminded of old habits or old times. I mean, I suppose it’s hard to look back at the things you used to do and not see them as part of your past. But I like that you still have the ink on your arm. It shows you’ve lived a bit. I know, and I still think there’s something cool about it. But I’m not getting any more. Not unless I’m really sure about it. So, what about you? Any new plans for the weekend? Honestly, I’m just trying to get through the week. Work’s been crazy, and I’m in the middle of a big project. I’m hoping to have some time at the weekend to catch up with some friends or maybe go to that new café near the museum. That sounds good. I’ve been meaning to try that place too. They said the food is really good. I’m just not sure if I’m ready to take the plunge with the renovation yet. The kitchen’s a mess, and I keep telling myself I’ll do it next week. You know, I was thinking about it the other day. Maybe you should get an intern or something. You’ve got the time, and it’d be good to have someone to keep an eye on things. That’s a good point. I’ve been meaning to talk about that with the landlord. I think he’s more open to it now. But I’m not sure if I’m ready to be in charge of someone else’s time.

So, do you think I should go to that yoga class next week? I’ve been feeling a bit stressed lately, and I heard it’s really good for calming the mind. Oh, I think it’s a great idea. I’ve been going to one myself for a few months now, and it’s made such a difference. I used to be so wound up all the time, but now I feel a lot more centered. That sounds amazing. I’ve always been a bit of a couch potato, but I’ve been trying to get more active. Do you think I should start with something else before jumping into yoga? Maybe. I started with a bit of walking, and then I moved on to yoga. It’s good to build up your strength and flexibility. But if you’re feeling overwhelmed, yoga is actually very gentle. You don’t have to be super flexible to do it. Yeah, that’s true. I’m a bit scared I’ll feel out of place if I’m not as flexible as everyone else. Don’t worry, everyone’s different. I remember my first class, I couldn’t even do a basic downward dog, and the instructor was super patient with me. She said it’s not about being perfect, it’s about showing up and trying your best. I like that approach. I think I’ll give it a try. What time does the class start? It starts at 6:30 PM, so that should work with your schedule. I can even come with you if you want. It’s always good to have a buddy. That would be great, thanks! I’d feel more comfortable knowing I’m not alone. Do you think I should bring any equipment? No, they usually provide mats and towels. You can bring a water bottle, though. It’s always good to stay hydrated. Oh, and if you’re not sure, you can always just ask the instructor. They’ll show you how to set up your mat and give you some basic instructions. Perfect, I’ll do that. I also want to try some new recipes this week. Any ideas for something healthy but not too complicated? Actually, I’ve been experimenting with making my own veggie burgers. They’re really easy and super tasty. I just blend up some lentils, add some oats, spices, and breadcrumbs, and shape them into patties.

So, did you get the email from Sarah about the meeting tomorrow? I was just thinking about it on the bus. Yeah, I did. She said it’s going to be a really important discussion about the new curriculum. I’m a bit nervous, honestly. I mean, it’s not like I don’t know my stuff, but it’s just the way the department is shifting things around. You know how it is with these meetings — they always seem to be about something else. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to keep up with all the changes. I even had to update my lesson plans last week. Honestly, I feel like I’m teaching the same content but in a completely different way now. It’s a bit overwhelming, but I think it’s for the best. I suppose it is. I mean, the students are benefitting from it, aren’t they? I just worry about the workload. I feel like I’m always in meetings or planning, and there’s not much time left to actually teach. I mean, not that I don’t enjoy it — I do, but it’s just a lot. Yeah, I can definitely relate. It’s like we’re both in this boat, trying to navigate the ever-changing waters of academia. I think the main thing is just to stay organized, and not let the stress get to us. You know, we’re both lecturers — we should be used to this by now! True, but sometimes I miss the days when things were simpler. I remember when we first started, we didn’t have to worry about all these updates and meetings. Now, it’s like we’re always in a state of transition. That’s the thing, though — the education system is always evolving. I guess that’s just part of the job. I mean, it’s not all bad. I do enjoy the challenge. And I have to say, working with you is one of the best parts of the job. You always have such great ideas. You’re too kind. I think you’re the one who keeps me grounded. I always come back to your classroom feeling inspired, even if I’m exhausted. You know, sometimes I think I’d rather be in the classroom than in a meeting. I know, right? But I’m also really glad we’re both in this together.

So, how’s the new job going? You mentioned you were going to start at the company last week. It’s going well, actually. I’ve been settling in, meeting the team, and getting to know the ropes. It’s a bit of a shift from what I was doing before, but I think I’m getting the hang of it. That’s great to hear. I can’t imagine how it must feel to move from being a teacher to running a company. It must be a huge change. Yeah, it’s definitely a big step up. But I’ve always had a passion for business and leadership. Teaching was a nice break, but I wanted to get back into something more dynamic. I get that. I’ve always found teaching to be fulfilling, but sometimes I wonder what it would be like to work in a different field. Although, I can’t imagine ever being in a position like yours. I know, it’s not for everyone. You have to have the drive and the resilience to handle the pressure. But I like the challenge. Speaking of challenges, I’ve been thinking a lot about conspiracy theories lately. I’ve seen some pretty wild stuff on social media. It’s hard to know what to believe. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve been reading some articles about the government and certain hidden agendas. It’s like everything’s connected, and no one’s telling the whole story. That’s what worries me. I mean, conspiracy theories are everywhere these days. I think people are just looking for answers in a world that feels increasingly complicated. I agree. But there’s also a lot of misinformation out there. It’s not just about the theories themselves—it’s about how they’re spread and the impact they have on people’s beliefs. Definitely. I remember when I first started teaching, I always told my students to question everything. But now I think that’s more important than ever. I think you’re right. People need to be critical thinkers, especially in this age of constant information overload. Yeah, and with all the fake news and social media, it’s easy to get caught up in something without really thinking through the facts. Exactly. I think it’s important to approach everything with a healthy dose of skepticism. But also, not to let it cloud your judgment entirely.

Dad, do you remember the book  Jamaica Inn ? I read it last week and it was so scary. I kept checking if the car was locked when I was alone in my room. Oh yeah, that's one of the classics. It's a bit of a gothic mystery, isn't it? I remember reading it when I was your age. You should try  Sherlock Holmes  too. A lot of people say it's a bit boring, but I actually think it's quite interesting. I tried  Sherlock Holmes  once, but I got bored. I prefer books like  The Wizard of Oz  because they're more fun and the characters are so colorful. I mean, do you think the road to Cornwall will be as colorful as the book? I hope so. We're going through some pretty scenic areas. You know, the colours of the countryside can change so much depending on the time of day. Sometimes it's like a painting. I remember when I was a kid, we used to drive to the coast and stop to look at the sea. It looked so blue, like it was made of glass. I’ve read  Alice in Wonderland  and  Through the Looking-Glass . I love how Lewis Carroll uses all these words that sound like they’re from a different language. It’s like he was making up new words. Do you think he used Morse code or something? No, I don’t think so. But you know, back in the day, people used telegraphs and Morse code to send messages. It was all about dots and dashes. It's amazing how much communication has changed. Now we can just send texts or emails. I used to work in customer services, so I dealt with a lot of phone calls and emails. Yeah, I love texting. I mean, it’s so much faster than writing letters, like using Morse code. Wait, Dad, can we stop at that caravan park on the way? I want to see the wind turbines. I’ve heard they’re really cool, and I want to take a photo of them. Sure, but we need to check the fuel level first. We don’t want to be stuck somewhere with no gas. I’ll check the map. Oh, and don’t forget your sunblock. The sun in Cornwall is really strong, even in the summer.

I can't believe we've got to talk about rent again. It’s been like three months, and I still haven’t got my head around how it works. Oh, come on, love. You know it’s only a few hundred pounds a month. You wouldn’t even notice it if it wasn’t for the fact that we’re both working and still haven’t saved anything. You should be saving, but I think you're just waiting for the perfect time to go and live in a flat with a private garden and a view of the sea. Well, I can’t afford that right now, mate. I’m still learning the ropes with my job, and I have to worry about things like petrol prices and how much my car’s eating out of my wallet. Speaking of which, have you seen how much it costs to fill up a tank these days? I still remember when a full tank was about £20. Now it’s like you’re paying for a taxi ride to get to the shops. It’s not just petrol prices, though. I think the whole country’s in a struggle. Even as a consultant engineer, I can’t afford to live in London anymore—it’s just too expensive. Yeah, I can’t even imagine living in London, honestly. I just want to be able to afford rent and maybe take a weekend trip somewhere. Like, what about a holiday to the coast? That’s the problem, love. We don’t have the money to do that. I remember when I was younger, I used to go to the cinema every week. Now I can’t even afford a ticket most of the time. I know what you mean. I used to be a regular at the cinema too. But these days, I just stick to the £5 tickets that the local chain offers. And I still feel like I’m being ripped off. Speaking of movies, have you ever watched Channel swimming? I saw this video online about someone swimming the English Channel. It looked absolutely insane. Oh, I’ve heard of that. My cousin tried it once, but he got so cold he had to give up after a few hours. I think it’s more about mental strength than physical. I mean, I can’t even go for a run without getting out of breath.

Mum, do you remember when we were kids and we used to go to the market on Saturday mornings? I swear you used to buy me this giant bag of sweets every time. Oh, yes! You were always the sweet tooth, weren’t you? You’d come home with your pockets full and your face sticky from the chocolate. I remember one time you even tried to eat a whole bag of caramels in one go and ended up with a sticky lip for a week. That was  so  you! You didn’t even scold me, you just laughed and said, “Well, I suppose it’s better than eating them in the car.” I miss those days, honestly. I know, love. You’ve grown up so much. It’s just surreal to see you back here, in the old house. The same one we moved into when you were about six. How’s everything going with your new job? I heard you’re teaching English in Brighton now? Yeah, I am. It’s been a few months now. I love it—especially the students. They’re all so eager to learn, and it’s a great way to meet people from all over the world. Though, honestly, I’m still adjusting to the jet lag from the last trip to Spain. My body’s been acting like it’s still on British time. That’s the worst part of travel, isn’t it? I still get that when I go to the seaside. You know, I was just thinking—what’s the list of things you need for the move? You said you were looking at a new place? Yeah, I am. We’re looking at a few places about ten minutes from the city. I’m trying to keep it simple this time. No more house hunting and constant stress. But I still need to get a list of all the things to take. Did you bring the old list from when you moved here? I think I did. Let me check the kitchen drawer. Wait, no, I left it at the top of the fridge. I’ll grab it in a minute. By the way, have you thought about what you’re going to do with the old sofa? It’s got so many scratches on the fabric now. I was thinking maybe we could sell it. I’ve seen some good prices for second-hand furniture lately.

I can't believe the NHS is still struggling like this. It's been ages since I last had a routine check-up, and I’m not even sure if I’d be able to get an appointment if I needed one. I know, I’ve been trying to book a vaccination slot for my mum and it’s like trying to win the lottery. I mean, if this is what the NHS is like now, what happens when there’s a real crisis? Exactly. It’s just so frustrating. I can’t even imagine how people in smaller towns or rural areas cope with this. You’d think with all the funding they’ve been getting, they’d manage better. Yeah, but I think part of the problem is the A-Level reforms. It’s like they keep changing the rules without really thinking about the impact. If the system is already under strain, making it harder for students to get into university is just going to make things worse. I couldn’t disagree more. I mean, the changes have been so confusing. I had a friend who was applying for a place at university last year and she was so stressed about the new grading system. It feels like they’re trying to make everything harder just to justify higher fees. I know, it’s all a bit of a mess. I think the way the government’s handling the petrol crisis is just another example of that. Gas prices have gone up so much, and yet they keep saying it’s due to global supply issues. But isn’t that just an excuse to keep the prices high? I’d say it’s a bit of both. There’s definitely a shortage, but I also think there’s a lot of political spin involved. And honestly, the impact on everyday people is real. I can’t afford to take my car anywhere these days. Yeah, I’ve had to rely on public transport more. It’s not ideal, but at least it’s cheaper. Although, I do miss having my own car. I mean, I used to drive everywhere, but now I’m just walking or taking the bus. It’s not the same. I know, but I’ve been thinking about getting a plant to keep me company. The house has been so empty lately, and it would be nice to have something growing.

So, do you know what’s up with the whole smoking ban in Leeds now? I saw it on the news yesterday, and I’m like, “What even is this?” Oh yeah, it’s a complete nightmare. I’ve been trying to find a spot to smoke all week, and it’s like every single place is off-limits. I mean, even the park's got that little sign saying “No smoking” now. I heard it’s because of the new health regulations or something. But honestly, it’s just so inconvenient. I mean, I’m not even a heavy smoker, but I still need a bit of a break sometimes. Yeah, I get it, but you can’t just smoke everywhere. I mean, it’s not like we’re in the middle of nowhere anymore. We’ve got to think about other people, right? Like, if you’re smoking in a café, it’s not just about you—it affects everyone else. I guess, but it’s kind of a bummer. I mean, I’ve got this whole group of friends who all smoke, and now we can’t even hang out together without being in a restricted area. It’s like we’re all on a mission to ruin our social life. Oh, I know, I’ve been trying to convince my roommate to quit. She’s been smoking like crazy, and now she’s trying to quit because of the new laws. She’s even said she’s starting to feel sick. That’s really sad. I mean, I’m not saying it’s a good idea to start smoking, but I feel like the government is pushing too hard on this. I mean, what about the people who can’t afford to quit? Like, if they’re on benefits and can’t afford nicotine patches or anything? That’s a good point, honestly. I mean, if you’re in a low-income area, and you’re trying to quit, you probably don’t have the money to buy all these expensive alternatives. I think they should have more support systems in place instead of just making it illegal everywhere. I guess it’s a bit of both. On one hand, it’s good that the government is trying to reduce smoking rates, but on the other hand, they’re making it harder for people, especially students, to manage their lives.

So, do you ever find it hard to say goodbye to people you've known for years, even if you don't really want to see them anymore? I mean, I've been thinking about this a lot recently. Like, some of the friends I used to hang out with all the time... it's just not the same anymore. I don't know if I want to see them as much. I get that. I think it's just a natural part of life, right? Like, as we grow and change, our interests and priorities shift. But it can be really awkward when you don’t want to seem like you’re just cutting people out. Yeah, exactly. It's like you don’t want to be rude or hurt their feelings, but you also don’t want to keep pretending things are the same. I think the hardest part is when you feel like you’ve outgrown them, but you don’t want to admit it. I know what you mean. I remember when I used to see this one friend every week, just hanging out, chatting, and then one day it just stopped working. I didn’t want to say anything, but it was like we were drifting apart. It’s so hard to be honest without it sounding like a rejection. Yeah, and it's not just about not wanting to see them anymore—it's also about not wanting to deal with the emotional baggage. Like, if we’re still in touch, it can feel like you’re still responsible for making things work, even when you’re not interested in it anymore. That’s true. I think the key is to be gentle but honest. Maybe you can start by reducing the frequency of contact. Like, instead of seeing them every week, just once a month or something. That gives you space to adjust without suddenly cutting off all communication. Maybe. I guess I just don’t want to burn bridges, even if I don’t feel that connection anymore. It’s one of those things where you don’t want to be the person who just disappears without a word. I totally agree. It’s not about being cruel, it’s about being respectful. And if the other person understands, it can even be a relief for them, too. Sometimes people don’t realize how much they’ve been holding on to.

So, how’s the new course going? You mentioned you were going to start a degree in art history next term. Oh, it’s going well, I think. I've been reading a lot, and it's really interesting. I mean, I’ve always loved art, but now I get to study it in a more academic way. It’s like getting to know it from the inside out. That sounds amazing. I wish I had the patience for that. I’m just trying to get through my first year of history. Sometimes I wonder if I made the right choice. You’ll get there. You just have to keep going. Besides, you’ve got the same kind of passion for learning as I did when I was your age. I remember when I was studying art, I used to stay up all night reading about the Renaissance. You’re not that different, really. Yeah, I guess. I just feel like I’m not getting enough out of it. I mean, I love history, but sometimes the lectures are just so dry. I can’t even remember half of what we’ve covered in class. Oh, I know what you mean. I used to get frustrated too. But I found that if I started drawing or painting from what I was learning, it helped me retain the information. Maybe you could try something like that? Hmm, maybe. I’ve been thinking about doing a bit of painting on the side. I mean, it’s just for fun, but it’s something I’ve always wanted to try. I guess I could combine it with my studies. That’s a great idea. You know, I’ve been thinking about a trip to Italy. I’ve always wanted to visit the cities where the Renaissance artists lived. Florence, Venice, maybe even Rome. I think it would help me connect the art I study to the places where it was created. That sounds incredible. I’ve been wanting to go there too, but I’ve never had the chance. I mean, I’ve heard so many stories about the art and the history there. It’s like a dream. Well, maybe you could come with me. You’d get to see it all, and you could learn so much. It’s not just about the art—it’s about the culture, the people, the way they lived.

So, do you ever find it weird that we're still eating before the gym? I mean, it's like... we're in Poland, and yet we're still acting like we're in the UK. It's like we've got this ingrained habit of having a proper meal before hitting the weights. Yeah, I know, it's just one of those things. I think it's because of the way we were brought up. Like, you always had to eat before exercising, or else you’d get all shaky. But now, I mean, I don’t know, when I was younger, I thought it was normal, but now I’m like, "Why do we do this?" Exactly! And it’s not even just the gym. It’s like, we still do all these things from back home, even when we’re miles away. I mean, even the way we drive is different. You know when you're in England, you just go with the flow, but here, it’s like everyone's trying to beat the traffic or something. Yeah, that’s true. I think it’s the way we’ve been socialized. You don’t just walk into a situation and say, "Look, I’ve got a different way of doing things." You have to adapt, but somehow, we still carry these old habits around with us, like they’re part of our identity. I think it’s also about feeling comfortable. When you're in your own country, you’re used to the pace and the environment. But when you’re in a different place, you kind of fall back on the things you know. It’s strange, isn’t it? Oh, it’s definitely strange. I mean, I’ve had moments where I just looked around and thought, "Wait, where are we? This doesn’t feel like England." But then again, I guess that’s part of the journey. It’s like you’re trying to find your place in a new environment, but you can’t escape your roots. I suppose so. I think the one thing that’s really interesting is how being English influences everything. Even with the language, you can tell people are from different parts of the country just by the way they speak. Sometimes it's subtle, like the way you pronounce certain words, or the way you use slang.

So, do you remember that time we had that power cut last winter? I was in the middle of making a cup of tea and it just went black. I couldn’t even see the kettle. Oh, yes, I remember that. You were so upset you couldn’t find the kettle. I had to go and check the fridge to see if the lights were on. And then I found the kettle on the side, like it had been there the whole time. It was so dark, I think I must have been in the kitchen for ages. Didn’t even realize the lights had gone out. I was just thinking, “Why is everything so quiet?” And then the fridge started humming, and I thought, “Oh, it must be the fridge.” I suppose you were just so used to the lights being on. I think it was the first time in years that we had a proper power cut. I remember the birds outside started chirping like mad, like they thought the world had ended. Yeah, I think the birds were more scared than we were. I was so annoyed, I didn’t even want to make tea. I just sat there in the dark, and the cat was staring at me like, “What are you doing? You’re supposed to be cooking.” She must have thought you were in some kind of crisis. I remember the time you left the oven on and the cat started trying to run through the kitchen. You had to chase her out with a broom. Oh, that was a nightmare. I was so embarrassed. I think she’d been watching me all morning, and then she just decided to make a break for it. It was funny though. You know, the other day I was out in the garden and I saw this spider. It was the biggest one I’ve ever seen. It was in the corner of the shed, like it was waiting for me. Spiders? You’re not telling me you’ve got one in the house now? No, just in the shed. I was trying to figure out what kind it was. I thought it might be one of the black ones, but no, it was a different kind. I was just so fascinated by it. It was like watching a tiny superhero. I’d rather have a spider than a power cut.

Mum, do you think we should go to the beach again this year? I’m really tired of the same old place. Oh, I’m more than happy to go to the beach, but I was thinking we could do something different this year. You know, maybe take a trip to somewhere new? I’d like that. I haven’t been on holiday for a while. Maybe we could go to the Lake District? I’ve always wanted to see those beautiful lakes and hills. That sounds nice, but I like the beach. I mean, it’s always fun to walk along the shore, build sandcastles, and collect shells. Plus, the waves are so calming. I get that, sweetie. The beach is a great place to relax, but I feel like we should try something new this year. You know, to make it more memorable. I guess... but then what about my friends? I’d like to invite them along. They always have so much fun on holiday. That’s a good point. As long as we have enough space, I’m sure we can make room for your friends. But let me check the dates again. I want to make sure we have enough time to plan everything properly. Yeah, I’ll get the calendar out. But before that, do you have any ideas about where you want to go? Maybe you could suggest a few places and we can vote. Well, someone said the Lake District would be nice. But I also really like the idea of a seaside town. Maybe somewhere with a bit of history? Like a historical seaside town? Oh, I know a few places like that. There’s a town called Whitby that has a great coastal walk and a very interesting history. The abbey there is amazing. That does sound interesting. Whitby has a lot to offer. And if we go there, we can have some great scenic views. Plus, there are plenty of places to eat and stuff to do. Yeah, I like that idea. But what about the weather? I don’t want to go somewhere that’s too hot or too cold. Well, if we go in the summer, it’s usually warm enough, but not too hot. And if we go in the late spring, it might be just right. Exactly. We could go at the end of June or beginning of July.

I can't believe we just watched  10 Things I Hate About You  again. It’s like the first time, but I’m so tired after school today. Yeah, I know, but it was so funny. I mean, Heath Ledger as Patrick —  classic ! I still remember when he said,  “I’m not an actor, I’m a plumber.”  It was so ridiculous. Oh yeah! And I loved how Kat and Patrycja were like,  “I hate you, I don’t hate you”  all the time. It was so dramatic, but also kind of sweet. Totally. I mean, it’s a teenage romance, but it still works. I guess it’s like how we feel sometimes — like we’re obsessed with someone, but we’re also trying to be cool about it. Exactly! And I still can’t believe that Kat’s brother, Hikaru, ended up being the one who helped her out. I mean, he was so into her, but he was like,  “I don’t know what I’m doing.”  Yeah, and then when he finally got her to open up, it was like…  boom . Suddenly, all the tension was gone. It was kind of like a real-life version of that movie. I mean, I did have a moment like that with my history teacher last week. She was so strict, but then she said,  “I’m not trying to be a villain, I just want you to pass.”  Oh my God, that’s so relatable! I had a teacher like that in math. I used to hate her because she never explained anything properly, but then I realized she just wanted us to succeed. I think it’s kind of like that. My mom always says,  “You don’t have to like your teachers — just learn from them.”  Exactly! So I guess we’re just waiting for our own  Patrick  to come along. Heh, I don’t think I’m ready for that. I mean, I’m trying to survive school right now. Yeah, but I think we’re getting closer to London next month. You know, the trip we were talking about. Oh my God,  finally!  I’ve been waiting for this all year. I can’t wait to see the Tower Bridge and the Museums. And we’re going to try to get tickets to a Shakespeare play. I heard there’s a performance of  Romeo and Juliet  at the Globe Theatre.

Well, I've just seen this post on Facebook from old Tom. He's saying he's going to start a church in the village, or something like that. Oh, Tom? He's been doing that for years. I remember the time he tried to start a church in the barn. Got chased out by the council for having a prayer mat on the floor and a cross on the wall. That’s funny. I remember that. But honestly, I don’t think he’s ever really been religious. Just likes the idea of being spiritual. Yeah, I think he just likes the attention. You know how he always used to post those “inspirational” quotes on Facebook? My mum still gets them in her inbox. He’s not the only one, though. I saw a post from the vicar last week saying he’s going to be holding a breakfast service every Sunday. I thought, “Why not? It’s a bit of a change.” You know, I used to go to church when I was younger. My gran used to take me every Sunday. She always said it was about community, not just religion. That’s probably why she liked it. But I’ve never really got into it. I prefer books. Although, I have to say, I do find some of the poetry in the Bible quite moving. Yeah, I think that’s the thing. It’s not just about the rules. It’s about the ideas. Like, the whole concept of love and kindness. Some of the messages are pretty profound. I suppose so. But then again, there’s also a lot of nonsense. I remember when I was a kid, my dad used to say that if you don’t believe in God, you’ll end up in hell. He was a bit strict. I think he was afraid of the dark. I think it’s a natural fear. We all have it. But I think the fear of the unknown is what makes people turn to religion. And that’s why some people with OCD might find comfort in it. The structure, the routine. It gives them something to hold on to. I’ve heard that. But I think some people just use it as an excuse. Like, if you’re scared of something, you blame it on God. Oh, I’ve seen that. But honestly, I’m not sure.

So, do you remember when we all went on that holiday to Germany back in 2015? I still remember the time we got lost in Munich and had to ask for directions in broken German. It was hilarious. Oh yeah, I remember that! You were so nervous about speaking German that you just mumbled something and then the guy just laughed and said, “You’re from Kent, right?” It was such a relief when he understood us. Oh, don’t forget the time you tried to order a beer and said "Ich will ein Bier, bitte" with such a serious face. It was like you were in a German film. We all thought you were going to get kicked out of the bar. I still remember the accents in Germany. Everyone sounds so posh compared to us, and then you think, “Wait, are they actually German or just really posh English people?” It was so confusing! I think it’s the way they pronounce things. Like, “Bier” is so different from how we say it. I still get confused when I hear it in movies. I think I’d be lost in a German town without a map. Yeah, but I think it’s not just the language. The culture is so different too – even though we’re all British, and sometimes it feels like we’re from different planets. You don’t even know what the other person is talking about half the time. Honestly, I think the biggest problem is the accents. When you’re in Germany, you can’t tell if someone’s from the north or the south, let alone if they’re from England. I once thought a guy was from Norfolk, and then he said he was from Dresden. I was like, “Wait, isn’t Dresden in Germany?” That’s the thing, isn’t it? You’re so used to British accents and then you go somewhere like Germany and it’s like, “Oh, wait a minute – this is a different sound altogether.” And when you’re out in the countryside, you hear that rural German accent, and it’s like a completely different world. It’s like you’re not even in Europe anymore – it’s like you’re in some foreign land. I think it’s also the food. You don’t expect the German food to be that different. But the sausages, the bread, the beer – it all just feels so different from what we’re used to.

So, how’s the kitchen doing? I heard you’ve been experimenting with some new recipes lately. It’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I’ve been trying to push myself out of my comfort zone. I’ve been working on a few new dishes that I think could really make the menu stand out. But honestly, it’s been tough. I feel like I’m not getting the recognition I deserve. That’s frustrating. Why do you think that is? Is it the competition or just the way the business is structured? It’s a mix of both. There are a lot of talented chefs around, and the restaurant scene is pretty competitive. Plus, I think people expect a certain level of consistency, and I’ve been playing around too much with the menu. I’m not sure if I’m hitting the right notes. I get that. It’s hard to balance creativity with what the customers actually want. Have you been doing any live performances or anything like that? I remember you used to play the drums in a band. Yeah, I did. I haven’t played in a while, but I’m thinking about getting back into it. It’s a different kind of creative outlet, but I feel like it’s something I’ve been neglecting. I’m not sure if I have the time, though. That’s a shame. You’ve got a real talent for music. Maybe you could do some side gigs? I mean, even if it’s just at local events or something. It might help keep your skills sharp and give you a different perspective. You’re right. I’ve been thinking about that too. It’s just hard to find the balance between work and personal projects. I’m also trying to apply for some internships in the food industry. I want to take my skills to the next level, but I’m not sure where to start. That’s a great idea. You should definitely look into some mentorship programs or internships. It could open up some doors for you. You’ve got a good eye for what works and what doesn’t. It’s just a matter of getting the right opportunities. Thanks, I appreciate that. I’m going to start reaching out to some places and see what’s on offer. I think it’s time I stopped trying to do everything on my own and started collaborating with others.

I can't believe we've got to this point, Christopher. It’s been a long time since we last saw each other, and now we’re both in the same place, just having a coffee. It’s a bit strange, isn’t it? Yeah, it is. Honestly, I didn’t expect to run into you here. I mean, I know you’re a teacher, but I didn’t think you’d be in a place like this. I mean, it’s not exactly where you’d expect to find someone with your…  gestures vaguely  …level of sophistication. You’re being too modest, dear. I mean, I do love a good cup of coffee, and this place isn’t that bad. Just a bit noisy, though. Can you hear that? The radio’s playing some kind of pop song, and the people in the drive-through are shouting at the baristas. It’s almost like a zoo in here. Haha, yeah, it’s like the whole place is on a constant loop of chaos. I mean, I guess it’s a sign of the times, though. Everyone’s in a rush these days. Even the waiters seem to be in a rush. I swear, they’re all watching their phones more than they are paying attention to customers. I know, I know. It’s all about convenience these days. You know, the loyalty promotions and all that. I’ve even heard some people talking about using their phones to order food in advance. It’s one thing, but I still think there’s something to be said for a good old-fashioned conversation. I agree. I mean, I used to love talking to people when I was in school. I mean, not all the time, but when I had time to. Now it’s all about apps and instant messages. I barely even remember the last time I had a real conversation with someone without a screen in between. That’s true. And I think it’s getting worse. You know, I was talking to a friend about it the other day. We were both wondering if we’ll ever get back to the days when people actually talked to each other instead of just typing. It’s like the world’s gone silent, except for the noise of the machines. It is, isn’t it? And don’t even get me started on the noise levels.

So, how’s the new flat? I heard you moved in a few weeks ago. How’s it going? It’s going okay, I guess. I’ve had a few issues with the heating, but other than that, it’s decent. I’ve got a nice view of the South Downs from the window. That’s great. I’ve always loved the South Downs. You know, I’ve been thinking about moving back to the area. I’ve been working from home more lately, and it’s making me consider settling down somewhere a bit more permanent. That’s understandable. I’ve actually been thinking about that too. I mean, with the cost of living going up and all, it’s hard to justify living in London anymore. Plus, I’ve got some savings, so I’m not in a rush. Yeah, I can see that. Although, I’m still waiting for the right opportunity. I’ve been thinking about doing some work abroad too. I’ve got a friend in South Korea who’s working there as a language instructor. He said it’s a great place to teach English. South Korea? That’s interesting. I’ve always wanted to go there, but I’m not sure if I’d be able to handle the culture. I mean, I know some basic Korean, but I’m not fluent. I’ve been trying to learn some phrases, though. It’s not easy. I can imagine. I’ve been learning Spanish for a bit now, but it’s also a challenge. You know, I’ve been thinking about doing some kind of recording project with some of the students I teach. Maybe some kind of podcast or something. You know, mixing linguistics with teaching. That sounds cool. I mean, I’m not a language teacher, but I know a bit about accents and dialects. I could probably help with the recording side of things. Maybe we could do something together? That’s actually a great idea. I was thinking about it the other day. Maybe we could start with a small project. It could be like a podcast where we discuss different aspects of language, like accents, slang, or even how people use language in different countries. Yeah, that could work. I’ve always been interested in how language varies across regions. I mean, I grew up in the Midlands, so I’ve got a strong accent, and I can hear the differences in how people speak in London versus the South.

I just got a call from the hospital. It's about Mum. They want to talk to us about her recent scans. Oh no, what's going on? It's the same thing as before. The cancer seems to be spreading again. They’re not giving us much hope, but they’re keeping her on some new treatment they’re trialing. That’s so hard. I can’t believe this is happening again. I mean, we've been through so much already. I know. I feel like we’re just running out of time. She’s been so weak lately, and even the doctors are saying she’s not going to make it through another round of chemo. I wish there was something more we could do. I know it’s not about what we can do—it’s about what she wants. Have you talked to her about it yet? Not really. I mean, she’s been in so much pain, and she’s been so tired, I’m not sure how to bring it up. I keep thinking maybe I should just tell her the truth, but I’m scared of what she might say. It’s not easy, but I think honesty is the only way. She needs to know what’s happening so she can make choices about her own life, you know? I know, but she’s always been so strong. I can’t imagine her accepting that this is the end. I mean, she’s got her own opinions and she’s not one to give up easily. That’s what I love about her. She’s always been headstrong. But I think she’s starting to see the reality. The other day, she was talking about the garden and how she wants to see the tulips bloom this spring. She said she wants to be there for it. That’s so sweet. I just keep thinking about her kids. I know she’s been worried about them, especially about the youngest. She said she wants to meet her grandbaby before she goes. I know. That’s what she keeps saying. She’s not giving up on that. I think she’s holding on for them, for the family. That’s what makes it harder. It’s not just about her—it’s about all of us. I don’t know how we’re going to deal with it when the time comes.

Alright, lads, how’s the schoolwork going? I know it’s been a tough term with all the exams and everything. Honestly, it’s been a bit of a struggle. I’m trying to keep up with all the stuff, but football practice takes up so much of my time. I just don’t know how to balance it all. You know, I remember when I was your age, I used to play tennis every day. It’s a bit different now, but it’s still important to find a balance between school and hobbies. Didn’t you get into some sort of tennis coaching program recently? Yeah, I did! It’s actually been pretty cool. My coach is amazing, and I’ve been getting better at serving and rallying. It’s just that I’m not sure if I can afford the fees for the whole season. Well, I can see how it could be a challenge. But I think if you can find a part-time job, you could save up for it. Have you thought about that? I’ve considered it, but I’m not sure what I’d do. I mean, football is a big part of my life. I’d hate to miss out on that. But I also don’t want to fail my exams. It’s a tough spot to be in. That’s understandable. I remember when I was in school, I used to have a part-time job at the local grocery store. It wasn’t much, but it helped me save up for things like my tennis equipment. Besides, it gives you a bit of structure and keeps you busy. Exactly. And if you’re thinking about the future, maybe an apprenticeship is something to consider. I know the area has a lot of opportunities in engineering and business. It could be a great way to get hands-on experience while still learning. Yeah, I’ve heard about apprenticeships. My dad mentioned something about his cousin doing one in the city. But I’m not sure if I’m ready for that yet. I mean, I’m still trying to figure out what I want to do when I grow up. That’s normal, lad. You don’t have to have everything figured out right now. What matters is that you’re making decisions that help you move forward. And if you’re thinking about starting a business, I know a few people who have started small ventures and are doing well.

So, do you think we’ll get to Lancaster on time? I’ve been trying to get a signal on my phone all the way from Aylesbury, and it’s been going crazy. Yeah, I think we should be fine. I mean, it’s only like an hour or so from Lincoln, right? But I’ve heard the train can be a bit delayed if there’s any kind of weather issue. Yeah, I saw a weather forecast earlier. It said there might be some heavy rain in the afternoon. I hope it doesn’t mess up our plans. I was really looking forward to visiting the coast. Me too. I mean, I haven’t been to the coast in ages. I remember my family used to take us to Scarborough when I was a kid. You know, the old fish and chips shop by the beach. It was always so busy, especially on weekends. Oh, I still remember that. My mum used to make us go there every time we visited. She said it was the best fish and chips in the whole county. Although, I think we had a cockle disaster once. Oh, you mean that time when we tried to shuck the cockles and ended up with all of them stuck in our teeth? I swear, I still have the scar from that one. Definitely. It was a mess. I think we even had to go back to the shop and ask for a refund. Who knew cockles could be so tricky? I know, right? But it was all part of the fun, wasn’t it? I mean, we had such a good time, even with the cockles. Yeah, I guess it was. I can’t wait to see the coast again. I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately, especially with my dissertation on language and regional dialects. I was wondering if I could do some fieldwork there. That sounds like a great idea. I mean, the coast has such a strong regional identity, and the dialects there are unique. Plus, it’s a chance to do some real-life research instead of just sitting in a library. Exactly. I’ve been trying to get some data from people who live there, but it’s been hard. I’m hoping that this trip will give me some new perspectives. I’m sure it will. You know, I’ve been thinking about writing my own dissertation as well.

So, do you still listen to that band we used to go to see back in high school? You know, the one with the lead singer who always wore that weird hat? Oh yeah,  The Echoes of the Past  – I still have that CD. It’s got that one track where the guitar solo just...  melts  into the background like it’s part of the vocals. It’s so weird, but I love it. My brother still plays that album on repeat when he’s trying to study. He says it helps him focus. I don’t know, it just makes me want to run out and buy a guitar. You should! I mean, you’ve been into music since we were kids. You used to play the piano for the school talent show. Remember? You were like,  “I’m gonna be the next Ed Sheeran!”  Oh, come on, that was only because I was trying to impress the girls. And I was  so  bad. I remember one of the teachers actually laughed so hard they had to go to the back of the room to wipe their eyes. I still laugh about that! But seriously, have you been into any new music lately? I’ve been trying to find a new band to vibe with. I’ve been into this indie-folk band called  The Hollows . They’re from Leeds, I think. Their lyrics are really poetic, and the guitar work is just... mind-blowing. Oh, I’ve heard of them! I think they did that festival last summer. I went with my cousin, and I swear, they played that one song where the lead singer just...  sang  the whole thing without any backing track. It was haunting. Yeah, I saw them too. It was weird, though – the crowd was so quiet during that song. Like, you could hear a pin drop. That’s the power of good music, right? It can just... stop the world for a second. Totally. I think that’s why I keep coming back to it. It feels like, even if we’re just hanging out, we’re not just talking – we’re  connected  through something bigger. Yeah, and that’s what I love about music.

Okay, so we've got to play Pandemic, right? I’m just trying to remember the rules. I think the goal is to stop the outbreak, but I’m not sure how exactly we do that.      Yeah, you have to stop the outbreaks in all the cities before the disease spreads globally. You get different roles like Scientist, Medic, and Quarantine Specialist. Each role has different abilities. I’ve played before, but I’m still a bit rusty.      Let me help. The game is about working together to contain the virus. I can't believe it's already April. I feel like I just started the year. How are you holding up? Honestly, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. So, do you two ever get tired of talking about food? I mean, it's like we're in a restaurant every day. Oh, come on, it's not like that. I can't believe I've got to go to that conference in Manchester next week. I mean, it's only a week away and I haven't even packed yet. I know, right? I was just thinking about that myself. So, do you think we're on the right road? I’m getting a bit lost in all these Polish signs. I think we are, but I’m not sure. I think we might need to check the map again. So, do you know what’s really fascinating about the Vikings? I was reading this article the other day about how they were actually quite advanced in terms of their medicine and their understanding of the human body. It’s a bit surprising because you think of them as raiders and warriors, but they had some pretty cool knowledge. Yeah, I remember reading that they used herbal remedies and even had some kind of surgical techniques. But I also heard that they believed in a lot of superstitions, like how they thought some diseases were caused by evil spirits. It's kind of a mix of science and myth. Exactly! It's like they had a blend of practical knowledge and spiritual beliefs. I think that’s part of why they were so successful in their travels and settlements. They were adaptable. But I was also thinking about how the idea of immortality is kind of tied into a lot of their mythology, like with Odin and the World Tree. That’s true. I guess it’s a universal theme, isn’t it? People have always been fascinated by the idea of living forever or at least living longer. I’ve been reading a bit about gerontology recently. It’s quite a big topic these days, especially with all the talk about telomeres and how they affect aging. Oh yeah, telomeres are interesting. I remember reading that they act like a clock in your cells, and as they get shorter, your cells age. If we could find a way to keep them from shortening, maybe we could extend human lifespan. But I wonder if that's really the answer we're looking for. I suppose it’s not just about living longer, but also about living better. I mean, people are starting to live longer now thanks to better healthcare and improved living conditions. But I'm not sure if that's always a good thing. I've heard some research about how people are aging more and more, and it's putting strain on healthcare systems. That’s a good point. It's not just about scientists trying to find a way to stop aging, but also about managing the resources and infrastructure that come with a longer-lived population. And then there's the whole idea of global warming and the impact it's having on our environment. It seems like everything's connected now.

Mummy, can we go to the fish and chip shop later? I’m starving. I thought we were going to have coffee first. But I didn’t have breakfast. I had toast and a banana. That’s not proper breakfast. I just got a text from the estate agent saying that the old man next door has finally decided to move. So that means the big, old tree in his garden is going to be taken down. Oh no, really? So, do you ever miss the North East? I mean, I know it's a bit of a cliché to say, but it's got that real grit to it, you know? The people, the culture, it's different from the Midlands or the South. Honestly, I do. I mean, I grew up in Birmingham, so I never really thought about it that much, but every time I go back, it just feels like home in a way. Like, you don’t wear something just because it’s trendy—you wear it because it suits you. Exactly. And I think that comes with the culture too. You don’t just follow trends—you create them. I mean, I remember growing up, there was this band from Sunderland that was huge. They were called The Healers, right? Grandpa, I heard you were talking about the election last night. What did you think? Oh, I thought it was a bit of a mess, to be honest. Oh, it’s not that I didn’t know what it was, but I didn’t really care. I was more interested in playing football and trying to get a job. Yeah, I guess that’s what life is like. You’re so busy trying to get by that you don’t really think about the bigger picture. That’s the thing, lad. So, do you remember the last time we had a proper family meal like this? I think it was when we all got together for the blood moon last year. Yeah, that was cool. I remember we all got dressed up and went to Fitzgeralds Park. It was like a proper night out. I think we even had a bonfire. Oh, I remember that. Speaking of which, I think we need to talk about the dinner table manners. I mean, I know it's been a while, but I think those rules are still important.

So, do you know what’s been on my mind all week? That Scottish referendum. I just can’t get it off my mind. I mean, I’m not sure I even understand all the arguments, but I can feel the tension in the air. It’s like the whole country’s holding its breath. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about it too. I reckon it’s not just about the money or the independence. It’s about identity, you know? For a lot of people, Scotland’s got a different history, a different culture. I mean, when I was a kid, the whole idea of being British felt like it was baked into the cake. But now, I’m not so sure. That’s true, isn’t it? I remember when I was teaching, there was always this debate about what it meant to be British. A lot of the students came from all over the UK, and it was fascinating to see how they saw the country. Some saw it as a collection of different nations, others as one big family. I think the referendum just made that divide more visible. I get that. I’ve got a colleague who’s from Glasgow, and he’s been pretty vocal about wanting independence. He says he feels like Scotland’s been dragged along by the rest of the UK. But then again, I’ve got a cousin in Manchester who just can’t imagine life without the Union. She was really into Scottish history and culture, and she asked me if I thought it would ever happen. I told her I didn’t know. But the thing is, I can’t help but feel like things are changing. I think they are. I mean, I’ve had a few business meetings lately with people from Scotland, and they’re all asking the same question—what’s the future holding? It’s like the whole country’s waiting for an answer. I just hope the outcome doesn’t tear the country apart. It’s not just about politics, it’s about people. Yeah, that’s what worries me. I’ve had a couple of job interviews lately, and I noticed how people are talking about the future.

We’ve got a bit of a way to go. I don’t mind making a stop. I’ve got a bit of a craving for a sausage roll or something. I think I saw a booth with those on the side of the road.
