You don’t have to worry about getting grease on your hands or anything like that. It’s all ready to go. But I’d rather eat something warm if we do stop. I’ve got this craving for something homemade. Maybe a bit of a meat pie? Meat pie’s a bit too heavy for lunch, don’t you think? I’d go for something lighter, like a salad or a sandwich. Or maybe even a burger? Honestly, I’ve been thinking about how much I miss proper food when I’m out and about. It’s one of the reasons I love teaching English – I get to eat good food every day in the café. You know what I miss the most? The ability to just stop in at a local store and get a bucket of crisps and a bottle of pop. No need to think about calories or anything like that. Yeah, but I think I’ve been trying to make more healthy choices. I’m even eating more vegetables now. It’s weird, but I’m starting to like them more. That’s a good thing, Aaron. Maybe we can do something like that for lunch. Let’s see if there’s a café with a decent salad or something on the way. I could go for a salad. You know, with some grilled chicken and a bit of avocado. It’s not too bad. I’m not sure I’d be able to handle a salad, honestly. I’m more of a chips and burger guy. But I’ll try if you’re going for it. Then let’s see what we can find.

I can't believe we've got to this point. I thought we'd be home by now. Well, I told you about the traffic on the M62. It's been a nightmare ever since we left Leeds. You wouldn’t believe the queue—like a motorway full of slow-moving lorries and broken-down cars. That’s not surprising, considering it’s the busiest time of the day. I’ve never seen so many farm animals on the road. I think one of those lorries was carrying sheep. It was like a mobile animal fair. Oh, really? I didn’t notice. I was too busy trying not to hit the car in front of me. I swear that driver was trying to park on the hard shoulder. You’re not the only one. I saw a pick-up truck trying to park there too. It must’ve been a farmer coming back from the market. He probably had a cow in the back or something. That would explain the smell, even if you can’t see the animal. I’ve had worse experiences driving through rural areas—like when I was on the way to a farm in the West Midlands and got stuck in a field with a herd of cows staring at me like I was a tourist from another planet. That sounds terrifying. I’ve never been on a farm, but I’ve heard stories. I don’t know if I’d be able to handle it. I mean, even the thought of being surrounded by all that noise and smell makes me dizzy. You’d get used to it, I think. It’s a different kind of life. I’ve been driving past farms for years, and I’ve started to notice the patterns—like the same tractor going past the same field every morning. Yeah, and it’s not just the animals. There’s a lot of machinery too. I saw a combine harvester the other day. It was massive, like a walking construction site. Wow, that must be intense. I can only imagine the noise. I’ve never been on a farm, but I’ve seen videos of people working on them. It’s all so different from the city. I mean, here in the car, it’s just the hum of the engine and the radio. And the silence of the countryside is just as different.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about joining the choir again. It’s been ages since I last sang, and I feel like I’ve missed out on something. I mean, sure, I retired from teaching, but I still feel like I have something to give. That sounds lovely. I’ve always thought singing is a great way to stay active and meet people. You know, it’s a bit like being in a group, and you don’t feel so alone. But are you sure it’s the right place for you? I mean, do you know anyone who’s in the choir? Well, I think Mary’s in one. She’s been singing with them for years. She said they’re always looking for new members, especially after the last few years when they had to cancel a few rehearsals. But I’d say go for it. You’ll be doing something you love and you’ll meet some nice people. Yeah, I think I’ll give it a try. I remember when I was teaching, I used to do a lot of group activities with the students. It was always a nice way to build connections. I mean, even though it’s not the same as teaching, it’s still a form of sharing knowledge, right? Exactly. You’re giving back in a different way, but it’s still meaningful. And it’s a great way to stay on your feet and keep your voice in shape. I mean, we’ve all heard the stories about people who’ve taken up music in their later years and found a new passion. It’s never too late. Speaking of which, I think I’ve got a bit of a new plan in the works. I was talking to my cousin the other day about starting a small mentoring program for kids in the village. I’ve got some experience in the oil industry and I know a few things about problem-solving and teamwork. Maybe I could help some local kids get their feet on the ground. That’s a fantastic idea. I think it’s important to give back, especially when you’re older. I mean, you’ve got so much to offer, and it’s great to keep the community spirit alive. I’d be happy to help you set it up, if you like.

Alright, let’s get this sorted out. The parent’s evening is tomorrow, and I’ve got a list of things I need to go through with the kids. Yeah, I know, I’ve got the report from Miss Jenkins too. She said things are going well with the reading, but they’re struggling with the Maths. Mmm, I heard that too. I don’t know how they’re supposed to do the fractions. I mean, I can’t even remember what fractions are, let alone teach them to a six-year-old. Oh, don’t worry, I’ve got a better system. I’ve been practicing with the children’s toy blocks. You know, like if you have four blocks and you give two to your friend, you’ve got two left – that’s half. That sounds like a good idea, but I’ve tried that with Lily. She just keeps saying, “But why can’t I just throw them away?” Oh, she’s always been a bit of a rebel. But that’s why I like her, right? Anyway, listen, I think I need to talk to both of you about the Maths. Yeah, I reckon we should work on it together. Maybe we can do some activities after dinner. Great, but first, what are we having for dinner? I thought I’d make some spaghetti bolognese. There’s a bit left from last week. That sounds good, but I’ve got an idea. What if we have a World Book Day activity tonight? I mean, it’s not exactly the official day, but we could read a story together. That’s a great idea. I’ve been thinking about doing that with the kids. I mean, it’s not like we’re doing anything else. Yeah, and maybe we can even pick a character from a book. I think Lily was really into the talking cat in  The Tale of Despereaux . Oh, yeah, that was a good one. I think I remember the cat being really smart. You know, I was thinking the other day – what if we went to see a real circus? I mean, it’s not like we’ve done anything exciting lately. A real one? That’s a great idea. I’ve been meaning to ask about it. Yeah, but I’ve heard they can be really expensive. I know, I’m not sure yet.

So, do you know what’s going on with Oisin? I’ve been trying to get him to help out with the curtain shop, but he keeps saying he’s too busy with his rugby training. Oh, I know, he’s been so focused on that. But isn’t he supposed to be working there this summer? I thought the manager was going to give him some responsibilities. Yeah, that’s what I thought too. But this morning, he came in with this big grin, saying he’s got a part-time job now. I asked him where, and he said he’s helping out at the local garage with some of the lads. I don’t know, it seems a bit strange. Oh, he’s just trying to be the big kid. You know how he is. I think he’s just playing with the idea of being responsible. He still talks like a toddler sometimes, you know. Exactly! I saw him the other day and he was saying, “I’m so big now, I can do it all myself!” and then he fell over immediately. It’s so typical of him. Like a baby with a big voice. I’ve been trying to get him to work on his birthday party. We’re having it at the park next weekend. He’s still not decided on the theme. I thought maybe he’d want something with his rugby team, but he keeps saying he wants a pirate ship. I mean, is that even possible? I think it is. It just depends on how much money we’re willing to spend. I was talking to the local shop owner, and she said she can do a pirate-themed party for a reasonable fee. I think we can manage it. Oh, I’ve got an idea. Why don’t you get the local charity to help out? I know they do a lot for kids’ events. They might even bring some games and decorations. That sounds good. I’ll check with them tomorrow. But I’m still not sure about the pirate theme. He’s never been into pirates. I always thought he’d prefer something more… practical. Yeah, but you can’t deny he’s growing up. Maybe he just wants to be a pirate for a day. It’s not like he’s going to be one for real, is he?

So, do you ever find it funny how people can be so bad at word games? Like, they just don’t get the point of it. Honestly, I think it’s more about how people are just not into it. I mean, I love word games. They’re like mental puzzles. You get to use your brain and have fun at the same time. Yeah, I agree. I’ve always found them challenging but rewarding. Like, the way you can stretch a word or twist a phrase to make something completely different. It’s like playing with language. Exactly. I mean, I remember when I was at university, we used to do these word association games in the pub. One time someone tried to make a rhyme with “sardine” and ended up saying “sardine, bin, pickled, in the fridge, sandwich…” It was just so random and funny. Oh, I’ve been in that situation too. I once tried to make a rhyme with “quantum” and ended up with “quantum, bomb, physics, domination, and then, um… mushroom.” It was so bad I almost died laughing. I think the worst part is when people try to be too clever. Like, they use obscure words or try to force a rhyme. It often ends up sounding forced and unnatural. Yeah, I think that’s when it stops being fun. If you’re trying too hard, it just becomes awkward. But if you’re having fun with it, it’s way more enjoyable. I think it’s also about the group you’re with. If you’re in a group where people are into it, it becomes a real game. But if you’re with people who don’t get it, it’s just a bunch of awkward silences. I mean, sometimes the best word games come from just going with the flow. Like, when you’re at a party and someone starts a game, and it just builds on itself. You can end up with some really creative and unexpected phrases. Like when I was at a friend’s house last week, we were playing “two truths and a lie.” One person said they once lived in a treehouse, another said they had a go-kart, and someone else said they had a parrot that could sing. It was ridiculous, but hilarious. Oh, I had one of those. I said I used to be a professional baker, I had my own shop, and I once won a competition for the best soufflé.

So, do you remember that time we tried to nap at the park during the festival and ended up getting caught by the bouncers? I swear, we were so tired we just fell asleep on the bench, and when we woke up, we were like, “Wait, where are we?” Oh man, that was the worst. I was so out of it, I thought we were in a sleepover at our flat. I even tried to argue with the guy who was watching us, like, “No, we’re not drunk, we’re just sleeping!” And he just stared at us like we were crazy. I still can’t believe we got away with it. It was like a dream. I remember you were snoring so loud, I thought someone was actually in the park with us. I mean, you screamed so loud when you woke up, like you were dreaming about something really intense. Oh yeah, I thought I was in a movie! I remember thinking, “Wait, is this the scene where the hero wakes up from the dream?” That was the best part. You looked so serious, like you were about to start a monologue about the meaning of life. I was! I was gonna say something like, “This is the most important moment of my life,” and then I remembered where I was and just fell back asleep. You were so dramatic, even for you. I swear, you could have gotten a role in a movie. You’re just jealous because you’re not the one who got a free drink out of the situation. Yeah, right. I was the one who had to pay for the whole thing. I didn’t even get a free drink. Oh, come on, you got to sit with me for the whole time. That was like a free VIP seat. You know what I was thinking the whole time? I was like, “I should take a picture of this. This is going to be the best story of my life.” Well, you’re not going to be telling it if you’re not here to hear it. I’ll tell it anyway. I’ll just say it was a dream. That’s what I’m gonna say. I’m gonna say I was dreaming about the whole thing. Yeah, and I’ll say I was just there to support you.

I just got a call from the council. They've agreed to let us proceed with the application for the new community center, but they want to hold a planning committee meeting next week to go through the details. Oh, good news. That’s a relief. I was worried they might put it on hold again. Yeah, I know. They’ve been quite cautious with these kinds of applications. But it looks like they’re open to the idea, especially with the support from the local MPs. That’s a good sign. Do you know when the meeting is? It’s scheduled for Thursday, the 12th, at 3 p.m. in the council’s main hall. We’ll need to bring all the documents and maybe some visuals to present the design. Sounds good. We should probably start preparing the presentation. I can help you with the slides if you want. That would be great. I was thinking we could include some of the community feedback we’ve received so far. It’ll show that there’s genuine support for the project. Exactly. And we should make sure to highlight the environmental benefits as well. The council is always pushing for sustainable development these days. Definitely. I’ll start compiling the data and send it to you tonight. Also, I need to make sure that all the zoning regulations are up to date. I can check that too. I remember reading a report about some changes to the planning laws last year. Let me dig it up and send it over. Perfect. If we can make sure everything is in order, we’ll be in a strong position for the meeting. Agreed. I’ll also reach out to some of the local volunteers to see if they can attend the meeting to show their support. That’s a smart move. More people at the meeting means more voices in favor of the project. I’ll make sure to mention the potential for job creation and how the center can serve as a hub for local businesses too. That’s a solid angle. It’s not just about the building—it’s about the community it serves. Exactly. I think we’re in a really good place. Hopefully, this will go smoothly, and we can get the green light soon. I really hope so. It’s been a long process, but I believe this is the right direction.

So, do you know what’s been going on with the neighbour since we came back from the weekend? Honestly, I’ve barely seen her. She’s been acting so weird lately. I heard she got thrown out of the local pub the other day for arguing with the barman about how he’s “too loud.” Oh no, is that true? I thought she was just a bit eccentric, but that sounds serious. What was the argument about? Something about her saying the barman was “changing the soul of the pub” or something like that. I don’t even know. It just sounds like she’s been going through some weird phase. Haha, you know how she always talks about “the good old days” like she’s from the 70s or something. Maybe she just needs a break from reality. Yeah, I guess. But I swear, last week she was in the garden shouting at the mailman for “not putting the letters in the right place.” I mean, what even? Speaking of weird things, have you seen the new graffiti on the wall by the back gate? It’s like some kind of ancient Roman symbol. I asked the landlord about it, and he just said, “It’s been there since I moved in.” Oh no, you’re not telling me you’re into that kind of stuff. You’re a project co-ordinator, not an archaeologist. I’m not, but it just feels like it’s got some kind of meaning. Maybe it’s from the old days when this place used to be a horse stable or something. Or maybe it’s just the work of some rebellious teenager trying to make a statement. I mean, that’s what I’d do if I were in a fight with the council. I don’t know. I think it’s just adding to the character of the place. Although, I did have a funny thought about it when I was making pasta the other day. What if it’s from a Roman settlement? And what if they used to cook in the same spot? That’s a bit too much. But hey, if you want to get into it, maybe we could go to the library and look up some historical stuff. I’m sure the local history group would love to hear about it. Maybe. But I’m more interested in going out to that film festival next week.

So, what do you think about that ad they just showed? It’s one of those ridiculous ones where they claim they can get you a perfect body in a week. Oh, I’ve seen those. They’re basically just trying to sell you some protein powder and a gym membership. I mean, if you really want to get fit, you need to actually do something. Not just buy stuff. Yeah, I know. I’ve tried some of these things. One time I bought this "miracle weight loss tea" and it made me feel like I was going to throw up. Not to mention it cost me more than a week’s worth of meals. Oh no, that’s not fun. I remember when I was in uni, I tried a few of those diet pills. They were all just sugar and caffeine, honestly. And they made me super anxious. That’s not a good look. I think I’m going to stick to cooking more and eating healthier. Also, I’ve been thinking about starting a blog about healthy eating, maybe even some tips for people with dyslexia. Like, how to read recipes when the text is confusing. That sounds cool. I mean, I know how tricky it can be – especially when you’re trying to follow a recipe and the instructions are all over the place. You don’t even know what the next step is. Yeah, exactly. I think there’s a market for that. Maybe even some kind of app or online resource. I’ve heard about some people using NLP techniques to help with reading difficulties. Maybe I could combine that with some simple, visual instructions. That’s a good idea. I’d love to see something like that. I’ve also been thinking about starting my own blog. I’m trying to get into journalism, so maybe writing about mental health and how it affects people’s ability to work or study. That’s awesome. You’ve always had a way with words. I think you’d do really well. As long as you stay consistent and keep building your portfolio. Thanks. I’m just waiting for the right opportunity. Oh, and I’ve been thinking about going to that car boot sale this weekend. They’ve got some cool stuff, like old books and posters. I might pick up some vintage magazines – you know, the ones from the 80s with all the big hair and neon.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about buying a house. I know it’s a bit early, but with the mortgage rates going up and everything, I feel like I need to get ahead of it. Yeah, I hear you. I’ve been thinking about that too. My sister’s got a friend who’s buying a place in the countryside. It’s not cheap, but she says it’s worth it. What’s your budget like? Honestly, I’m not sure. I think it’s one of those things where you just keep putting it off, but the older you get, the more you realize you need to act. I mean, with the cost of living, you can’t really live in the city forever. I think I’m in the same boat. I’ve been saving for a while now, but every time I think I’m ready, something comes up. The last time, I was going to put down a deposit, but then my car broke down, and I had to spend all the money on that. I can’t even imagine buying a house, honestly. I’d rather rent forever. I’m not even sure I’ve got the patience for it. Plus, I’ve got this job that’s so flexible, I’d be worried about being tied down. I guess it’s not just about the money, though. It’s about finding the right place. I mean, I want something close to the city, but not too expensive. I’ve been thinking about looking in the suburbs. You know, maybe just a small place with a garden. That sounds nice. I’ve been thinking about that too. We’ve got this friend who moved out of the city and now lives in a place with a garden. It’s so much cheaper, and he says he loves it. But I think the housing market is so strange now; it’s like you can’t just go in and buy anything. I know, it’s all so uncertain. I think I might have to start looking for a place soon. My parents are getting older, and I don’t want to be the one responsible for taking care of them if I have to move them. I’d rather be in a place where I can have the space and the stability. I can see that.

So, do you remember when we first moved into the area in the 1960s? It was a real scramble to find somewhere to live, wasn’t it? I mean, we didn’t have much money back then, and the housing market was a bit of a nightmare. Oh, I remember that well. I was just starting out as a teacher, and I had to rent a small flat in the city centre. It was tiny, and the landlord was a bit of a grump, but it was the best we could afford. And you know, we had to be careful with the rent because of the time change when we travelled. I remember once I got back from a weekend trip to the coast and the clock had changed, so I was late for my first day back at work. I had to explain to the headmaster why I was late, and he just gave me that look like I’d done something wrong. I had a similar experience when I was studying for my postgraduate course in dentistry. I remember going to Athens for a week to attend a lecture, and the very next day, the dictatorship started. We were all sitting in the lecture hall, and the professor just said, “Well, that’s a new political reality for us.” We didn’t know what to do. Some of us decided to leave, but I stayed and finished the course. It was a surreal time. And what about you, Bob? I remember you were the one who got the job in this area first. How did you manage to find somewhere to live? Oh, I had a friend who was a dentist and worked nearby. He let me stay in his flat for a few months while I was looking for something more permanent. I remember the place had a lot of character—old wooden floors, and the walls were covered in peeling paint. But it was cheap, and that’s what mattered back then. I still have that old photograph of me in the flat. I remember you mentioned once that you met your wife in a college lecture hall. I think it was during one of your early teaching days. You were always trying to find a way to meet someone, weren’t you? Yes, I did. I was teaching at a local college in Manchester when I met my wife.

Well, it’s a lovely place, isn’t it? Taunton – I mean, it’s not like the big cities, but it’s got that quiet charm. I’ve lived in Somerset all my life, so I know the area quite well. Although I must say, I’ve never been to Taunton before, so it’s a new experience for me. Oh, really? That’s interesting. I grew up in Sydney, so I’ve never been to England at all. It’s quite a contrast, isn’t it? I mean, I always thought of England as being more… traditional, you know? But I guess it depends on where you are. Oh, definitely. Somerset’s like that – it’s got that old-world feel to it. I used to run an art gallery back in the day, and I’d often get people from all over the world coming in, just to see the pieces. It was such a mix of cultures, which I loved. But now, I’m retired and just enjoying the slower pace of life. That sounds amazing. I worked as a speech and language therapist for most of my career. It was quite a rewarding job, but I think I’ve had enough of the professional world. I’ve always preferred the quiet, the slower way of living. I guess it’s just the way I’m built. I can relate to that. I did have a few years where I was working full-time, but after the kids grew up, I just wanted to focus on my own interests. I used to love collecting antiques, especially old paintings and furniture. It was a passion of mine. I still do it a bit, though, just for fun. That’s lovely. I always found it fascinating how people can have such deep connections with things they collect. I never really got into collecting, but I did love reading. I used to read so much when I was younger. It was like my escape. Reading’s a great escape. I think it’s one of the things I miss most since I retired. I used to read so much when I was working – always trying to find new inspiration for my art. Now, I just read for pleasure. That sounds like a perfect balance. I go out walking a lot these days, just to get some fresh air and clear my head.

I can't believe we've got everything ready. I mean, I've been trying to get the pasta out of the box for the last ten minutes. You're not the only one struggling with that. I swear, the pasta seems to have a mind of its own. I know, right? I think it's trying to escape. Maybe it's a rebellion against being cooked. Like,  I'm not a vegetable, I'm a free spirit!  You're just saying that because you’re a baker, and you've seen too many things in the oven. Exactly! Besides, the real hero here is the garlic. Without that, this dish wouldn’t even be worth the effort. You’re right. I mean, I used the garlic from the jar. It's been sitting there for ages, but it still smells amazing. Yeah, I used the fresh garlic from the garden. Mmm, you can really taste the difference. I wish I had a garden. I mean, I’ve got a flat in London, and the only thing growing is my plants. You could always start with something simple. Maybe a few herbs? Or even a small tomato plant. You could have your own little food source. That sounds like a lot of work. I’d probably forget to water it. Well, you could always ask me for help. I mean, I’m a professional at growing things. You’re a baker, not a gardener. Yeah, but I’ve got a thriving business. And I’ve got a little green corner in the back of the shop where I grow some herbs. That’s impressive. I mean, I’ve got a few plants, but I’ve never actually tried growing anything. Well, maybe it's time. And think about the Christmas decorations. You could grow your own Christmas tree. Oh, come on. That’s too much. No, it’s not. I mean, think about it. You’ve got a flat, you’ve got space. You could grow a few things, and then you wouldn’t have to buy all that stuff from the market. I guess. But you know, I’ve been thinking about Christmas. Oh yeah? What’s on your mind? I was wondering if we could do something different this year. Like, maybe have a little dinner and decorations at the café. That sounds like a great idea. You know, the café is usually closed during Christmas, but maybe we could open it up for a couple of days.

So, do you think I should go to Oxford or stay in Cambridge for my thesis? Hmm, well, it really depends on what you're studying. If it's something that requires a lot of resources or specialized libraries, Oxford might have more to offer. But Cambridge is a great place too—do you know what your department’s focus is? I’m actually thinking of doing a thesis on postcolonial literature. I’ve been reading a lot of books by writers like Salman Rushdie and Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie. That sounds fascinating. You know, Oxford has a strong reputation in postcolonial studies, with some incredible scholars in that field. But Cambridge has its own unique strengths too. I remember when I was your age, I did my thesis on the representation of empire in modern British fiction. It was a very different time, but it gave me a lot of insight. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that a lot. I mean, I love Cambridge—this place is so close to home, and I’ve built up such a good network here. But I also want to push myself and see what other possibilities there are. I get that. It’s always hard to leave the comfort of what you know. But remember, this is your chance to explore, to grow. Oxford’s got a lot of opportunities—especially in terms of interdisciplinary work. You could even combine literature with something like history or philosophy. I guess that’s something I haven’t really considered. I’ve been so focused on the literature side. But I do want to make sure I’m not missing out on other possibilities. Exactly. And you’re not alone in that. I know how much pressure it can be to make these decisions. You should talk to your supervisors and maybe even some current students at Oxford. Ask them what their experience has been. I will. But I also have to think about the practicalities. I don’t want to be thousands of miles away from my family. That’s completely understandable. It’s not just about the academics—it’s about your well-being too. If you’re going to be away for a while, you need to feel supported. Yeah, that’s true. I mean, I love the idea of being in Oxford, but I also know that it’s a big move.

So, I heard you're both involved in language research. That’s interesting—especially with the focus on Chinese and Arab culture. I’m actually doing a lot of work on dialect variation in the UK, but I’ve always been fascinated by how languages evolve, especially in places with rich historical backgrounds like Cambridge.      Yeah, I agree. It’s fascinating how languages reflect the history of a place. Speaking of history, I was just reading about the Roman influence on English place names. Some of them are quite interesting—like “Cambridge” itself, which comes from the Latin “Campania.” But I think you’re more into the linguistic side of things, right?      Definitely. I’m also working on a project about how dialects in the South East of England have changed over the past century. It’s a bit of a sad trend, actually. A lot of local dialects are disappearing, especially among younger generations. I wonder if this has anything to do with the influence of global languages like Chinese and Arabic, especially with the way they’re taught in schools now.      That’s a very valid point, and one I’ve touched on in my lectures. I’ve always found it interesting how language and culture are so closely intertwined. For example, when I was doing fieldwork in the Middle East, I noticed how much the structure of Arabic influenced the way people thought about time and space. It’s not just about vocabulary—it’s about perception.      That’s so true. I was just at an alumni event in Oxford where a lecturer was talking about how different language families affect cognitive processes. Well, I've been meaning to bring this up, Fran. I've been getting a bit concerned about the recent increase in supermarket prices. So, do you guys ever just get together and talk about what we love? Like, our favourite holidays, foods, or even animals? Nothing beats a good roast with Yorkshire puddings and chips. Yeah, I agree. I think there’s something comforting about a traditional meal. But I also really love trying new things. So, do you think we’re going to end up like our parents? I mean, like, working 9 to 5, buying a house, getting married, all that? Honestly, I don’t know. I mean, I like the idea of having a job I love, but I also want to travel more. I don’t think I want to be stuck in one place all my life. Yeah, I can see that. I mean, I love art, and I’d like to work in something creative. But I also know how hard it is to make a living doing that. I’ve seen some of my art teachers struggle. It’s scary, isn’t it? I mean, you look around and everyone seems to have a plan, like, “I’m going to be a doctor,” or “I’m going to be a lawyer.” But what about people like us? We’re not sure what we want to do. It’s like we’re stuck in limbo. I guess that’s the thing with university. It’s supposed to help you figure it out, but sometimes it just makes you more confused. I mean, I’m doing this essay on postmodernism, and I’m like, “Why does everything have to be so complicated?” Exactly! I mean, I understand it, but I don’t know if I’m ever going to be able to explain it to someone else. I feel like I’m just learning the language of art, not actually creating anything meaningful. That’s the struggle, isn’t it? I think about the people I see in the gallery and they look so sure of themselves. But I feel like I’m just trying to find my voice. And I’m not even sure what that voice sounds like. I think it’s easier to be creative when you’re younger, though. I mean, I’ve been playing computer games for years. I used to think it was just a hobby, but now I realize it’s actually a form of storytelling. It’s just not something people usually talk about as “art.” Yeah, I guess that’s true. I mean, I’ve been thinking about starting a podcast where I talk about games and how they relate to visual art. I know it sounds weird, but I think there’s a lot of overlap. It’s just not something I’ve ever seen explored in an academic way.

So, do you think I should make fish and chips for dinner tonight or just stick with the lasagna? Honestly, I’m not sure. I think you need something a bit different, you know? I mean, if we’re cooking, maybe we can just make the main dishes and go out for dessert? That sounds like a plan. I’ll go out and pick up some chocolate cake from the shop. Perfect. And maybe I’ll make the fish and chips after all. It’s been too long since I’ve had it.

Right, so I just wanted to go through the speaker consent forms again. I know we’ve all signed them, but I want to make sure we’re all on the same page regarding the seminar we’re presenting on international business communication. No worries, I’ve read through them again. It was pretty straightforward. Just confirming that we’re all willing to be public speakers and that our names will be on the event program. Yeah, I got that. I’m a bit nervous about being on stage, but it’s just a seminar, not a TED talk. We’ll be in a lecture hall, not a conference. Exactly, and it’s a short session—only an hour. We’ll be doing a bit of interactive work with the students, so it’s not just a lecture. I think the content will be more engaging than the usual dry seminar. Definitely. I was thinking we could start with a quick poll to see what the students think about cross-cultural communication challenges. That might help set the tone and get them involved from the start. I like that idea. I’ve had some experience with interactive seminars before, and it definitely keeps the audience more engaged. It also gives us a chance to see what they already know before we dive in. Agreed. I was also thinking about including case studies from different countries. Maybe something from the Middle East, Asia, and Europe. That way, we cover a range of cultural contexts. That sounds good. We should also include some practical tips on how to communicate effectively across different cultures. The students might find that more useful than just theory. Absolutely. I’ve heard from students before that they struggle with understanding non-verbal cues in different cultures. Maybe we can touch on that. It’s a common issue, especially in international business settings. Yes, and we could also mention the importance of language and tone. Sometimes even if you’re speaking the right words, the way you say them can have a different impact. I think that’s a solid structure. We could break it into three parts: understanding cultural differences, language and communication styles, and practical strategies for international business communication. That way, it flows logically. I like the flow. We could even include a short role-play activity where the students have to communicate in a simulated international business scenario.

I can't believe we actually made it through the whole semester without being completely overwhelmed by the workload. I feel like I’ve been living off coffee and sheer willpower for the past three months. I know, right? I feel like I’ve been in a constant state of panic since the first lecture. I mean, I  am  a lecturer, but I haven’t had to teach full-time in years. It’s like trying to run a marathon when you’ve never even run a sprint. Yeah, and now we’re both doing the same thing. It’s kind of ironic, isn’t it? We’re both lecturers who are now students again, learning how to teach again. It’s like we’ve gone full circle. I know. I keep thinking about how I used to tell my students, “Don’t be afraid to ask questions. It’s how you learn.” But now I’m the one sitting in the lecture hall, trying not to fall asleep while my own professor talks about postcolonial theory. I mean, I actually like it, in a way. It’s refreshing to be back in the classroom, but it’s definitely a different kind of pressure. And don’t even get me started on the house. I don’t know how we’re going to manage all of this. We’ve got a mortgage, bills, and now we’re also paying for courses and materials. I know. Between our jobs and trying to make ends meet, it’s a bit of a balancing act. I mean, we’re both still earning, but it’s like we’re working full-time and studying part-time. I wonder how we’re going to keep this up. I keep telling myself that this is temporary. We’ll get through it, and then we’ll be back to our normal lives. I just hope we don’t end up with a house that’s as overcomplicated as our schedules. Ha! That’s one way to put it. I mean, we  are  living in a house that’s basically a museum of our own making. Every room has some kind of academic reference or relic from our past.

So, do you remember how we used to cook in our grandparents’ house? It was always such a mess, but somehow the food always tasted better. I miss that chaos. Yeah, I do. I mean, it wasn’t just the food—it was the whole environment. We’d all be in there, like, cooking and arguing about who was going to do what, and somehow it always ended up being a great meal. I think that’s one of the things I miss most about growing up there. Exactly. It was like a family tradition. Even though we didn’t always agree on the recipes, we all had our part to play. I think that’s the real magic of cooking with family. But do you ever think about how different it is now? I mean, most people just order takeaway or use meal replacement shakes. Yeah, I can’t believe how much the food scene has changed. I mean, when I was in school, the kitchen in our old house was the heart of everything. Now, even in my own flat, the kitchen is just a place to store things and maybe make a quick meal. It’s sad, in a way. It is. I think part of it is the way we’re raised. Schools don’t teach cooking anymore. They focus more on STEM subjects and less on practical skills like how to cook a decent meal. I’m trying to change that with my own kids. I even signed them up for a cookery class, which I think is a good start. That’s great. I’ve thought about doing the same with my son, but I’m not sure how much time I’ll have. I’m working in engineering, and it’s about as far from cooking as you can get. Although, I did try to make a stew once, and it turned into a disaster. I think I burned the whole thing. That’s the thing with cooking—it’s not just about following a recipe. It’s about intuition, and sometimes you have to just go with your gut. I remember my mum always saying, “If you don’t like how it’s turning out, just add more of what you like.” It’s amazing how much wisdom she had. I can see that. Maybe that’s why I’m really into urban farming initiatives these days.

I just need to chop these onions, and then I'll get the pan ready. You know, I've been thinking a lot about work lately. It's been so intense with all these research proposals due soon. So, do you know if there's any news about the new job opportunities in the care sector? I’ve been thinking about expanding my hours, maybe even looking for something closer to home. So, do you remember that study we read about last week? The one about how blue light from phones affects our sleep? Oh, yes! I still can’t believe how much our devices are messing with our circadian rhythms. I’ve been trying to cut down on screen time before bed, but it’s harder than it sounds. I know, I’ve been doing the same. Though I’ve been thinking about how much worse it is when you’re on a trip or something. Like, when you’re camping and you have to rely on a phone for navigation, but then the light from the screen messes up your sleep even more. Oh, right! I had that exact problem last summer. My friend and I went camping in the Lake District. We tried to set up camp early, but then we got lost and had to use the phone for directions. By the time we got back, we were both so tired and the light from the phone kept us awake for hours. Yeah, I can imagine. I once tried to find my way through Edinburgh by myself. I thought I had a good map, but I ended up walking in circles for over an hour. It was only when I found a café that I could ask for directions. That sounds like a nightmare! I’ve been there too. I once tried to take the underground to a friend’s house in London and got off at the wrong station. I spent the next hour wandering through the city, trying to figure out where I was. It was so frustrating. I remember that. I think it was something to do with the red and green lines being similar. I ended up walking past the place I was supposed to be for over 30 minutes. I was so lost, I even considered going back to my hotel and staying there. I feel for you. But I guess that’s just part of living in a city. Although, I’ve heard about some people using apps to find the best routes. I’ve never tried them, though. I always prefer to read a map or ask for directions. Yeah, but sometimes you just can’t trust the apps. I’ve had friends who’ve relied too much on them and ended up in the wrong place. I think it's a mix of knowing where you're going and trusting your instincts.

So, do you know what’s up with the new guy in our flat? He’s got this  huge  ginger beard and he’s always talking about his hamster. Alright, do you think we've got this game mapped out? I swear the map's more confusing than the rules. Honestly, I think the map is just a cover for the real chaos that's going on in this game. You know, like how sometimes you think you're winning, and then it's all over. It's like trying to predict the weather. You never know what's going to happen next. I think the game is as much about learning as it is about strategy. That’s what I’ve been thinking too. My sister used to teach geography, so she always said the best way to go about it is to see if you can pronounce the place names correctly. Oh, I tried that once with a friend, and we ended up arguing about the pronunciation of "Genghis Khan."

So, do you ever just lie awake at night thinking about what you're going to do after uni? So, do you know what we're doing for the school project? I’m so confused. Yeah, I think it's about scientific research and how it affects everyday life, right? Our teacher said it's supposed to be something we can relate to. Yeah, but how do we even start? I mean, we’re just kids. How do we know enough about all that? So, how’s the recording process going? You mentioned you were going to start recording your songs again. It’s going okay, I guess. I’m just not sure if I’m up for it. Look, I’m not saying it’s easy. But you’ve got a lot of potential. You just need to believe in your own voice. I hope so. I really do. And don’t forget, you’re not alone in this.

So, do you want some of these chips? I’ve just popped them in the oven. Yeah, thanks. I’m starving. I haven’t had a proper meal all day. How long have you been cooking? Not long. So, do you guys remember that movie we watched last week? The one with the time travel and the guy who ended up in the future? It was so weird, right? Yeah, I remember that one. I thought it was pretty good, but the ending confused me. Like, why did he go back to the past again? It felt like it just didn’t make sense. I agree. I think the director tried too hard to make it deep, but it ended up being more confusing than anything. I was like, "What was the point?" Honestly, I didn’t even get half of it. I just stayed until the end and then asked my sister what happened. She said it was "a metaphor for growing up." Oh, I saw that one too. I thought it was actually pretty cool. It made me think about how our lives can change so much in a short time. Like, how one decision can lead to something completely different. Yeah, that was a good point. I mean, I still don’t get the ending, but I can see why people liked it. It was different from the usual sci-fi movies. I think it’s because we’re all in our final year of school, right? So we’re all thinking about the future and all that. It’s like, you know, life is like a movie, and we're just trying to figure out our plot. Exactly. I mean, I’ve been watching a lot of old horror movies lately. They’re so campy, but they’re fun to watch. The dialogue is so cheesy, but it’s kind of entertaining. I prefer the newer stuff. Like, the ones with all the CGI and explosions. I mean, that’s what I watch when I want to escape for an hour. But yeah, horror movies are cool too. I’m more into documentaries. You know, like the ones about space or something. They’re educational, and I always learn something. I think I'm getting into more dramas recently. I watched one about a girl who had to deal with her family’s issues after her dad died. It was really emotional. That sounds intense. I think I'd have cried. I prefer the action ones. I mean, if I can't run away from something, at least I can pretend I'm fighting it.

So, I just got back from Paris with my mum, and I’m still in shock. I mean, it was  amazing , but I was so tired after the flight. I didn’t think I’d be able to do it after that long-haul flight, but I made it through.      That’s a long flight. I remember when I used to travel for work all the time, I used to get jet lag so bad I’d be confused for days. But you’re a grown-up now, so you can handle it, right?      Honestly, I’m still not over the fact that I had to carry my own suitcase through Charles de Gaulle Airport. I mean, I’m a mental health nurse, not a tourist! I thought they’d have someone to help, but I ended up dragging my bag through security like a toddler.      Oh, I feel you. I was so nervous about the airport, but once I got there, it was just chaos. I couldn’t believe how many people were running around with luggage. One guy was carrying a suitcase bigger than he was, and he was like, “I’m going to Paris for a week, and this is all I need!”      Sounds like the kind of guy who’d be the one who forgets to pack a toothbrush. I’ve had that kind of roommate before. Anyway, how was the trip overall? Did you see all the places you wanted to?      We did! We saw the Eiffel Tower, Montmartre, the Seine River, and a bunch of cute little cafes. I got a croissant and it was  so  good. I’ve never had one that wasn’t just like... okay, not bad. But this one? It was like a work of art.      I bet it was. I still can’t believe you managed to take a whole week off work. I was stuck in hospital all weekend with a patient who had a funny habit of holding onto the bed rail like it was a security blanket. You know, the one that’s got a  bit  of a history.      Yeah, I heard about that. Some people just can’t let go, no matter how uncomfortable it gets. That must have been frustrating.      It was. But at least I got to spend quality time with my mum. She was amazing—she’s been through some stuff lately, and it was good to see her happy and relaxed.

Hey, Sally! How's it going? You're early for class. Hey, Tom! I just finished my coffee, and I thought I’d grab a quick chat before heading in. How are you? I’m good, thanks. So, do you think I should add some jalapenos to the curry? I mean, it’s not like I’m making it for a bunch of people or anything. Oh, you don’t need to go overboard with the heat, love. Your mum wouldn’t be happy if you burned her tongue. But a little bit of jalapeno adds some nice kick. Just don’t drown it in oil. Yeah, I guess. But I’m not even sure how to cook rice properly. Well, there are some signs. If it’s discolored, has a strong smell, or feels slimy, it’s probably not safe. And if it’s been in the fridge for more than a couple of days, it’s better to play it safe. Okay, I’ll remember that. I just hope the rice comes out okay. I’ve never cooked it from scratch before. You’ll get the hang of it. Just take your time. And don’t forget to check the salt.

Though I have to say, I’ve been thinking about Hitler a lot lately. Not in a bad way, just… I don’t know, it’s just something that keeps coming up in my head. Why? What’s with Hitler? So, do you think we should get new furniture for the flat? I've been thinking it's time to upgrade a bit, you know, with the kids moving out and everything. Honestly, I don't know. I mean, we have what we need, but maybe it's time to get some fresh stuff. I've been eyeing that IKEA catalog online. It's got some really nice pieces. I think you're right, love. You can always go for a few new pieces and see how it goes. I mean, the old sofa is starting to look a bit sad. Her partner's got dementia, and she's had to sort of start over with everything. You know, the furniture, the house, the whole thing. It's just so hard. Oh, I can only imagine. That's a massive change. I think getting new furniture is a small thing compared to what she's going through. But it's good that we can have a bit of a normal day, you know? Exactly. I mean, I don't know if it's the same for us, but it's nice to have that stability. I mean, we've got our extended family around us, and even though we're not close to them, we know they're there. That's the thing, isn't it? You know, sometimes when you're out and about, like at the tip or the shops, you see people doing things you wouldn't think of. Like, I saw someone washing their clothes in the car park the other day. It's not like they're rich or anything, but it's just so strange.

Mum, do you know I got a message this morning about my job? I’m supposed to be meeting with the head of the department to discuss my redundancy. Oh no, really? That’s not good news at all. So, what are we doing today? I'm bored, dad. I need something fun to do. I know, love. I’m just trying to figure it out too. You know, with the weather being so nice and everything. Swim? Swim! I wanna swim! Yeah, swimming’s a good idea. We could go to the local pool. Yeah, but I also want to play guitar. I’ve been practising a bit. That sounds good. But don’t forget, we’ve got some jobs to do around the house. Yeah, I know, but I can do both. I’ll do the jobs first, then play guitar. That’s the spirit. And what about Mick? I remember when I was your age, I used to watch it too. It was quite a big thing. Yeah, but I also want to do something with my friends. We could go to the park or – I want to go to the park! We can do that later. Right now, I think we should try to get the garden sorted. It's been a bit of a mess. Yeah, I can help with that. But then I’d like to go to the library and try to find some books about Japanese. Japanese? That’s interesting. Why Japanese? I just thought it would be fun to learn some phrases. I saw this app online that helps you learn languages. That sounds like a good idea. But don’t get too carried away. You’ve got a lot to do. I know, I know. I’ll just stick to one thing at a time. Can I have a snack? Sure, love. Let’s get you something. What about the summer holidays? I think we should do something special. Maybe go on a trip? That could be nice, but we’ll have to save up for it. Yeah, maybe we can do a day trip somewhere. I’m thinking of going to Stonehenge or something. That’s a long way. What about somewhere closer? Maybe the coast? Yeah, the coast sounds good. I’ve never been there. Can we go to the beach? We can go to the beach, but only if we do the jobs first, okay?

Alright, so I just watched this film called  The Dentist —you know, the one with that guy who got turned into a human tooth? Oh yeah, that one where he ends up in a dental clinic and gets tortured by the dentist? Exactly! It’s so weird and disturbing, but in a kind of fascinating way. I mean, it’s like a horror film with a psychological twist. I got halfway through it and then just couldn’t watch it anymore. Too much. Didn’t you get the whole point? It’s supposed to be uncomfortable. I know, but the thing is, I’ve been trying to get over my fear of dentists for ages. This just reminded me of that. Aww, that’s sweet. You should try to take your mum to a dentist. She’s always complaining about her teeth. Yeah, she’s been needing a filling for months. I’m not even sure she knows how bad it is. She probably thinks it’s just a small chip. I mean, we all think that way. Exactly. You know, I was reading this book the other day about how people rationalise their fears. It’s like, you tell yourself, “It’s not that bad,” or “I can handle it,” but deep down you’re panicking. That’s so true. I remember when I was a kid, I used to be terrified of the dentist. I’d lie about my teeth, and my mum would just say, “Oh, you’re just being dramatic.” I remember that. You’d have to lie to her, like, “No, my teeth are fine.” Yeah! And she’d just nod and say, “Okay, then.” It’s like we’re all just avoiding the truth. But I think it’s also about control. When you’re at the dentist, you lose control. You can’t move, you can’t speak, and you can’t even really hear what they’re doing. That’s a good way to put it. It’s like being on a Citibike in a crowded city. You’re stuck, you can’t really move, and you’re just hoping it doesn’t crash. Exactly! Except with the dentist, you can’t even get off the bike. Haha. I think I’m going to start writing about this. I’m trying to get back into writing, and this whole dentist thing is giving me so much material.

So, how’s the new job going, love? I heard you got the teaching post in the village school. Oh, it’s going really well, Mum. I’ve been there for a month now, and it’s such a nice place. And look where that’s got me. I’m still there, but I’ve never felt like I’m in the right place. I think you’re a lot wiser than I was at your age. You’re being too kind. I think I’m just in a better place now. I mean, I’m not the same person I was when I left university. I’ve grown up a bit. I know you have. And speaking of growing up, how are things with the family? It’s been ages since we’ve had a proper family gathering.

So how’s life treating you, Ann? You know, since we last caught up, it’s been a while. Oh, it’s been a few months, hasn’t it? Life’s been pretty busy, as usual. I’ve been juggling work and family, like always. My daughter’s just started her first year at university, so it’s been a whirlwind of exams and applications. That’s amazing. There’s so much pressure on teachers, and the funding is still not up to scratch. But I’ve managed to keep things going. I’ve even started a small tutoring business on the side, helping students with their exam prep. That’s a smart move. I was thinking about getting back into something like that, but I don’t know if I have the time. I’m already juggling my job as a language teacher and looking after my two kids. You’d be surprised how much time you can manage with the right systems in place. I’ve got a pretty solid routine now. I make sure I set aside specific times for work and family. It helps a lot. I suppose you’re right. I need to start thinking about that. Speaking of which, have you heard about the new beauty product line that’s been getting so much attention? I’m thinking of trying it out. Oh, I’ve heard about it. It’s supposed to be really good for sensitive skin. I’ve been looking into natural skincare products lately, especially since my skin has been a little more sensitive lately. That’s a good idea. I’ve been feeling a bit self-conscious about my skin lately, especially with the weather changing so much. Maybe I should look into some of those natural options.

So, do you think we’ve got enough food for everyone? I mean, with all the matzah and everything. I’m not sure. I think we need more wine. It’s a Seder, after all. You know, the journey from slavery to freedom. It’s kind of like what we’re doing now, with our own journeys. It’s just more comfortable. Yeah, but I still think the food is worth it. I’m more into Italian food. I’ve been planning to visit Naples. I’ve heard the pizza there is incredible. I’ve even been looking into a recipe for Neapolitan pizza. It’s got to be better than the stuff you get in London. I’m not sure about that. I mean, I know the food’s good, but I’d rather be in New York. There’s this amazing baker in Brooklyn that makes the best bagels I’ve ever had.

So, do you think we should bring up the new BBC series we’ve been talking about? I’ve been dying to discuss it. I’m more than happy to, but I think we should wait until we’ve all had our coffee. I was thinking of  The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo —it’s a bit of a romance, but I’ve heard great things about it. I’ve also been curious about trying a new genre. Maybe something more mysterious? I’ve been getting into some of the newer mystery authors, like Tana French. She’s really good, and the characters are so well-developed.

So, do you know how to set up this new phone? I’ve got this Samsung Galaxy, and it’s all in English, but I can’t find the settings for the Bluetooth. I’m a bit of a tech newbie, you know? Sounds simple enough. But I’m still not sure about the Bluetooth. I tried pairing my headphones, but they just keep blinking. What’s the trick? Let me take a look. Oh, you probably have to enable Bluetooth from the quick settings panel. You can swipe down from the top of the screen. Then tap on Bluetooth and make sure it’s turned on. Mum, can we talk about my birthday party? I really want to have it at the park.      Oh, love, the park is great, but we need to think about the weather. What if it rains?      Well, I can bring a tent. And I want to invite all my friends from school.      That sounds lovely, but let’s make a list of people first. We don’t want to forget anyone.      Okay, but can we also have a cake? I really like chocolate cake.      Of course, love. And maybe we can get a few cupcakes too, just in case.      Cool. Oh, and I got a new book about red pandas. They’re so cute!      Red pandas? I love animals, but I’ve never seen one in the wild.      Me neither! I read that they live in the mountains of China, right?      Yeah, I think so. I remember seeing a documentary about them once. They’re really rare.      Yeah, and they have those fluffy tails. I want to have a red panda decoration for the party.      That’s a great idea, but let’s not get too carried away. We have to keep things simple.      I know, but it would make the party more special.      Well, if you’re sure, then let’s start planning. What about the games?      I want to play tag and maybe some board games. I brought a few with me.      That sounds good. I can set up a little table for the games.      And what about my superhero costume? I want to wear it for the party.      Of course, love. You’ve worked really hard on that. I’m so proud of you.      Thanks, Mum. Oh, and I saw a Malamooche dog on a walk today. It was so friendly!      A Malamooche? That’s a big dog. I hope it wasn’t too rowdy.      No, it was really gentle. I think it was on a lead.      That’s good to hear. We should be careful with dogs, especially at the park.      Yeah, I know. But I think the dog was just being friendly.      Maybe it was. I’m just being cautious, that’s all.      I understand, Mum. So, when do you think we should start preparing for the party?      Let’s start tomorrow. I’ll make a list of people and send out the invitations.      Great! And I’ll bring the cake and the decorations.      Perfect. I’ll also check the weather forecast to make sure we’re ready for anything.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to have that huge Christmas tree in the living room? It was like a real forest in there! Yeah, I remember that. My nan used to wrap all the presents in those shiny silver and gold paper things. They looked like they were from a spaceship or something. Oh, I remember that too. I used to love the way the lights would flicker and make the tree look magical. But I also remember how messy it all got. We’d have to clean up for weeks after. I still remember the one year when the tree collapsed on top of the TV. My wife nearly had a heart attack. It was a real disaster. Oh man, that must have been a wake-up call. I think I still have a few of those old lights tucked away in the loft. I was about to sell them, but I just couldn’t part with them. I think they’re worth something. I remember one of the garlands had a little tin star on it, and that was from when we were kids. We used to hang them up every year like it was a tradition. You know, I think there was something about the way we used to celebrate Christmas growing up. It wasn’t just about the food or the gifts, it was about the whole experience. The traditions, the family, the togetherness. And the food! I still remember those roast dinners, all the sides, the gravy. My mum made the best plum pudding. I can still taste it in my dreams. I think it’s funny how different people celebrate Christmas in different ways. I mean, I’ve been to a few places where the decorations are different, the food is different, and even the way people talk about it is different. Yeah, I remember when I was in the Philippines, Christmas was completely different. They had all these light displays, and they celebrated it with a lot of music and dancing. I loved it, but it was a bit confusing at first. That’s interesting. I always thought that Christmas was more of a British tradition, but I guess it's just a holiday that's adapted in different cultures. It really is. I think that's what makes it so special—how it can be embraced in so many different ways, while still keeping the core spirit of the season.

So, how’s the new workload at work? I know you’ve been working on that big project for the last few months. It’s been a bit intense, to be honest. But I think we’re close to wrapping it up. I’m just waiting on a few final approvals from the higher-ups. It’s been a long process, but I’m glad it’s almost over. I can only imagine. I’ve been trying to get into a routine, but with the holidays and everything, it’s been hard to stay on track. I think I’m going to try to set a daily writing goal, even if it’s just a few hundred words a day. That sounds like a solid plan. I always found that setting small, achievable goals helps. It also keeps you motivated. I tried that with my own writing, and it made a massive difference. Maybe we should all set some kind of writing or work goals for the next few months. I know I’ve been wanting to get back into some kind of routine. I’ve been working too much and not enough on personal projects. Definitely. I think having a structured plan would help. Speaking of which, have you been keeping up with the detective series you mentioned last week? I think it’s coming back to the finale soon. Oh, I haven’t gotten around to watching it yet. I’ve been so busy with work and family stuff. But I’ve been meaning to. I think I’ll try to catch up this weekend. That’s a good idea. I think I’ll try to do the same.

Well, I've just been taking a walk in the fields, and I thought I’d pop in for a bit of chat. It’s been ages since we last saw each other. Oh, good to hear from you, John. It’s been a while. How are things with you? Not too bad, honestly. It’s the same old, same old. I’ve been keeping myself busy with the garden, but I must admit, I’m getting a bit fed up with the weeds. They just keep coming back no matter how much I try to chase them out. That’s the problem with old age, isn’t it? You get tired and your back starts to ache, and you just don’t have the energy to do all the work. I used to be able to dig for hours, but these days, I’m lucky if I manage to get through a morning’s gardening without needing a rest. I know what you mean, Martin. I used to be the man in the garden, but now I can’t even lift a spade properly without taking a break. Well, listen, I’ve been thinking about your health. You know, I’ve started taking some more time for myself lately—more rest, more pacing, more walks. It’s helped me a lot. Maybe you could try something like that? I suppose I could. It’s just hard to get started. I always tell myself I’ll do it tomorrow, and then tomorrow comes and I still haven’t done it. It’s a common problem, John. I had the same habit when I was running the business. I’d always put things off, and before I knew it, I was behind schedule. But I learned the hard way that you can’t keep putting things off forever. You’ve got to make time for yourself. That’s right. And you know, I’ve been thinking about taking up some sort of hobby. I used to love painting, but I haven’t touched a brush in years. Maybe I should try again. It’s a way to keep your mind active and your hands busy. That sounds like a good idea. I’ve always enjoyed drawing a bit, even if it’s just sketches of the garden or the birds. I think it would do me good to get back into something like that.

So, I just wanted to check if we've got all the details sorted for the team party next week. I got the email from the office about the venue, and I think it's that new bar in the city centre. Maybe it’s just trying to find a way out.      Maybe if we open a window or something, it might just fly out on its own. I don’t want to hurt it, but I’m not sure how to go about saving it.

So, do you know what’s going on with the exams? I swear I’ve seen the schedule for next term, but it’s like someone randomly erased half of it. Yeah, I know! It’s so confusing. I think they’re trying to trick us into thinking we’re getting more time, but then they just squeeze everything into the same week as the last term. Honestly, I feel like we’re just running on a treadmill. One day it’s revision, the next it’s a test, and then we’re just expected to remember everything. It’s not fair. I totally agree. And don’t even get me started on the mocks. I had this one history test about the French Revolution, and I was so sure I knew it all, but then I messed up the date of the storming of the Bastille.
