I swear, I just got an email from Amazon saying they’re going to deliver a package to my house in like... three hours. But I haven’t even ordered anything yet. Oh no, are you sure it’s not a phishing email? I mean, you know how many fake emails pop up these days, especially when you’re unemployed and just scrolling through your phone. Yeah, I know. But I actually clicked on the link just to see what it was. And it was legit—like, it had my name and everything. It even said “Your order is being processed.” I don’t know, it just feels like they’re trying to get me to buy something I don’t need. My brother’s been telling me the same thing. He says that now, if you’re not shopping online, you’re not living. Like, he’s got an app for everything—groceries, clothes, even his old textbooks. He just re-enrolled for his degree and ordered all his books in one go. Yeah, I guess it’s kind of convenient. I mean, I don’t have to leave the house. I can just order anything and have it delivered. But I feel like I’m losing track of real life. Like, I don’t know if I’ve ever actually gone to a shop in person since I got laid off. I know, right? It’s so easy to just sit on the couch, scroll through your phone, and order everything. But I think it’s making us more detached from the real world. I mean, I still do some shopping in person, but it’s rare. I feel like I’m just buying stuff I don’t need because it’s easy. I think I’m starting to feel that way too. I just ordered a new phone because I couldn’t find the one I had on sale. But honestly, I don’t even use the old one that much. It’s like I’m just buying things to feel like I’m doing something. Like, I’m working. You’re not the only one. My cousin just got a job doing online retail stuff. He says it’s not much, but it pays enough to cover the basics. He’s got a nice setup—his room’s basically a go-to-place for ordering stuff from everywhere.

So, do you think we should get a new cooker, or is the old one still okay? I mean, it’s been in the house for over twenty years, and I can’t say I’ve ever had a problem with it. Not that I’ve ever cooked much, but it’s always worked. Well, I think the new one would be better. I mean, the old one’s not exactly a work of art, but if it's still functioning, why replace it? Although, you know, there's something about a new cooker. It makes you feel like you're starting fresh. I agree with Helen. I think it’s time. I mean, the old one only has one ring and a few burners, and I’ve already had to replace the hob. Not to mention the fact that the timer doesn’t work anymore. If we’re going to spend money on anything, let’s do it properly. I suppose you’re right. I mean, if we’re planning the walk later, maybe we should do some shopping first. I heard there’s a furniture store in Exeter that’s having a sale this week. Maybe we can check that out. That sounds like a good idea. We could even combine it with buying some new chairs for the living room. I’ve been thinking about getting a couple of nice, comfortable ones for the evenings. Especially now that we’re all home more. Oh, I already got a few pieces from the charity shop. They had a nice wooden table and two chairs. It was a bit of a struggle to move them, but it was worth it. I think we can still use some of them, but maybe we can add a few more to make the place feel a bit more like home. Yeah, and I’ve been thinking about the heating. I know it’s not the best, but maybe we could do something about it. I mean, if we’re going to be here for a while, we might as well make sure it stays warm during the winter. You’re right. We could look into upgrading the boiler. I’ve heard that some people do that and it saves money in the long run. Although, I’d be careful with the bills. We don’t want to end up in the same situation as last year.

So, how’s the new project at work going? I know you’ve been trying to get it off the ground for a while now. It’s going okay, I guess. There’s been a few hiccups with the funding, but I think we’re on track. It’s just figuring out how to balance the different stakeholders. You know, the school board, the parents, and the kids themselves—it’s a bit of a balancing act. Sounds like the usual. I remember when I was working on that mental health initiative at the university. It was a nightmare trying to get everyone on the same page. But it paid off in the end. Yeah, I suppose it does. But I’m starting to wonder if I’m actually making a difference. I mean, I’m working with kids, and they’re so open and honest. Sometimes I feel like I’m just a voice in the crowd. You’re not. You’re helping them navigate a system that’s not always designed with them in mind. I think the real impact isn’t always immediate, but it’s there. I hope so. I just worry that sometimes the focus is on the numbers and the reports rather than the actual kids. You know, it’s easy to get lost in the paperwork. I get that. But I think it’s important to remember why you started. You’re not just doing this for the job or the promotion. You’re doing it for the kids. And that’s what matters. That’s true. It just feels like sometimes the pressure’s so high, you have to keep pushing through. I’m trying to take it one day at a time, but it’s not always easy. I know the feeling. I had a really tough time when I was doing my postdoc. The pressure was intense, and there were days I questioned whether I was on the right path. But I kept going because I believed in the work. That’s inspiring. I think I need to remind myself of that more often. I mean, we’re not just working to get ahead—we’re trying to make a difference in people’s lives. Exactly. And remember, you’re not alone in this. We’re in this together. You’ve got a great team, and you’ve got me. If you ever need someone to talk to or just vent to, I’m here.

So, I was just thinking about that time we tried to train the cat to fetch. It was a disaster. I don’t know what we were thinking.      Oh, I remember! You tried to use a ball and a command, and then it just ran off with it and knocked it into the fish tank.      That was  so  dramatic. The cat looked like it was trying to save the fish.      Oh, I’ve had a similar experience with my dog. He was obsessed with the ball, but when he’d run after it, he’d just crash into the wall and knock everything over.      That sounds like my dog too. My dog is left-handed, you know. He’s always grabbing things with his left paw. It’s almost like he’s trying to be a little rebel.      Left-handed? I didn’t even think about that. My brother was left-handed, and he used to get in so much trouble at school. He’d always have to use the right-handed pencils and stuff.      I think it’s pretty cool, actually. Left-handed people are often seen as more creative. I mean, I’m left-handed, and I love writing.      Yeah, I think that’s true. I’ve always heard that left-handed people are more creative or maybe more intuitive.      I don’t know about that, but I do know that left-handed people are often more independent. That might be a good trait for someone like me, being self-employed.      Hey, speaking of left-handedness, did you ever notice how most people are right-handed? It’s like there’s a social norm that makes people feel like they have to conform.      Definitely. I remember as a kid, my parents used to try to force me to use my right hand. It was so frustrating. I just wanted to write with my left.      I feel you. I used to get so annoyed when people would comment on my left-handedness. It’s just a part of who I am.      You know, I think it’s interesting how left-handedness is still kind of a mystery. I mean, we know it’s genetic, but I wonder how much of it is environmental.      I think some of it could be environmental. I’ve seen kids who are left-handed in some cultures, but not in others. It’s like it’s not just about genes.

So, do you reckon we should go to the market tomorrow? I’ve been thinking about getting some fresh vegetables and maybe some local cheese from the farm down the road. Oh, I’d love that. I’ve been meaning to try some of the local produce. I remember my mum used to buy cheese from that farm when I was a kid. She always said it was the best in the area. Yeah, I think that sounds like a great idea. I've actually been planning to go there myself. I heard they have some really good artisanal goods. Maybe we could all meet up and go together? That'd be nice. I've got the day off tomorrow, so I can definitely do that. Just need to make sure I don't forget my shopping list. I’m getting a bit forgetful these days. Oh, I know what you mean. I forget things all the time. I had a cup of tea yesterday and I couldn’t remember where I put the milk. It was in the fridge, of course. I think I need to start writing down my lists. I’ve started using a notes app on my phone. It’s been a lifesaver. I still make mistakes, but it helps me remember things more clearly. I got into the habit when I was working on projects. It’s just so much easier to have everything in one place. That’s a good idea. I’ve got an iPhone, but I never use the notes app. Maybe I should start. I’ve been trying to get better at organisation, especially with work. I had a bit of a mess with my schedule last week. I can relate. I had a few things I needed to do but kept putting them off. It’s funny how things can slip through your fingers. I think that’s why I’ve started taking it a day at a time. One thing at a time, you know? Yeah, that’s a good way to look at it. I think it’s about managing expectations too. Not trying to do too much at once. I’ve been going on trips to different places, and it’s been a good way to clear my mind and get some perspective. That sounds like a great way to relax. I really need to get out more.

So, do you think we should go through the whole syllabus for the next class or just focus on the key points? I think we should stick to the key points, honestly. It’s a bit overwhelming trying to cover everything in one go, especially with the time we have. We’ve got two weeks before the next session, so we can spread it out a bit. Yeah, I agree. I was just thinking about the food we had for lunch. Oh, and the way the catering here is—it’s so different from back home. I mean, the variety of dishes is amazing, but I still haven’t figured out how to order anything that’s not either too spicy or too bland. My friend said it’s all about the balance here. You have to mix the flavors, right? I tried the dumplings the other day and they were perfect. I was just sitting there thinking how different this is from the British food I’m used to. I miss the comfort food. You know, the kind of food that feels like home. I mean, I could eat a plate of chips with some fish and chips every day if I had the chance. But here, it’s all about the spices and the variety. I get it. I miss home too. Especially the TV. I mean, I know we have some streaming services here, but the shows just don’t feel the same. You don’t get the same kind of cultural references or the same humor. Oh, I remember when we first moved here, I tried to watch some British shows with subtitles. It was a bit of a struggle, but I got used to it. We can still binge-watch our favorite shows on the weekend. It’s a bit of a ritual. Yeah, I think that’s important. Having that routine helps. It gives us a sense of normalcy. I mean, planning the classes is part of our routine too, right? It keeps us grounded. Exactly. I was just thinking about how we’re both lecturers, but we’re also trying to adapt to a new environment. It’s a bit of a balancing act. But I think we’re doing pretty well. I think we are. I mean, even though we’re on opposite sides of the world, we still manage to find common ground in work, food, and TV.

I can't believe we've got this coffee machine now, can we? I was just thinking, it's like having a mini café in the kitchen. Yeah, it's great, isn't it? I mean, we've spent so much on it, but it's worth it. I can make proper coffee now, instead of that instant stuff we used to have. Oh, you’ve only just got it? I thought this was a top priority for you. I mean, you’ve been talking about it for ages. Well, it took a while to get the right one. And then there was the whole removal and storage thing. I had to get rid of half my stuff just to fit it in the van. I know, I know. You were so stressed about it. But honestly, I think it's worth it. And besides, it’s a small price to pay for proper coffee. Yeah, but you know what I'm thinking, though? I mean, isn't this just another example of how we overcomplicate things? We used to have a coffee machine that worked, and now we’ve got this complicated thing that takes ages to set up. That’s not fair. This one is so much better. And besides, I’ve got a new routine now. I like the process. I like the way it starts the day. Maybe you’re just being idealistic. Like, someone who thinks everything has to be perfect. But I get it. You want to do things properly. Or maybe it’s just another symptom of the Labour leadership crisis. You know, all this talk about change, but nothing gets done. Oh, come on, don’t start that. I’m not saying Labour is perfect, but I do think they’re the only ones who can fix the country. Yeah, but I’m not sure. I mean, if they’re not even getting their own house in order, how can they fix the country? Exactly. And it’s not just politics. It’s everywhere. People like us, with no jobs for ages, still trying to make the best of things. It’s frustrating. I know. But I think we’re just trying to do the best we can. Even if it means getting a new coffee machine. Yeah, and maybe that’s the point. Even with all the chaos, we still find ways to make life better.

So, do you know what we're going to call the restaurant? I was thinking maybe "The Breadcrumb Café" or "The Gouda Gap." It's got that kind of vibe, you know? Oh, I like "The Breadcrumb Café." It sounds like a place where you can get lost in the menu. But then again, I'm just a baker, so maybe I should stick to something that doesn’t involve bread. I’m not sure about the name, but I think it’s a shame we’re not using the actual name of the place. It's called "The Waterfront," after all. The river’s right outside, and the canal boat moorings are just across the road. Yeah, but the owner’s a bit of a cryptic character. You know, the one who said the restaurant was named after the river because it’s “the place where the breakfasts float.” I’m not sure if that’s a metaphor or a literal thing. Oh, I think it's a metaphor. Or maybe it's just a sign that the owner is a bit eccentric. But hey, I mean, we’re not here to judge. We’re just here for the food. Exactly. And I’m here for the bread. I brought my own sourdough starter, actually. I’ve been experimenting with some new flavors. Would you like a taste? It’s got a little bit of chili and a hint of cumin. Oh, I’d love that. But before that, can I ask—what do you think about the kosher law? I mean, I know it’s a big deal in some communities, but do you think it’s necessary? Honestly, I think it’s a matter of personal choice. But you know, in some places, like some parts of London, if you run a café, you have to be careful about what you serve. I’ve heard about places that get shut down over the smallest things. Yeah, I’ve heard about that too. I mean, the whole point of being a student is to explore different things, but sometimes you can't even do that in a café. I know. I’ve had to make some compromises when I started my café. But it’s all about balance. You have to respect the customers, but you also have to be true to yourself. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about starting a club for people who love condiments.

So, do you guys ever actually go on dates with the guys you meet on Tinder? Or do you just end up talking to them for hours and then never see them again? Honestly, I’ve only gone on one proper date. And it was so awkward. The guy asked me if I had a boyfriend and I said, “No, but I’m not looking for one,” and then he immediately said, “Okay, so you’re just here for the drinks?” Oh, that’s so rude! I mean, I get it, some people are just like that, but you can’t just assume that. I’ve had a few guys message me saying they’re “into me” but then they never follow up. It’s like they just use Tinder as a way to flirt with random people. Yeah, and then there are the ones who actually do show up. Like, last week, I met this guy at a coffee shop after we matched. He was really nice, and we talked for, like, an hour. But then he just said, “Well, I should probably go—my housemates are waiting for me.” And then he left. No further contact. That’s so typical. I’ve had that happen too. You just get so invested in the conversation, and then they’re like, “Well, I need to go,” and boom, they’re gone. I think it’s just the way the app is. Like, someone’s always waiting for the next match. You’re not really supposed to build a real connection with someone. It’s just a game. That’s probably why so many people end up just being friends with their Tinder matches. I’ve had a few people message me after we met and say, “Hey, you were cool, let’s hang out again sometime.” But then they never do. I mean, I do like the idea of meeting people, but sometimes it feels like you’re just putting yourself out there for no reason. Like, what if I meet someone who’s actually into me? What if they’re not? It’s so confusing. I’ve even had some guys message me after a date and say they want to be exclusive, but then I find out they’re still swiping. It’s like, “Oh, so you’re into me, but you’re still looking for someone else?” I think we’re all just trying to find someone who’s genuine.

I just don’t know what’s going on with the benefits system anymore. It feels like it’s getting more complicated every day, and yet people are still struggling. I know, I’ve been trying to get my claim sorted for months now, and it’s just a never-ending loop of forms and waiting. I feel like I’m being treated like an inconvenience rather than a person in need. I’ve been through the same thing. It’s so frustrating, especially when you’re just trying to get by. I can’t even afford to take my cat to the vet, and the government says I’m entitled to help. I’ve been thinking about the whole political debate around it. It seems like everyone’s blaming the other side, but no one’s actually doing anything about the real issue – the cost of living. I mean, what’s the point of having benefits if you can’t even afford basic things? Exactly. And it’s not just the benefits – the whole cost of living has gone through the roof. I remember when I was working, I could buy a loaf of bread for less than a pound. Now, even that’s a struggle. It’s not just food either. I’ve had to cut back on everything – utilities, clothes, even groceries. I used to be able to afford a few treats for the kids, but now I can’t even justify that. It’s heartbreaking. I understand the government’s situation, but they have to be more transparent. People are being punished for things they can’t control. I’ve been retired for years, and I’d rather have a fair system than a system that’s just trying to make money off of us. I agree. I think there’s a lack of empathy in the whole debate. Politicians talk about “hardworking people” like we’re not even real people. Maybe they’re not even from the same background as the people they’re supposed to represent. That’s the worst part – it feels like we’re being ignored. I don’t know how much longer I can keep going like this. I feel like I’m just waiting for something to break. I’m sorry you’re going through this, luv. It’s not fair, and it’s not right. But maybe if more people start speaking out, we can get some real change.

So, did you get the meeting done today? I was just thinking about the email you sent me about the charity event. Oh, I’m afraid not. I had a call from the hospital this morning, and then I got stuck in a meeting with the board for over an hour. I was so late getting home that I didn’t even have time to make dinner. That’s not good. You know how stressful that can be. I’ve been trying to juggle my work and my family as well. We’ve had the kids at school all week, and it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I can imagine. I think the real problem is that we’re both trying to do too much. You’ve got your career, and I’ve got my work, and then there’s the family stuff. I think we need to make sure we’re both prioritising what matters most. Yeah, I agree. I’ve been thinking about that a lot. I mean, we’ve always been pretty good at looking after each other, but lately, I feel like we’re both running on empty. I was up late last night, trying to finish that report for work. I didn’t even get a chance to watch the football match on TV. I know, I felt the same. I was glued to the TV for a while, but then my phone started buzzing with emails. You know, it’s funny how one thing leads to another. I think the worst part is that we’re both so used to trying to do everything ourselves. Exactly. I mean, we’re both used to being the ones who make sure things get done. But maybe it’s time we stopped trying to be perfect and just started being real. I mean, we’re not kids anymore. We’ve got responsibilities, but we also need to take care of ourselves. That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve been trying to cut down on the long hours at work, and I’ve even started going for a walk with the kids in the evenings. It helps clear my head. That’s a great idea. I’ve been thinking about going to that yoga class I saw advertised. It might help me get some balance in my life. But I’m not sure if I can afford it.

I just saw this photo on Instagram of my cousin at the funeral. She looks so sad, and it’s like... I don’t know, it just hits me so hard. I mean, I didn’t even know she was ill. I know, it’s weird. We haven’t talked about it much, but I remember hearing something about her struggling with her health. I guess it’s not easy to know when someone is going to go. Yeah, it’s like... it’s not something you can prepare for. I keep thinking about how we used to meet up in Cambridge every weekend, like, just to catch up. Now I’m here, in this flat in Tarnow, and it feels so far away. I know, it’s funny how the sense of home changes. I feel like I’m still in Bury sometimes, even though I’ve been here for almost a year. But then I see something on social media and I just... miss it. I get that. I was working in Cambridge, teaching English, and I had this routine, this sense of purpose. Now I’m not working, and it’s like... I don’t know, everything feels... hollow. I’ve been thinking about that too. I used to be a teacher, but I got a job here teaching English as a foreign language. It’s not the same as what I did in England. I miss the classroom, the energy, the interaction. I remember when you first moved here, you said you were worried about not being able to find work. But now you’re actually here, and it’s like... you’re coping better? I think I am. I mean, the job is okay, and I like being around people. But sometimes I feel like I’m not quite... belonging. Maybe that’s just how it is for people who move abroad. I’ve been thinking about going back. Not for any job, just to see the place, you know? I feel like I’ve lost touch with what home meant to me. That’s understandable. But I’ve also been thinking about maybe staying here. I’ve got this idea of moving to somewhere else in Europe, maybe even Spain or France. It’s not like I have a plan, but I’m just wondering. You know what? I think you should do it. I mean, why not?

So, do you know what’s the deal with the tea in this pub? It’s like it’s been brewed for a week. Honestly, I’ve had worse. I think the only thing that’s worse is the crumpets they serve. They’re like rubber. I know, right? I asked the barista if it was fresh, and she said, “It’s been sitting here since breakfast.” Classic. I mean, I’m not complaining, but it’s just… weird. I expected better from a pub in London. Yeah, but I guess it’s not like we’re in a Michelin-starred place. Still, I brought my own teabag just in case. Smart move. I’ve been trying to cut down on sugar anyway. I think I’ve had three teaspoons in my tea already. I’m trying to do the same, but I think my system’s too used to the strong, sweet stuff. I feel like I’m going through withdrawal. You should try the herbal ones. I’ve been using chamomile lately. It’s calming and not too sweet. Sounds good. I’ll have to try that. So, how’s your work going? Still messing around with surveys? Oh, you know, same old. It’s a bit tedious, but I’m getting the hang of it. I mean, I’m not in the same position as you, though. Yeah, I can only imagine. I mean, I write ads for a living. Sometimes I feel like I’m talking to a wall. That’s what I thought when I first started. But then I realized that people actually  do  listen to ads. It’s just not always obvious. I guess. I mean, I hope my work doesn’t end up on a billboard next to a strip club. That would be awkward. You’d be the first person to notice. Anyway, I think I’m going to order a sandwich. I’m starving. Me too. Do you want something? Yeah, a club sandwich with extra bacon. I’ll take it with a side of chips, please. Alright, I’ll get that for you. And maybe a second cup of tea? Only if it’s not the same one I’m currently sipping on. Deal. Let me go get that sorted. Thanks. I feel like I’ve been sitting here for hours, and I haven’t even finished my tea yet.

Alright, did you both manage to get to sleep last night? I was up until 1 a.m. trying to get the kids to quiet down. I was up too, but I managed to get some sleep. I think I finally fell asleep when the twins were both snoring at the same time. I was woken up by the dog barking at something in the garden, and then I couldn’t get back to sleep.
