I think I’m going to ask mum if I can have some for breakfast. I love the way it smells. That sounds good. I was going to make pancakes, but maybe I should just go to the market and get some fresh ingredients instead. I heard there’s a new local produce stand that’s really popular. That’s a good idea. And I was thinking, maybe we could go to the market later today too. I’ve heard there are some Australian phrases being taught in the town center. Do you think we should try that? Yeah! I think it would be fun. I like learning new words, even if they’re from another country. It’s like a game. I’ll check the schedule for the market today and let you know what time we can go.

So, do you think the recent election results were a good sign for the country? I mean, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster, hasn’t it? I think it’s a bit too early to tell. I mean, I respect what the people chose, but it’s also pretty clear that the political landscape is changing rapidly. I was just saying to my wife the other day that it feels like we’re in a new era, one where things are moving much faster than we expected. Yeah, I guess it's kind of like that. I mean, I'm a student, so I don’t really get involved in politics that much, but I’ve been following the news. It's like everyone’s got an opinion now, even if they don’t know much about the details. It’s true. I think the younger generation is more politically aware now, especially with social media. I still remember when I was your age, politics was something you talked about at the dinner table, not scrolling through Twitter or Instagram for the latest news. It’s interesting how the way we get our information has changed. I still prefer reading the paper or listening to the radio, but I can see how people get their news so quickly now. It’s both a blessing and a curse. You can be informed in seconds, but you can also be misinformed just as fast. I know what you mean. I've been trying to read more about the issues, but it feels like there's so much information out there. It's a bit overwhelming. I mean, I’m in a university, so I have access to all these resources, but I still feel like I’m not getting the full picture. That’s a common problem, especially with the amount of information out there. I think part of the issue is that people are so quick to take sides without understanding the nuances. I remember reading an article once that said people are more likely to share something if it confirms their beliefs, rather than seeking out the truth. That’s exactly what I was thinking. It’s like we’re in this echo chamber where everyone just reinforces what they already believe. I’ve had some really interesting conversations with my colleagues, though. We’ve had some debates about the role of the government, the economy, and even social policies.

Alright, do you remember the story we were working on last night? The one with the talking hedgehogs? Yeah, I think so. Wasn’t it something about a magic seed that could grow anything? I think I remember! It was supposed to be a story about a girl who found a seed in the woods and planted it, and then it turned into a tree that could talk. Exactly! That’s the one. And then the tree started talking to her and told her about a magical place called Linton, which is where the Book Festival is held. You remember that, don’t you? Oh, yes! I think we were going to make the girl go to the festival and meet Helen Moss. She’s the one who writes the stories, right? Yeah, I think she’s like a real-life wizard, isn’t she? She makes up all these amazing stories that people love. Absolutely. And we even thought about making the girl meet Helen Moss at the festival and ask her for help with her story. It would’ve been a nice twist. I like that idea! It would make the story more real, like the book characters are actually meeting the authors. Yeah, and maybe Helen Moss could even help her with the magic seed. Like, maybe the seed is special because it was written by her? That’s a great idea! It would tie the story together nicely. But we need to make sure the plot doesn’t get too complicated. We don’t want it to be too hard for the other kids to follow. Right, we should keep it simple but still fun. I mean, the main thing is that the story should be engaging and keep the imagination going. Yeah, and maybe we can add some details about the festival. Like, the smell of books, the sound of people talking, and the way the books feel when you open them. That’s a good point. We should make the setting vivid so the reader can picture it in their head. Let’s think about how we want the story to end too. Do you want the girl to find the magic seed again, or does it stay with the tree? I think it would be nice if the seed stayed with the tree and the girl got to meet Helen Moss. That way, the story has a happy ending and inspires people to read more.

So, do you think we should go vegetarian for dinner tonight? I’ve been thinking about it for a while. I mean, I’m not sure if I’m ready to cut out all meat, but I do feel like I’m being more conscious about what I eat lately. Honestly, I’ve been on and off with that. I try to eat more plant-based meals, but I still have my moments. I’ve been experimenting with shmeat, you know, that synthetic meat thing. It’s kind of weird, but it’s not bad. It’s like a meat substitute, but it doesn’t have the same texture. I guess it’s better than nothing. I’ve only tried it once, and honestly, I didn’t like it. It felt too rubbery. I think I’m more into the idea of cultured meat than the actual product. But I can see how it could help with the environment. I mean, if we don’t have to raise animals for food, that would reduce a lot of animal cruelty, right? Yeah, I agree. I’ve heard that factory farming is super bad for the environment. Plus, I don’t like the idea of animals being treated like that. But then again, I also feel like abattoirs have their own issues. I mean, is it better to kill animals in a controlled, humane way or just let them be raised in cages? It’s a tough one. I think the real problem lies in the system, not in the act itself. But I also think that not everyone is ready to go fully plant-based. I mean, I’d rather have a piece of real meat than synthetic meat any day. But I do feel guilty when I eat it. I try to buy organic and free-range, but it’s not always possible. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to cut down on meat, especially red meat. I’ve started taking vitamin tablets to make sure I’m getting all the nutrients I need. I feel like it’s easier to just take a pill than have to eat more veggies. But I’m not sure if that’s the best approach. I’ve heard that some people do take supplements, but I think it’s better to get your nutrients from food. That said, I do take some vitamin D if I’m not getting enough from the sun.

I just can’t believe how long it’s taking to get the washing done. That machine’s been going for like an hour and it’s still not finished. It’s not even a full load. Yeah, I know. I’ve been trying to get it to work properly for weeks now. It’s like it’s got a mind of its own. I swear I heard it make a noise like it was laughing. Oh, I had a washing machine once that did that. It was a bit of a nightmare. It would start up, and then just stop in the middle of the cycle. I had to call a technician, and apparently, it was a faulty motor. I had to replace it, and now I’m stuck with a machine that takes forever to dry clothes. I was just thinking, maybe we should just throw away the clothes that don’t get used much. I mean, I’ve got these old jumpers that I haven’t worn in years. They’re just taking up space and costing me money in the long run. That’s a good point. I do feel like I’ve got this massive wardrobe that I don’t even use. I’ve got this whole drawer of shirts that I only wear on special occasions. I should probably get rid of them. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to declutter my apartment, and it’s crazy how much stuff you have that you never actually use. I’m even thinking about selling some of my clothes online. It’s a bit of a hassle, but it helps with the space. That’s a great idea. I might be tempted to do that too. I’ve got this old scarf I bought for a trip to Spain. I haven’t used it since, and it’s just taking up space. Maybe I’ll sell it on eBay. Yeah, I’ve got that jacket I bought for the winter. It’s still in perfect condition, but I just don’t wear it anymore. I was thinking of giving it to my sister. She’s always saying she needs more winter clothes. That’s a good plan. I think I’m going to start with my wardrobe and then work my way through the rest of the house. I’ve been meaning to go through my books too.

Alright, let’s get this sorted. I’ve got the butterfly forks ready. You two can help me set the table. Butterfly forks? What’s that? Are they like… those fancy ones with little wings? No, I think they’re the ones with the little tongs on the side. Like, you use them to pick up food and then eat it with the fork. Aha, that’s the one! I got them online for a special dinner last week. They’re a bit of a gimmick, but they’re fun. Especially for kids. Are they easy to use? I mean, I’ve never seen one before, so I might mess it up. Oh, you’ll get the hang of it. They’re not that hard. Just don’t try to use them like a normal fork. It’s more about the tongs than the fork, honestly. So, are we having a themed dinner? Like, is this one of those fancy events? No, not really. Just a normal supper, but I thought it’d be fun to have something a bit different. It’s for the O and I, so I figured a little something extra would make it special. Wait, who’s the O and I? Is that like a nickname? Oh, it’s short for “Oscar and Ian.” They’re the ones who invited us over. They live just down the road. We haven’t seen them in a while, so it’s a catch-up dinner. That’s cool. So, are they coming over tonight? Yeah, they’re supposed to arrive in about 20 minutes. I’ve already lit the candles and set the table. I just need to make sure the food is ready. What are we having? I’m not sure if I should bring anything. No, no need. I’ve got everything covered. Just make sure the chairs are pulled out and the drinks are ready. We’re having wine, and I’ve got some soft drinks for you two. Cool. So, do you ever have any special traditions for these dinners? Like, any rituals or things you go through? Hmm, not really. But I always try to make it feel a bit more special. Maybe a two-minute silence at the start? It’s a thing I picked up from a friend who’s into mindfulness. A two-minute silence? Like, for what? Just to be present.

Alright, do you remember when we were talking about our holiday plans for next year? I think we were all excited about going to Cornwall again. Yeah, I remember you saying you wanted to take us to Adventure Island. I think you said it's like a theme park with water slides and all that? Yeah, I remember that! But I thought we were going to the V&A exhibition instead. Was that not the plan? Oh, right, that was the original plan, but I think we changed our minds. I really wanted to go to Adventure Island with you two. It’s been ages since we had a proper family day out. I’d love to go! But I’m not sure if I’m old enough for all the rides. I mean, I’m only eight, so maybe some of the bigger ones are too scary? Yeah, I think I’m too little for most of the rides. Maybe we can just go on the smaller ones and have a picnic? I like the idea of eating outside. That sounds perfect. I can see us having a picnic on the beach, maybe with some fish and chips from the local shop. I think that would be nice. It’s been a while since we had a proper seaside holiday. I love fish and chips, especially with mushy peas and tartar sauce. But I don’t know if I can have that. I have a food intolerance now. Oh, that’s right. You mentioned it before. You can’t have gluten, right? Yeah, and some of the fish and chips here might be battered with flour, which is gluten. I think I’d have to bring my own food or look for something gluten-free. I don’t have any food intolerances, so I’d be okay. But I do have to do my exam marking for the summer. I was thinking about taking some time off for the holiday, but I need to make sure I don’t fall behind. You’ll be fine. We can plan the holiday around your schedule. And if you need to do some work on the trip, that’s okay too. I think you’ll still have a great time. I hope so. I really want to go to Adventure Island. I think it’s going to be fun, even if I can’t ride the biggest slides.

So, did you hear about what happened in the maths class today? What? Did someone get sent to the head’s office again? Yeah, actually, it was Tom. He was talking over the teacher and then he got caught on camera. Oh no, that’s not good. I thought they took the cameras out last week. They did, but apparently, someone put one back in the corner. And Tom didn’t even know. That’s ridiculous. Why would someone do that? I don’t know. Maybe they wanted to catch someone else, or maybe it was a joke. Either way, Tom is in trouble. I can imagine how annoying that would be. I mean, I wouldn’t want to be in the spotlight like that. Yeah, especially when you’re trying to be cool. Speaking of cool, did you hear about the party next weekend? Yeah, I think it’s at Jake’s house. His dad said he’s inviting everyone. Cool, but I don’t know if I’ll be able to go. I have a bunch of coursework due. Yeah, I know. But I heard the school is giving an extension if you’ve got a good reason. That’s a relief. I was worried I’d miss out. Oh, and also, I think the prefects are going to be doing a movie night in the hall this week. Really? That sounds fun. Yeah, I heard they’re showing  The Matrix  again. Oh no, not again. That’s been on since like, forever. I know, but apparently they said it’s a classic. Well, I guess it’s better than sitting in the library all night. Speaking of sitting in the library, my friend Alex has a severe peanut allergy. Oh no, that’s not fun. Yeah, and the other day, someone brought a snack to class, and he had to leave. That’s pretty harsh. I mean, I can’t even imagine having to stay away from food. I know, it’s really hard. But he’s been working so hard on his science project, and he’s been doing really well. That’s awesome. I hope he gets to finish it. Me too. And, uh, do you think we should get bikes this week? Yeah, maybe. I heard there are some good deals at the bike shop near the station. Yeah, and it would make getting to school a lot easier.

So, do you think we're gonna make it to the meeting on time? I don’t know, the roads have been a bit of a nightmare since they started that construction work near the motorway. Yeah, I saw some of the signs. It’s gonna be a long drive. It’s ridiculous. I mean, it's a major road, and they’ve just done a complete mess of it. I don’t get why they don’t do it during the off-season. I heard the council said it’s because of some new infrastructure they’re putting in. But honestly, I can’t see how that’s worth the chaos. My uncle told me once that he used to cycle all the way from Sunderland to London when he was younger. He said it was a long ride, but he never had to worry about traffic. That’s probably true. I mean, I used to ride my bike to uni, and even then, the roads near the campus were pretty busy. Yeah, but you get used to it. I guess I’m just not used to driving in this kind of traffic. I heard there’s a new bike lane being built along the A1. Maybe that’ll help reduce some of the congestion. That’s what I heard too. But I don’t know if it’ll make much of a difference. People are still going to want to get where they’re going quickly. It just feels like every time there’s a project, it’s a nightmare. I mean, what’s the point of building something new if it just causes more problems? I agree. I think it’s all about trying to be efficient, but sometimes you end up creating more issues than you solve. I just hope we don’t end up stuck in gridlock on the way. I don’t want to be late for the meeting. Me neither. I’ll just keep my finger on the blinker and hope for the best. You know, I think I’ve got a better chance of getting there on a bike than in this car. You really think so? I mean, I guess if I had a bike, it would be faster. But I don’t know if I’d be able to handle the hills. You’d be surprised. I mean, I’ve never had a problem with the hills.

I just got a text from the delivery guy saying they're running late. I was hoping it would be here by now. Yeah, I’m getting pretty hungry. I thought we’d have something to eat before we watch the new series tonight. I agree. We haven’t had proper Chinese food in ages, and I’m starting to miss it. I mean, I know it’s not the same as being in China, but the takeaway from the local place is always a comfort. I know, I'm just so used to the variety they have here. Do you remember the first time we ordered from that place? It was so exciting, like we were exploring a new culture. Oh, definitely. I remember you were so excited about the spicy mapo tofu. I still remember how you ate it like it was the first time. You were practically dancing with joy. I was! And I still do. Even though I’m not a big fan of the heat, that dish always hits the spot. I mean, why do we even order Chinese food if we’re not going to try something new? Exactly! It’s like a ritual. It’s not just about the food, it’s about the experience. The way the food comes out in little boxes, the smell of the noodles, the way the delivery guy always shouts something like, “Your order’s hot and ready!” Oh, he’s a real character. I think he's been delivering here for years. He always has a joke or a story to tell. Last time he said he had a bet with his mates about whether the chicken would be delivered before the fish. That’s so typical of him. I love that. He makes the whole experience more fun. I wish we could meet him in person. Maybe we could take him out for a proper meal sometime. That would be great. I mean, he’s been working so hard, he deserves a thank you. But I think he might have already had his meal for the day. He’s always eating on the go. Maybe not. He’s probably been surviving on Chinese food all week. We should really do something for him. I agree. But back to our order. I’m starting to think maybe we should just go and pick it up ourselves. I don’t want to wait forever.

So, how’s the NHS been treating you lately? I heard there’s been a bit of a bottleneck with appointments. Honestly, it’s been a bit of a struggle. I’ve had to wait weeks for a follow-up after my last check-up. It’s frustrating, especially when you’re trying to manage your health on a budget. I know what you mean. I’ve been working on a research project about healthcare accessibility in the North West, and it’s been really eye-opening. It’s not just about the system—it’s about the people who are working in it too. Yeah, I’ve noticed that. The staff are amazing, but they’re stretched so thin. I’ve even had a few nurses tell me they’ve been working double shifts just to make ends meet. That’s heartbreaking. I’ve been thinking about doing a piece on how the NHS is adapting to the pressures. I’ve been in touch with a few colleagues from Finland—do you know anything about their system? A little. I remember reading that they have a more preventative approach and a lot of focus on public health. They also have a strong emphasis on community care. But I don’t know if it’s something we can realistically replicate here. It’s got to be a challenge. I mean, with the way things are, it’s not just about funding—it’s about policy and how we value healthcare as a right, not a privilege. Absolutely. I also wonder how the system would handle something like the recent flu outbreak. It just feels like we’re always one step behind. I think the key is having more local support and better communication between different levels of healthcare. I’ve been speaking to a few people from the local area, and they’re really passionate about making changes. That’s good to hear. I’ve also been trying to be more proactive with my health. I’ve started going to the local community centre for exercise classes. It’s a small step, but it helps. That’s great. I think the more people take initiative, the better. It also helps build a network of support, which is so important in places like this. Yeah, I agree. I’ve met some really interesting people there. It’s nice to connect with others who are trying to make the most of their circumstances.

I heard the news today, mate. That new immigration policy is going to be a real headache for the council. I got a call from one of the students I teach—she’s from Poland, and she’s been put on a waiting list for housing. That’s not right at all. Aye, I heard about that too. It’s one thing to have problems with the system, but it’s a different kettle of fish when people are actually in need. I’ve seen plenty of folks down on their luck in Liverpool. You can’t just ignore the fact that some people are struggling, no matter where they’re from. I agree, but I think the government’s just trying to paint a picture of a problem that’s not really there. There’s talk of a national corpus of data, you know, to track immigrants and their contributions. It’s all about control, not actually helping people integrate. That’s a bit of a shame. I remember when I was younger, I used to work in a factory, and there were a few Polish workers who helped me out when I was laid off. We all had our ups and downs. I don’t think the world’s so black and white as they’d like to make it out to be. Yeah, but the way things are now, even people who are fairly well-off can find themselves in a pickle. I had a friend who was a lecturer like me—got a job teaching in Manchester, then the council decided he wasn’t suitable because of his accent. Sounds a bit ridiculous, doesn’t it? That’s what I mean—there’s a real lack of fairness here. I’ve been watching the news about the police and immigration again. It’s like they’re trying to make the public feel like they’re being targeted. I’ve got a nephew who’s been in the army, and he says the border control has gone too far. I heard that. They passed some law about people being detained for longer if they’re on benefit. It’s supposed to deter people from coming over, but I don’t think it’s going to work. The real issue is the welfare system. If people are struggling at home, they’re going to look for a better deal somewhere else.

So, do you know what’s going on with the new project? I’ve been trying to get some clarity on it, but it’s all so vague. Honestly, I’m still trying to figure it out myself. I think it’s something to do with the language data we’re compiling for the ELT department. But I’m not exactly sure what the end goal is. Yeah, I’ve been following along too. I think they want to create a more standardized framework for how we categorize dialects and sociolects in our research. It’s a bit overwhelming, honestly. That sounds familiar. I remember working on a similar initiative a few years back, but back then it was more about integrating data from different regions into a single platform. I wonder if they’re expanding on that now. I’ve been thinking the same thing. It feels like they’ve been working on it for months, but no one’s really been able to give us a clear timeline or objectives. It’s like they’re building something but not sure what it’s for. I know, it’s frustrating. I mean, we’re all in this field for a reason, and we’re supposed to be experts in language, but sometimes it feels like we’re just being tossed around like pawns in some bigger game. I think it’s more about adapting to the changing needs of the industry. With everything going digital, they want to ensure we’re not falling behind. But I also wonder if they’re just trying to keep us busy while they figure out what they want to do next. Maybe. Or maybe they’re being cautious. You know, with the amount of data we handle, even a small misstep could have big consequences. I can see why they’d want to be careful. That’s true. I mean, if you think about it, the publishing side of things is also evolving. There’s more demand for interactive content, audio-visual resources, and real-time language updates. We might be on the cusp of something big. Yeah, and I have to say, I’m trying to stay positive. It’s just been so hectic lately, with all the meetings and deliverables. I’m starting to wonder if we’re overworked or if they’re just trying to push us to be more innovative.

So, do you watch much TV these days? I’ve been trying to catch up on some documentaries, but it’s hard to find anything that’s not either too slow or too intense. I mean, where’s the middle ground? Honestly, I kind of stopped watching regular TV a while back. Got too much on my mind with research and all. But I do still use it for streaming. You know, I’ve been binge-watching some BBC dramas from the 70s. They’re quite different from what’s on now, but there’s something nostalgic about them. Oh, I’ve heard about those. My mum used to watch them when she was younger. She always says they’re "much more civilized." I guess it’s just the language and the pacing, you know? I’m trying to learn French, so I thought I’d watch some French shows to practice, but they’ve got such a different rhythm, it’s almost like a whole other language. That’s true. I tried that too, but honestly, the accents and the way people speak can be so different from what you learn in a classroom. I mean, I can read French quite well, but listening to it? It’s like trying to read in another country. I tried watching some French comedies, but it was too fast for me. Though I did find one show that was really good— Les Ch'ti . It’s got this kind of rural humor that’s just so different from British comedy, but I laughed a lot. That sounds interesting. I’ll have to look that up. I’m also trying to get better at speaking, so maybe I should find a language exchange group. I’ve been thinking about it, but I’m not sure where to start. You should. I know a few people who do it through the university. I mean, it’s not always easy—being confident in speaking a language is tough, especially when you’re used to writing. But it helps to have someone to practice with. Do you have any specific goals with learning French? I’m trying to reach B1 level, at least. I want to be able to hold a conversation in a café or something. Though I’m not sure I’d ever be able to order a croissant in Paris without sounding like a tourist.

Well, I've just been talking to the young’un about his homework. He's got a maths test coming up, and he's not really on top of it yet. I think he needs a bit more help. Aye, he’s got that maths exam on Thursday. He’s been trying to do the past papers, but he keeps getting stuck on the algebra problems. Oh, I remember when I was his age. I used to be terrible at maths. My dad used to get so frustrated with me. He’d say, "You're never going to get this if you don’t start paying attention!" But I didn’t listen, and I ended up having to take extra lessons. Aye, and I remember my wife used to have to help me with my sums. I used to be a bit of a duffer. I still can’t remember how to divide a number properly. Wait, does anyone remember when we had that dinner with the in-laws and the cook asked us to split the bill? I said it was about £20 for six people, so I just divided it by six and said it was around £3 each. The whole room laughed at me. I still remember that! Oh, that’s a classic! I was like that too. I remember my nan used to say, “If you don’t know how to count, you won’t know how to live.” But she always had a way of making it seem like it was just part of everyday life. She made it fun, in a way. That’s true. She was a real character. I think she’d have loved being around the young’un now. She’d have found a way to make even the most complicated equations seem simple. She’d have loved it. She always said that if you couldn’t explain something in a way that a child could understand, then you didn’t really understand it yourself. That’s something I’ve carried with me. Aye, and I think it’s something we should all remember. You know, when I was younger, I used to think being good at numbers was a sign of being clever. But now I’ve come to think it’s just a matter of practice and patience. Yeah, and that’s something the young’un needs to learn. Just like we had to.

So, do you remember when we first came to China? It felt like we were on some kind of adventure. I still can’t believe we ended up living here for so long. Yeah, I remember that first day when we arrived at the airport. It was so hot, and everything was so different. I couldn’t believe how quiet everything was compared to London. It was like walking through a completely different world. Exactly! I mean, I got lost on the first day, and I couldn’t even ask for directions because I didn’t know what the words meant. I was so nervous. You were so scared of speaking Chinese, weren’t you? I remember you kept muttering to yourself in English, like you were trying to practice. Oh, I was terrified! And then we met this lovely couple who gave us a tour of the city, and we ended up staying with them for a few days. It was such a kind introduction to life here. Yeah, they were amazing. I think they even took us to some of the best places in the city, like the old town and the market. I still remember the smell of the food there. I do too. The first time I tried dumplings, I was so overwhelmed. I thought they were going to burn my mouth, but they were actually really good. I’ve never looked back since. Silly me, I still can’t cook dumplings properly. I always end up making them too soggy. But you, on the other hand, have become a bit of a foodie here. Hey, I’ve learned a lot! We’ve been to so many places, and I’ve even started taking photos of the food. I think I have over 200 pictures of local dishes by now. You're obsessed with food photography. I think you’re going to start a blog or something. You’ve got that kind of eye for it. Maybe I will. I’ve been thinking about it. I could call it “Tastes of China.” It’s a bit grand, but I think I could do it. That sounds like a great idea. I’d definitely follow it. And I can go through your photos and tell you what you're missing or what you’re getting right. That would be nice. Although sometimes I feel like I’m missing out on the actual experience because I’m too busy taking pictures.

So, did you go out last night? I haven’t seen you since the weekend. Yeah, I did! I went to this new bar down by the station. It was pretty cool, but I got completely wasted. Oh no, you again? I thought you were over that phase. Yeah, I know, but it's easy to slip back in. Anyway, I met this guy there. He was really into football, like,  really  into it. So, what happened? Did you end up talking? We did, yeah! He’s got this massive tattoo of the team he supports. It’s like a full sleeve, and he was telling me about how he’s been going to matches since he was five. That’s intense. I mean, I like football, but I’m not that into it. I’m more of a… cricket fan. Yeah, I get that, but it’s kind of the whole thing for some people. It’s like their whole identity, you know? I guess. But I’m more into the  people  part of it. Like, hanging out with friends, going to a game, just having a good time. I can see that. Anyway, I think he was a bit of a tosser, though. He kept talking about how he’s got a job in finance and he's going to make a fortune. Oh, typical. That’s so common. Some people just need to have a fantasy life. Exactly! I was like, "Sure, mate, whatever you say." But I had a good time, even if I didn’t really connect with him. Well, I’m glad you had fun. I was out with some friends last night. We went to this new pizza place near the campus. It was amazing. Pizza? That’s not adventurous. Yeah, I know, but it was just nice to hang out. We didn’t do anything crazy, just talked and laughed. I need to find a balance. I mean, I love going out and having a good time, but I also feel like I’m slipping into this "drinking every weekend" habit. I get that. It’s easy to get lost in the moment. But you know, you should try to do something different this week. Maybe go to that yoga class I heard about? Yoga? I don’t know. I feel like I’d fall asleep. Okay, fair enough. But you could always try one class.

Well, I've just got the last of the peas and chips down. I know it's not much, but it's the best we can do after the week we've had. It's not bad, really. I mean, peas and chips are as good as any meal when you're trying to stretch a budget. But I was just thinking, we need to make sure the grandparents know when they're coming. Yeah, I've been meaning to call them. They’re coming next week, right? I haven't heard from them in ages. Didn’t they say they wanted to see the new garden? They did, and I reckon they’re excited. I’ve been working on the flower beds all week, and I’ve even got a couple of new plants from the market. I think they’ll be impressed. That’s good to hear. I was just wondering, have we got the chairs ready for them? I remember they always bring a lot of stuff, and the garden is quite small. Yeah, I’ve moved the extra chairs out from the shed. Might need a few more, but I’m sure we’ll manage. And the tent, by the way. I’ve been meaning to check if it’s still in good condition. I remember the last time they came, it got a bit wet, and we had to clean it up afterwards. Oh, right. I think it’s still there. I saw it in the garage the other day. But maybe we should get a new one just in case. Yeah, that’s a good idea. I don’t want them to get all wet and uncomfortable. Although, I have to say, I’m not too keen on the idea of them watching the kids all day. You know they love the kids. It’s not like they’re going to do anything wrong. They’ve been through so much, and they’re just trying to make the best of the time they have. I know, but I just worry about them getting too involved. I mean, I remember the last time they were here, they were up until midnight with the younger ones, and it was a bit of a mess in the morning. That’s true. I think it was Liam who had a fight with his cousin over a toy, and they ended up with mud all over the garden.

So, do you think we should get rid of the old laptop? It’s been acting up for ages, and I got a new one last week. I’m so used to the old one, though. It's like it knows me now. Yeah, I think it’s time. I mean, it’s been giving us more problems than it’s worth. But if we throw it out, what do we do with the old one? Do you think we can sell it? I don’t know, lass. I was just thinking the same thing. But if we sell it, how do we even know who to sell it to? I mean, it's not like we’re in a place where everyone’s tech-savvy. I still can’t figure out how to use the SAT nav properly, and I’m not even sure I should be using it. Oh, you’re not alone. I’ve been trying to set up my Blackberry for weeks. It’s like it’s not listening to me, or it’s just not working. I think I need to take it back and get a new one. I’ve had enough of it. Yeah, I remember when I first got my phone. It was so easy, just a few clicks, and it was done. Now, it’s like you have to be a tech expert just to use it. I’m glad I don’t have to deal with that anymore. I’m just an English teacher now, not a tech wizard. I remember when I first got my phone. I thought I was so clever with it. Then, a few months later, I was back to square one. I still can’t remember how to put on contact lenses without crying. Oh, you’re not the only one. My eyesight’s gone, and I can barely see the TV. I think I need to start using reading glasses for everything. I mean, even my bin strike notice was hard to read. I had to ask my neighbor to read it for me. You’re not the only one with bad eyesight. My eyesight’s getting worse by the day, and I can’t even see the path to the shops anymore. I have to take my time, and sometimes I just end up getting lost on the way. That’s why I think we should go out and walk around Brighton today.

So, do you know what’s going on with the football results? I’ve been trying to check them on my phone, but the internet here is so unreliable. Yeah, I saw something about a match between Leeds and Manchester United. Wasn’t it a big one? I think it was, yeah. Leeds got a win, but I’m not sure if it was a fair result. A lot of people were complaining about the referee. It was a bit of a shock, wasn’t it? I mean, Leeds are not the strongest team, but they pulled it off. I guess. I’m just so tired of not being able to access my usual news sources. It’s like being in a bubble. I hear you. I’ve been feeling a bit homesick lately too. Especially with the weather being so gloomy. I get that SAD feeling again. Oh, I know exactly what you mean. I’ve been stuck in this place for a while now, and it’s like the clouds never clear up. I miss the sunshine of Cambridge. I miss the dogs too. I’ve been working with a group of students, and one of them has a dog. It’s so cute – a golden retriever. I even tried to take photos of it, but the dog keeps running off. That sounds lovely. I miss having a dog. I used to have a labrador when I was younger. He’d follow me everywhere. You’d think being a teacher would be a good way to be around dogs, but I’m more focused on preparing my students for their exams. I feel a bit responsible for them. I can see that. I used to teach part-time too, but I haven’t done it for a while. My kids are grown up now. I feel like I’m always trying to balance my work and my personal life. I’ve been working on a farm recently too, which is a bit of a break from teaching. Oh, farming? That sounds different. I’ve never done that. I think I’d get lost in the fields! It’s not that bad if you like being outdoors. I think I’m just trying to keep busy. I get that. I’ve been trying to read more books, too. I’ve been going through some old favourites. I think I’m going to start a book club.

So, do you know what’s up with Jake? He’s been acting really weird lately. I’ve seen him with this girl at the café, but he’s been completely ignoring me ever since. Oh, don’t be ridiculous. He’s just busy with work. You know how it is. He’s been working overtime like crazy, and he’s got this new project on. He said it’s a big one, and he’s got to finish it before the end of the month. Yeah, but you can’t just ignore your friends like that. I mean, I’ve seen him with her a few times. He even took her to that concert last weekend. What’s going on? I don’t know. I guess he’s just not into me like he used to be. I mean, we’ve been friends for years, but now he’s always with this other girl. It’s like he’s moved on or something. Maybe he just needs some space. You know, sometimes people get stressed out with work and stuff, and they need to focus on their own stuff. Yeah, but he’s been acting really strange. He’s not even responding to my texts. Like, I sent him a message the other day, and he just replied with a single “later.” That’s not normal. I know, it’s so frustrating. I don’t know what to do. Should I just cut him out of my life? Or is there a way to talk to him about it? Maybe you should give him some space. If you push too hard, he might just push back. But if you give him time, maybe he’ll come around. Or maybe you could just do something for yourself. You know, like go out with your friends or start dating someone new. I mean, it’s not like you’re the only one who can be happy. I know, but it’s just hard to move on when you’ve been friends with someone for so long. I mean, I still care about him, but I don’t know if he’s even interested in me anymore. I get it. It’s tough when you’re used to someone being there. But sometimes, people change. And sometimes, you have to change with them. Yeah, and if he’s not into you anymore, maybe it’s better to just let him go.

So, do you remember that time we were in Chengdu and we got lost trying to find the panda reserve? I swear, the map app was useless, and we ended up walking for an hour through this maze of alleys until we finally found it. Oh, I remember that perfectly. You were so frustrated, and I kept trying to calm you down. But honestly, I think you were more annoyed at the fact that we were late for the tour. Oh, don’t get me started. I was just so excited to see the pandas. Didn’t even realize how much of a walking tour it was. But it was worth it—those pandas were incredible. You could tell they were used to being around people. Definitely. I mean, I’ve seen pandas in zoos before, but there’s something different about seeing them in the wild. Or at least, in a more natural habitat. I still can’t believe they’re in China. I mean, isn’t that where the pandas are from? Yeah, but I think they’ve been moved around a lot over the years, especially for breeding programs. I remember one of my Chinese colleagues talking about how pandas were originally only in certain areas, but now they’re spread out across the country. And then there’s the whole issue of the death penalty in China. I mean, I know they don’t use it as much as some countries, but it’s still a controversial topic. I know. It’s kind of funny that we were just talking about pandas and then it went into the death penalty. I mean, what’s next—talking about the tea ceremonies and then discussing drug laws? Oh, come on, we did talk about drugs earlier. You mentioned the problem with recreational drugs in China. It’s complicated, isn’t it? I mean, I’ve heard it’s a lot stricter than in the UK, but then again, you can’t really compare the two. Right. And it’s not just about the laws. It’s about the culture, the way people view certain substances, and how the government deals with it. I suppose it’s a nuanced issue. I guess it is. But you know, after all that, we ended the day by having goji berries and some tea, and it was actually quite peaceful. Yeah, that was a good day.

So, do you know where we're going again? I mean, I thought we were meeting someone at the station, but now I’m not sure. I think we’re going to the museum, right? The one with the old trains? I got the text from Mom saying she’s meeting us there. Oh, right, the one that’s got that dusty old ticket machine? I mean, I don’t know if it even works anymore. I’ve tried using it before, and it’s like it’s from the 80s. Yeah, but it’s not too bad. It’s a bit of a trip, but I think it’s worth it. Plus, I heard they’ve got a new exhibition on Victorian railways. You know, the ones from the 19th century. I think that’s the one. But I’m still not sure if we need to take the car or if we can just take the train. I mean, if we take the car, we can park right near the entrance, but if we take the train, we might have to walk a bit. I think we should take the train. It’ll be easier for everyone. Plus, there’s a direct service from the station. I’ll check the website again just to be sure. Yeah, that sounds better. I mean, the weather’s not great today, and if we take the car, we might end up stuck in traffic. I don’t want someone to miss the tour because of that. Exactly. I’ll send you the link to the website so you can check the schedule. Also, maybe we should make sure we’ve got enough time to get there. I know the museum opens at 10, but we don’t want to be late. Right. I’ll set a reminder on my phone. I don’t want to forget. I’ve got that meeting with the client at 11, so I need to make sure I’m not running late. Perfect. I’ll also bring the map just in case. You know how hard it is trying to find the right entrance when you’re in a museum. Once you get lost, it’s a nightmare. Yeah, I remember when I tried to find the gift shop last time. I ended up going through the entire building, and I still couldn’t find it. That’s why I always take the map.

So, do you think you've caught something? I've been feeling really off all day. Headache, sore throat, and I’m not even sure if it's just stress or something else. You’re not the only one. I’ve been kind of under the weather too. I was trying to push through at work, but I felt like I was dragging. I think I might’ve picked it up from the gym. I wasn’t even sure if it was a virus or just fatigue. That sounds rough. I'm not feeling too bad, but I’ve been sleeping a lot. I think I just needed a break. I mean, I’ve been working crazy hours lately, and I’ve been kind of stressed about my relationships too. It’s like everything is piling up. Yeah, I can relate. I’ve been feeling the pressure from work and from my personal life. I think it's all starting to catch up with me. I’ve been in a relationship for a few months now, and I’m not sure if it’s working. I mean, we have good times, but sometimes I feel like we’re not on the same page. That’s tough. I’ve been in a situation like that too. Sometimes you just don’t know if it’s worth it. I mean, it’s hard to tell if it’s the relationship or if it’s just me being overly critical. I’ve been trying to work on communication, but it’s not easy. I get that. I think part of the problem is that we’re all so busy with our own stuff. We don’t have time to really focus on each other. I mean, I’ve been so wrapped up in my job and my personal goals that I’ve barely had time to think about my relationship. It’s like I’m not even sure what I want anymore. Yeah, I think that’s a common thing. I’ve been thinking about my relationship too. I’m not sure if I want to keep going or if I need to take a step back. It’s just so confusing. I can’t say I’ve had that much time to think about it. I mean, I’m just trying to get through each day. I’ve been so stressed about work and my family that I haven’t even had the chance to think about my relationship.

I just got a message from Lucy. She’s been acting really weird lately. I think she’s going through something. Oh no, is she okay? I haven’t heard from her in a while. You know how she can be sometimes, always got her head in the clouds. I know, but she’s been so quiet. She didn’t even reply to my text last night. I sent her like five messages. I’m worried. Maybe she’s just busy. She’s been working crazy hours at the clinic. You know how it is, mental health nurses don’t have a lot of downtime. Still, it’s not like her to ignore people. Yeah, but I think it’s more than that. She mentioned something about a break-up the other day. I didn’t take it seriously, but now I’m starting to wonder if she’s struggling more than she lets on. That does sound serious. You know, she’s been through a lot lately. Her ex was abusive, and she’s still trying to recover. Maybe that’s why she’s keeping to herself. Yeah, I guess. But it’s not just her. I’ve noticed that a lot of people at work are going through something. Even Tom from the support team. He’s been really stressed lately. I asked him about it, and he just said he’s “dealing with stuff.” I heard he’s been having trouble with his family. His mum’s been in the hospital for a while. That must be a lot to handle. It’s all so much. I can’t even imagine what they’re going through. Sometimes I feel like I’m not doing enough. I mean, I’m not the one who’s suffering. You’re doing more than enough. You’re there for them, you listen, you care. That’s not easy. And I know you’re not perfect—sometimes you get overwhelmed too. I know. It’s just... I feel like there’s so much going on, and I’m trying to keep up. I’ve been thinking about taking some time off. Maybe a short break. I need to recharge. You should. You deserve it. And if you go, I’ll make sure someone covers for you. Just don’t push yourself too hard, okay? Thanks, I really appreciate that. I’m just so tired of feeling like I’m constantly fighting to keep everything together.

Alright, do you remember the story about the witch who lived in the woods? Yeah! I think it was about a woman who was really mean and cursed all the animals. But wasn’t she also really powerful? I mean, she could make things disappear. Yeah, exactly. But then one day, a little girl found her in her cave. What did the girl do? Did she help the witch? No, actually, she tried to escape, but the witch caught her. Was the witch really evil then? Or was she just misunderstood? That's a good question. Sometimes people think of witches as evil, but maybe they’re just protecting something or someone. Like, maybe she was trying to keep the forest safe? Exactly! And when the girl tried to run away, the witch let her go. Why would she do that? Maybe because the girl was kind. The witch saw that she didn’t want to hurt anyone. So, it wasn’t all bad? No, it wasn’t. There was a little bit of good in her too. I think I remember another story about a giant. Was that one about good versus evil too? Yes, that one was more about a giant who was actually just lonely. Oh! I remember that one. He had a big house and a big heart. Exactly. He was scary at first, but when the girl came to visit, he showed her kindness. So, even giants can be good? Sometimes, yes. It’s not always about being good or evil. It’s about understanding. I like that. So, the stories are not just about bad guys and good guys. That’s right. They’re about the choices people make and how they affect others. So, the witch and the giant were both doing what they thought was right? Exactly. That’s what makes these stories so interesting. Maybe that’s why we like them? Because they’re complicated. Definitely. They make us think. I wonder if there’s a story where the good guy turns bad? Oh, there are plenty of those too. It’s all about the journey. Maybe we should read more stories like that. I agree. They’re a great way to learn about the world and ourselves. Yeah, and it’s fun too. I like how the stories make us imagine things. That’s the best part. It’s like we’re on an adventure every time we read one.

So, did you get the photos from the school filming trip? I was just thinking about it, and I couldn’t remember if we sent them all. I think we did, but I’m not sure if they were all uploaded properly. I’ll check later. But honestly, the kids had such a good time. They were all so excited about the trip. I think it was the best thing they’ve done all year. Yeah, I saw a few of the photos on Instagram. They looked like they had a lot of fun. I especially liked the one where they were all laughing in the café. That was a good one. That’s the one with the big doughnut in the background? My brother was in that photo too. He got so excited about the doughnuts, he ate three of them in one go. Oh, you’re not the only one who got excited. I remember seeing a photo of you and your brother holding up doughnuts like they were trophies. It was hilarious. Yeah, and he actually said something like, “I’m the king of doughnuts.” It was so typical of him. But honestly, it was a great way to start the trip. They got to try different things, and it was all so much fun. I was also thinking about the warm enough at night thing. I was trying to figure out if we should have brought extra blankets for the kids. I didn’t want them to get cold. Oh, I remember you mentioning that. I thought it might be a bit chilly, but it ended up being just fine. I think the weather was kind to us this time. Yeah, I was actually surprised. I thought it would be colder, especially with the wind. But it was actually quite mild. I even got to sleep without a blanket, which was a relief. That’s the kind of weather we should have all the time. I wish we could go to the gym and just work out in that kind of weather. It would be perfect for running. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about trying the running machine at the gym lately. I’ve been feeling a bit sluggish lately, and I think it might help. But I’m still not sure if I’ll get up early enough. You could always try the gym in the morning.

So, how’s the new place doing, Tony? I heard you took over that café in the old market square. Oh, it’s going alright, I suppose. It’s a bit of a struggle, but I’m trying to make it work. You know how it is with small businesses these days—everyone wants to be an entrepreneur, but very few actually know what they’re doing. I’ve always said that. I think the real challenge isn’t just running a business, it’s keeping up with the changes in the market. And with the way people are shifting towards more sustainable practices, you’ve got to adapt or get left behind. That’s true, Phil. I’ve been thinking about going green, you know. I mean, not that I’m a massive fan of the Green Party, but I do believe in reducing our carbon footprint. It’s just that customers aren’t always willing to pay a premium for eco-friendly products. I hear you. I’ve been trying to get my school to adopt more sustainable policies. It’s not always easy, but I think it’s the right thing to do. I mean, I’m not saying we should all be living in treehouses, but we can do better. Yeah, I agree. I mean, I’ve got this friend who started a boot sale every Sunday. It’s a bit of a community thing, you know? People bring their old stuff, and it’s a way to keep things circulating instead of throwing them away. That’s a good idea. I’ve thought about doing something similar with my students—maybe a recycling or upcycling project. I think it could be a great way to teach them about responsibility and sustainability. That sounds like a solid plan. It’s surprising how much you can learn from old things. Speaking of which, have you heard about the new relationship I’m in? No, really? Who is it? It’s someone from the local gym. We met a few months ago, and it’s been going pretty well. She’s really into fitness, which is a bit of a contrast to me, but that’s the charm, isn’t it? Still, I’ve got to admit, it’s been a while since I’ve had a real connection like that. That’s great to hear. I’ve been thinking about starting to date again myself.

So, do you ever just sit there and think, like, “I could be out there working real jobs, but no, I’m just sitting here doing PhD stuff?” Yeah, I mean, it’s funny. I feel like I’m in a bubble sometimes. I can’t even remember the last time I had to worry about money. It’s like, I’m getting paid to think, which is a bit weird, but I guess that’s the gig. I know, right? I mean, I have a proper job, but sometimes I feel like I’m still in that PhD bubble. I just keep thinking, “What if I did something else?” But the thing is, I’ve got this research job now, and it’s actually pretty stable. I mean, not like the kind of stability I had in my previous roles, but it’s good. Yeah, I can see that. I envy you a bit, to be honest. You’ve got a proper career, you’re not in that PhD limbo. I mean, I still have time, but I don’t know if I’ll ever get out of it. Sometimes I think about what I’d do if I didn’t have to do this. Maybe go into finance? Or maybe just work in a bar like my cousin. He’s got a good job, he doesn’t even have to think about his future. My cousin did that too. He’s in a bar in Sunderland, and he’s got a great life. He doesn’t have to worry about politics or Trump or anything. He just serves drinks and tells jokes. I’d be fine with that, honestly. But I guess I like the research part. There’s something about solving problems and finding answers. It’s not always the most exciting, but it gives me a sense of purpose. I can see that. I mean, I do enjoy my work, even if it’s not the most glamorous. I like the idea of contributing something to the world. I just wish it was easier to get there. I mean, I’ve got a full scholarship, and I’m not struggling financially, but I still feel like I’ve got a long way to go. That’s true. But you’re not alone in that. I remember when I was in my first job, I felt like I was just trying to keep my head above water.

I can't believe we've got to the point where we're watching  Blue Peter  just for the badges. It's like we're back in primary school. Well, it's not just the badges, it's the whole thing. The way they present things — it's so educational, isn’t it? I mean, I used to think they were just about the boat and the badges, but now I see that they actually do cover a lot of interesting stuff. Yeah, I suppose. But it’s just so different from the way we used to watch it. I remember when we were kids, we’d all gather around the TV every Sunday. Now, we’re just sitting here, drinking wine and trying to remember what the  Blue Peter  badge even looks like. I know, it’s nostalgic, isn’t it? I think part of it is that it’s a bit of a throwback, you know? It’s a bit like a time capsule — all the old stuff they used to do, like building model ships or making patchwork quilts. I do like the way they used to do those really long segments with the land-based activities. I remember when they started doing that with the killer whales — watching them in their tanks, interacting with them. It was so fascinating. Oh, I still remember that! It was like a documentary, wasn’t it? I think it was one of the first times I ever saw a killer whale live, even if just on TV. It was so majestic. I can still picture it, the way it moved through the water, the way it interacted with the trainers. Yeah, it was amazing. I think it was one of those rare moments where you could really see the beauty of nature, even in a controlled environment. It made me think about how important it is to protect marine life, you know? Exactly. I mean, even if it was just on TV, it sparked a lot of interest in people. Do you think there’s a way to bring that back? Like, maybe make more educational content that’s as engaging as that? I think there is, but I also think it’s hard in this age of fast-paced, snackable content. People don’t have the patience for long, educational shows anymore. They just want quick fixes. I guess. But maybe there’s something to be said about slower, more thoughtful content.

Well, I've been meaning to talk to you both about that hostel we've been managing down in Bury. It's been a bit of a nightmare, honestly. I don't know what's going on with the management, but the place is falling apart. Oh, I heard about that. I think they've been trying to cut costs, but it's just making things worse. You know how these places work – if you don't maintain them, they just decay. It's sad, really. I remember when we first started managing it. We had a good team, and things were running smoothly. But now, it's like everything's been left to rot. I wonder if they’ve even got someone in charge anymore. I don't know. I’ve been trying to reach the manager, but they’re always on holiday or something. I had an email yesterday about a maintenance issue – the boiler’s broken again. I said we need to get it fixed, and they just said, “We’ll get to it when we can.” That’s not a way to run a hostel. I can imagine. I’ve got a friend who’s in hospital with a broken leg. He was staying there for a while, and he said it was quite a mess. He said the rooms were damp and the heating didn’t work, and he had to borrow a blanket from another resident. That’s not acceptable. If we’re supposed to be helping people in need, then we should be providing proper facilities. I mean, I know it's not a luxury place, but basic comfort is still important. I agree. I think we need to make a decision. Maybe we should put in a formal complaint or even consider taking over the management ourselves. We can’t let it keep getting worse. That’s a big step, though. We’d have to do a lot of planning. Maybe we should start by getting more volunteers involved. The hostel’s been a bit of a burden on us, but it’s also a way to give back to the community. Yeah, and it’s not just about the hostel. I’ve been thinking about the old school days too. My parents ran a small shop in Birmingham, and they worked their fingers to the bone to keep it going. It’s not about money; it’s about hard work and making a difference.

So, do you know, I was just thinking about your old job in recruitment. I mean, it must have been quite a different experience from being an associate lecturer, right? Oh, it was totally different. I mean, recruitment was like a fast-paced, high-pressure environment. You were always on your feet, meeting people, trying to match candidates with jobs. It was more about people skills than academic stuff. That sounds intense. I can imagine. I used to think teaching was stressful, but I guess recruitment was another kind of stress. Do you miss it? Not really. I mean, I like being an associate lecturer now. It’s more flexible, and I get to work with students in a different way. But I do miss the energy of the office and the interactions with people from all walks of life. I can see how that would be appealing. But I wonder if you ever found it hard to switch gears? Like, from being in a fast-paced, sales-driven environment to being in a more reflective, educational role. Honestly, it took some time. I had to adjust my approach. In recruitment, you’re always pushing, always selling. Here, it’s about guidance, support, and helping students develop their own ideas. It’s a completely different kind of influence. That’s true. I mean, I did have a lecturer at university who was really passionate about their subject, and it made all the difference. But then again, some lecturers seemed to just go through the motions. Yeah, I’ve heard that too. It’s kind of a double-edged sword. You want someone who’s knowledgeable and engaging, but also someone who can manage the classroom and keep students motivated. It’s not always easy to find that balance. Exactly. I think that’s why the evaluation of academic literacy in courses is so important. If a lecturer isn’t engaging students or making the material relevant, it can really affect how well they learn. Totally. I’ve had a few students who said they didn’t feel their lecturers were really connecting with them. It’s hard to measure, but you can tell when someone’s not putting in the effort. It’s a shame. I think part of the issue is the pressure on universities to increase enrollments and meet targets, which can lead to some lecturers being less invested in the learning experience.

So, do you know anyone here? I’ve been trying to find a study group for my sociology paper, but it’s proving a bit tricky. Not really, I’m just here to grab a coffee and catch up with my friends. Although, I do know a few people in the library. They’re all in the same year as me, though. Hey, isn’t that the guy from the coffee shop earlier? He was talking about his job, right? Yeah, that’s the one. He was saying how he doesn’t get a break during the day. I thought it was funny because he even mentioned taking a nap at his desk. That’s actually kind of sad. I mean, I’ve had a few jobs where I could take a short nap if I needed to, but I guess it depends on the workplace. Yeah, and I think it’s even worse for people working in retail. I’ve heard stories about people being forced to work through their lunch breaks, even if they’re hungry. I can’t even imagine working in retail. I mean, I’ve done some part-time shifts, but it’s not the same as working full-time. At least in university, we can take breaks and study when we want. Exactly. Plus, I’m not sure I could handle the pressure of working in a sales role. I’d end up talking to customers all day and probably get annoyed at the smallest things. I think it’s also about the type of work you like. For instance, I prefer working in a more academic or creative environment. I’d be bored out of my mind if I had to sell stuff all day. I get that. I think the key is finding something that aligns with your interests. If you don’t like it, you’ll end up hating it no matter how much money you make. Totally. I mean, I know some people who work in sales and they actually enjoy it. It’s just about how you approach it. If you’re good at it, it can be rewarding. I guess I’m more of a people person, but I don’t think I’d ever want to work in a place where I have to talk to random strangers all day. It’s just not my thing. I can relate.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing about the military? I mean, I’ve been reading this magazine about it, and it’s like, everything’s so structured. You can’t even think about going to the loo without asking permission. Oh yeah, I remember my cousin was in the army, and he said the same thing. You had to get permission to use the bathroom, like, a full sentence. “Sir, may I be excused to attend to nature’s call?” It was ridiculous. Yeah, I mean, it’s all about hierarchy and rules. But isn’t it like, the opposite of how we do things in civil life? Like, no one’s ever told me I can’t go to the loo without asking. Exactly! I think part of it is training, you know? If you’re used to following orders, it’s just how you’re taught. But honestly, if I had to go through all that in a regular job, I’d go mad. I can’t imagine it. I mean, I like structure, but this is way too much. Although, I guess it does make sense for certain roles. Like, if you’re in a war zone, you need that kind of order. Yeah, but even then, I think some of the rules are just outdated. You know, like the ones about not speaking above a certain volume or not wearing shoes in certain areas. It’s like, who even cares? I heard about this film that came out a few years ago about the military. It was called  Black Hawk Down . I think it’s based on a real incident in Somalia. You know, it’s about how the military can be both heroic and messed up. Oh yeah, I’ve heard of that. I think it was a really intense film. But I haven’t seen it yet. I’ve been meaning to, though. I heard it’s got some really cool action scenes. Although, I’m not sure I’d want to watch it if I was feeling emotional. Yeah, I think it’s more about the chaos of war than the heroics. They show how the military can be so overwhelmed, even with all the training. I guess it’s a bit like how some computer programs work. You have these strict rules, but when something goes wrong, it all falls apart.

So, do you think we should go to the new bar in town or stick to the usual one? I heard it’s got a great vibe and the drinks are more affordable now. Honestly, I’d say we stick with the usual one. I mean, it’s familiar, and I don’t want to risk getting lost in some new place with questionable Wi-Fi and questionable people. Fair enough. But I’ve been thinking—what if we just went to that new café down by the park? You know, the one with the live music and the good coffee? It’s not too far. That sounds nice, honestly. I like the idea of the live music. Although, I have to say, I still can’t get over how weird it is that people from London keep coming here like it’s some kind of getaway. Do they even know what the countryside is? Yeah, I mean, I get it. London’s expensive, and people like to escape, but sometimes it feels like they’re not even trying. Like, they pack up their lives, move out here for a few weeks, and then act like they’ve discovered something. It’s rude. For real. I had a mate from London last week, and he was talking about how “different” everything was here. Like, he said, “You know, I’ve never seen a pub without a TV.” I just stared at him for a second. What’s the point of coming here if you’re just going to miss the whole vibe? Exactly. Besides, I don’t think they’re even looking at it the right way. It’s not about the pubs or the countryside—it’s about the people. I mean, I’ve had friends from London, and the first thing they do is ask if I’ve met any “interesting people.” Like, they’re not even trying to be genuine. That’s just the thing, though. I mean, it’s not just them. There’s a lot of racism here, even in the most subtle ways. You hear it in the way people talk, in the way they look at you when you’re from London or the South. It’s like, “Where are you from?” and you say “London,” and the next thing you know, you’re being judged about your accent or your lifestyle. I know.

So, you're here for the first time, right? How’s the flat looking to you?      Honestly, it’s a bit more than I expected. I mean, it’s cozy, but it feels like we’ve got the whole place to ourselves. Just like a little haven.      Oh, it’s very much like that. You know, it’s not too big, but it’s got all the essentials. The kitchen, for one, is spotless.      And the flat has a nice flow. From the living room to the kitchen, it’s like everything is in its place. Though I do notice you’ve got a load of plastic bags in the bin. My son always says that’s a sign of someone who’s not sure where they’re going with their life.      Oh, come on, it’s just a bit of recycling. I mean, we’re trying to be eco-friendly, aren’t we?      Yeah, but even so, the flat could do with a bit more personality. I mean, it’s all very functional, but maybe a few decorations would make it feel more like home.      Decorations? You know, I tried putting up a little picture on the wall. My wife said it looked like a gift from a funeral.      That’s not quite right, but I can see where she’s coming from. You know, the flat’s got character, but it could use a bit more warmth.      I agree. We’re planning to redecorate soon. I mean, it’s not like we’re  that  far into the project. I just need to get a bit of time to figure out what we want to do.      Oh, that’s great. I was just thinking about the kitchen. It’s a good size, but it could do with a few more shelves. I mean, we’ve got all these spices and nuts, and it’s all just lying around on the counter.      Yeah, I’ve got a lot of nut jars in the kitchen. They’re all different sizes, and I can’t tell which is which.      Oh, go on then, maybe you could label them. That would be a help.      I’ve tried, but the labels keep getting lost. It’s like they have a life of their own.      I know what you mean. I’ve got a drawer full of labels over there. They’ve all got different colors, and I can’t even remember what they’re for.

So, do you ever just sit there and scroll through the internet for hours without even realizing how much time has passed? I’m starting to think I’m not the only one. I mean, I found myself on a rabbit hole about house prices the other day, and I didn’t even remember how long I was on my phone. Oh, I’ve definitely done that. I think it’s the same with politics. I’ll start reading an article, and before I know it, I’ve gone through half the news feed. It’s like the internet has this weird way of making you want to keep going even when you’re not sure why. Yeah, and it’s not just the internet, is it? I mean, work keeps pulling me in too. I got so caught up in a project the other week that I didn’t even notice I was late for dinner. My flatmate was like, “You’re not even here!” and I was like, “I was here, I just didn’t notice the time.” That’s the worst. I once had a meeting that was supposed to start at 2 PM, and I walked in at 3:15 because I was trying to finish off a report. My boss was like, “What are you doing?” and I just said, “I was just… scrolling.” And I didn’t even know I was scrolling until she said that. It’s so funny how we all seem to be doing the same thing, just in slightly different ways. Oh, and I’m not even sure if I’m just bad at time management or if it’s the internet itself. Or maybe it’s being a graduate with a degree but still not sure what I want to do with my life. I think the internet is just the most convenient excuse. You can say you were working, you were reading, you were doing something productive, and then you’re like, “Oh, no, I was just…” And honestly, I’m not sure if it’s a bad thing. I mean, I’ve learned so much from the internet, but I also feel like I’m just being pulled in every direction. I guess that’s the trade-off, isn’t it? You get a lot of information, but sometimes it’s hard to know what to do with it.

So, do you ever find it weird how people always seem to have everything sorted out in the end? Like, no matter what happens, they just…  poof —everything’s fine. I mean, I guess that’s the British way, isn’t it? We always make the best of things. Even if we’re not exactly making the best of things. Oh, I’ve seen it all. I once had a patient who had a heart attack and started screaming, “I don’t want to die!” and the next day he was back, arguing with his wife about who did the laundry. Wow. That’s… weirdly reassuring, honestly. Yeah, I mean, you get used to it. I’ve been a nurse for years now, and I’ve seen people go from the brink of death to arguing with their kids about something trivial. It’s like… life’s just a continuous loop of drama. I can relate. I’m a copywriter, so I’m always writing about people’s lives, their struggles, their problems. But in real life, I’m like, “I can’t even decide what to have for breakfast today.” Doesn’t sound like a problem. Oh, it is! I’m not a morning person, and I’ve got this thing where I don’t like coffee, but I still have to drink it because it’s part of my routine. It feels like a full-blown lifestyle crisis. That sounds oddly therapeutic. I know, right? I used to be the same. I’d panic about every little thing. But now I just try to stay positive. Even if it’s just pretending I’m happy. Yeah, that’s the key. Pretend. It works for me. I just say, “I’m so happy, I could cry,” and then I immediately start crying. That’s not happiness, that’s just sadness with a performance attached. Exactly. Anyway, I’ve been meaning to tell you about my new colleague. She’s this elderly lady who’s always telling me, “You’ve got to live life to the fullest, love.” And then she goes and spends the whole day at bingo. That’s… living life to the fullest? It’s called “bingo.” It’s a sport, it’s a lifestyle, it’s a way of life. I think she’s right, though. You know, I’ve been so busy with work, and I’ve been neglecting my own life.
